2-0091-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Asszony, Biztos Urak! Az ír elnökségtől mi, Patrióták, azt várjuk, hogy az európai polgárok valós érdekeit tartsa szem előtt: biztonságukat és jólétüket. A biztonságuk garantálása érdekében az illegális migrációt megállítani kell, nem pedig menedzselni. Európának vissza kell szereznie az ellenőrzést a külső határai felett. A visszaküldési irányelv hatékony alkalmazása kulcskérdés lesz.

Az európai jóléthez a versenyképességünk visszaszerzése elengedhetetlen. Ehhez alacsonyabb energiaárakra és kevesebb bürokráciára van szükség. A következő uniós költségvetésben ellenezzük a mezőgazdasági és a kohéziós források csökkentését. Elutasítjuk a további központosítást, a bürokratikus kiadások növelését és az ideológiai alapú feltételességi mechanizmust, mert mára bebizonyosodott, hogy a jogállamisági feltételeket ideológiai alapon alkalmazzák.

Jól mutatja a Bizottság által alkalmazott kettős mércét az a mélységes hallgatás, amelyet az új magyar kormány demokráciát leromboló alkotmánymódosításai kapcsán látunk. A köztársasági elnök és az Alkotmánybíróság tagjainak elmozdítása, a parlamenti képviselők választhatóságának korlátozása Európában példa nélküli lépések, amik minden létező demokratikus és jogállami alapelvvel szembemennek. Az előző patrióta, szuverenista kormány évekig tartó alaptalan vegzálása után úgy tűnik, ennek a Háznak és a Bizottságnak csak szelektíven fontos a demokrácia és a jogállam.

Nincs helye kettős mércének és ideológiának a bővítés kérdésében sem. Nem lehet figyelmen kívül hagyni, hogy Ukrajna háborúban áll, csatlakozása pedig súlyos következményekkel jár majd az európai mezőgazdaságra, a munkaerőpiacokra, a kohéziós politikára és a biztonságunkra nézve. Mi, Patrióták az ír elnökségtől több józan észt és kevesebb ideológiát várunk.
2-0091-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President, Commissioners! We, Patriots, expect the Irish presidency to keep the real interests of European citizens in mind: their security and well-being. In order to guarantee their safety, illegal migration must be stopped, not managed. Europe must regain control of its external borders. Effective application of the return policy will be a key issue.

Regaining our competitiveness is essential for European prosperity. This requires lower energy prices and less bureaucracy. In the next EU budget, we oppose the reduction of agricultural and cohesion funds. We reject further centralization, increased bureaucratic spending and an ideologically based conditionality mechanism because it has now been proven that rule of law conditions are applied on ideological grounds.

The double standard applied by the Commission is clearly demonstrated by the profound silence we see in relation to the constitutional amendments of the new Hungarian government that destroy democracy. The removal of the President of the Republic and the members of the Constitutional Court, and the restriction of the electability of parliamentarians are unprecedented steps in Europe that go against all existing democratic and constitutional principles. After years of baseless condemnation of the previous patriotic, sovereignist government, it seems that democracy and the rule of law are only selectively important to this House and the Commission.

There is no place for double standards and ideology in the issue of enlargement either. It cannot be ignored that Ukraine is at war and its accession will have serious consequences for European agriculture, labor markets, cohesion policy and our security. We Patriots expect more common sense and less ideology from the Irish presidency.

2-0092-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowny panie premierze! Przede wszystkim chcę bardzo serdecznie podziękować panu premierowi za przedstawienie wizji prezydencji irlandzkiej. Rzeczywiście bardzo dużo ważnych wyzwań i trzymamy kciuki, żeby te cele zostały zrealizowane. Bezpieczeństwo niewątpliwie jest kwestią dzisiaj dla Unii Europejskiej, dla nas wszystkich najistotniejszą.

Natomiast ja chciałam skoncentrować się w swojej wypowiedzi na kwestiach dotyczących – wydaje się – najtrudniejszego zadania, przed którym stoi prezydencja irlandzka i również my wszyscy, czyli budżet Unii Europejskiej na następne lata, ramy finansowe na kolejną perspektywę finansową. To jest ogromne wyzwanie, ale też wiele znaków zapytania. Przede wszystkim, myślę, że wszyscy stoimy na stanowisku, przynajmniej w mojej grupie politycznej, że absolutnie nie może być mowy o tym, ażeby nakładać nowe obciążenia podatkowe na przedsiębiorców i na Europejczyków.

Mówicie państwo o tym, że trzeba zwiększać budżet. My również nie chcemy, żeby wydatki były cięte w tych najistotniejszych, najważniejszych dla Unii Europejskiej projektach, ale nie może się to odbywać kosztem Europejczyków. Nie może się to odbywać kosztem konkurencyjności przemysłu europejskiego. I to kolejne zadanie, na które chciałam zwrócić uwagę.

Wszyscy czekamy z niecierpliwością na propozycję rewizji systemu ETS. Od tego będzie zależało – to jest kluczowe – czy gospodarka europejska wreszcie będzie mogła rozwinąć skrzydła i stać się konkurencyjna, a nie tak jak do tej pory po prostu być gnieciona rozwiązaniami, które niestety sama Unia Europejska przygotowała. Trzymam kciuki, panie premierze, za państwa prezydencję i mam nadzieję, że będzie ona, tak jak wszyscy oczekujemy, niezwykle ważna, istotna i konstruktywna dla nas wszystkich.
2-0092-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Dear Mr. Prime Minister! First of all, I would like to thank the Prime Minister very much for presenting his vision for the Irish Presidency. There are indeed many important challenges and we keep our fingers crossed that these goals will be achieved. Security is undoubtedly an issue for the European Union today, the most important issue for all of us.

However, I wanted to focus my statement on issues related to what seems to be the most difficult task facing the Irish Presidency and all of us, i.e. the European Union budget for the coming years and the financial framework for the next financial perspective. This is a huge challenge, but also many question marks. First of all, I think that we all take the position, at least in my political group, that there is absolutely no question of imposing new tax burdens on entrepreneurs and Europeans.

You say that the budget needs to be increased. We also do not want spending to be cut in these most important projects for the European Union, but this cannot be done at the expense of Europeans. This cannot be done at the expense of the competitiveness of European industry. And this is another task to which I would like to draw attention.

We are all looking forward to the proposal to revise the ETS system. This will determine - and this is crucial - whether the European economy will finally be able to spread its wings and become competitive, and not, as before, simply be crushed by the solutions that, unfortunately, the European Union itself has prepared. I keep my fingers crossed, Mr. Prime Minister, for your presidency and I hope that it will be, as we all expect, extremely important, important and constructive for all of us.

2-0093-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, cher Taoiseach – cher Micheál –, d’abord un grand merci de cette présentation et de vos priorités, qui sont résolument ambitieuses pour l’Europe. Alors, ce n’est un secret pour personne: on a l’habitude de travailler ensemble. Vous êtes un membre éminent de la famille Renew, et vous ne serez pas surpris, donc, de m’entendre dire que les priorités de votre présidence – compétitivité, valeurs, sécurité –, eh bien c’est aussi la feuille de route de notre groupe politique, Renew Europe.

Alors, cher Taoiseach, oui, vous avez raison: avançons sur notre compétitivité, achevons enfin notre marché unique, investissons davantage dans l’innovation, simplifions nos règles, donnons à nos entreprises les moyens de grandir en Europe plutôt que d’aller réussir ailleurs, avançons sur le prochain budget européen! Le cadre financier pluriannuel sera un test de vérité: si nous voulons une Europe puissante, nous devons lui donner les moyens de ses ambitions. Avançons enfin sur notre influence géopolitique: en poursuivant notre soutien à l’Ukraine, en préparant l’élargissement de notre Union et en défendant, sans jamais transiger, l’état de droit et les valeurs qui fondent notre projet européen!

Je voudrais dire un mot sur un dossier plus précis, parce que votre présidence sera l’occasion de démontrer que l’Europe sait protéger sans renoncer à ses principes. C’est exactement le sens du règlement sur la protection des enfants en ligne, dont vous faites une priorité absolue, et je voudrais vous en remercier. Cela fait quatre ans – quatre ans! – que nous attendons ce texte. Il n’y a plus de temps à perdre, et nous comptons sur votre présidence pour conclure au plus vite les négociations sur la réglementation à long terme. Vous pourrez compter sur le soutien absolu de mon groupe politique sur cette question, qui est fondamentale.

Ces réformes, cher Taoiseach, elles ne sont plus une option: elles sont une exigence pour les citoyens européens, parce que votre présidence, elle débute dans une époque troublée. Le monde est redevenu brutal, la force veut remplacer le droit, les puissances s’affrontent, les démocraties sont défiés, et, dans ce monde, l’Europe ne peut plus subir. Face à cette brutalité, notre réponse doit être l’affirmation de la puissance européenne, mais d’une puissance qui nous ressemble: une puissance démocratique, une puissance fondée sur nos valeurs, sur nos libertés et sur l’état de droit. Ces valeurs ne sont en aucun cas un frein à la puissance européenne – et je sais que nous partageons cela –, elles en sont au contraire la condition, parce que l’Europe, elle ne veut pas être brutale – ce n’est pas ça, notre modèle –, mais elle ne veut pas, évidemment, non plus disparaître – et pour cela, il faut assumer délibérément le rapport de force. On ne renie en rien ce que nous sommes.

Alors, cher Micheál, vous le savez, vous pouvez compter sur Renew pour la réussite de votre présidence, et puisque l’Irlande est aujourd’hui à l’honneur, permettez-moi de citer l’un de vos plus grands écrivains, Oscar Wilde: «Le progrès est la réalisation des utopies.» Alors, faisons en sorte que, pendant ces six mois, nos utopies européennes deviennent des progrès bien réels!
2-0093-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear Taoiseach – dear Micheál –, first of all, thank you very much for this presentation and for your priorities, which are resolutely ambitious for Europe. So, it’s no secret: we’re used to working together. You are an eminent member of the Renew family, and you will not be surprised, therefore, to hear me say that the priorities of your presidency – competitiveness, values, security – are also the roadmap of our political group, Renew Europe.

So, dear Taoiseach, yes, you are right: let's move forward on our competitiveness, let's finally complete our single market, let's invest more in innovation, let's simplify our rules, let's give our businesses the means to grow in Europe rather than going to succeed elsewhere, let's move forward on the next European budget! The multiannual financial framework will be a truth test: if we want a powerful Europe, we must give it the means to achieve its ambitions. Let us finally move forward with our geopolitical influence: by continuing our support for Ukraine, by preparing the enlargement of our Union and by defending, without ever compromising, the rule of law and the values ​​which underpin our European project!

I would like to say a word on a more specific issue, because your presidency will be an opportunity to demonstrate that Europe knows how to protect without renouncing its principles. This is exactly the meaning of the regulation on protecting children online, which you make an absolute priority, and I would like to thank you for it. It’s been four years – four years! – that we are waiting for this text. There is no more time to waste, and we are counting on your presidency to conclude the negotiations on long-term regulations as quickly as possible. You can count on the absolute support of my political group on this issue, which is fundamental.

These reforms, dear Taoiseach, are no longer an option: they are a demand for European citizens, because your presidency begins in troubled times. The world has become brutal again, force wants to replace law, powers clash, democracies are challenged, and, in this world, Europe can no longer endure. Faced with this brutality, our response must be the affirmation of European power, but of a power that resembles us: a democratic power, a power based on our values, on our freedoms and on the rule of law. These values ​​are in no way a brake on European power - and I know that we share this -, on the contrary, they are the condition, because Europe does not want to be brutal - that is not our model -, but it obviously does not want to disappear either - and for that, we must deliberately assume the balance of power. We in no way deny what we are.

So, dear Micheál, as you know, you can count on Renew for the success of your presidency, and since Ireland is in the spotlight today, allow me to quote one of your greatest writers, Oscar Wilde: “Progress is the realization of utopias.” So, let's ensure that, during these six months, our European utopias become very real progress!

2-0098-0000.sourceText:
, от името на групата ESN. – Г-жо Председател, Европейският съюз бавно, но сигурно губи позициите си в световната икономика. Възстановяването на конкурентоспособността вече не е въпрос на избор, а на оцеляване. Нужна е по-благоприятна среда за инвестиции, предприемачество и индустриално развитие. Предприятията се нуждаят от опростени правила и достъпна енергия, а не от нови регулации.

Шансът на Европа е в изобилието от таланти на нашия континент. Смелостта на предприемачите, които продължават напред, въпреки недомислиците на зелената сделка. И те заслужават подкрепа. Деиндустриализацията не просто отслабва икономическата сила на европейските държави, тя накърнява достойнството на професионалиста, останал без работа, ограничава възможностите за по-младите поколения, а оцеляването на цели региони е изложено на риск. Укрепването на отбранителните способности е необходимо, но трайната сигурност изисква и активна дипломация, защото устойчивите решения и мирът се постигат чрез диалог. Не бива да забравяме, че овладяването на миграционните потоци също е в основата на сигурността.

Затова приветствам ангажимента на ирландското председателство за намаляване на административната тежест за развитие на единния пазар и изграждане на по-сигурна и достъпна енергийна система. Самата Ирландия показва как благоприятната среда за инвестиции, предприемачество и иновации се превръща в устойчив икономически успех. Именно по този път Европа може да възстанови своята конкурентоспособност и мястото си в световната икономика.
2-0098-0000.englishText:
, on behalf of the ESN Group. - Madam President, the European Union is slowly but surely losing its position in the world economy. Restoring competitiveness is no longer a matter of choice, but of survival. A more favorable environment for investment, entrepreneurship and industrial development is needed. Businesses need simplified rules and affordable energy, not new regulations.

Europe's chance lies in the abundance of talent on our continent. The courage of entrepreneurs who press ahead despite the setbacks of the green deal. And they deserve support. Deindustrialization not only weakens the economic strength of European countries, it undermines the dignity of the unemployed professional, limits opportunities for younger generations, and the survival of entire regions is at risk. Strengthening defense capabilities is necessary, but lasting security also requires active diplomacy, because durable solutions and peace are achieved through dialogue. We should not forget that the control of migration flows is also the basis of security.

I therefore welcome the commitment of the Irish Presidency to reduce the administrative burden to develop the single market and build a more secure and affordable energy system. Ireland itself shows how a favorable environment for investment, entrepreneurship and innovation translates into sustainable economic success. It is in this way that Europe can restore its competitiveness and its place in the world economy.

2-0105-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, meine sehr geehrten Damen und Herren! Das Motto der irischen Ratspräsidentschaft, Strength with unity, Stärke durch Einheit, lädt mich als Oppositionellen gerade dazu ein, den Vorwurf zu machen, dass diese Einheit ein Festhalten an einer verfehlten Politik ist. Und gerade das sonst so sehr EU-freundliche Irland leidet jetzt unter dieser verfehlten Politik. Zwei Beispiele: erstens einmal etwa die Migrationspolitik, die auch in Irland durch das Opt-in beim Migrations- und Asylpakt immer mehr zu einem Problem wird, und auf der anderen Seite etwa der Green Deal und die Auswirkungen auf Irland, die auf Irland sehr, sehr unangenehme Auswirkungen haben und dort die Landwirtschaft sehr auch in Stress bringen.

Aber ungeachtet aller politischen Diskussionen möchte ich Irland ausrichten: Sie haben ein wundervolles Land, Sie haben wundervolle Menschen, Sie haben eine wundervolle Kultur, und Sie haben alles Recht dazu, stolz auf Ihr Land zu sein.
2-0105-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen! The motto of the Irish Council Presidency, Strength with unity, invites me, as an opposition member, to accuse me of saying that this unity is an adherence to a failed policy. And Ireland, which is otherwise very EU-friendly, is now suffering from this failed policy. Two examples: firstly, migration policy, which is also becoming more and more of a problem in Ireland due to the opt-in to the migration and asylum pact, and on the other hand, the Green Deal and the effects on Ireland, which have very, very unpleasant effects on Ireland and are also putting a lot of stress on agriculture there.

But regardless of any political discussions, I would like to say to Ireland: you have a wonderful country, you have wonderful people, you have a wonderful culture and you have every right to be proud of your country.

2-0106-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, buongiorno Irlanda.

La Presidenza irlandese sulla competitività afferma certamente valori condivisibili, però è un po' carente, secondo me: non cita mai le microimprese, eppure, sono 25 milioni le microimprese europee, e generano il 20 % del prodotto interno europeo e hanno problemi enormi.

L'accesso al credito, anzitutto. Dal 2011, i prestiti bancari alle imprese più piccole sono crollati del 37 %, schiacciati da algoritmi di rating e da una regolamentazione sbagliata per l'asimmetria regolatoria fra le stesse imprese.

Infine, la concorrenza sleale della Cina è sussidiata dallo Stato e rovina i nostri distretti.

Inoltre, sul 28º regime, di cui sono relatore ombra, la sinistra in Parlamento ha avanzato modifiche ideologiche di impronta ipersindacale – peraltro prive di base giuridica – e di maggior rigidità per gli investitori, che vanno in senso contrario allo spirito della proposta.

La Presidenza come intende salvaguardare questo aspetto? Buon lavoro.
2-0106-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, good morning Ireland.

The Irish Presidency on competitiveness certainly affirms values ​​that can be shared, but it is a bit lacking, in my opinion: it never mentions micro-enterprises, and yet, there are 25 million European micro-enterprises, and they generate 20 % of the European domestic product and have enormous problems.

Access to credit, first and foremost. Since 2011, bank loans to smaller businesses have collapsed by 37 %, crushed by rating algorithms and misguided regulation due to regulatory asymmetry between the businesses themselves.

Finally, China's unfair competition is subsidized by the state and ruins our districts.

Furthermore, on the 28th regime, for which I am shadow rapporteur, the left in Parliament has advanced ideological changes with a hyper-union imprint - which however have no legal basis - and with greater rigidity for investors, which go against the spirit of the proposal.

How does the Presidency intend to safeguard this aspect? Good work.

2-0113-0000.sourceText:
Liebe Frau Präsidentin, Micheál Martin, Maroš Šefčovič, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Drei Punkte hat der Kollege hier hervorgehoben: wirtschaftliche Prosperität, Werte und Sicherheit. Wirtschaftliche Prosperität hat die EU selbst zerstört durch die unsinnigen Embargos gegen Russland. Unsere Unternehmen haben jetzt die teuersten Energiepreise, sind nicht mehr konkurrenzfähig auf den Weltmärkten, verlassen die Europäische Union oder gehen pleite. Gleichzeitig zahlt die Europäische Union an die Ukraine – 300 Mrd. Euro waren das in dem ganzen Zeitraum seit Anfang des Krieges.

Und wie viel geht in die Forschung, zur Förderung der Wirtschaft und der Prosperität? Der Forschungs- und Innovationsfonds bekommt 90 Milliarden, lediglich 90 Milliarden im gleichen Zeitraum, und mickrige 10 Milliarden davon sind für Start-ups. Wir müssen die Embargos beenden und die Wirtschaft und Innovation stärken.

Werte? Über welche Werte reden Sie? Gleich wird hier abgestimmt über das Verbot der EU-Partei, der stärksten Partei in Deutschland, auf Antrag der Kommunisten, Sozialisten und der Grünen: Das sind die wahren Feinde der Demokratie; hier werden demokratische Werte, europäische Werte mit Füßen getreten.

Und Sicherheit? Sicherheit in der EU? Ich bin gespannt. Erklären Sie das den zwei kleinen Mädchen und der Ehefrau von dem schwedischen Polizisten Christian Zedig, der neulich umgebracht wurde. Sie haben in der EU die Sicherheit der EU-Bürger durch die Massenmigration zerstört. Und nur wir, nur wir durch die Remigration, wir liefern bereits aus der Opposition, und wir beschützen die Bürger Europas.
2-0113-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President, Micheál Martin, Maroš Šefčovič, dear colleagues! The colleague highlighted three points here: economic prosperity, values ​​and security. The EU itself has destroyed economic prosperity through the senseless embargoes against Russia. Our companies now have the most expensive energy prices, are no longer competitive on world markets, are leaving the European Union or are going bankrupt. At the same time, the European Union is paying Ukraine 300 billion euros in the entire period since the beginning of the war.

And how much goes into research to promote the economy and prosperity? The research and innovation fund gets 90 billion, just 90 billion in the same period, and a measly 10 billion of that is for start-ups. We must end the embargoes and strengthen the economy and innovation.

Values? What values ​​are you talking about? A vote is about to take place here to ban the EU party, the strongest party in Germany, at the request of the communists, socialists and the Greens: These are the real enemies of democracy; Democratic values ​​and European values ​​are being trampled on here.

And security? Security in the EU? I am excited. Explain this to the two little girls and the wife of the Swedish policeman Christian Zedig, who was recently killed. They have destroyed the security of EU citizens in the EU through mass migration. And only we, only we through remigration, we are already delivering from the opposition, and we are protecting the citizens of Europe.

2-0116-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, começo naturalmente por saudar a Presidência irlandesa e estou certa de que a cooperação com este Parlamento será estreita e profícua.

Sabemos também que uma das prioridades é o orçamento de longo prazo da União e sabemos bem, também, de um compromisso de um trabalho intenso e ambicioso com todos os líderes da União Europeia para que seja possível ter um acordo até ao final de 2026.

Como a Senhora Presidente sabe, para o Parlamento Europeu, para nós, é absolutamente claro que é preciso que esse acordo exista até ao final do ano.

Mas não é possível trabalhar no QFP olhando só para o lado da despesa. É importante olharmos também para a ambição orçamental e é preciso olhar para a receita. Falo, obviamente, dos novos recursos próprios que tornem o orçamento europeu mais justo, mais robusto e menos dependente das contribuições nacionais.

Não se pode fazer mais com menos e este Parlamento apoia a abordagem da Comissão de um cabaz para obter um acordo sobre novos recursos próprios.

Precisamos de uma União Europeia mais segura, competitiva e coesa e de um orçamento à altura dessa ambição. Novas prioridades requerem maior investimento. Uma Europa mais forte exige um orçamento também mais forte.
2-0116-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I naturally begin by welcoming the Irish Presidency and I am sure that cooperation with this Parliament will be close and fruitful.

We also know that one of the priorities is the Union's long-term budget and we are also well aware of a commitment to intense and ambitious work with all European Union leaders so that it is possible to have an agreement by the end of 2026.

As Madam President knows, for the European Parliament, for us, it is absolutely clear that this agreement needs to exist by the end of the year.

But it is not possible to work on the MFF looking only at the expenditure side. It is important that we also look at the budgetary ambition and we need to look at revenue. I am obviously talking about new own resources that make the European budget fairer, more robust and less dependent on national contributions.

More cannot be done with less and this Parliament supports the Commission's basket approach to reaching agreement on new own resources.

We need a safer, more competitive and cohesive European Union and a budget that matches this ambition. New priorities require greater investment. A stronger Europe also requires a stronger budget.

2-0123-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Premier ministre, au moment où il vous revient de présider les négociations sur le budget pluriannuel, nous voulons vous adresser un message clair: on ne construit pas la compétitivité en sacrifiant la solidarité ou en léguant une planète invivable à nos enfants. Car, comme le dit le proverbe irlandais: «C’est en nous abritant les uns les autres que nous vivons.» Aussi, tant que le Conseil ne renoncera pas à liquider le Fonds européen ou à rogner les Fonds de cohésion pour financer le Fonds de compétitivité, il n’y aura pas de consentement du Parlement européen.

L’autre clash annoncé, c’est sur l’écologie. Je vois bien les tentations de tuer le principe consistant à «ne pas causer de préjudice important» à coups de dérogations, qui permettraient aux bénéficiaires de l’argent européen de s’asseoir sur les dégâts collatéraux qu’ils font subir à la nation. Mais j’ose espérer que, après l’épisode terrible de canicule que nous venons de vivre, votre présidence portera haut cette idée que, si l’union fait la force, l’unité se forge dans la justice sociale et dans la responsabilité environnementale.
2-0123-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Prime Minister, at a time when it is up to you to chair the negotiations on the multiannual budget, we want to send you a clear message: we do not build competitiveness by sacrificing solidarity or by bequeathing an unlivable planet to our children. Because, as the Irish proverb says: “It is by sheltering each other that we live.” Also, as long as the Council does not give up liquidating the European Fund or cutting back the Cohesion Funds to finance the Competitiveness Fund, there will be no consent from the European Parliament.

The other clash announced is over ecology. I can clearly see the temptations to kill the principle of “not causing significant harm” with derogations, which would allow the beneficiaries of European money to sit on the collateral damage they inflict on the nation. But I dare to hope that, after the terrible heatwave episode that we have just experienced, your presidency will uphold this idea that, if there is strength in unity, unity is forged in social justice and environmental responsibility.

2-0124-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, aujourd’hui, nos agriculteurs n’étouffent pas sous le manque de promesses, ils étouffent sous leur accumulation. L’Union européenne est devenue une usine à contraintes. Le programme de la présidence irlandaise affiche de beaux objectifs: compétitivité, sécurité alimentaire, simplification. Dans les faits, elle recycle des débats interminables qui encombrent et étouffent encore un peu plus ceux qui produisent.

Nos agriculteurs et nos producteurs n’ont pas besoin de longs discours, ils ont besoin de revenus dignes et d’une vision à long terme. Pourtant, ils subissent une triple peine: des importations qui ne respectent pas nos standards, des coûts et des règles qui changent sans cesse et une bureaucratie qui est devenue hors de contrôle. On les enferme dans toujours plus de pacte vert, de De la ferme à la table, ou de baisse de la PAC, et d’écologie punitive.

Comment prétendre prioriser l’agriculture en réduisant et en désacralisant l’enveloppe de la PAC? Prenons l’élevage: ce n’est pas un problème à corriger, c’est une richesse à défendre, c’est un pilier de notre souveraineté.

Vous nous parlez d’autonomie, de facilité et de nouvelle agriculture sans jamais rencontrer, sans écouter et sans comprendre ce que vivent les agriculteurs. Nous attendons donc, pleins d’espoir, que cette nouvelle présidence entende les agriculteurs et défende une PAC forte, autonome, au service de la production et de ses producteurs.
2-0124-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, today our farmers are not suffocating under the lack of promises, they are suffocating under their accumulation. The European Union has become a factory of constraints. The Irish presidency's program displays some fine objectives: competitiveness, food security, simplification. In fact, it recycles endless debates which further encumber and suffocate those who produce.

Our farmers and producers do not need long speeches, they need decent income and a long-term vision. Yet they suffer a triple penalty: imports that do not meet our standards, costs and rules that are constantly changing and a bureaucracy that has become out of control. We lock them into ever more green pact, from farm to table, or lowering of the CAP, and punitive ecology.

How can we claim to prioritize agriculture by reducing and desacralizing the CAP envelope? Let's take breeding: it is not a problem to correct, it is a wealth to defend, it is a pillar of our sovereignty.

You talk to us about autonomy, ease and new agriculture without ever meeting, without listening and without understanding what farmers experience. We therefore wait, full of hope, for this new presidency to listen to farmers and defend a strong, autonomous CAP, serving production and its producers.

2-0125-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Premierze! Było dużo uprzejmości jak dotąd. A teraz parę szczegółów. Jeden z europejskich think tanków wyliczył właśnie, że w 2025 roku Unia Europejska straciła 90 miliardów euro, dlatego że jest ogromna ofensywa przemysłu chińskiego w Unii Europejskiej i upadają firmy. Mówimy dużo o Zielonym Ładzie, a ja chcę powiedzieć bardzo wyraźnie: najpierw energia powinna być tania dla przedsiębiorców, a później zielona.

Zwracam uwagę prezydencji irlandzkiej również na to, że historycznie Unia jest w tej chwili w największym długu. Jeszcze nigdy Unia Europejska nie była tak zadłużona, jak jest teraz. Mamy ogromny problem, czego świadkami są wszyscy obecni tu na tej sali, bo w Unii Europejskiej upadają firmy albo przenoszą swoją działalność do Indii, do Stanów Zjednoczonych. Ostatnio austriacka firma napisała wprost, gdy głosowaliśmy nad pomocą z funduszu globalizacji, że ucieka do Indii, bo nie wytrzymuje z cenami. Na takie rzeczy trzeba zwrócić uwagę. Życzę powodzenia.
2-0125-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Mr. Prime Minister! There's been a lot of kindness so far. And now a few details. One of the European think tanks has just calculated that in 2025 the European Union will lose EUR 90 billion because there is a huge offensive of the Chinese industry in the European Union and companies are going bankrupt. We talk a lot about the Green Deal, and I want to say it very clearly: first, energy should be cheap for entrepreneurs, and then green.

I also draw the attention of the Irish Presidency to the fact that, historically, the Union is currently in the greatest debt. The European Union has never been as indebted as it is now. We have a huge problem, as everyone present in this room is witnessing, because companies in the European Union are going bankrupt or moving their operations to India or to the United States. Recently, an Austrian company wrote directly, when we voted on aid from the globalization fund, that it was fleeing to India because it could not cope with the prices. You need to pay attention to such things. I wish you good luck.

2-0127-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'Europa ha due grandi priorità.

La prima: combattere tutte quelle follie green ed ecologiste che abbiamo visto nell'ultimo mandato, prima tra tutte l'ETS, quell'odiosa tassa ambientale che fa danni continuamente alle nostre imprese e ai nostri cittadini. Fermare il Green Deal: questo serve per una migliore competitività europea.

E l'altra, che non è seconda a questa prima priorità, è quella della sicurezza dei cittadini, la loro sicurezza che i cittadini europei pretendono di avere per le loro strade, nelle loro città, nelle loro nazioni.

E si combatte con due modalità. La prima è una lotta attiva al fondamentalismo islamico – rispetto al quale troppe persone qui in quest'Aula non stanno parlando, e lo stanno dimenticando – e l'altra è quella della lotta all'immigrazione clandestina: dobbiamo rimpatriare tutti gli immigrati illegali, perché, altrimenti, i problemi di sicurezza peggioreranno giorno dopo giorno, come hanno mostrato i recenti attacchi.
2-0127-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, Europe has two great priorities.

The first: fight all those green and ecological follies that we have seen in the last mandate, first of all the ETS, that hateful environmental tax that continually damages our businesses and our citizens. Stop the Green Deal: this is necessary for better European competitiveness.

And the other, which is not second to this first priority, is that of the safety of citizens, their safety that European citizens claim to have on their streets, in their cities, in their nations.

And we fight in two ways. The first is an active fight against Islamic fundamentalism – about which too many people here in this House are not talking, and are forgetting – and the other is the fight against illegal immigration: we must repatriate all illegal immigrants, because, otherwise, the security problems will get worse day by day, as the recent attacks have shown.

2-0133-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, EU-kuplassa eletään aivan toisessa todellisuudessa kuin missä tavalliset eurooppalaiset elävät. Irlanti on uusi EU-puheenjohtaja, ja tämän puheenjohtajakauden toimintaohjelma on tästä todellisuusharhasta täydellinen esimerkki.

Kun eurooppalaiset pyytävät päättäjiltä yksinkertaisia asioita, kuten turvallisuutta, kohtuuhintaista energiaa ja asumista sekä suojattuja ulkorajoja, mitä he saavat? Arvojulistuksia, LGBTIQ-ohjelmia sekä antirasismistrategioita. Tässä toimintaohjelmassa käytetään sivukaupalla tilaa siihen, mitä ihmisten pitäisi ajatella ja mitä arvoja omaksua. Nämäkö asiat valvottavat eurooppalaisia öisin? No, eivät toden totta valvota. Lakatkaa siis jo tuputtamasta näitä ideologisia ohjelmianne ja alkakaa huolehtia siitä, josta teidät on valittu pitämään huolta: siitä, että kansalaisilla on turvallinen Eurooppa, jossa leivän päälle saa muutakin kuin pelkän ylähuulen.
2-0133-0000.englishText:
Dear President, in the EU bubble we live in a completely different reality than the one in which ordinary Europeans live. Ireland is the new EU presidency, and the action program for this presidency is a perfect example of this reality bias.

When Europeans ask policymakers for simple things like security, affordable energy and housing, and secure external borders, what do they get? Declarations of values, LGBTIQ programs and anti-racism strategies. In this action program, space is used in the side shop for what people should think and what values ​​to adopt. Are these things keeping Europeans up at night? Well, they don't really control it. So stop pushing these ideological programs of yours already and start taking care of what you were elected to take care of: that the citizens have a safe Europe, where you get more than just an upper lip.

2-0160-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Sommer, Sonne, Massenüberwachung. So stellen sich einige EU‑Eliten den Start in die Sommerferien vor. Kurz vor der Pause soll noch schnell eine Überwachungsstruktur beschlossen werden. Und das, obwohl das Parlament bereits die Chatkontrolle abgelehnt hat. Jetzt wird derselbe Vorschlag einfach wieder aufgewärmt.

In diesem Hohen Haus der Demokratie wird offenbar so lange abgestimmt, bis das Ergebnis passt. Sie alle wissen genau, dass es für die dauerhafte Chatkontrolle keine Mehrheit gibt. Deshalb versucht man nun gemeinsam mit dem Rat, das Ganze durch die Hintertür wiederzubeleben, deshalb wählt man, wie so oft, immer wieder die Salamitaktik.

Übersetzt heißt das: Private Nachrichten sollen technisch durchsuchbar gemacht werden, Bilder, Videos und sogar Texte automatisch geprüft werden. Dass man heute versucht, das Ganze durch einen Dringlichkeitsantrag durchzubringen, zeigt doch den Geist dieses Vorhabens.

Seit 2021 versucht Ursula von der Leyen schon, Zugang zu unseren privaten Nachrichten zu bekommen. Sie selbst kann ihre SMS nicht offenlegen: Jeder weiß, was 2021 auf unserem Kontinent los war während der Corona‑Maßnahmenzeit.

Und natürlich – dieses Argument zieht nicht, ich bin selbst Mutter –, natürlich wollen wir alle Kinder schützen. Aber echter Kinderschutz beginnt nicht damit, jeden Bürger unter Generalverdacht zu stellen. Echter Kinderschutz beginnt dort, wo wirklich Täter gefährlich werden: bei harten Strafen statt Bewährung; es müssen offene Täterregister her; bei besserer Strafverfolgung und der Zerschlagung von Grooming-Gangs. Wer Kinderschänder mit Samthandschuhen anfasst, aber Millionen Bürger unter Generalverdacht stellen möchte, setzt bewusst die Prioritäten falsch.

Und an jeden Bürger: Jeder Bürger kann heute einsehen und sollte dies auch tun, welcher Abgeordnete heute dafür gestimmt hat, dass seine privaten Nachrichten künftig durchsuchbar gemacht werden. Schauen Sie genau hin! Merken Sie sich die Namen! Jeder Abgeordnete, der für diesen Dringlichkeitsantrag stimmt, stimmt auch für eine Massenüberwachung.
2-0160-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Summer, sun, mass surveillance. This is how some EU elites imagine the start of the summer holidays. Shortly before the break, a monitoring structure should be decided quickly. And this despite the fact that Parliament has already rejected chat control. Now the same suggestion is simply being rehashed.

In this House of Democracy, people apparently vote until the result is correct. You all know full well that there is no majority for permanent chat control. That's why they're now trying, together with the council, to revive the whole thing through the back door, which is why, as is so often the case, they're always choosing the salami tactic.

Translated, this means: Private messages should be made technically searchable and images, videos and even texts should be checked automatically. The fact that people are trying to get the whole thing through with an urgent motion today shows the spirit of this project.

Ursula von der Leyen has been trying to get access to our private messages since 2021. She herself cannot disclose her SMS: Everyone knows what was going on on our continent in 2021 during the Corona measures period.

And of course – this argument doesn't work, I'm a mother myself – of course we want to protect all children. But real child protection does not start with placing every citizen under general suspicion. Real child protection begins where perpetrators really become dangerous: with harsh punishments instead of probation; there needs to be open registers of perpetrators; with better law enforcement and the dismantling of grooming gangs. Anyone who treats child molesters with kid gloves but wants to place millions of citizens under general suspicion is deliberately setting their priorities wrong.

And to every citizen: Every citizen can and should see today which MP voted today to make their private messages searchable in the future. Take a close look! Remember the names! Every MP who votes for this emergency motion is also voting for mass surveillance.

2-0006-0000.sourceText:
Als nächster Punkt der Tagesordnung folgt die Aussprache über die Erklärung der Kommission zu den dringenden Maßnahmen zur Stärkung der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und zur Sicherung hochwertiger Arbeitsplätze im Automobilsektor der EU (2026/2806(RSP)).

Ich möchte die Rednerinnen und Redner daran erinnern, dass angesichts der derzeit durchgeführten Testmaßnahmen und des festgesetzten Zeitpunkts für den Abschluss der Aussprache die Redezeit bitte strikt eingehalten wird. Die Regeln zu Blue Cards und Catch-the-Eye sind Ihnen, glaube ich, mittlerweile ausreichend bekannt.
2-0006-0000.englishText:
The next item on the agenda is the debate on the Commission statement on urgent measures to strengthen competitiveness and secure quality jobs in the EU automotive sector (2026/2806(RSP)).

I would like to remind speakers that, given the testing measures currently in place and the time set for the conclusion of the debate, please strictly respect the speaking time. I think you are sufficiently familiar with the rules for Blue Cards and Catch-the-Eye by now.

2-0007-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Mesdames et Messieurs les députés, le secteur automobile européen est en danger de mort. J’avertissais de ce constat il y a plus d’un an et aujourd’hui, constructeurs, équipementiers, c’est l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur qui est sous tension, et l’avenir de millions d’emplois en jeu – soyons lucides, derrière ces emplois, c’est la prospérité, c’est la cohésion sociale de beaucoup de nos territoires, en particulier des territoires ruraux…

Ces secteurs affrontent en même temps un retard technologique, des chaînes d’approvisionnement fragilisées par l’instabilité géopolitique, des bilans financiers plombés par les droits de douane, des restrictions d’accès aux marchés étrangers, une stratégie prédatrice de la Chine pour déverser des surcapacités en Europe.

Le résultat est sans appel: des pertes de parts de marché pour nos constructeurs, l’importation massive de modèles chinois, qui représentent aujourd’hui plus de 15 % des segments électrifiés en Europe, des usines européennes qui tournent au ralenti et le spectre, évidemment, des licenciements collectifs. La Commission européenne mesure pleinement l’urgence de la situation.

Depuis le début de ce mandat, nous nous employons à bâtir, autour du dialogue stratégique avec l’ensemble de la filière, une véritable politique industrielle sur le secteur. Avec le paquet automobile de décembre, complété par la proposition d’accélération industrielle en mars, nous déployons pour la première fois une stratégie sur l’entièreté de la chaîne de valeur du secteur de l’automobile. Avec les règles de contrôle des émissions de CO2, nous introduisons des flexibilités tout en gardant notre cohérence sur nos objectifs. Avec le règlement sur la décarbonation des flottes, nous protégeons un segment essentiel pour nos constructeurs, garantissant la disponibilité de véhicules électriques de seconde main pour les foyers européens. Avec les efforts de simplification, nous accélérons le déploiement des petits véhicules électriques abordables. Avec le «Battery Booster», nous finançons la montée en puissance de notre propre industrie européenne de la batterie. Avec l’accélérateur industriel, nous protégeons les emplois en Europe, nous stoppons l’hémorragie chez les équipementiers et renforçons leur place dans la chaîne de valeur électrifiée.

Alors, vous comprenez, Mesdames et Messieurs les députés, l’urgence qu’il y a à envoyer aujourd’hui des signaux clairs à la filière, et donc la responsabilité collective de l’ensemble des institutions européennes pour ce qui est d’adopter le plus rapidement possible ces textes, qui sont sur la table. L’objectif est clair: casser le cycle mortifère du triple déclin européen – baisse de la production, baisse des parts de marché pour nos constructeurs, baisse de la valeur ajoutée en Europe. Nous le devons à notre industrie. Nous le devons à ses salariés. Nous le devons à nos régions, qui sont sur ce segment automobile.

Vous pouvez compter en tout cas sur moi pour déployer cette stratégie industrielle, tout comme les commissaires Tzitzikóstas et Hoekstra et l’ensemble de la Commission européenne.
2-0007-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, the European automotive sector is in mortal danger. I warned of this observation more than a year ago and today, manufacturers, equipment manufacturers, it is the entire value chain which is under tension, and the future of millions of jobs at stake - let's be clear, behind these jobs, it is prosperity, it is the social cohesion of many of our territories, in particular rural territories...

At the same time, these sectors face technological lag, supply chains weakened by geopolitical instability, financial balance sheets weighed down by customs duties, restrictions on access to foreign markets, and a predatory strategy by China to dump excess capacity in Europe.

The result is clear: losses of market share for our manufacturers, the massive importation of Chinese models, which today represent more than 15% of the electrified segments in Europe, European factories which are idling and the specter, obviously, of collective layoffs. The European Commission fully appreciates the urgency of the situation.

Since the start of this mandate, we have worked to build, around strategic dialogue with the entire sector, a real industrial policy for the sector. With the December automotive package, supplemented by the industrial acceleration proposal in March, we are deploying for the first time a strategy across the entire value chain of the automotive sector. With the rules for controlling CO2 emissions, we are introducing flexibilities while remaining consistent with our objectives. With the regulation on the decarbonization of fleets, we are protecting an essential segment for our manufacturers, guaranteeing the availability of second-hand electric vehicles for European households. With simplification efforts, we are accelerating the deployment of small, affordable electric vehicles. With the “Battery Booster”, we are financing the rise of our own European battery industry. With the industrial accelerator, we are protecting jobs in Europe, we are stopping the bleeding among equipment manufacturers and strengthening their place in the electrified value chain.

So, you understand, ladies and gentlemen, the urgency of sending clear signals to the sector today, and therefore the collective responsibility of all European institutions to adopt these texts, which are on the table, as quickly as possible. The objective is clear: to break the deadly cycle of triple European decline – drop in production, drop in market share for our manufacturers, drop in added value in Europe. We owe it to our industry. We owe it to its employees. We owe it to our regions, which are in this automotive segment.

In any case, you can count on me to deploy this industrial strategy, just like Commissioners Tzitzikóstas and Hoekstra and the entire European Commission.

2-0008-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, dobbiamo riconoscere che quello che sta accadendo nell'assetto dell'industria europea vede nel pacchetto automotive uno dei punti centrali, decisivi per garantire un futuro all'intera manifattura europea.

Quindi, è assolutamente benvenuta la proposta di revisione della Commissione europea sul regolamento per le emissioni di CO2 in atmosfera per veicoli leggeri.

L'industria europea nel settore automobilistico ha investito miliardi di euro per accettare tutte le nuove sfide, in primis la sfida dell'elettrificazione, oggi le nostre case automobilistiche possono produrre motori elettrici e motori endotermici.

Il mercato, però, segnala che il ritmo previsto dall'ambizioso regolamento non viene rispettato: abbiamo un 20 % di penetrazione dell'elettrico a maggio 2026, ma le previsioni sono per un 38 al 2030 e un 64 al 2035, quindi è necessario un intervento.

Cosa serve? Servono condizioni abilitanti. Quindi, innanzitutto ci vuole un'accessibilità economica per i consumatori, ci vuole una diffusione dei sistemi di ricarica capillare e un sistema energetico europeo adeguato. Questo consentirà di avere investimenti europei completi, che tengano conto delle dinamiche di mercato e che tengano conto delle esigenze dei cittadini.

L'alternativa sarebbe quella di ridurre la produzione europea e acquistare crediti, magari da case automobilistiche non europee, una prospettiva che non possiamo accettare. Abbiamo la modifica del regolamento sulle emissioni di CO2, che è lo strumento più veloce per ottenere i risultati attesi e per adeguarci al mercato attraverso due grandi asset tecnici, giuridici e industriali: la flessibilità e la neutralità tecnologica. Lavoreremo in questa direzione.
2-0008-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, we must recognize that what is happening in the structure of European industry sees the automotive package as one of the central, decisive points for guaranteeing a future for the entire European manufacturing industry.

Therefore, the European Commission's proposed revision of the regulation for CO2 emissions into the atmosphere for light-duty vehicles is absolutely welcome.

The European automotive industry has invested billions of euros to accept all the new challenges, primarily the challenge of electrification, today our car manufacturers can produce electric motors and internal combustion engines.

The market, however, signals that the pace envisaged by the ambitious regulation is not being respected: we have a 20 % electric penetration in May 2026, but the forecasts are for a 38 in 2030 and a 64 in 2035, so intervention is necessary.

What is needed? Enabling conditions are needed. Therefore, first of all we need economic accessibility for consumers, we need widespread widespread charging systems and an adequate European energy system. This will allow for comprehensive European investments, which take into account market dynamics and take into account citizens' needs.

The alternative would be to reduce European production and buy credits, perhaps from non-European car manufacturers, a prospect we cannot accept. We have the modification of the regulation on CO2 emissions, which is the fastest tool to obtain the expected results and to adapt to the market through two great technical, legal and industrial assets: flexibility and technological neutrality. We will work in this direction.

2-0009-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, ik ben bang dat we elk half jaar — ik hoop het niet — in debat gaan over de toekomst van de auto-industrie, dat er weer een fabriek gaat sluiten en de producent van die autotechniek waarschijnlijk ergens buiten Europa een fabriek gaat opzetten.

We hebben te lang lacherig gedaan over elektrisch rijden. In Brabant hebben wij een autodealer die trots een heel groot bord voor zijn showroom heeft staan dat elektrisch rijden iets is voor de kermis. Maar ik denk dat er heel veel automobilisten de afgelopen maanden van een koude kermis thuis zijn gekomen, in de rij hebben gestaan bij Turnhout, Brecht of Poppel om goedkoop te tanken in België.

Wij hebben last van cognitieve dissonantie. We houden vast aan een technologie waarvan we zien dat de wereldwijde vraag daalt: de verbrandingsmotor. Tegelijkertijd wint de elektrische auto aan terrein. De vraag naar nieuwe elektrische auto's en tweedehands elektrische auto's stijgt.

Achter die ontwikkeling schuilt een veel grotere trend. Terwijl partijen hier koste wat kost vasthouden aan die technologie, focust de rest van de wereld op elektrisch vervoer. Ethiopië heeft de import van auto's met een verbrandingsmotor verboden. Laos gaat hetzelfde doen. Landen in Azië en Zuid-Amerika schakelen in hoog tempo over op elektrisch vervoer.

Naar verwachting zal in 2035 de helft van alle wereldwijd verkochte auto's elektrisch zijn. De vraag is dus niet wanneer die omslag gaat komen, maar waar we die auto's gaan bouwen en waar de banen straks liggen: in Europa of in China?
2-0009-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I am afraid that every six months - I hope not - we will have a debate about the future of the car industry, that another factory will close and the manufacturer of that car technology will probably set up a factory somewhere outside Europe.

We have laughed about electric driving for too long. In Brabant we have a car dealer who proudly has a very large sign in front of his showroom that electric driving is something for the fair. But I think that many motorists have come home from a rude awakening in recent months, queuing at Turnhout, Brecht or Poppel to refuel cheaply in Belgium.

We suffer from cognitive dissonance. We are sticking with a technology for which we see declining global demand: the combustion engine. At the same time, the electric car is gaining ground. The demand for new electric cars and second-hand electric cars is increasing.

Behind this development lies a much larger trend. While parties here hold on to that technology at all costs, the rest of the world focuses on electric transport. Ethiopia has banned the import of cars with a combustion engine. Laos will do the same. Countries in Asia and South America are rapidly switching to electric transport.

It is expected that half of all cars sold worldwide will be electric by 2035. So the question is not when that change will come, but where we will build those cars and where the jobs will be: in Europe or in China?

2-0010-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, vážení kolegové, je moc fajn, že Evropská komise ve svém akčním plánu konečně přiznává to, na co automobilový průmysl upozorňuje už několik let. Vysoké ceny energií, rostoucí náklady na výrobu, narušené dodavatelské řetězce i sílící konkurence ze třetích zemí ohrožují jedno z nejdůležitějších evropských průmyslových odvětví. Bohužel správná diagnóza ještě neznamená správnou léčbu. Komise mluví o konkurenceschopnosti, ale zároveň zachovává regulační rámec, který naši konkurenceschopnost systematicky oslabuje. Mluví o zjednodušení, ale přidává další administrativní náklady. Mluví o inovacích, ale stále více předepisuje, jaké technologie mají být používány, místo toho, aby nechala inovace vznikat přirozenou soutěží. Evropské automobilky nepotřebují další strategické dokumenty. Potřebují levnější energie, předvídatelná pravidla, méně byrokracie a skutečně technologicky neutrální prostředí. Jestliže budou evropské podniky vyrábět za výrazně vyšší náklady než jejich konkurenti v Číně nebo ve Spojených státech, nebude rozhodující kvalita našich inženýrů ani zkušenosti našich pracovníků. Rozhodující budou náklady. Milá Komise, neztrácejte čas dalšími plány. Začněte odstraňovat překážky, které jste evropskému průmyslu sami vytvořili.
2-0010-0000.englishText: Madam President, dear colleagues, it is very nice that the European Commission finally acknowledges in its action plan what the automotive industry has been drawing attention to for several years. High energy prices, rising production costs, disrupted supply chains and increasing competition from third countries threaten one of Europe's most important industrial sectors. Unfortunately, the correct diagnosis does not mean the correct treatment. The Commission talks about competitiveness, but at the same time it maintains a regulatory framework that systematically weakens our competitiveness. It talks about simplification, but adds additional administrative costs. It talks about innovation, but it increasingly prescribes what technologies are to be used, rather than letting innovation emerge through natural competition. European car companies do not need additional strategic documents. They need cheaper energy, predictable rules, less bureaucracy and a truly technology-neutral environment. If European companies produce at significantly higher costs than their competitors in China or the United States, the quality of our engineers and the experience of our workers will not be decisive. Cost will be decisive. Dear Commission, don't waste your time with other plans. Start removing the obstacles you yourself have created for European industry.

2-0011-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, grazie per la Sua chiarezza, la Sua durezza e l'analisi.

È sulla ricetta che abbiamo delle differenze, perché, come ricordava Lei, ma io ricordo, addirittura, due anni fa, luglio 2024, qui si faceva un dibattito sull'automotive. Cos'è cambiato? Niente rispetto all'indirizzo della Commissione – poco, direi – mentre il mercato è decisamente peggiorato: la Cina ha invaso il nostro mercato delle auto e assistiamo alla perdita di posti di lavoro. Lei stesso, in Commissione, ha ricordato che abbiamo già perduto 200 000 posti di lavoro. Una delle più grandi aziende europee, Volkswagen, dichiara la riduzione di ulteriori 100 000 posti di lavoro, di solito uomini con famiglia.

Questo è un impoverimento dell'Europa. E, dall'altro lato, chiusura di fabbriche e l'impoverimento dell'intera filiera – come Lei ha ben ricordato – della supply chain. Una filiera che è una filiera ricca, che ha investito, che ha investito anche in contenimento dei danni ambientali, che si suppongono da un'industria.

Ma è sulla ricetta che non ci siamo. Noi chiediamo fortemente neutralità tecnologica. Il mercato non sta chiedendo auto elettriche, il mercato vuole essere libero, i consumatori sono liberi, siamo in un'Europa libera. Abbiamo necessità di fare in modo che tutta la neutralità tecnologica riguardi anche i carburanti e abbiamo la necessità di non penalizzare un settore, come quello dei camion, del trasporto pesante, che noi ci illudiamo possa andare con una batteria elettrica fatta in Cina.
2-0011-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, Commissioner, thank you for your clarity, your toughness and your analysis.

It is on the recipe that we have differences, because, as you remembered, but I even remember, two years ago, July 2024, there was a debate on the automotive industry here. What has changed? Nothing compared to the Commission's direction - little, I would say - while the market has decidedly worsened: China has invaded our car market and we are witnessing the loss of jobs. You yourself, in the Commission, pointed out that we have already lost 200 000 jobs. One of the largest European companies, Volkswagen, declares the reduction of a further 100 000 jobs, usually men with families.

This is an impoverishment of Europe. And, on the other hand, the closure of factories and the impoverishment of the entire supply chain - as you well remembered - of the supply chain. A supply chain that is a rich supply chain, which has invested, which has also invested in containing environmental damage, which is assumed by an industry.

But it's the recipe that we're not sure about. We strongly demand technological neutrality. The market is not asking for electric cars, the market wants to be free, consumers are free, we are in a free Europe. We need to ensure that all technological neutrality also concerns fuels and we need not to penalize a sector, such as trucks, heavy transport, which we delude ourselves can go with an electric battery made in China.

2-0013-0000.sourceText:
Collega's, kunnen jullie de mensen van Volkswagen vandaag recht in de ogen kijken en beweren dat de toekomst van hun job in diesel- en benzinemotoren ligt?

Wat er vandaag gebeurt bij Volkswagen is verschrikkelijk. Honderdduizend arbeiders vrezen voor hun job. Dat zijn mensen die vaak al heel hun leven voor het bedrijf werken; het is hun familie geworden; het zijn vrienden geworden.

Dit doet mij denken aan de ontslagronde die we bij Audi in Brussel hebben gezien. Ook daar hebben mensen erg geleden onder de ontslagronde. Een koppel dat er al 33 jaar werkte, getuigde hoe koud ze afscheid moesten nemen, via een brief, een veiligheidsagent die hen begeleidde om hun spullen op te halen. Zij kregen niet eens de mogelijkheid om afscheid te nemen.

Hadden de CEO's van Volkswagen meer tijd gestoken in de concurrentie met China op de markt van de elektrische voertuigen in plaats van sjoemelsoftware te installeren, dan hadden die mensen vandaag nog een job. Laat ons diezelfde fout niet opnieuw maken.
2-0013-0000.englishText:
Colleagues, can you look the people of Volkswagen straight in the eye today and claim that the future of their jobs lies in diesel and petrol engines?

What is happening today at Volkswagen is terrible. Hundreds of thousands of workers fear for their jobs. These are people who have often worked for the company all their lives; it has become their family; they have become friends.

This reminds me of the round of layoffs we saw at Audi in Brussels. People there have also suffered greatly from the round of layoffs. A couple who had worked there for 33 years testified how coldly they had to say goodbye, via a letter, a security guard who accompanied them to collect their belongings. They didn't even get the opportunity to say goodbye.

If Volkswagen's CEOs had spent more time competing with China in the electric vehicle market instead of installing cheating software, those people would still have a job today. Let us not make that same mistake again.

2-0014-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar! Die Beschäftigten von Mercedes-Benz wehren sich dagegen, ohne Lohnausgleich länger zu schuften, während überhohe Dividenden an die Großaktionäre ausgeschüttet werden. Das Management von Volkswagen hat einen drastischen Stellenabbau angekündigt; vier Standorte sollen allein in Deutschland geschlossen werden. Und Konzernchef Blume ist so unverschämt, jedes Jahr über 10 Millionen Euro einzusacken, die von diesen Beschäftigten erwirtschaftet worden sind.

Die Automobilindustrie steht vor großen Herausforderungen: internationale Konkurrenz, die Umstellung auf E-Autos, die Digitalisierung. Aber das anhaltende Versagen des Managements verschärft diese Krise nur. Werke sollen jetzt sogar zur Aufrüstung genutzt werden: Raketenabwehrsysteme statt Volkswagen und Panzer mit Mercedesstern, wenn es nach Herrn Blume und Mercedes-Boss Källenius geht.

Nicht mit uns! Schluss mit dem Kürzungskurs auf dem Rücken der Beschäftigten! Wir fordern Zukunftsinvestitionen, um Standorte langfristig zu sichern, mit Beschäftigungsgarantien. Schluss mit den Angriffen auf Arbeitszeit und Tarifverträge!
2-0014-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner! Mercedes-Benz employees are resisting working longer without compensation while excessive dividends are paid out to major shareholders. Volkswagen management has announced drastic job cuts; four locations are to be closed in Germany alone. And CEO Blume is so shameless that he pockets over 10 million euros every year that these employees earn.

The automotive industry is facing major challenges: international competition, the switch to electric cars, digitalization. But continued management failure is only exacerbating this crisis. Plants should now even be used for rearmament: missile defense systems instead of Volkswagens and tanks with Mercedes stars, if Mr. Blume and Mercedes boss Källenius have their way.

Not with us! Stop making cuts at the expense of employees! We call for future investments to secure locations in the long term, with employment guarantees. Stop the attacks on working hours and collective agreements!

2-0015-0000.sourceText: Vážená pani predsedajúca, kolegovia. Je mi jasné, že zelení fanatici v Bruseli, ako je pán Hojsík, by najradšej všetky normálne autá zakázali a v podstate nenávidia šoférov. Ale realita je taká, že dnes, v dnešnom svete, bežná rodina bez auta proste nemá šancu. A kvôli vašim opatreniam sú tie autá čoraz drahšie a nedostupnejšie. Teraz Volkswagen oznámil, že plánuje prepustiť 100 tisíc ľudí a plánuje sa preorientovať na výrobu zbraní, pretože Green deal pre zbrane jednoducho neplatí. Tak prosím vás, vy tu neobviňujte teraz nejakých Číňanov, že nás v automobiloch predbehli. Obviňujte v prvom rade samých seba, že ste to dopustili, pretože to je realita a to je výsledok vašej práce. Pozrite sa za posledné roky, čo sa tu udialo. Najprv ste prišli so zákazom spaľovacích motorov, ktorý doteraz nebol zrušený. Potom ste presadzovali normu Euro 7, ktorú aj inžinieri označovali za technicky nerealizovateľnú. Teraz najnovšie pretláčate povinné tachografy už aj pre malé dodávky. Pre ľudí, pre obyčajných ľudí chcete zdražieť palivá, benzín, naftu cez emisné povolenky ETS 2. Firmy nútite do nakupovania povinného podielu elektromobilov, ktoré stoja na európskych skladoch. A dokonca do vedenia firiem cez genderové kvóty tlačíte polovicu žien, pričom ja absolútne nerozumiem, čo má nejaké pohlavie spojené s nejakými riadiacimi schopnosťami. Prosím vás, kedy ste naposledy niečo zjednodušili alebo uvoľnili? Všetko len komplikujete a zdražujete. A to je to, čo chceme zastaviť, a to je to, čo chceme napraviť.
2-0015-0000.englishText: Dear Madam President, colleagues. It is clear to me that green fanatics in Brussels, such as Mr. Hojsík, would prefer to ban all normal cars and basically hate drivers. But the reality is that today, in today's world, the average family without a car simply doesn't stand a chance. And because of your measures, those cars are becoming more and more expensive and unaffordable. Now Volkswagen has announced that it plans to lay off 100,000 people and plans to refocus on arms production because the Green Deal simply does not apply to arms. So please, don't blame some Chinese here for having overtaken us in cars. First of all, blame yourself for allowing it, because that is the reality and that is the result of your work. Take a look at what has happened here in recent years. First, you came up with the ban on internal combustion engines, which has not yet been lifted. Then you promoted the Euro 7 standard, which even engineers called technically unfeasible. Now you are pushing mandatory tachographs even for small vans. For people, for ordinary people, you want to make fuels, gasoline, diesel more expensive through ETS 2 emission allowances. You are forcing companies to buy a mandatory share of electric cars that are in European warehouses. And you even push half of the women into the management of companies through gender quotas, while I absolutely do not understand what gender has to do with any management skills. Please, when was the last time you simplified or freed up something? You are only complicating everything and making it more expensive. And that's what we want to stop, and that's what we want to fix.

2-0016-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, revenons d’abord peut-être sur les facteurs de compétitivité que vous avez chacun mentionnés dans vos interventions.

Retards technologiques, je l’évoquais en introduction, ce sont d’une part des choix industriels – et il y a eu, en toute honnêteté, des mauvais choix industriels de la part de nos constructeurs sur des stratégies industrielles, et il y a eu également des choix dans notre capacité à pouvoir aller conquérir un certain nombre de marchés. Nous sommes exposés à la concurrence internationale, avec le choix des autres pays de se concentrer sur leur marché domestique. Je pense notamment à la Chine, où un certain nombre de constructeurs chinois viennent aujourd’hui remplacer les constructeurs européens. Ce sont, d’autre part, des choix politiques de nos concurrents à l’international sur des marchés, d’où l’ouverture d’autres marchés à l’étranger, la constitution et l’organisation de nouveaux accords commerciaux pour pouvoir trouver des débouchés. Et puis, de notre côté, un travail sur notre compétitivité interne au niveau européen qu’il faut poursuivre.

Chaînes de valeur et d’approvisionnement fragilisées liées à la géopolitique, bilan financier plombé par les droits de douane, avec des constructeurs qui avaient un concept de production global pour le local, avec des chaînes de valeur morcelées à travers le monde, qui aujourd’hui se retrouvent dans une difficulté où le retour du protectionnisme, le retour des droits de douane viennent fragiliser les modèles économiques de nos constructeurs.

Perte également de compétitivité domestique au niveau européen. Le prix de l’énergie fera l’objet probablement de nombreux débats ici pendant cette session. Règles européennes complexes et un travail sur la simplification d’un certain nombre de dispositifs pour pouvoir faciliter la commercialisation de nouveaux types de véhicules. Bref, la Commission s’est attaquée à l’ensemble des facteurs de la compétitivité.

Un dernier mot sur quelques chiffres que vous évoquez. En Europe, nous avons atteint 25 % de parts de marché pour le véhicule électrique et plus de 35 % si on ajoute les hybrides rechargeables. Dans le monde, nous dépassons aujourd’hui les 13 millions de véhicules électriques produits et, aujourd’hui, nous atteignons à peu près 20 % des véhicules vendus dans le monde qui sont électriques. Cette tendance est en augmentation très forte, et, au dernier trimestre, c’est plus de 40 % des ventes supplémentaires de véhicules électriques en Europe. Pourquoi? Tout simplement parce que le marché permet la vente de ce genre de véhicules. Tout simplement parce que, pour rouler en électrique, ce sont aujourd’hui 80 euros économisés pour un mois de carburant pour un certain nombre de travailleurs. Ce sont 1 000 euros économisés pour un mois de travail pour un taxi dans une capitale européenne du fait d’avoir aujourd’hui un véhicule électrique.

Donc nous avons la capacité de pouvoir convaincre aussi avec des véhicules qui vont arriver sur le marché, plus de 200 nouvelles séries de véhicules qui vont arriver sur le marché cette année, des véhicules qui seront beaucoup moins chers et qui bénéficieront également des réformes européennes sur la simplification, sur la capacité à pouvoir justement proposer aux classes moyennes et aux classes populaires un véhicule à moins de 20 000 euros. C’était l’objectif que nous nous étions fixés avec le petit véhicule électrique européen.

Voilà: pour vous dire que la Commission, à travers ces trois textes que nous vous avons présentés, touche l’ensemble des points de compétitivité que nous voulons aujourd’hui débattre. Le message est clair: aller rapidement sur l’adoption de ces textes – pour adopter ces textes, pour qu’ils puissent entrer en vigueur et pour qu’ils puissent avoir aussi un impact sur notre industrie et sur nos emplois.
2-0016-0000.englishText:
Madam President, let us first perhaps return to the competitiveness factors that you each mentioned in your interventions.

Technological delays, as I mentioned in the introduction, are on the one hand industrial choices – and there have been, in all honesty, bad industrial choices on the part of our manufacturers on industrial strategies, and there have also been choices in our capacity to be able to conquer a certain number of markets. We are exposed to international competition, with other countries choosing to focus on their domestic market. I am thinking in particular of China, where a certain number of Chinese manufacturers are now replacing European manufacturers. These are, on the other hand, political choices of our international competitors in markets, hence the opening of other markets abroad, the constitution and organization of new commercial agreements to be able to find outlets. And then, on our side, work on our internal competitiveness at the European level which must be continued.

Weakened value and supply chains linked to geopolitics, financial balance sheet weighed down by customs duties, with manufacturers who had a global production concept for the local, with value chains fragmented across the world, who today find themselves in a difficulty where the return of protectionism, the return of customs duties are weakening the economic models of our manufacturers.

Also loss of domestic competitiveness at European level. The price of energy will likely be the subject of much debate here during this session. Complex European rules and work on the simplification of a certain number of systems to facilitate the marketing of new types of vehicles. In short, the Commission has tackled all the factors of competitiveness.

A final word on some figures you mentioned. In Europe, we have reached 25% market share for electric vehicles and more than 35% if we add plug-in hybrids. Worldwide, we now exceed 13 million electric vehicles produced and, today, we reach approximately 20% of vehicles sold worldwide that are electric. This trend is increasing very sharply, and, in the last quarter, it represented more than 40% of additional sales of electric vehicles in Europe. For what? Quite simply because the market allows the sale of this type of vehicle. Quite simply because, to drive electric, today 80 euros are saved for a month of fuel for a certain number of workers. This is 1,000 euros saved for a month of work for a taxi in a European capital due to having an electric vehicle today.

So we have the capacity to be able to convince also with vehicles which will arrive on the market, more than 200 new series of vehicles which will arrive on the market this year, vehicles which will be much cheaper and which will also benefit from European reforms on simplification, on the capacity to be able to offer the middle and working classes a vehicle for less than 20,000 euros. This was the objective we set for ourselves with the small European electric vehicle.

Here it is: to tell you that the Commission, through these three texts that we have presented to you, touches on all the points of competitiveness that we want to debate today. The message is clear: move quickly to adopt these texts – to adopt these texts, so that they can come into force and so that they can also have an impact on our industry and on our jobs.

2-0017-0000.sourceText:
Sehr geehrte Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Wenn Europas größter Automobilhersteller 100 000 Stellen abbauen will, dann ist das mehr als eine Unternehmensentscheidung, dann ist das ein verzweifelter Hilfeschrei. Die Automobilindustrie ist eine der Schlüsselindustrien Europas; wenn sie an Wettbewerbsfähigkeit verliert, verliert Europa – und genau das erleben wir seit Jahren.

Während China und die USA ihre Industrie massiv unterstützen, hat Europa seine Industrie mit Verboten und Bürokratie überfordert. Das zeigt, es braucht einen echten Kurswechsel. Nur eine wirtschaftlich starke Industrie kann die Transformation meistern und Jobs in unseren Regionen erhalten. Deshalb müssen wir Bürokratie abbauen, Verfahren beschleunigen und Lade- und Wasserstoffinfrastruktur ausbauen. Und wir brauchen CO2-Flottengrenzwerte, die praxistauglich sind und die Technologieoffenheit gewährleisten. Wer Innovation fördern will, darf Unternehmen nicht mit immer neuen Belastungen die Luft zum Atmen nehmen.

Die Beschäftigten in der Industrie erwarten zu Recht, dass wir nicht nur über Arbeitsplätze reden, sondern diese sichern. Dafür braucht es eine Industriepolitik, die Vertrauen schafft, Investitionen ermöglicht und Europa als Produktionsstandort stärkt. Unser Ziel ist klar: klimaneutrale Mobilität – aber mit europäischen Fahrzeugen, europäischen Innovationen und europäischen Arbeitsplätzen. Deshalb möchte ich heute einen Appell an alle demokratischen und verantwortungsbewussten Kräfte dieses Hauses richten: Lassen Sie uns gemeinsam Europas Automobilindustrie zurück an die Weltspitze führen – für Beschäftigte, Unternehmen und unseren Wohlstand.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0017-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! When Europe's largest car manufacturer wants to cut 100,000 jobs, it's more than a corporate decision, it's a desperate cry for help. The automotive industry is one of Europe's key industries; if it loses competitiveness, Europe loses – and that’s exactly what we’ve been seeing for years.

While China and the USA massively support their industry, Europe has overwhelmed its industry with bans and bureaucracy. This shows that a real change of course is needed. Only an economically strong industry can master the transformation and maintain jobs in our regions. That's why we need to reduce bureaucracy, speed up procedures and expand charging and hydrogen infrastructure. And we need CO2 fleet limits that are practical and ensure technological openness. If you want to promote innovation, you must not keep companies from losing their breathing space by constantly introducing new pressures.

Employees in industry rightly expect that we not only talk about jobs, but also secure them. This requires an industrial policy that creates trust, enables investments and strengthens Europe as a production location. Our goal is clear: climate-neutral mobility - but with European vehicles, European innovations and European jobs. That's why today I would like to make an appeal to all democratic and responsible forces in this House: Let us work together to bring Europe's automotive industry back to the top of the world - for employees, companies and our prosperity.

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question about the “blue card” procedure.)

2-0018-0000.sourceText: Szanowny Panie Pośle, Pan mówi tutaj, że przemysł motoryzacyjny jest w trudnej sytuacji. Ja się zgadzam z Panem absolutnie. Natomiast jednocześnie Pan mówił tutaj o przyspieszeniu celów klimatycznych. Ja chciałbym zrozumieć Pana wypowiedź. Czy Pan uważa, że przyspieszenie celów klimatycznych w Europie ma pomóc przemysłowi motoryzacyjnemu? Czy ja dobrze Pana rozumiem? Czy jednak właśnie my powinniśmy podejść do tego w sposób bardziej pragmatyczny i cele, które Państwo wyznaczyli jeszcze niedawno na tej sali, są de facto powodem, dla którego przemysł motoryzacyjny ma takie kłopoty w Europie (między innymi zakaz rejestracji samochodów spalinowych od 2035 roku).
2-0018-0000.englishText: Dear Mr. MP, you are saying here that the automotive industry is in a difficult situation. I agree with you absolutely. However, at the same time, you talked about accelerating climate goals. I would like to understand your statement. Do you think that accelerating climate goals in Europe will help the automotive industry? Do I understand you correctly?
