However, should we approach this in a more pragmatic way and the goals that you recently set in this room are in fact the reason why the automotive industry is having such problems in Europe (including the ban on registering combustion cars from 2035).

2-0019-0000.sourceText: (PPE), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Ich glaube, offensichtlich haben Sie mich da missverstanden. Ich habe nicht gesagt, dass wir die Klimaziele beschleunigen müssen, sondern ich habe gesagt, dass wir technologieoffen sein müssen und praxisgerechte Möglichkeiten finden müssen, die Transformation zu gewährleisten. Das heißt, keine Beschleunigung, sondern an den Zielen festhalten, aber einen Mix an Möglichkeiten und einen Wettbewerb der Technologien zulassen. Insofern ist das, glaube ich, ein Ansatz, den wir gemeinsam vertreten können.
2-0019-0000.englishText: (PPE), response to a question about the “blue card” procedure. – I think you obviously misunderstood me. I didn't say that we have to accelerate the climate goals, but I said that we have to be open to technology and find practical ways to ensure the transformation. That means no acceleration, but sticking to the goals, but allowing a mix of possibilities and competition between technologies. In this respect, I believe this is an approach that we can support together.

2-0020-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Es ist doch auf jeden Fall klar, dass die Beschäftigten diese Krise nicht verursacht haben. Kommissar Séjourné hat das gesagt – wir haben es hier auch mit massiven Managementfehlern zu tun, die wir hier nicht verschweigen können, und gleichzeitig auch mit einem Mangel an Innovationsfähigkeit. Und wenn wir da ran wollen, müssen wir mit dem Industriebeschleuniger beschleunigen.

Wir brauchen ein made in Europe, und das brauchen wir relativ schnell. Und noch mal: Wenn man jetzt aufgrund der Fehler, die im Management begangen wurden, die Arbeitnehmer und Arbeitnehmerinnen die Zeche zahlen lässt, dann ist das doch schändlich.

Wir haben bislang auch als EU nicht geliefert mit dem Versprechen der fairen Übergänge. Hier muss nachgerüstet werden; alle Maßnahmen zur Unterstützung der Beschäftigten. Wir haben SURE; wir haben die Erfahrung, dass es funktioniert. Sind wir ready hier, um das einzusetzen? Auch wenn wir öffentliche Gelder geben, dann nicht ohne Konditionen. Gute Arbeit, tarifvertragliche Lösungen finden für diese Krise – das ist das Gebot der Stunde.
2-0020-0000.englishText:
Madam President! In any case, it is clear that employees did not cause this crisis. Commissioner Séjourné said this – we are also dealing with massive management errors here, which we cannot keep quiet about, and at the same time a lack of ability to innovate. And if we want to get there, we have to accelerate with the industrial accelerator.

We need something made in Europe, and we need it relatively quickly. And again: If you now make the employees pay the bill because of the mistakes made in management, then that is shameful.

So far, we as the EU have not delivered on the promise of fair transitions. This needs to be upgraded; all measures to support employees. We have SURE; we have experience that it works. Are we ready here to use this? Even if we give public money, it is not without conditions. Good work, finding collective bargaining solutions to this crisis - that's the order of the day.

2-0021-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, sono allibito dal fatto che in quest'Aula nessuno si ponga la domanda se l'elettrico a tutti i costi possa essere compatibile con quelli che sono i limiti in termini di generazione elettrica.

Se noi analizziamo il contesto, abbiamo un mercato americano chiuso alla Cina, una domanda interna cinese in stagnazione e, dall'altra parte, l'Europa che è diventata valvola di sfogo, terreno di conquista, per la sovraccapacità industriale di Pechino.

Per cui, il titolo di questo dibattito mi sembra suoni un po' come se fosse una beffa: si parla di posti di lavoro di qualità, ma qua è già tanto se di posti di lavoro ne rimarrà qualcuno. Ricordo che tra qualche giorno Volkswagen valuterà un piano industriale che prevede il taglio di 100 000 posti di lavoro e la chiusura di quattro stabilimenti.

Allora, a questo punto, io mi chiedo se qui ci sia nessuno che pensa che un prezzo vada pagato, ma, soprattutto: vi sentite tutti sereni? C'è nessuno che si sente responsabile?
2-0021-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, I am appalled by the fact that in this House no one is asking the question whether electricity at all costs can be compatible with the limits in terms of electricity generation.

If we analyze the context, we have an American market closed to China, a stagnant Chinese domestic demand and, on the other hand, Europe which has become a relief valve, a land of conquest, for Beijing's industrial overcapacity.

Therefore, the title of this debate seems to me to sound a bit like a joke: we talk about quality jobs, but here it is already a lot if there will be any jobs left. I remind you that in a few days Volkswagen will evaluate an industrial plan that involves cutting 100,000 jobs and closing four factories.

So, at this point, I wonder if there is anyone here who thinks that a price must be paid, but, above all: do you all feel calm? Is there anyone who feels responsible?

2-0022-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Sektor motoryzacyjny jest niezwykle ważny dla całej Europy. Wiemy doskonale, jak wyglądają łańcuchy dostaw, jak wiele państw członkowskich jest zaangażowanych w ten przemysł, jeżeli chodzi o możliwości zarobkowania właśnie na nim. Dziwię się więc dzisiaj na tej sali, gdy słucham tej dyskusji, ponieważ mam wrażenie, że właściwie nic nie da się zrobić. To znaczy wy uważacie, że na przykład cele klimatyczne do 2040 roku – 90% – mają pomóc przemysłowi motoryzacyjnemu, że zakaz rejestracji samochodów spalinowych od 2035 roku ma pomóc naszemu przemysłowi. Czy to, że ceny energii w Europie mamy dwa, trzy razy wyższe niż w Stanach Zjednoczonych czy Chinach, to ma pomóc temu sektorowi?

Dzisiaj na tej sali mam wrażenie, że wiele osób uważa, że wszystko jest w porządku. I będziecie mówić o pomocy publicznej dla zakładów, a ja wolałbym, żebyście dzisiaj powiedzieli o rezygnacji z celów klimatycznych tych wysokich, które w tej chwili są, o likwidacji ETSu, o likwidacji zakazu rejestracji samochodów spalinowych po 2035 roku. To trzeba zrobić, bo inaczej europejski przemysł samochodowy po prostu upadnie.
2-0022-0000.englishText:
Madam President! The automotive sector is extremely important for all of Europe. We know perfectly well what supply chains look like, how many Member States are involved in this industry, in terms of earning opportunities from it. So I am surprised today in this room when I listen to this discussion, because I have the impression that nothing can actually be done. That is, you believe that, for example, the climate goals by 2040 - 90% - are intended to help the automotive industry, and that the ban on registering combustion cars from 2035 is intended to help our industry. Is the fact that energy prices in Europe are two or three times higher than in the United States or China supposed to help this sector?

Today in this room I have the impression that many people think that everything is fine. And you will talk about public aid for plants, and I would prefer that you talk today about abandoning the high climate goals that are currently in place, about abolishing the ETS, about abolishing the ban on registering combustion cars after 2035. This must be done, otherwise the European car industry will simply collapse.

2-0023-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Hunderttausende Jobs bei Autobauern und Zulieferern sind in Gefahr, weil wir derzeit in Europa nicht wettbewerbsfähig sind. Und, liebe Freundinnen und Freunde, die bisherigen Regeln, die wir haben, nämlich das Verbrenner-Aus in 2035, verschärfen die Krise bei den Autobauern. Die Zukunft ist elektrisch – ja, aber sie kommt nicht so schnell, wie sich das hier einige gedacht haben, und sie wird auch nicht zu 100 Prozent elektrisch sein.

Unsere Regeln, die wir uns gegeben haben, sind nicht flexibel genug; sie strangulieren heute unsere Automobilindustrie. Deshalb brauchen wir mehr Flexibilität. Nicht alle Vorschläge, die die Kommission vorgelegt hat, sind diesem Ziel gewidmet, aber ich glaube, dass wir im Rahmen des parlamentarischen Verfahrens daran arbeiten können, diese Flexibilität, die vorgeschlagen wurde von der Kommission, noch zu erweitern.

Wir brauchen Technologieoffenheit, damit wir alternative Kraftstoffe zur CO2‑Reduktion in Europa nutzen können.
2-0023-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! Hundreds of thousands of jobs at car manufacturers and suppliers are at risk because we are currently not competitive in Europe. And, dear friends, the current rules we have, namely the end of combustion engines in 2035, are exacerbating the crisis among car manufacturers. The future is electric - yes, but it's not coming as quickly as some here thought, and it won't be 100 percent electric either.

The rules we have given ourselves are not flexible enough; They are strangling our automotive industry today. That's why we need more flexibility. Not all of the proposals that the Commission has put forward are dedicated to this aim, but I believe that we can work, within the framework of the parliamentary procedure, to further extend this flexibility that has been proposed by the Commission.

We need openness to technology so that we can use alternative fuels to reduce CO2 in Europe.

2-0024-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar! Der Verbrennermotor – das war große und gute Ingenieurskunst, und darauf können die Beschäftigten in der Automobilindustrie stolz sein. Aber ganz ehrlich – der Verbrennermotor, das war einmal. Dass Volkswagen und Bosch und viele Arbeitsplätze streichen, liegt daran, dass wir bei der Umstellung auf die E‑Mobilität nicht schnell genug sind, dass die anderen uns die Butter vom Brot nehmen.

Seit 2017 sinken die Absatzzahlen von Verbrennermotoren – seit 2017 um 30 %. Und selbst in Deutschland werden heute mehr Elektroautos verkauft als Benziner. Ihr nostalgisches Festhalten am Verbrennermotor zerstört letztlich Arbeitsplätze, denn die Autos der Zukunft, die sind elektrisch, die sind digital, die sind bezahlbar; und entweder wir bauen sie, oder sie werden in China gebaut und bei uns schließen die Fabriken.

Wir können Weltklasseautos bauen – das haben wir 100 Jahre lang gezeigt; aber für Weltklasse muss man zehn Jahre in die Zukunft schauen und nicht 50 Jahre in den Rückspiegel.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0024-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner! The combustion engine – that was great and good engineering, and the employees in the automotive industry can be proud of it. But honestly – the combustion engine was a thing of the past. The reason why Volkswagen and Bosch are cutting many jobs is because we are not moving quickly enough to switch to e-mobility and the others are taking the butter from our bread.

Since 2017, sales of combustion engines have been falling – by 30% since 2017. And even in Germany, more electric cars are sold today than gasoline ones. Their nostalgic clinging to the combustion engine ultimately destroys jobs, because the cars of the future are electric, they are digital, they are affordable; and either we build them or they are built in China and our factories close.

We can build world-class cars – we’ve shown that for 100 years; but for world class you have to look 10 years into the future, not 50 years in the rearview mirror.

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question about the “blue card” procedure.)

2-0025-0000.sourceText:
Quería compartir con usted si considera que lo que necesitamos, teniendo en cuenta la normativa que tenemos en tramitación, es realmente un acompañamiento mayor a nuestras empresas, una definición clara del «Made in Europe», única y armonizada, fácil de aplicar y, sobre todo, fácil de auditar, y, sobre todo, que cualquier definición de origen deba ser clara, estable y fácilmente verificable.

Asimismo, creo que necesitamos unas condiciones marco que favorezcan la inversión industrial en Europa, promoviendo así empleos de calidad. Y también si considera usted que debemos reforzar el desarrollo de cadenas de valor estratégicas europeas, especialmente en el ámbito de las baterías, como manera de conseguir blindar el coche eléctrico.
2-0025-0000.englishText:
I wanted to share with you if you consider that what we need, taking into account the regulations we have in the pipeline, is really greater support for our companies, a clear definition of "Made in Europe", unique and harmonized, easy to apply and, above all, easy to audit, and, above all, that any definition of origin must be clear, stable and easily verifiable.

Likewise, I believe that we need framework conditions that favor industrial investment in Europe, thus promoting quality jobs. And also if you consider that we must reinforce the development of European strategic value chains, especially in the field of batteries, as a way to protect the electric car.

2-0027-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, 50 000, c’est le nombre d’emplois détruits dans l’automobile en France depuis 2017. Si nous ne faisons rien, ce sont des milliers d’autres qui vont être sacrifiés demain. Voilà la réalité du séisme qui frappe notre industrie, et plus nous tardons à réagir, plus la facture sera lourde à payer pour toute notre société. Je parle ici de toute notre société, car, n’en déplaise à la droite et à l’extrême droite de cet hémicycle, face au dérèglement climatique, aux canicules qui s’enchaînent, la transition électrique n’est plus négociable. C’est une urgence vitale, alors que 30 % de nos émissions dépendent directement du secteur du transport.

Donc oui, il faut investir massivement, mais évidemment pas pour alimenter la spéculation, comme nous avons pu le voir: l’argent public doit servir vraiment à protéger les salariés, à transformer notre industrie et pas à enrichir des actionnaires. Pour réussir, il faut évidemment un bouclier, un véritable «made in Europe» dans l’automobile, afin de maîtriser nos batteries et nos technologies. En ce sens, les plans actuels ne vont pas assez loin sur la préférence locale et sur l’aide à l’acquisition de véhicules abordables électriques pour tous les citoyens. Donc, il faut sortir de ces logiques mortifères du libre-échange et vraiment protéger notre marché et notre industrie.
2-0027-0000.englishText:
Madam President, 50,000 is the number of jobs destroyed in the automobile industry in France since 2017. If we do nothing, thousands more will be sacrificed tomorrow. This is the reality of the earthquake that is hitting our industry, and the longer we delay in reacting, the heavier the bill will be to pay for our entire society. I am talking here about our entire society, because, with all due respect to the right and the extreme right of this hemicycle, faced with climate change and heatwaves which follow one another, the electric transition is no longer negotiable. This is a vital emergency, when 30% of our emissions depend directly on the transport sector.

So yes, we must invest massively, but obviously not to fuel speculation, as we have seen: public money must really be used to protect employees, to transform our industry and not to enrich shareholders. To succeed, we obviously need a shield, a truly “made in Europe” in the automobile industry, in order to control our batteries and our technologies. In this sense, current plans do not go far enough on local preference and on support for the acquisition of affordable electric vehicles for all citizens. So, we must get away from these deadly logics of free trade and truly protect our market and our industry.

2-0028-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, peut-être un mot pour vous dire que l’objectif est bien de stopper l’hémorragie et de repositionner notre industrie sur un secteur de l’avenir, de l’innovation, avec des conditions de compétitivité, y compris à l’international, qui sont améliorées.

Quelques messages sur les propositions de la Commission: nous avons proposé d’avoir une définition d’une voiture européenne pour pouvoir discriminer positivement, quand il y a engagement de l’argent public européen, dans le cadre des marchés publics, dans le cadre des subventions à l’achat, pour qu’il y ait une préférence d’achat européenne à partir du moment où le consommateur souhaite bénéficier de cette fiscalité particulière.

Je trouve normal aujourd’hui, au vu du constat que vous faites toutes et tous ici, dans cet hémicycle, que l’argent public qui est prélevé par l’impôt puisse profiter avant tout à la création de la demande, en Europe, sur des segments particuliers, notamment sur les segments des véhicules électriques. C’est la proposition que nous avons faite, avec 70 % de composants européens dans une voiture électrique (hors batterie), avec 50 % de composants européens pour la chaîne de propulsion électrique et 50 % de composants européens pour l’électronique.

Voilà la proposition qui est sur la table, sur laquelle vous devez débattre, mais qui est une partie de la solution que nous vous proposons – pas toute la solution, mais une partie de la solution qu’on vous propose dans le cadre de ce texte.

Encore un dernier message: il faut absolument que ce texte puisse arriver à destination le plus rapidement possible – et l’urgence de la situation démontre que le vote de l’accélérateur industriel est aussi une question d’urgence pour le secteur de l’automobile.
2-0028-0000.englishText:
Madam President, perhaps a word to tell you that the objective is indeed to stop the bleeding and to reposition our industry in a sector of the future, of innovation, with conditions of competitiveness, including internationally, which are improved.

Some messages on the Commission's proposals: we proposed to have a definition of a European car to be able to discriminate positively, when there is a commitment of European public money, within the framework of public procurement, within the framework of purchase subsidies, so that there is a European purchasing preference from the moment the consumer wishes to benefit from this particular taxation.

I find it normal today, in view of the observation that you all make here, in this chamber, that the public money which is collected through taxes can benefit above all the creation of demand, in Europe, in particular segments, in particular in the electric vehicle segments. This is the proposal we have made, with 70% European components in an electric car (excluding battery), with 50% European components for the electric propulsion chain and 50% European components for the electronics.

This is the proposal that is on the table, which you must debate, but which is part of the solution that we are proposing to you – not the whole solution, but part of the solution that we are proposing to you within the framework of this text.

One more final message: it is absolutely necessary for this text to reach its destination as quickly as possible – and the urgency of the situation demonstrates that the vote on the industrial accelerator is also a matter of urgency for the automobile sector.

2-0029-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, meine Damen und Herren! Die Kommission sorgt sich um die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit unserer Autoindustrie, um die Sicherung von Arbeitsplätzen. Im Ernst? Wer hat denn diese großartige Industrie an die Wand gefahren? Warum stecken unsere Betriebe in der tiefsten Krise ihrer Geschichte? Warum werden Zigtausende von Arbeitnehmern entlassen? Das ist doch das Ergebnis auch Ihrer Politik. Sie haben sich angemaßt, in einen Markt einzugreifen, der funktioniert hat: Es gab Autos für jeden Geldbeutel, für jeden Zweck, für jeden Geschmack. Aber jetzt stellt sich Frau von der Leyen hin und verlangt, dass kleine Batterieautos gebaut werden.

Politiker haben unseren Unternehmern nicht vorzuschreiben, welche Autos sie bauen sollen. Politiker haben einen Rahmen für den Markt zu schaffen, mehr aber auch nicht. Jetzt werden in Deutschland Werke geschlossen, Arbeitsplätze abgebaut, die Produktion nach China und in die USA verlagert. Sieht so das Erfolgsmodell in Europa aus? Nein! Diese Kommission setzt auf Weltrettung statt auf Marktwirtschaft. Sie setzt auf Verbote statt auf Technologieoffenheit. Sie setzt auf faule Kompromisse statt auf faire Rahmenbedingungen und treibt die Energiepreise in Höhen, die jeden Wettbewerb abwürgen.

Noch ist es nicht zu spät. Noch können allein in Deutschland 50 000 Arbeitsplätze gerettet werden, wenn Sie sich vom Verbrenner-Aus verabschieden. Verabschieden Sie sich von grünen Träumereien, denn mit dem Kampf gegen unsere Industrie ändern Sie nicht das Weltklima, Sie verschlechtern nur das Investitionsklima. Europa ist zur No-go-Area für Innovation geworden, und das ist leider auch Ihre Schuld.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0029-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! The Commission is concerned about the competitiveness of our automotive industry and about securing jobs. Seriously? Who drove this great industry to the wall? Why are our companies in the deepest crisis in their history? Why are tens of thousands of workers being laid off? That is also the result of your politics. They presumed to intervene in a market that worked: there were cars for every budget, for every purpose, for every taste. But now Ms. von der Leyen is standing up and demanding that small battery cars be built.

Politicians don't have to tell our entrepreneurs which cars they should build. Politicians have to create a framework for the market, but nothing more. Now factories are being closed in Germany, jobs are being cut, and production is being relocated to China and the USA. Is this what the successful model looks like in Europe? No! This commission focuses on saving the world instead of a market economy. It relies on bans instead of openness to technology. It relies on lazy compromises instead of fair framework conditions and drives energy prices to levels that stifle any competition.

It's not too late yet. In Germany alone, 50,000 jobs can still be saved if you say goodbye to combustion engines. Say goodbye to green dreams, because by fighting our industry you are not changing the world climate, you are only worsening the investment climate. Europe has become a no-go area for innovation, and unfortunately that is also your fault.

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question about the “blue card” procedure.)

2-0030-0000.sourceText:
Cher Monsieur, vous nous parlez d’économie de marché, mais n’avez-vous pas l’impression que l’économie de marché, justement, elle donne la victoire aux véhicules électriques, aujourd’hui? Vous parlez d’économie de marché, mais en fait vous niez la réalité même du marché.

Vous parlez par ailleurs d’énergie, d’énergie de plus en plus chère, et vous défendez le fait qu’on continue à acheter cette énergie cher plutôt que de passer à une énergie qui nous permet d’avoir notre souveraineté et un prix moins cher – et qui est l’électricité.

Il y a là deux paradoxes qu’il me semble simplement impossible de justifier.
2-0030-0000.englishText:
Dear Sir, you talk to us about the market economy, but don't you have the impression that the market economy, in fact, gives victory to electric vehicles today? You talk about a market economy, but in fact you deny the very reality of the market.

You also talk about energy, increasingly expensive energy, and you defend the fact that we continue to buy this expensive energy rather than switching to energy which allows us to have our sovereignty and a cheaper price – and which is electricity.

There are two paradoxes here that it simply seems impossible to justify.

2-0031-0000.sourceText:
(ESN), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Vielen Dank für die Frage. Sie gestatten mir, dass ich wieder auf Deutsch antworte.

Natürlich gibt der Markt auch einen Markt für Elektroautos her; das ist überhaupt gar keine Frage. Wir haben auch nie abgelehnt, dass es Elektroautos geben soll, aber wir haben immer gesagt, es muss beide oder mehrere Antriebsformen geben. Denn Elektroautos eignen sich für viele Zwecke – der Herr Kommissar hat es ja auch gesagt, für Taxen, zum Beispiel, für Kurierdienste, für die Post – sehr, sehr gut, aber sie eignen sich eben nicht für alle. Und der Erfolg, der angebliche Erfolg, liegt ja auch an den Subventionen, an hohen Subventionen, mit denen der Staat in den Markt eingegriffen hat. Und das ist keine Marktwirtschaft, das ist Planwirtschaft, und die lehnen wir ab.
2-0031-0000.englishText:
(ESN), answer to a question about the “blue card” procedure. – Thank you for the question. Please allow me to answer in German again.

Of course there is also a market for electric cars; That's not a question at all. We have never rejected the idea that there should be electric cars, but we have always said that there must be both or more forms of drive. Because electric cars are suitable for many purposes - the Commissioner also said it, for taxis, for example, for courier services, for the post office - very, very well, but they are not suitable for everyone. And the success, the alleged success, is also due to the subsidies, high subsidies, with which the state has intervened in the market. And that's not a market economy, it's a planned economy, and we reject that.

2-0032-0000.sourceText: Vážená pani predsedajúca. Už hodinu tu rečníme o urgentných opatreniach na záchranu pracovných miest v automobilovom priemysle, ktorý vždy patril k pilierom európskej ekonomiky. No za posledné roky musel Stellantis pozastaviť linky v Poissy, Eisenachu či ďalších miestach. Audi kompletne zatvorilo závod v Bruseli. Mercedes prerušuje výrobu svojho elektronického GLC v Bremene. A Volkswagen po prvýkrát v histórii zvažuje zatvorenie až štyroch nemeckých výrobní, čo by znamenalo prepustenie 100 tisíc ľudí. Toto nie sú náhodné problémy ani dočasné ťažkosti prechodu na elektromobilitu. Je to dôsledok toho, že európska výroba už nie je konkurencieschopná, a kľúčovou príčinou, o ktorej tu dnes takmer vôbec nepočuť, je drahá elektrická energia – dvakrát drahšia ako v Spojených štátoch a o viac ako polovicu drahšia oproti Číne. Prečo je taká drahá? Pretože politika Európskej komisie, ideologický tlak na zelenú transformáciu bez ohľadu na cenu a spoľahlivosť, nás pripravila o lacnú a stabilnú energiu. A namiesto toho, aby sme to tu dnes riešili – túto prapríčinu – tak si tu tlieskame, ako míňame miliardy, ktoré nemáme na rekvalifikáciu prepustených observatória či dotácie na batérie. Prosím vás, prestaňme už donekonečna riešiť symptómy a začnime riešiť príčiny. Ďakujem.
2-0032-0000.englishText: Dear Madam President. For an hour now, we have been talking about urgent measures to save jobs in the automotive industry, which has always been one of the pillars of the European economy. But in recent years, Stellantis had to suspend lines in Poissy, Eisenach and other places. Audi has completely closed the plant in Brussels. Mercedes is suspending production of its electronic GLC in Bremen. And for the first time in its history, Volkswagen is considering closing up to four German factories, which would mean the layoff of 100,000 people. These are not random problems or temporary difficulties of the transition to electromobility. This is a result of European manufacturing no longer being competitive, and a key reason, which is almost unheard of here today, is expensive electricity – twice as expensive as in the United States and more than half as expensive as China. Why is she so expensive? Because the policy of the European Commission, the ideological pressure for a green transformation regardless of price and reliability, deprived us of cheap and stable energy. And instead of dealing with it here today - this root cause - we are applauding how we are spending the billions we don't have on the retraining of dismissed observatories or battery subsidies. Please, let's stop endlessly dealing with the symptoms and start dealing with the causes. Thank you.

2-0033-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, ¿hasta cuándo vamos a asistir, resignados, al declive del emblema de la industria europea?

La situación que vive hoy el sector de la automoción en Europa es la consecuencia de años de muchos errores; también años de errores políticos, años de obligaciones imposibles, objetivos inalcanzables, costes energéticos inasumibles y también trabas administrativas inaceptables. Frente a eso, una consecuencia —un resultado—: la incertidumbre que vive hoy el sector y los cierres y despidos que estamos conociendo.

Sin embargo, la Comisión ha presentado —y están en tramitación parlamentaria— dos iniciativas que nos pueden ayudar a revertir esta situación. La primera de ellas es el paquete de la automoción, una iniciativa que va en la buena dirección, pero que, para ser realmente útil y eficaz, debe colocar los principios de flexibilidad y neutralidad tecnológica como eje fundamental en su planificación y desarrollo, sin subordinación, por cierto, a otros principios climáticos. La segunda de ellas es el acelerador industrial, una herramienta que nos va a servir para acelerar inversiones estratégicas, para reducir trabas administrativas, pero, sobre todo, para hacer posible que invertir, que producir, en Europa sea una ventaja competitiva, sea un valor añadido y nunca un lastre para nuestras empresas.

Europa necesita hoy más que nunca una industria fuerte, innovadora, capaz de crecer, de crear empleo, respaldada por las instituciones públicas. Si no, es imposible que podamos hablar ni de autonomía estratégica ni de Estado de bienestar, ni tampoco de generación de empleo.
2-0033-0000.englishText:
Madam President, until when are we going to witness, resigned, the decline of the emblem of European industry?

The situation that the automotive sector in Europe is experiencing today is the consequence of years of many mistakes; also years of political errors, years of impossible obligations, unattainable objectives, unaffordable energy costs and also unacceptable administrative obstacles. Faced with that, a consequence—a result—: the uncertainty that the sector is experiencing today and the closures and layoffs that we are experiencing.

However, the Commission has presented—and they are being processed in parliament—two initiatives that can help us reverse this situation. The first of them is the automotive package, an initiative that is going in the right direction, but which, to be truly useful and effective, must place the principles of flexibility and technological neutrality as a fundamental axis in its planning and development, without subordination, of course, to other climate principles. The second of them is the industrial accelerator, a tool that will help us accelerate strategic investments, to reduce administrative obstacles, but, above all, to make it possible for investing and producing in Europe to be a competitive advantage, to be an added value and never a burden for our companies.

Today more than ever, Europe needs a strong, innovative industry, capable of growing and creating jobs, supported by public institutions. If not, it is impossible for us to talk about strategic autonomy or a welfare state, nor about job creation.

2-0034-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, domnule Séjourné, sunteți vicepreședintele Comisiei Europene și astăzi sunteți prezent la o dezbatere extrem de importantă despre industria producătoare de automobile din Uniunea Europeană. Astăzi, când vorbim, în România, Dacia a anunțat primele concedieri colective din ultimii 22 de ani. Este un simptom care arată cât de gravă este situația industriei producătoare de automobile și părți pentru coindustria de automobile în România și în Uniunea Europeană, aceeași situație. De ce este asta și ce așteaptă de la noi cei care se uită cu mare îngrijorare? Pentru că dacă această coloană vertebrală este bolnavă - industria producătoare de automobile - economia Uniunii Europene este într-o situație foarte proastă.

Certificate de dioxid de carbon: în România plătim 80 de euro tona de certificate de dioxid de carbon, în China de șapte ori mai puțin. Nu este, evident, o lipsă de competitivitate? Și eu cred că primele măsuri care ar trebui să fie luate, luați în vedere, nu știu, alocări de certificate gratuite de dioxid de carbon, pentru a aduce la același nivel competitivitatea.

Poate ca toți cei care nu plătesc niciun fel de taxe la importul de mașini în Uniunea Europeană să fie supus reglementării CBAM și eu cred că toate aceste lucruri trebuie făcute acum, când nu este prea târziu.
2-0034-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Séjourné, you are the Vice-President of the European Commission and today you are present at a very important debate about the car manufacturing industry in the European Union. Today, as we speak, in Romania, Dacia announced the first collective redundancies in the last 22 years. It is a symptom that shows how serious is the situation of the industry producing automobiles and parts for the automobile co-industry in Romania and in the European Union, the same situation. Why is this and what do those who watch with great concern expect from us? Because if this backbone is sick - the car manufacturing industry - the economy of the European Union is in a very bad situation.

Carbon dioxide certificates: in Romania we pay 80 euros per ton of carbon dioxide certificates, in China seven times less. Isn't that obviously a lack of competitiveness? And I think that the first measures that should be taken, take into account, I don't know, allocations of free carbon dioxide certificates, to bring competitiveness to the same level.

Maybe everyone who doesn't pay any kind of tax when importing cars into the European Union should be subject to CBAM regulation and I think all these things need to be done now before it's too late.

2-0035-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, llevo siete años hablando con dureza, pero con respeto, de las políticas ruinosas de Europa en materia de automóvil.

Estamos hartos, hartos de la Comisión, hartos hasta las narices de ese discursito de descarbonización, transición, resiliencia y objetivos climáticos. Cada mes, en Estrasburgo, hay un debate sobre el sector del automóvil y cada mes los datos de producción caen en toda Europa.

Europa hizo la revolución industrial, cambió el mundo, cambiamos la producción y la vida de millones de personas. La historia de nuestra industria es una historia de innovación, de adaptación y crecimiento. Y ustedes, la pasada legislatura, lo destruyeron todo. Nuestros coches —los mejores del planeta— dominaban los mercados mundiales. Era empleo, riqueza, clases medias, democratización del movimiento. Ahora China produce más del 90 % de las baterías eléctricas y traslada su producción a Marruecos y Turquía para utilizar las operaciones triangulares y entrar en nuestro mercado con mejores condiciones.

Esta es la realidad y ustedes son culpables del cierre de empresas, son culpables de 104 000 despidos en los dos últimos años. Yo sueño con el día en que todos ustedes algún día sean responsables y así se declare.
2-0035-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I have been speaking harshly, but respectfully, for seven years about Europe's ruinous automobile policies.

We are fed up, fed up with the Commission, fed up with this little speech about decarbonisation, transition, resilience and climate objectives. Every month in Strasbourg there is a debate on the automobile sector and every month production data drops across Europe.

Europe made the industrial revolution, it changed the world, we changed production and the lives of millions of people. The history of our industry is a story of innovation, adaptation and growth. And you, the last legislature, destroyed everything. Our cars—the best on the planet—dominated world markets. It was employment, wealth, middle classes, democratization of the movement. Now China produces more than 90% of electric batteries and moves its production to Morocco and Türkiye to use triangular operations and enter our market with better conditions.

This is reality and you are guilty of closing companies, you are guilty of 104,000 layoffs in the last two years. I dream of the day when all of you will one day be responsible and it will be declared so.

2-0036-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, nous pouvons dire bravo et merci au groupe politique de M. le commissaire Stéphane Séjourné, ainsi qu’aux différents gouvernements d’Édouard Philippe, puisque, du prix de l’énergie au coût du travail et de l’interdiction des moteurs thermiques en 2035 à la concurrence déloyale chinoise, ses responsables politiques de gauche et du centre ont tout fait méthodiquement pour mettre cette industrie européenne automobile à genoux, avec comme dernière victime en date l’emblématique site de Stellantis à Poissy, qui ne produira plus de voitures neuves à compter de 2028.

Parce que votre pacte vert a abouti à un véritable «Buy China Act»: alors que la Chine avait vingt ans d’avance dans le domaine des véhicules électriques, vous n’avez rien trouvé de mieux que de lui dérouler le tapis rouge en imposant dogmatiquement la fin des moteurs thermiques. Pis, vous persévérez dans l’erreur en refusant de remettre vraiment à plat les objectifs dogmatiques de ce pacte vert. Vous aggravez par là, d’ailleurs, une dépendance étrangère aux hydrocarbures, à une dépendance encore plus concentrée, encore plus critique: celle aux batteries et aux terres rares.

Nous avions en 2019 un excédent commercial automobile de 23 milliards d’euros avec la Chine. Il s’agit aujourd’hui d’un déficit de 6 milliards d’euros, et il y a encore des gens dans cet hémicycle pour se féliciter de cette situation.

(L'oratrice accepte une question carton bleu)
2-0036-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, we can say bravo and thank you to the political group of Mr. Commissioner Stéphane Séjourné, as well as to the various governments of Édouard Philippe, since, from the price of energy to the cost of labor and the ban on thermal engines in 2035 to unfair competition from China, its political leaders from the left and the center have done everything methodically to bring this European automobile industry to its knees, with the latest victim to date the emblematic Stellantis site in Poissy, which will no longer produce new cars from 2028.

Because your green pact resulted in a real “Buy China Act”: while China was twenty years ahead in the field of electric vehicles, you found nothing better than to roll out the red carpet for it by dogmatically imposing the end of thermal engines. Worse, you persevere in the error by refusing to really review the dogmatic objectives of this green pact. By doing this, you are aggravating a foreign dependence on hydrocarbons, an even more concentrated, even more critical dependence: that on batteries and rare earths.

In 2019, we had an automobile trade surplus of 23 billion euros with China. Today there is a deficit of 6 billion euros, and there are still people in this chamber to welcome this situation.

(The speaker accepts a blue card question)

2-0037-0000.sourceText: Madame Marion Maréchal, vous nous parlez de souveraineté. Est-ce que vous pouvez juste me dire quelle est la part du pétrole qu’on produit en France et quelle est la part de l’électricité qu’on produit en France? Ça me semble un sujet important, qu’on veuille passer à l’électrification, ou qu’on veuille, comme vous, rester dépendants du pétrole et refuser l’électrification.
2-0037-0000.englishText: Madame Marion Maréchal, you talk to us about sovereignty. Can you just tell me what share of oil is produced in France and what share of electricity is produced in France? It seems to me an important subject, whether we want to move to electrification, or whether we want, like you, to remain dependent on oil and refuse electrification.

2-0038-0000.sourceText:
C’est un sujet tout à fait central. Vous avez raison puisque, en effet, des responsables politiques tels que vous ont milité pendant des années pour la loi Hulot, qui interdit toute nouvelle exploration et exploitation des hydrocarbures potentiellement présents sur le sol français, nous privant ainsi d’ailleurs d’une nouvelle part de souveraineté – puisque nous savons que, notamment au large de la Guyane, il y aurait potentiellement des gisements d’hydrocarbures extrêmement importants – et, de ce fait, nous voilà en effet largement dépendants des hydrocarbures étrangers.

Mais, comme je viens de le préciser, le drame avec le «tout électrique» tel que vous l’avez construit, c’est que nous remplaçons une dépendance par une autre, une dépendance encore plus critique, encore plus concentrée, qui est celle aux batteries, qui est celle aux terres rares. D’où le fait, évidemment, que je parle de dogmatisme et que je parle d’idéologie, que paient au premier chef, bien sûr, les employés du secteur automobile.
2-0038-0000.englishText:
This is a very central subject. You are right since, in fact, political leaders such as yourself have campaigned for years for the Hulot law, which prohibits any new exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbons potentially present on French soil, thus depriving us of a new part of sovereignty – since we know that, particularly off the coast of Guyana, there would potentially be extremely important hydrocarbon deposits – and, as a result, we are in fact largely dependent on foreign hydrocarbons.

But, as I have just clarified, the tragedy with “all-electric” as you have built it is that we are replacing one dependence with another, an even more critical, even more concentrated dependence, which is that on batteries, which is that on rare earths. Hence the fact, obviously, that I am talking about dogmatism and that I am talking about ideology, which is primarily paid for, of course, by employees in the automobile sector.

2-0039-0000.sourceText:
Visiblement, Mme Marion Maréchal ne connaît pas les chiffres, donc je vais les lui expliquer: la part du pétrole qu’on produit en France, c’est 1 %. C’est pas pour des questions de loi Hulot, etc. C’est simplement pour un truc qui s’appelle la géologie: on n’a pas de pétrole en France, et les Français le savent, contrairement à vous.

Par contre, en France, on a l’électricité: on produit plus de 100 % de l’électricité grâce aux renouvelables et grâce au nucléaire. Refuser l’électrification des voitures, c’est refuser de bâtir un système énergétique français, et je suis très, très surpris que vous disiez oui au nucléaire dans vos mots, mais que, quand il s’agit de voter ici, vous alliez contre l’électrification, qui est essentielle pour l’avenir de notre filière nucléaire.
2-0039-0000.englishText:
Obviously, Ms. Marion Maréchal does not know the figures, so I will explain them to her: the share of oil produced in France is 1%. It’s not for questions of the Hulot law, etc. It's simply for something called geology: we don't have oil in France, and the French know it, unlike you.

On the other hand, in France, we have electricity: we produce more than 100% of electricity thanks to renewables and nuclear power. Refusing the electrification of cars is refusing to build a French energy system, and I am very, very surprised that you say yes to nuclear power in your words, but that, when it comes to voting here, you go against electrification, which is essential for the future of our nuclear sector.

2-0040-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur, je connais parfaitement les chiffres. La seule chose, c’est que j’étais en train de vous expliquer que nous pourrions avoir, contrairement à ce que vous dites, une production d’hydrocarbures français plus importante, mais que nous nous sommes interdit, pour des raisons idéologiques – du fait des Verts, avec le soutien, d’ailleurs, des centristes et de la Macronie –, d’en bénéficier, puisque nous nous sommes même interdit d’explorer la potentialité de ces gisements, dont nous savons d’ailleurs, sur le plan géologique, qu’ils pourraient exister, pas seulement d’ailleurs pour les hydrocarbures, mais également pour le gaz, par exemple, au large de Mayotte. Donc oui, je regrette cela.

Vous avez raison de dire qu’heureusement il y a eu des gens tels que nous, pendant des années, pour défendre le nucléaire, parce que s’il avait fallu compter sur le centre ou sur la gauche, nous aurions mis fin à l’énergie nucléaire française.

Je ne suis pas contre l’industrie automobile électrique, je considère que, en revanche, quand on a une avance technologique telle que la nôtre, avec l’industrie à moteur thermique, c’est évidemment dramatique de la s…

(La Présidente retire la parole à l'oratrice)
2-0040-0000.englishText:
Sir, I know the numbers perfectly. The only thing is that I was explaining to you that we could have, contrary to what you say, a greater production of French hydrocarbons, but that we have forbidden ourselves, for ideological reasons - due to the Greens, with the support, moreover, of the centrists and the Macronie -, to benefit from it, since we have even prohibited ourselves from exploring the potential of these deposits, of which we also know, on a geological level, that they could exist, not only for hydrocarbons, but also for gas, for example, off the coast of Mayotte. So yes, I regret that.

You are right to say that fortunately there were people like us, for years, to defend nuclear power, because if we had had to rely on the center or the left, we would have put an end to French nuclear energy.

I am not against the electric automobile industry, I consider that, on the other hand, when we have a technological advance such as ours, with the thermal engine industry, it is obviously dramatic to see the situation...

(The President cuts off the speaker)

2-0041-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, je ne rentrerai pas dans le débat, et je crois qu’il ne me reste que très peu de temps de parole. D’abord, peut-être, quelques éléments pour étayer l’impact, notamment de la Chine, sur le marché de l’automobile. Les conséquences pour notre industrie automobile sont catastrophiques et présentes un peu partout en Europe. Ce n’est pas qu’un débat allemand, c’est un débat pour l’ensemble des Européens sur l’ensemble des chaînes de valeur. Et vous avez une industrie allemande très forte, mais vous avez aussi une industrie, des équipementiers, des sous-traitants, très présents, partout en Europe, qui alimentent l’industrie automobile.

En Europe – que ce soit en Italie, par exemple, où plus de la moitié du marché hybride rechargeable est dominé par des modèles chinois, ou en Allemagne aussi, où le premier bénéficiaire des aides publiques nationales est aujourd’hui BYD –, nous avons construit un modèle qui finance des constructeurs chinois. Ce que nous vous proposons, avec la loi d’accélération de l’industrie, c’est de revenir là-dessus et de privilégier justement la préférence européenne, le made in Europe, quand il s’agit d’argent public européen.
2-0041-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I will not enter into the debate, and I believe that I have very little speaking time left. First, perhaps, a few elements to support the impact, particularly of China, on the automobile market. The consequences for our automobile industry are catastrophic and present almost everywhere in Europe. This is not just a German debate, it is a debate for all Europeans on all value chains. And you have a very strong German industry, but you also have an industry, equipment manufacturers, subcontractors, very present throughout Europe, which supply the automobile industry.

In Europe – whether in Italy, for example, where more than half of the plug-in hybrid market is dominated by Chinese models, or in Germany too, where the main beneficiary of national public aid is today BYD – we have built a model that finances Chinese manufacturers. What we are proposing to you, with the law to accelerate industry, is to come back to this and to favor European preference, made in Europe, when it comes to European public money.

2-0042-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, werte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Wer immer und immer und immer wieder die falsche Ausfahrt nimmt, kommt nicht ans Ziel. Über 100 000 Arbeitsplätze sind bereits in der Automobilindustrie verloren gegangen; und das war erst der Anfang. Übrigens, das ist nicht nur in Deutschland, sondern in ganz Europa eine riesige Herausforderung. Das ist eine direkte Folge des Verbrennerverbots, das hier von einer Mehrheit beschlossen wurde. Nun besteht die Chance, diesen Fehler zu überarbeiten.

Wir brauchen die besten Lösungen, nicht politische Besserwisserei, keine Verbote. Unsere Aufgabe ist es, Klimaziele vorzugeben, nicht Antriebsstränge. Arbeitgeber und Gewerkschaften fordern gemeinsam genau diesen Kurs, und trotzdem legen es Grüne und Sozialdemokraten immer nur darauf an, Recht behalten zu wollen. Wenn sich nun die Realität ändert, muss Politik bereit sein, ihre Entscheidungen zu überprüfen. Wer einen Fehler begeht und ihn nicht berichtigt, begeht einen zweiten. Deshalb: Geben wir endlich unseren Ingenieurinnen und Ingenieuren wieder die Chance, die besten Technologien entwickeln zu können.
2-0042-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues! If you take the wrong exit over and over and over again, you won't reach your destination. Over 100,000 jobs have already been lost in the automotive industry; and that was just the beginning. By the way, this is a huge challenge not only in Germany, but throughout Europe. This is a direct result of the ban on combustion engines, which was passed by a majority here. Now there is a chance to correct this error.

We need the best solutions, not political know-it-alls, not bans. Our job is to set climate targets, not drivetrains. Employers and trade unions are jointly demanding exactly this course, and yet the Greens and Social Democrats are always only interested in wanting to be right. If reality changes, politicians must be prepared to review their decisions. Anyone who commits a mistake and does not correct it commits a second one. That's why: Let's finally give our engineers the chance to develop the best technologies again.

2-0043-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la Fiat, FCA, ha perso quasi 50 000 lavoratori tra il 2000 e il 2020, ben prima del Green Deal.

Quindi, l'assenza di politiche industriali europee era già un problema. E cosa abbiamo fatto? Niente.

I nostri competitor investivano in nuove tecnologie? Noi davamo i dividendi agli azionisti, invece di reinvestirli.

Gli stipendi perdevano potere d'acquisto? Si producevano sempre più auto di lusso, perché fanno più profitti.

Aumentava la cassa integrazione? Si delocalizzavano le produzioni per pagare meno.

Quindi, colleghi, fatemi capire: noi siamo qui perché non abbiamo investito, non abbiamo pianificato, non abbiamo capito qual era la direzione del futuro e la vostra soluzione è tornare indietro e fare tutti gli errori del passato?

Dobbiamo investire nelle tecnologie del futuro, diventare esperti nella produzione di batterie e motori elettrici. Dobbiamo supportare la domanda e creare più infrastrutture per la mobilità elettrica, creare un mercato per il made in Europe – però quello vero, quello che riguarda l'Europa, Commissario – dobbiamo investire sulle competenze, formando lavoratori e lavoratrici per la transizione.

Parlate tanto di competitività nell'automotive, ma non volete metterci un euro: se volete aiutare lavoratrici e lavoratori, investite su di loro.
2-0043-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, Fiat, FCA, lost almost 50 000 workers between 2000 and 2020, well before the Green Deal.

Thus, the absence of European industrial policies was already a problem. And what did we do? Nothing.

Were our competitors investing in new technologies? We gave dividends to shareholders, instead of reinvesting them.

Were salaries losing purchasing power? More and more luxury cars were produced, because they make more profits.

Did the redundancy fund increase? Production was relocated to pay less.

So, colleagues, let me understand: we are here because we didn't invest, we didn't plan, we didn't understand what the direction of the future was and your solution is to go back and make all the mistakes of the past?

We must invest in the technologies of the future, become experts in the production of batteries and electric motors. We must support demand and create more infrastructure for electric mobility, create a market for products made in Europe - but the real one, the one that concerns Europe, Commissioner - we must invest in skills, training workers for the transition.

You talk a lot about competitiveness in the automotive sector, but you don't want to put a euro into it: if you want to help workers, invest in them.

2-0044-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, non voglio ripetere qui cose già dette dai colleghi.

Le sfide che abbiamo davanti sono enormi e serviranno anni, decenni, per recuperare il tempo sprecato, aumentare il potere di acquisto delle persone, rafforzare la competitività dell'auto europea e proteggere i lavoratori.

Possiamo, tuttavia, adottare da subito piccole misure, con grandi effetti: una norma tecnicamente semplice e a costo marginale, prossima allo zero, è lo State of Health – lo stato di salute della batteria – l'indicatore dello stato delle prestazioni che conserva la batteria rispetto a quando era nuova.

Per un veicolo elettrico usato è uno dei principali indicatori del suo valore reale, perché il valore residuo della batteria è più importante dei chilometri percorsi, incide direttamente sul valore dell'auto usata ed è decisivo per le flotte aziendali che, dopo pochi anni, alimentano il mercato dell'usato.

Rendiamo lo State of Health armonizzato, gratuitamente visibile sul display di bordo dell'auto e obbligatorio negli annunci dell'usato. Più trasparenza significa più fiducia, più domanda e quindi più lavoro e industria in Europa.
2-0044-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, I do not want to repeat here what my colleagues have already said.

The challenges we face are enormous and it will take years, decades, to make up for wasted time, increase people's purchasing power, strengthen the competitiveness of European cars and protect workers.

We can, however, immediately adopt small measures, with big effects: a technically simple and marginal cost rule, close to zero, is the State of Health - the state of health of the battery - the indicator of the state of performance that preserves the battery compared to when it was new.

For a used electric vehicle it is one of the main indicators of its real value, because the residual value of the battery is more important than the kilometers travelled, it directly affects the value of the used car and is decisive for company fleets which, after a few years, fuel the used market.

Let's make the State of Health harmonized, visible for free on the car's on-board display and mandatory in used ads. More transparency means more trust, more demand and therefore more jobs and industry in Europe.

2-0045-0000.sourceText:
Szanowna Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Albo uratujemy europejski przemysł motoryzacyjny, albo 14 milionów Europejczyków będzie bezrobotnych, a nasz kontynent stanie się gospodarczą marginalizacją. I wszyscy na tej sali wiemy, doskonale wiemy, że to Europa stworzyła marki samochodów, które od dziesięcioleci, dokładnie od dziesięcioleci, wyznaczają światowe standardy. I dziś nie możemy sobie w żaden sposób pozwolić, aby ten nasz kontynent, nasza Europa, stała się jedynie miejscem zbytu dla pojazdów z Chin i Stanów Zjednoczonych.

Oczywiście musimy inwestować, inwestować w nowoczesne technologie i innowacje, ale też musimy pamiętać o zwykłych obywatelach. To, że kupują chińskie samochody, to tylko dlatego, że są dużo tańsze. Po prostu europejskie samochody dla Europejczyków są zbyt drogie i musimy sobie to też powiedzieć. A skoro jesteśmy przy konkurencyjności, to musimy postawić na niezależność. Nie zamieniajmy dawnego uzależnienia od rosyjskiej ropy na uzależnienie od chińskich baterii i surowców.

I w tym całym zalewie niepokojących informacji mam też dobrą wiadomość. Otóż w Polsce podjęliśmy decyzję – w tym chyba dość trudnym momencie dla całej motoryzacji europejskiej – o budowie pierwszej fabryki pojazdów elektrycznych. W tym roku wbijamy szpadel, rozpoczynamy budowę fabryki, a pierwsze pojazdy zjadą w 2029 roku. Pierwsze 400 tysięcy sztuk. Dlaczego? Dlatego że nie możemy rezygnować z własnych ambicji. Dlatego to robimy. Ale chodzi też o miejsca pracy, o naszą gospodarkę europejską i polską. I udowodnijmy całemu światu, że najlepsza przyszłość motoryzacji wciąż nosi dumną markę Made in Europe.

(Mówca zgodził się na pytanie zasygnalizowane przez podniesienie niebieskiej kartki)
2-0045-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President, Mr Commissioner! Either we save the European automotive industry, or 14 million Europeans will be unemployed and our continent will become economically marginalized. And all of us in this room know, we know perfectly well, that it is Europe that has created car brands that have been setting global standards for decades, exactly for decades. And today we cannot in any way allow this continent, our Europe, to become only a sales place for vehicles from China and the United States.

Of course, we need to invest in modern technologies and innovations, but we also need to remember about ordinary citizens. The fact that they buy Chinese cars is only because they are much cheaper. European cars are simply too expensive for Europeans and we have to tell ourselves that too. And speaking of competitiveness, we must focus on independence. Let's not replace our former dependence on Russian oil with dependence on Chinese batteries and raw materials.

And in all this deluge of disturbing information, I also have good news. Well, in Poland we decided - at this probably quite difficult moment for the entire European automotive industry - to build the first electric vehicle factory. This year we are breaking ground, we are starting the construction of the factory, and the first vehicles will arrive in 2029. The first 400 thousand pieces. Why? Because we cannot give up on our own ambitions. That's why we do it. But it is also about jobs, about our European and Polish economy. And let's prove to the whole world that the best future of the automotive industry still bears the proud brand of Made in Europe.

(The speaker agreed to the question signaled by raising a blue card)

2-0046-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Pośle, to jest ten moment. Ja nawet zgodziłbym się z pańskim wystąpieniem, gdyby nie fakt – co prawda nie pańskiego – ale głosowania w zeszłej kadencji nad sprawami unijnymi, które właśnie blokują i niszczą europejski przemysł.

Więc teraz proste pytanie: czy rekomendowałby Pan Europejskiej Partii Ludowej to samo głosowanie, w taki sam sposób w sprawie ETS2? Czy dzisiaj powiedziałby Pan, że ETS2 należy wyrzucić do kosza?
2-0046-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Mr. MP, this is the moment. I would even agree with your statement, if it were not for the fact - not yours, actually - but for the voting last term on EU matters, which is blocking and destroying European industry.

So now a simple question: would you recommend to the European People's Party the same vote, in the same way on ETS2? Would you say today that ETS2 should be thrown away?

2-0047-0000.sourceText: Rozmawiamy o przemyśle samochodowym. Wydaje mi się, że wszyscy tutaj, jeśli chodzi o polską delegację, byliśmy jednomyślni w tej sprawie. Natomiast, Panie Pośle Ozdoba, Państwo rządziliście 8 lat. Szkoda, że nic nie zrobiliście, chociaż obiecywaliście, że zbudujecie tę fabrykę samochodów, a nawet nie wbiliście przysłowiowego szpadla. Więc dzisiaj, akurat w tym momencie, mógłby Pan nie zabierać głosu na tej sali.
2-0047-0000.englishText: We're talking about the car industry. It seems to me that all of us here, as far as the Polish delegation is concerned, were unanimous on this matter. However, Mr Ozdoba, you ruled for 8 years. It's a pity that you didn't do anything, even though you promised to build this car factory and you didn't even put in the proverbial shovel. So today, at this very moment, you could not speak in this room.

2-0048-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, à 53 ans, mon père, handicapé, s’est retrouvé au chômage. L’usine de composants automobiles où il travaillait avait fermé. L’adolescent que j’étais a connu l’angoisse, les discussions sur l’hypothèque de la maison, la peur de l’avenir. C’est de là que je viens, de cette terre industrielle où nous avons vécu dans notre chair ce que ces licenciements font à nos familles. MPI Lisieux a disparu, mais l’usine Renault Cléon fait encore aujourd’hui travailler plus de 2 500 Normands. Ces emplois, nous pouvons les préserver. Ce qui les sauvera, ce n’est pas la nostalgie de l’extrême droite pour le moteur thermique, car, à Cléon, ce sont les moteurs électriques de la R5 et d’autres modèles électriques de Renault que nos ouvriers fabriquent.

Il est vrai que la Chine les menace. C’est pour ça qu’il faut adopter la préférence européenne, pour que les voitures achetées en Europe soient fabriquées en Europe, construites par des travailleurs européens. L’usine où travaillait mon père a fermé; celle de Cléon, nous pouvons la sauver.
2-0048-0000.englishText:
Madam President, at age 53, my disabled father found himself unemployed. The auto components factory where he worked had closed. As a teenager I experienced anxiety, discussions about the house mortgage, fear of the future. This is where I come from, from this industrial land where we have experienced in our flesh what these layoffs do to our families. MPI Lisieux has disappeared, but the Renault Cléon factory still employs more than 2,500 Normans today. We can preserve these jobs. What will save them is not the nostalgia of the far right for the thermal engine, because, in Cléon, it is the electric motors of the R5 and other electric Renault models that our workers manufacture.

It is true that China threatens them. This is why we must adopt European preference, so that cars purchased in Europe are manufactured in Europe, built by European workers. The factory where my father worked closed; that of Cléon, we can save it.

2-0049-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, la Commission, en bon pompier pyromane, a allumé l’incendie – avec l’interdiction des moteurs thermiques en 2035 au profit de la Chine –, et la voilà qui prétend l’éteindre avec une petite cuillère. Alors, pour vous donner bonne conscience, vous organisez ici même un énième débat sur la manière de sauver la compétitivité de notre industrie automobile. Mais quel cynisme! Car derrière vos objectifs climatiques, il y a des emplois en jeu. Il y a les salariés de l’usine Stellantis de Poissy et tant d’autres – les sous-traitants, les concessionnaires, les garagistes… –, les familles qui vivent de cette industrie, et qui voient leur avenir partir en fumée à cause de votre obstination. Ils sont en plus obligés d’entendre vos mensonges sur les créations d’emplois liées à l’électrification du parc automobile, mais au prix de combien d’emplois supprimés ailleurs?

Alors, si vous voulez réellement sauver la filière automobile, soyez plus ambitieux dans vos propositions sur la préférence européenne et pour la reconquête de la souveraineté de notre industrie. Car tous ceux qui connaissent bien mieux que vous le secteur l’affirment: il est minuit moins une avant la mort de cette industrie.
2-0049-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the Commission, like a good arsonist firefighter, started the fire – with the ban on thermal engines in 2035 for the benefit of China – and here it is claiming to put it out with a teaspoon. So, to clear your conscience, you are organizing yet another debate here on how to save the competitiveness of our automobile industry. But what cynicism! Because behind your climate objectives, there are jobs at stake. There are the employees of the Stellantis factory in Poissy and so many others – subcontractors, dealers, mechanics, etc. –, the families who make a living from this industry, and who are seeing their future go up in smoke because of your obstinacy. They are also forced to hear your lies about job creation linked to the electrification of the vehicle fleet, but at the cost of how many jobs lost elsewhere?

So, if you really want to save the automobile industry, be more ambitious in your proposals on European preference and for the reconquest of the sovereignty of our industry. Because everyone who knows the sector much better than you says it: it is one minute to midnight before the death of this industry.

2-0050-0000.sourceText:
Paní předsedající, vážený pane komisaři, k otázce automotive se na tomto fóru vracíme opakovaně. Rád bych připomněl, že to byla právě skupina ECR, kdo jako první tlačil na přijetí rezoluce v době, kdy hrozily evropským automobilkám nesmyslné pokuty. Tlačili jsme i na urychlení změny legislativy směrem ke zrušení zákazu spalovacích motorů po roce 2035 a k nastavení skutečné technologické neutrality. Ne kvůli spalovacím motorům samotným, ale hlavně kvůli tomu, abychom s automobilkami mohli sladit evropská pravidla, a hlavně, aby automobilky mohly dodat zákazníkům to, co od nich chtějí. To znamená kvalitní auta s různými pohony za férové ceny.

Teď se snažíme opravit poslední návrhy Komise a problematická je i automotive část průmyslového akcelerátoru. A o to přesně jde. Buď chceme zachovat vlastní tradiční výrobu a tradiční partnerství se spolehlivými partnery, anebo pod vlajkou klimatické politiky plně otevřeme brány invazi čínských elektromobilů. Já si přeji to první.
2-0050-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, we return to the automotive issue repeatedly on this forum. I would like to remind you that it was the ECR group that first pushed for the adoption of the resolution at a time when European car companies were threatened with senseless fines. We also pushed for the acceleration of legislative changes towards the abolition of the ban on internal combustion engines after 2035 and the establishment of true technological neutrality. Not because of the internal combustion engines themselves, but mainly so that we can harmonize the European rules with the car manufacturers, and mainly so that the car manufacturers can deliver to the customers what they want from them. This means quality cars with different drives at fair prices.

Now we are trying to correct the latest proposals of the Commission, and the automotive part of the industrial accelerator is also problematic. And that's exactly the point. Either we want to preserve our own traditional production and traditional partnerships with reliable partners, or we will fully open the gates to the invasion of Chinese electric cars under the banner of climate policy. I want the first one.

2-0053-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, CEO's zijn in paniek omdat de Europese automobielindustrie aan het verdwijnen is. Maar waar was die paniek toen miljoenen werknemers werden ontslagen? Ik ben er één van. In 2010 raakten duizenden collega's en ikzelf mijn job kwijt nadat Opel Antwerpen sloot. Nadien is het enkel maar verslechterd. Audi Brussel, Van Hool in Lier en nu Volkswagen in Duitsland.

Steeds opnieuw krijgt China de schuld. Maar waar is de eigen verantwoordelijkheid? Winsten werden niet geherinvesteerd. Productie werd verplaatst en subsidies verdwenen in de zakken van aandeelhouders. Van neoliberaal extremisme gesproken.

Nu ziet iedereen wat werknemers en vakbonden al lang zeggen. Dit kon perfect voorkomen worden. Fabrieken hadden een nieuwe bestemming kunnen krijgen, werknemers hadden kunnen worden omgeschoold, jobs hadden hier kunnen blijven en we waren concurrerend geweest.

Nu halen we de industrie terug. Geweldig! Maar wie gaat alle slachtoffers van herstructureringen, delokalisatie en sluitingen compenseren? Dit mogen we nooit meer doen.

Productie moet weer in publieke handen komen. We moeten een economisch langetermijnplan opstellen en investeren in de economie en in onze werknemers.
2-0053-0000.englishText:
Mr President, CEOs are panicking because the European automotive industry is disappearing. But where was the panic when millions of workers were laid off? I am one of them. In 2010, thousands of colleagues and I lost my jobs after Opel Antwerp closed. Afterwards it only got worse. Audi Brussels, Van Hool in Lier and now Volkswagen in Germany.

China is blamed again and again. But where is personal responsibility? Profits were not reinvested. Production was relocated and subsidies disappeared into the pockets of shareholders. Talk about neoliberal extremism.

Now everyone sees what employees and unions have been saying for a long time. This could have been perfectly prevented. Factories could have been repurposed, workers could have been retrained, jobs could have stayed here and we would have been competitive.

Now we're bringing the industry back. Great! But who is going to compensate all the victims of restructuring, relocation and closures? We must never do this again.

Production must be returned to public hands. We must create a long-term economic plan and invest in the economy and in our workers.

2-0054-0000.sourceText:
Gospa predsednica! V samo dveh letih je v evropski avtomobilski industriji izgubilo službo več kot 100 000 ljudi. To je približno 140 ljudi na dan. 140 družin vsak dan, ki se je soočilo z izgubo službe. In v prihodnjih letih jih lahko pričakujemo samo še več. Zakaj?

Ker smo se odločili vsiliti eno samo tehnologijo in ignorirati realnost. Trinajst milijonov osemsto tisoč Evropejcev je odvisnih od avtomobilske industrije. Lani so različne vrste hibridov prekosile čiste električne avtomobile v prodaji za več kot dva proti ena. Ker ljudje si želijo izbire, ne želijo si ideologije.

Medtem Kitajska nadzoruje že več kot 80 odstotkov svetovnih baterij za električna vozila. Tog pristop „samo elektrika“ ne stane le delovnih mest, ampak nas stane naše industrijske suverenosti in oddaja našo prihodnost drugim. Seveda ne bi smeli biti odvisni od fosilnih goriv, ampak ne smemo zamenjati ene odvisnosti z drugo. In nujen ukrep, ki ga potrebujemo, je tehnološka nevtralnost.

Široko moramo odpreti vrata vsem učinkovitim rešitvam in naj odločata konkurenca in inovacije. In ne vem, zakaj se nekateri tako bojite tega – ker samo tako bomo zaščitili kakovostna delovna mesta, ohranili svetovno priznano evropsko inženirstvo in dejansko dosegli hitrejšo dekarbonizacijo.

Ker naši delavci poganjajo Evropo že generacije in tehnološka svoboda v Evropski uniji ne sme biti le fleksibilnost – mora biti standard. In zdaj imate priložnost, da spremenimo napake, ki so bile storjene in dejansko rešimo evropsko avtomobilsko industrijo.
2-0054-0000.englishText:
Madam President! In just two years, more than 100,000 people have lost their jobs in the European car industry. That's about 140 people a day. 140 families every day faced with job loss. And we can only expect more of them in the coming years. Why?

Because we chose to impose a single technology and ignore reality. Thirteen million eight hundred thousand Europeans depend on the automotive industry. Last year, various types of hybrids outsold pure electric cars by more than two to one. Because people want choice, they don't want ideology.

Meanwhile, China already controls more than 80 percent of the world's electric vehicle batteries. A rigid 'electricity only' approach not only costs jobs, it costs us our industrial sovereignty and outsources our future to others. Of course, we should not be dependent on fossil fuels, but we should not confuse one dependency with another. And the urgent measure we need is technological neutrality.

We must open the door wide to all effective solutions and let competition and innovation decide. And I don't know why some of you are so afraid of it - because that's the only way we'll protect quality jobs, preserve world-renowned European engineering and actually achieve faster decarbonisation.

Because our workers have been driving Europe for generations and technological freedom in the European Union must not just be flexibility – it must be the standard. And now you have the chance to change the mistakes that have been made and actually save the European car industry.

2-0055-0000.sourceText:
Fru formand! Europas bilindustri står ved en skillevej. Vi kan blive ved med at beskytte fortiden, eller vi kan investere i fremtiden. For mig er valget klart: Vi skal gøre reglerne enklere for den europæiske bilindustri, men uden at svække Europas grønne ambitioner. Hvis de europæiske bilproducenter bliver ved med at hænge fast i gårsdagens teknologi, så taber vi ikke bare endnu mere marked til Kina og USA, vi taber også de gode europæiske arbejdspladser.

Derfor er der brug for, at vi får flere elbiler på de europæiske veje, og mange, mange flere af dem skal bygges i Europa. Og ja, det kan godt være, at den europæiske elbil hverken er bedst eller billigst lige nu, men det bliver den aldrig, hvis ikke vi tør investere ægte i den grønne omstilling. Det handler om, at vi skal styrke vores konkurrenceevne, klimaet og de gode job. For at vi når derhen, kræver det politisk mod, og det mod handler om ikke at give op på den grønne pagt.
2-0055-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Europe's automotive industry is at a crossroads. We can continue to protect the past or we can invest in the future. For me, the choice is clear: We must make the rules simpler for the European car industry, but without weakening Europe's green ambitions. If the European car manufacturers continue to cling to yesterday's technology, then we will not only lose even more market to China and the USA, we will also lose the good European jobs.

That is why we need more electric cars on European roads, and many, many more of them must be built in Europe. And yes, it may well be that the European electric car is neither the best nor the cheapest right now, but it will never be if we don't dare to invest genuinely in the green transition. It is about strengthening our competitiveness, the climate and the good jobs. For us to get there, it requires political courage, and that courage is about not giving up on the Green Pact.

2-0056-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, kolegyně a kolegové, pokaždé, když některý z evropských výrobců automobilů oznámí omezení výroby nebo propouštění, měli bychom si položit jednoduchou otázku: „Jaký signál vysíláme jednomu z nejvýznamnějších evropských průmyslových odvětví?“ Všichni chceme čistší dopravu. Musíme ale vycházet z reality. Transformace postupuje pomaleji, než se očekávalo, zatímco tlak na výrobce stále roste. Pokud bude naší odpovědností a odpovědí jen další regulace a další povinnosti, automobilový průmysl nezachráníme. Přesuneme výrobu i pracovní místa mimo Evropu. Evropa potřebuje méně byrokracie, jednodušší pravidla a respekt k technologické neutralitě. Dejme našim výrobcům prostor pro konkurenceschopnost a inovace. Chceme-li zachovat kvalitní pracovní místa a výrobu automobilů v Evropě, potřebujeme politiku založenou na realitě, a nikoli ideologii.
2-0056-0000.englishText: Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, every time a European car manufacturer announces production cuts or layoffs, we should ask ourselves a simple question: "What signal are we sending to one of Europe's most important industries?" We all want cleaner transport. But we have to start from reality. The transformation is proceeding more slowly than expected, while the pressure on manufacturers continues to grow. If our responsibility and response is only more regulation and more obligations, we will not save the automotive industry. We will move production and jobs outside of Europe. Europe needs less bureaucracy, simpler rules and respect for technological neutrality. Let's give our manufacturers room for competitiveness and innovation. If we want to keep quality jobs and car manufacturing in Europe, we need a policy based on reality, not ideology.

2-0057-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Wystarczy spojrzeć na dwa duże kraje na świecie – oprócz Unii Europejskiej, gdybyśmy patrzyli na Unię Europejską łącznie: Chiny i Stany Zjednoczone. Za chwilę dołączą do nich Indie i Brazylia. Dlaczego chińskie samochody są tańsze? Dlatego, że koszty produkcji w Europie są większe. Jeżeli chińskie samochody mają nowoczesną technologię, to dlatego, że koszty produkcji pod względem kosztów energii są po prostu mniejsze.

Jeżeli spojrzymy na Stany Zjednoczone, tam również koszty energii są dwa razy mniejsze, koszty benzyny są mniejsze. No ale co robi ta sala? Ta sala w tej chwili debatuje nad tym, co zrobiliście w zeszłej kadencji. Proste pytanie o ETS2. Przecież można się z tego wycofać. Za chwilę koszty benzyny będą jeszcze wyższe. Koszty energii ETS1 są coraz wyższe. Nowoczesne technologie, sztuczna inteligencja potrzebują więcej energii. Więcej energii to większe koszty.

Można by było zadać proste pytanie, ale nie chciałbym być nieuprzejmy wobec Pana Komisarza: ci, którzy to wymyślili, może niektórzy z tych urzędników powinni zostać zweryfikowani, czy nie pracują na przykład dla przemysłu amerykańskiego czy chińskiego, bo niemożliwe jest, żeby tak zamordować europejski przemysł.
2-0057-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Just look at the two large countries in the world - apart from the European Union, if we looked at the European Union together: China and the United States. India and Brazil will soon join them. Why are Chinese cars cheaper? Because production costs in Europe are higher. If Chinese cars have modern technology, it is because the production costs in terms of energy costs are simply lower.

If we look at the United States, energy costs there are also twice as low, gasoline costs are lower. Well, what is this room doing? This room is currently debating what you did last term. A simple question about ETS2. You can withdraw from it. Gasoline costs will soon be even higher. ETS1 energy costs are getting higher. Modern technologies and artificial intelligence need more energy. More energy means higher costs.

A simple question could be asked, but I would not like to be rude to the Commissioner: those who came up with this idea, maybe some of these officials should be verified whether they are not working for, for example, American or Chinese industry, because it is impossible to murder European industry like this.

2-0058-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, ymmärrän, että autoteollisuus on monessa Euroopan maassa keskeinen talouden ala, ja se työllistää noin 13 miljoonaa ihmistä tämän maanosan puitteissa. On selvää, että jos puhumme strategisesta autonomiasta, niin teollisuus on siinä keskeinen asia, niin autoalan kuin muunkin teollisuuden osalta. Samalla tietenkin ne suuret keskustelut, kun tehdään toimia ilmastonmuutoksen vastustamiseksi ja sen torjumiseksi ja samalla koetamme edesauttaa teollisuutemme pärjäämistä, niin näiden ei pitäisi olla mitenkään toisiaan poissulkevia.

Emme saa tehdä sellaista sääntelyä, että tärkeät toimialamme ajautuvat Euroopan ulkopuolelle, koska siellä päästöt ovat varmasti suuremmat.
