Ilmakehä on kuitenkin yksi yhteinen, joten on tärkeää pitää nämä toimialat Euroopassa, mutta samalla tehdä järkeviä, teknologianeutraaleja toimia ja olla kunnianhimoinen niiden suhteen. Suomessa autoala on kärsinyt, mutta toisaalta tämä sama suomalainen autotehdas on nyt aloittanut panssariautojen ja diesel- ja sähkökäyttöisten linja-autojen valmistuksen, joten ei kannata taistella taantuman harjalla, vaan olla kehityksen kärjessä.
2-0058-0000.englishText:
Dear President, I understand that the automotive industry is a key economic sector in many European countries, and it employs approximately 13 million people within the framework of this continent. It is clear that if we talk about strategic autonomy, then industry is a key issue, both in the automotive industry and in other industries. At the same time, of course, the big discussions, when actions are taken to oppose and combat climate change and at the same time we try to help our industry to survive, these should not be mutually exclusive.

We must not make such a regulation that our important industries drift outside of Europe, because the emissions are certainly higher there. However, the atmosphere is one common, so it is important to keep these industries in Europe, but at the same time to take sensible, technology-neutral actions and be ambitious about them. In Finland, the car industry has suffered, but on the other hand, this same Finnish car factory has now started the production of armored cars and diesel and electric buses, so it is not worth fighting on the crest of a recession, but to be at the forefront of development.

2-0059-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Erstmals übersteigen Chinas Autoimporte in die Europäische Union die europäischen Exporte in die Volksrepublik. 250 000 Arbeitsplätze sind in der Automobilindustrie bereits verloren gegangen; weitere über 100 000 Arbeitsplätze stehen auf dem Spiel. Arbeitsplätze wandern ins Ausland ab, und Investitionen in Forschung und Entwicklung gehen auch ins Ausland. Die Lage ist wirklich dramatisch, aber die Lage ist kein Naturereignis, sondern auch das Ergebnis politischer Entscheidungen, die wir jetzt dringend korrigieren müssen.

Was ist zu tun? Erstens: Wir müssen die CO2‑Ziele korrigieren und echte Technologieoffenheit zulassen. Die CO2‑Flottengrenzwerte müssen angepasst werden. Abzulehnen sind Quoten zur Elektrifizierung von Flotten; das ist nämlich nichts anderes, als das Verbrennerverbot wieder über die Hintertür einzuführen. Zweitens: Wir müssen den Plug‑in‑Hybrid in Europa halten; der Utility Factor muss eingefroren werden. Und drittens: Wir brauchen bessere Standortbedingungen, und das heißt vor allen Dingen, dass wir die Energiepreise, die Stromkosten senken müssen. Die europäische Industrie zahlt heute rund doppelt so viel wie die amerikanische. Wir müssen Netzentgelte und Abgaben reduzieren, Einnahmen aus dem Emissionshandel zur Entlastung der Industriestrompreise nutzen, Genehmigungen beschleunigen und vor allen Dingen auch Bürokratie abbauen.

Nur auf eine Technologie zu setzen, ist falsch, ist falsch gewesen und wird immer falsch bleiben.
2-0059-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! For the first time, China's car imports to the European Union exceed European exports to the People's Republic. 250,000 jobs have already been lost in the automotive industry; Another 100,000+ jobs are at stake. Jobs are moving abroad and investments in research and development are also going abroad. The situation is really dramatic, but the situation is not a natural event, but also the result of political decisions that we now urgently need to correct.

What should be done? First: We must correct the CO2 targets and allow real openness to technology. The CO2 fleet limits must be adjusted. Quotas for the electrification of fleets should be rejected; This is nothing other than reintroducing the ban on combustion engines through the back door. Second: We have to keep the plug-in hybrid in Europe; the utility factor must be frozen. And thirdly: We need better location conditions, and that means, above all, that we have to reduce energy prices and electricity costs. European industry today pays around twice as much as American industry. We have to reduce network fees and taxes, use income from emissions trading to reduce pressure on industrial electricity prices, speed up approvals and, above all, reduce bureaucracy.

Relying on only one technology is wrong, has been wrong and will always remain wrong.

2-0060-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, questo dibattito arriva in un momento cruciale, con il pacchetto automotive in discussione nelle varie commissioni competenti.

E non vi è dubbio che le scelte che verranno fatte nei prossimi mesi saranno decisive per il settore, chiamato a decarbonizzarsi, salvaguardando competitività e posti di lavoro. Penso anche alla componentistica, per una buona parte non riproducibile nella dimensione dell'elettrico.

Promuovere l'innovazione e accompagnare la trasformazione: per rilanciare il principale settore della manifattura europea servono cospicui investimenti, anche pubblici – lo abbiamo detto e lo ripetiamo – anche perché, visibilmente, regole e sanzioni, da sole, sono insufficienti a produrre il cambiamento auspicato, soprattutto in presenza di una concorrenza cinese ampiamente sussidiata dallo Stato.

Ma, in assenza di investimenti adeguati, serve ragionevolezza. Spero quindi che i negoziati dei prossimi mesi mettano al centro la sostanza, tenendo fermi gli obiettivi di decarbonizzazione, da una parte, e, dall'altra, trovando la giusta misura delle flessibilità necessarie a governare il processo di transizione.
2-0060-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this debate comes at a crucial moment, with the automotive package being discussed in the various competent committees.

And there is no doubt that the choices that will be made in the coming months will be decisive for the sector, called to decarbonise, safeguarding competitiveness and jobs. I'm also thinking of the components, a good part of which cannot be reproduced in the electric dimension.

Promote innovation and accompany transformation: to relaunch the main European manufacturing sector, substantial investments are needed, including public ones - we have said it and we repeat it - also because, visibly, rules and sanctions alone are insufficient to produce the desired change, especially in the presence of Chinese competition largely subsidized by the State.

But, in the absence of adequate investments, reasonableness is needed. I therefore hope that the negotiations in the coming months will put substance at the centre, keeping the decarbonisation objectives firm, on the one hand, and, on the other, finding the right measure of flexibilities necessary to govern the transition process.

2-0061-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, Monsieur le Vice-Président, l’industrie européenne est en panne. Il y a urgence! La production a chuté de 20 % en cinq ans, et 100 000 emplois ont été détruits en 2024. Pourtant, ici, la droite préfère garder le véhicule thermique, alors que l’Europe brûle.

Pendant ce temps, la Chine accélère. Cette année, sa part de marché a doublé en Europe. Elle vend plus véhicules en Allemagne que les Allemands n’en vendent en Chine. Pour sauver nos emplois, il nous faut de toute urgence des droits de douane de 35 % – y compris sur l’hybride – et des critères de contenu local strict. Lancez la petite voiture made in Europe accessible pour booster la demande!

Chers collègues, le choix est simple: investir dans l’électrique made in Europe pour assurer un avenir serein aux 3 millions et demi de travailleurs du secteur, ou bien regarder dans le rétroviseur – et en 2035, nous aurons 1 million d’emplois en moins et toujours plus de pollution.

(L'orateur accepte une question carton bleu)
2-0061-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Mr Vice-President, European industry is broken. There is an emergency! Production has fallen by 20% in five years, and 100,000 jobs have been destroyed in 2024. Yet here, the right prefers to keep the thermal vehicle, while Europe is burning.

Meanwhile, China is accelerating. This year, its market share has doubled in Europe. It sells more vehicles in Germany than the Germans sell in China. To save our jobs, we urgently need 35% tariffs – including on hybrid – and strict local content criteria. Launch the small accessible car made in Europe to boost demand!

Dear colleagues, the choice is simple: invest in electricity made in Europe to ensure a peaceful future for the 3 and a half million workers in the sector, or look in the rearview mirror – and in 2035, we will have 1 million fewer jobs and ever more pollution.

(The speaker accepts a blue card question)

2-0062-0000.sourceText:
Cher collègue, pas plus tard que ce matin, une étude d’un cabinet d’experts est sortie et elle affirme qu’une usine automobile sur trois en Europe est «inutile à cause de nos surcapacités de production». Nous savons tous ici comment cela va finir si vous ne vous réveillez pas: des suppressions d’emplois massives et des fermetures d’usines, notamment en France – et cela a déjà commencé.

Alors, cher collègue, j’ai une question à vous poser: est-ce que vous assumez d’avoir bradé notre industrie automobile au profit de la Chine, en soutenant des normes irréalistes, hors sol, et l’interdiction du thermique en 2035? Et surtout, est-ce qu’un jour vous allez enfin présenter, avec vos collègues, vos excuses à tous les salariés et à nos constructeurs et équipementiers qui se sont retrouvés au chômage, dans la précarité par votre faute?
2-0062-0000.englishText:
Dear colleague, just this morning, a study by a firm of experts was released and it states that one in three automobile factories in Europe is “useless because of our excess production capacity”. We all know here how this will end if you don't wake up: massive job cuts and factory closures, especially in France – and it has already started.

So, dear colleague, I have a question to ask you: do you accept that you have sold off our automobile industry for the benefit of China, by supporting unrealistic, above-ground standards and the ban on thermal power in 2035? And above all, will one day you finally present, with your colleagues, your apologies to all the employees and to our manufacturers and equipment manufacturers who found themselves unemployed, in precariousness because of you?

2-0063-0000.sourceText: Chère collègue, je vous invite à ouvrir les journaux et à voir que le nombre de véhicules vendus en France, électriques, a doublé en un an. Vous êtes en retard par rapport au marché, vous êtes en retard par rapport aux citoyens européens, et ce que nous faisons avec l’électrification, c’est qu’au contraire nous rattrapons notre retard par rapport à la Chine. Vous, vous regardez dans le rétroviseur, et bientôt, avec votre action, c’est l’ensemble de l’industrie automobile européenne qui connaîtra un krach.
2-0063-0000.englishText: Dear colleague, I invite you to open the newspapers and see that the number of electric vehicles sold in France has doubled in one year. You are behind the market, you are behind European citizens, and what we are doing with electrification is, on the contrary, we are catching up with China. You look in the rearview mirror, and soon, with your action, the entire European automobile industry will experience a crash.

2-0065-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Storslagna mål som inte tar hänsyn till förutsättningarna att förverkliga dem indikerar inte ledarskap.

Europa har inte råd att ägna sig åt önsketänkande eller fler politiska luftslott. Ändå valde EU att göra just det under förra mandatperioden. Förbränningsmotorförbudet är det tydligaste exemplet. I ivern att driva den gröna omställningen ignorerades basala frågor. Var finns den stabila elproduktionen och laddinfrastrukturen? Blir klimatet bättre av åtgärderna? Svaret är nej. Förbudet minskar inte vårt beroende, det flyttar det: från rysk olja till kinesiska kritiska råmaterial. Det är inte en grön omställning, det är geopolitisk naivitet.

Medan Europa kväver den egna industrin, jobben och investeringsviljan fortsätter världens stora klimatbovar att öka sina utsläpp. Politik måste utgå från verkligheten. Europa behöver teknikneutralitet, innovation och konkurrenskraft, inte fler symboliska förbud.
2-0065-0000.englishText:
Madam Speaker! Grand goals that do not take into account the conditions to realize them do not indicate leadership.

Europe cannot afford to indulge in wishful thinking or more political castles in the air. Yet the EU chose to do just that during the last term. The internal combustion engine ban is the clearest example. In the zeal to drive the green transition, basic issues were ignored. Where is the stable electricity production and charging infrastructure? Will the climate improve as a result of the measures? The answer is no. The ban does not reduce our dependence, it shifts it: from Russian oil to Chinese critical raw materials. It's not a green transition, it's geopolitical naivety.

While Europe is suffocating its own industry, jobs and the will to invest, the world's major climate criminals continue to increase their emissions. Politics must be based on reality. Europe needs technology neutrality, innovation and competitiveness, not more symbolic bans.

2-0066-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, domnule comisar, ați început intervenția dumneavoastră spunând că anul trecut ați spus că industria auto este în pericol de moarte. Și așa este. Problema este să întrebăm de ce? Comisia Europeană cred că a plecat la un program, neluând în seamă situația concretă. Un manager privat ține cont de situația globală și iată de ce acum suntem în situația în care, global, noi nu putem să producem ca și China, avem costuri, inputuri mai mari și la energie, evident, și infrastructura ne lipsește, sistemul de încărcare în tot spațiul Uniunii Europene și să ne mai gândim și la clasa de mijloc, domnule comisar: credeți că poate? Mașina nu este un lux, doar cele care merg la curse.

Mașinile sunt acum o necesitate pentru mobilitate și atunci noi trebuie să ne gândim să construim un sistem auto care să nu mai disponibilizeze, ci să aducă în Europa. Și foarte bine că ați venit cu această propunere. Da, aș vrea să se țină cont de Made in Europe în tot lanțul valoric al construcțiilor de mașini și să ne gândim să adaptăm din mers programul pentru sistemul mașinilor electrice.
2-0066-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, you started your intervention by saying that last year you said that the car industry was in mortal danger. And so it is. The problem is to ask why? I think the European Commission has gone to a program, not taking into account the concrete situation. A private manager takes into account the global situation and this is why we are now in a situation where, globally, we cannot produce like China, we have costs, higher inputs and energy, obviously, and we lack the infrastructure, the charging system throughout the European Union and let's also think about the middle class, Commissioner: do you think it is possible? The car is not a luxury, only the ones that go racing.

Cars are now a necessity for mobility, and then we have to think about building a car system that no longer provides, but brings to Europe. And very good that you came up with this proposal. Yes, I would like Made in Europe to be taken into account throughout the car building value chain and to consider adapting the program for the electric car system on the fly.

2-0067-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, ομολογήσατε ότι θα γίνουν 600.000 απολύσεις, 100.000 μόνο στον όμιλο Volkswagen. Καημός της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης είναι να στηρίξει τους ομίλους στον οξυμένο ανταγωνισμό με Κίνα και ΗΠΑ σε μια σειρά τομείς —μπαταρίες, ηλεκτροκίνηση—, πάνω απ' όλα όμως με στροφή στην πολεμική οικονομία ως διέξοδο κερδοφορίας μέσα από την παραγωγή οχημάτων, αρμάτων και ειδών διπλής χρήσης. Χαλαρώνετε περαιτέρω τις πράσινες προδιαγραφές για τις επιχειρήσεις, για να ενισχυθεί η κερδοφορία τους και, στον αντίποδα, τα λαϊκά νοικοκυριά φορτώνονται νέα βάρη για παλιά σπίτια, οχήματα, καυστήρες πετρελαίου.

Με το Ταμείο Ανάκαμψης πριμοδοτήθηκε το ξεχαρβάλωμα συλλογικών συμβάσεων, κλιμακώθηκε η ενεργειακή φτώχεια, η ακρίβεια, ο πληθωρισμός. Ο καπιταλιστικός τρόπος παραγωγής που διαφημίζουν η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, οι κυβερνήσεις και τα κόμματά της στην ανάπτυξη και στην κρίση εκτοξεύει την εκμετάλλευση των εργαζομένων για τα κέρδη του κεφαλαίου.

Στηρίζουμε τις μεγαλειώδεις εργατικές κινητοποιήσεις στη Γερμανία, για να μη χαθεί καμία θέση εργασίας, να στηριχτεί το εργατικό εισόδημα με συλλογικές συμβάσεις και ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις στους μισθούς. Συμπέρασμα και ανάγκη: η παραγωγή να οργανωθεί με κριτήριο τις σύγχρονες ανάγκες και όχι τα κέρδη και τον πόλεμο.
2-0067-0000.englishText:
Madam President, you have admitted that there will be 600,000 redundancies, 100,000 in the Volkswagen Group alone. It is a pity for the European Union to support the groups in the intensified competition with China and the USA in a number of sectors—batteries, electrification—but above all with a shift to the war economy as an outlet for profitability through the production of vehicles, tanks and dual-use items. You further relax the green standards for businesses to boost their profitability and, on the contrary, ordinary households are burdened with new burdens for old houses, vehicles, oil burners.

With the Recovery Fund, the dismantling of collective agreements was rewarded, energy poverty, precision, inflation escalated. The capitalist mode of production promoted by the European Union, its governments and parties in growth and crisis catalyzes the exploitation of workers for the profits of capital.

We support the great labor mobilizations in Germany, so that no jobs are lost, workers' incomes are supported by collective agreements and substantial wage increases. Conclusion and need: production should be organized according to modern needs and not profits and war.

2-0069-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, el sector de la automoción es vital para Galiza, para mi país, donde hay miles de trabajos directos e indirectos —como sabe usted— en el sector y, además, donde estamos reclamando un plan industrial que no pueda ser un cheque en blanco para darle subvenciones a la industria automovilística mientras se destruye y se precariza el empleo.

Se paga por deslocalizar, como hemos visto en estos años, para perder empleos. No puede ser, señor comisario, que se le dé el mismo tratamiento a los vehículos fabricados en Europa que a los vehículos fabricados fuera. No puede ser que la crisis la sigan pagando los trabajadores. Si hay competencia desleal, Europa tiene que actuar: fabricar en Europa, crear puestos de trabajo con salarios dignos, porque se le han dado muchas ayudas al sector, pero la transición, a pesar de que tenga que ser justa, tiene que ser también para las personas, para las economías locales.

Por eso, le pregunto: ¿más ayudas para quién? ¿Para las multinacionales del sector del automóvil o para crear empleo digno y de calidad?
2-0069-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the automotive sector is vital for Galiza, for my country, where there are thousands of direct and indirect jobs - as you know - in the sector and, furthermore, where we are demanding an industrial plan that cannot be a blank check to give subsidies to the automotive industry while employment is destroyed and made precarious.

It pays to relocate, as we have seen in recent years, to lose jobs. It cannot be, Commissioner, that vehicles manufactured in Europe are given the same treatment as vehicles manufactured outside. It cannot be that the workers continue to pay for the crisis. If there is unfair competition, Europe has to act: manufacture in Europe, create jobs with decent wages, because a lot of aid has been given to the sector, but the transition, although it has to be fair, has to also be for people, for local economies.

Therefore, I ask you: more help for whom? For multinationals in the automobile sector or to create decent, quality employment?

2-0070-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Seien wir ehrlich: Die aktuelle Krise ist keine Krise der Profite, sondern eine Krise der Arbeitsplätze. Hunderttausende Arbeitsplätze wurden in den letzten Jahren abgebaut, und Hunderttausende stehen weiterhin auf der Streichliste. Die Kolleginnen und Kollegen bei VW, bei Mercedes, bei Bosch, in der Industrie in Deutschland und europaweit streiken derzeit, kämpfen um ihre Arbeitsplätze und bessere Löhne, und ihnen gehört unsere Solidarität.

Die Wahrheit ist, diese Krise ist kein plötzlicher Schock; es ist eine Krise mit Ansage. Die Transformation wurde verschleppt und der letzte Tropfen für den Profit ausgequetscht. Die einzige Industriepolitik der Kommission bestand darin, die Rüstungsindustrie auszubauen, was aber volkswirtschaftlich Bullshit ist. Ihr Einstieg in den Ausstieg, Ihr Ausstieg aus dem Ausstieg hat wirklich keinem geholfen, das Hin und Her hilft niemandem. Milliardenhilfen sind geflossen, aber keine Konditionen für Arbeitsplatzerhalt wurden diktiert – und genau das ist der Fehler. Die Frage aktuell ist: Auf welcher Seite stehen Sie eigentlich?
2-0070-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Let's be honest: the current crisis is not a crisis of profits, but a crisis of jobs. Hundreds of thousands of jobs have been lost in recent years and hundreds of thousands remain on the cut list. Our colleagues at VW, at Mercedes, at Bosch, in industry in Germany and across Europe are currently on strike, fighting for their jobs and better wages, and our solidarity belongs to them.

The truth is, this crisis is not a sudden shock; it is a crisis with an announcement. The transformation was delayed and every last drop was squeezed out for profit. The Commission's only industrial policy was to expand the arms industry, which is economically bullshit. Your entry into the exit, your exit from the exit really didn't help anyone, the back and forth doesn't help anyone. Billions in aid have flowed, but no conditions for job retention have been dictated - and that is exactly the mistake. The current question is: Which side are you actually on?

2-0071-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, kolegyně a kolegové, víte, kdy přestal být automobilový průmysl konkurenceschopný? Ve chvíli, kdy nastoupila Ursula von der Leyenová a její „poskoci“ do čela Komise, přesně v ten moment. My jsme tady slyšeli pana komisaře, jak nám řekl: „Zabráníme smrtícímu cyklu, dlužíme to našemu průmyslu.“ A potom nám oznámí, že chystá další legislativu, další regulace, že budeme definovat evropský vůz. Prosím vás, my, než si vydefinujeme, co je evropský vůz, tak tady nebude žádná továrna na automobilový průmysl. To jediné, co bychom v tuhle chvíli měli udělat, pane komisaři, je škrtat, rušit, okamžitě přestat s tou obrovskou byrokracií a podpořit jakýmkoliv způsobem automobilky, například v tom, co slibujete dva roky, co sedíte v Komisi, že snížíte ceny energií. S ničím takovým jste nepřišel, takže jediné, co pomůže automobilovému průmyslu, je, že vy skončíte, navždy.
2-0071-0000.englishText: Madam President, colleagues, do you know when the automotive industry ceased to be competitive? At the moment when Ursula von der Leyen and her "goons" came to head the Commission, exactly at that moment. Here we heard the Commissioner tell us: "We will prevent a deadly cycle, we owe it to our industry." And then he informs us that he is preparing another legislation, another regulation, that we will define a European car. Please, before we define what a European car is, there will be no car factory here. The only thing we should do at this moment, Commissioner, is cut, cancel, immediately stop the huge bureaucracy and support the car companies in any way, for example, in what you have been promising for the two years that you have been sitting in the Commission, that you will lower energy prices. You didn't come up with anything like that, so the only thing that will help the auto industry is for you to quit, forever.

2-0072-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjereniče, danas smo ovdje jer su postavljeni ciljevi za europsku automobilsku industriju bili preambiciozni, previše rigidni i nedovoljno usklađeni sa stvarnim mogućnostima naših proizvođača.

Europska industrija koja zapošljava gotovo 14 milijuna ljudi suočila se s visokim troškovima, gubicima radnih mjesta i premalo tehnološke fleksibilnosti, sve radi inzistiranja radikalne ljevice i zelenih.

Istodobno su kineski proizvođači jačali zahvaljujući državnim subvencijama, niskim troškovima te kontroli nad baterijama i ključnim sirovinama, a u prvih šest mjeseci ove godine dosegnuli su rekordni tržišni udio u Europi od 7,3 posto.

Zato pozdravljam automobilski paket i ambiciozniji nacrt izvješća kolege Salinija. Oni zadržavaju smjer prema klimatskoj neutralnosti, ali i našoj industriji daju više vremena, fleksibilnosti i tehnoloških mogućnosti.

Europa ne smije donositi političke odluke koje dobro zvuče na papiru, a u praksi slabe našu industriju, ulaganja i radna mjesta.
2-0072-0000.englishText:
Honorable Chairperson, Commissioner, we are here today because the goals set for the European automotive industry were too ambitious, too rigid and insufficiently aligned with the real capabilities of our manufacturers.

European industry employing almost 14 million people has faced high costs, job losses and too little technological flexibility, all at the insistence of the radical left and the Greens.

At the same time, Chinese manufacturers have strengthened thanks to government subsidies, low costs and control over batteries and key raw materials, and in the first six months of this year they reached a record market share in Europe of 7.3 percent.

That is why I welcome the car package and the more ambitious draft of my colleague Salini's report. They maintain the direction towards climate neutrality, but also give our industry more time, flexibility and technological possibilities.

Europe must not make political decisions that sound good on paper, but in practice weaken our industry, investments and jobs.

2-0073-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, Monsieur le Commissaire, trois priorités pour préserver les emplois de qualité dans l’automobile européenne: premièrement, investir massivement dans les compétences; deuxièmement, relocaliser les segments à forte valeur ajoutée (batteries, logiciels, électronique de puissance, semi-conducteurs, recyclage); troisièmement, renforcer l’attractivité des métiers industriels (conditions de travail, perspectives d’évolution, partenariats entre entreprises, universités et centres de recherche).

L’Union européenne s’est donné des objectifs climatiques ambitieux, mais une question s’impose: a-t-on évalué avec la même rigueur les conséquences de ces décisions sur notre capacité à produire, investir, créer des emplois durables de qualité? La réponse est malheureusement non. La transition écologique et numérique crée de nouvelles occasions, mais exige des investissements importants dans les compétences, l’innovation et l’accompagnement des employés.

Je propose que, à l’avenir, toute initiative législative majeure soit soumise à deux évaluations complémentaires: son impact sur notre compétitivité industrielle et son impact sur l’emploi de qualité dans l’Union européenne.
2-0073-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Commissioner, three priorities to preserve quality jobs in the European automobile sector: firstly, invest massively in skills; second, relocalize high value-added segments (batteries, software, power electronics, semiconductors, recycling); thirdly, strengthening the attractiveness of industrial professions (working conditions, career prospects, partnerships between companies, universities and research centers).

The European Union has set itself ambitious climate objectives, but one question remains: have we assessed with the same rigor the consequences of these decisions on our ability to produce, invest and create quality sustainable jobs? The answer is unfortunately no. The ecological and digital transition creates new opportunities, but requires significant investments in skills, innovation and employee support.

I propose that, in the future, any major legislative initiative be subject to two complementary assessments: its impact on our industrial competitiveness and its impact on quality employment in the European Union.

2-0074-0000.sourceText:
Gospa predsednica! Morda je prihodnost avtomobilske industrije res električna, nisem pa povsem prepričan, da smo danes pripravljeni na električno prihodnost. Ali so na to pripravljena omrežja, ali je na to pripravljena proizvodnja električne energije? Ali imamo rudnine, potrebne za električne baterije? Odgovor je ne. In zato seveda potrebujemo neko razumno prehodno obdobje, kjer bomo zagotavljali tehnološko nevtralnost.

Evropa je svetovni prvak pri proizvodnji najčistejših motorjev z notranjim izgorevanjem in morali bi biti resnično nori, da bi se temu odpovedali in se popolnoma podredili novi odvisnosti, to je odvisnosti od kitajskih električnih vozil. Zato je edina prava pot tehnološka nevtralnost, da damo priložnost tako klasičnim vozilom kot električnim vozilom.
2-0074-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Maybe the future of the automotive industry is indeed electric, but I'm not entirely sure we're ready for an electric future today. Are the networks ready for this, is the electricity production ready for this? Do we have the minerals needed for electric batteries? The answer is no. And that is why, of course, we need some reasonable transition period where we will ensure technological neutrality.

Europe is the world champion in the production of the cleanest internal combustion engines and we would have to be really crazy to give that up and completely submit to a new dependence, which is the dependence on Chinese electric vehicles. Therefore, the only right way is technological neutrality, to give both classic vehicles and electric vehicles a chance.

2-0075-0000.sourceText: Paní předsedající, vážený pane komisaři, z debaty o autech se nám vytrácí to nejdůležitější – zájem zákazníků, běžných motoristů, kteří potřebují levné a dobré auto. Ne nesmysly, kvůli kterým jsou auta drahá, špatná a plná „kazítek“. Kdyby unijní regulace nebylo, tak moderní, jednoduché auto by mohlo stát 6 000 EUR a kvalitní rodinné auto třeba 10 000 nebo 12 000 EUR. Ve světě to jde. Ale naši lidé platí třikrát tolik nebo jezdí v průměru 16 let starými ojetinami, protože na nové nemají. Pojďme proto seškrtat regulace, protože na papíry to nejezdí, jak se říká mezi motoristy. Nechme lidi kupovat taková auta, která opravdu chtějí, ne jaká jim předepisujete. A firmy, ty ať nevyrábí podle regulací, ale podle přání zákazníka jako před lety, když byl náš automobilový průmysl ještě mladý a úspěšný. A kdo neumí vyrobit dobré a levné auto, tak ať zkrachuje a uvolní místo lepším.
2-0075-0000.englishText: Madam President, Commissioner, the most important thing is missing from the debate about cars - the interest of customers, ordinary motorists who need a cheap and good car. Not the nonsense that makes cars expensive, bad and full of "defects". If there was no EU regulation, a modern, simple car could cost EUR 6,000, and a quality family car could cost EUR 10,000 or EUR 12,000. It works in the world. But our people pay three times as much or drive used cars that are 16 years old on average because they don't have the money to buy new ones. So let's cut back on regulations, because it doesn't work on paper, as they say among motorists. Let's let people buy the cars they really want, not the cars you prescribe. And companies, let them not produce according to regulations, but according to the wishes of the customer, as years ago, when our automotive industry was still young and successful. And whoever can't make a good and cheap car, let them go bankrupt and make way for better ones.

2-0078-0000.sourceText:
Die Aussprache ist geschlossen.

Die Sitzung wird kurz unterbrochen. Sie wird in wenigen Minuten mit der Erläuterung des Tätigkeitsprogramms des irischen Ratsvorsitzes wieder aufgenommen.

Schriftliche Erklärungen (Artikel 178)
2-0078-0000.englishText:
The debate is closed.

The meeting is briefly interrupted. It will resume in a few minutes with the presentation of the Irish Presidency's program of activities.

Written declarations (Article 178)

2-0094-0000.sourceText:
Tá fáilte romhat, a Thaoisigh.

You are very welcome in this House, Taoiseach. I said this to you in Dublin and I really mean it, so I think I have to repeat it now also in this House: Europe loves Ireland. I think you are not going to find one colleague in this House that doesn't have a soft spot for Ireland. So we are all looking forward to the Irish Presidency.

But what we need from you is action, action, action. Heat waves are torturing Europe – forest fires, temperature records. The Green Deal is more important than ever. Strong commitment to green targets, especially when we speak about money. The budget and continuing the Green Deal will be your responsibility in the next six months, Taoiseach. And we trust on your commitment here.

Yet – and I have to say it – what we have seen also in Ireland in the recent months has cast some doubt over whether you will be ambitious enough on climate action in Europe. Dismantling parts of the Climate Act in Ireland, delaying climate action plans – Taoiseach, how will you make sure that in Europe we will not experience the Irish Presidency as climate laggards, or even worse, climate quitters. Because with unprecedented heat waves, but also with our still-immense dependency on fossil autocrats around the world, the pressure is on. We have to see action on this.

And – you said this – our values are under attack. We can clearly see it with Russian disinformation campaigns. Ireland can play a crucial role here. A lot of the US tech giants are actually sitting in Ireland, so you have a key role in regulating their business models. Rest assured, this Parliament across the board stands behind you if you are going to take action on enforcing, for example, the Digital Services Act.

We all know that if Ireland wants to, you can, because Ireland has consistently shown over the past decades how the EU is a powerful stage also for smaller and medium-sized countries. Instead of having never-ending pointless debates about how the EU is a barrier to national sovereignty, Ireland has consistently punched above its weight in Europe and gained more sovereignty through European cooperation.

This is what we want to see in the next six months from you. All the best to your presidency.
2-0094-0000.englishText:
You are welcome, Pastor.

You are very welcome in this House, Taoiseach. I said this to you in Dublin and I really mean it, so I think I have to repeat it now also in this House: Europe loves Ireland. I think you are not going to find one colleague in this House that doesn't have a soft spot for Ireland. So we are all looking forward to the Irish Presidency.

But what we need from you is action, action, action. Heat waves are torturing Europe – forest fires, temperature records. The Green Deal is more important than ever. Strong commitment to green targets, especially when we talk about money. The budget and continuing the Green Deal will be your responsibility in the next six months, Taoiseach. And we trust on your commitment here.

Yet – and I have to say it – what we have also seen in Ireland in recent months has cast some doubt over whether you will be ambitious enough on climate action in Europe. Dismantling parts of the Climate Act in Ireland, delaying climate action plans – Taoiseach, how will you make sure that in Europe we will not experience the Irish Presidency as climate laggards, or even worse, climate quitters. Because with unprecedented heat waves, but also with our still-immense dependency on fossil autocrats around the world, the pressure is on. We have to see action on this.

And – you said this – our values ​​are under attack. We can clearly see it with Russian disinformation campaigns. Ireland can play a crucial role here. A lot of the US tech giants are actually sitting in Ireland, so you have a key role in regulating their business models. Rest assured, this Parliament across the board stands behind you if you are going to take action on enforcing, for example, the Digital Services Act.

We all know that if Ireland wants to, you can, because Ireland has consistently shown over the past decades how the EU is a powerful stage also for smaller and medium-sized countries. Instead of having never-ending pointless debates about how the EU is a barrier to national sovereignty, Ireland has consistently punched above its weight in Europe and gained more sovereignty through European cooperation.

This is what we want to see in the next six months from you. All the best to your presidency.

2-0096-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, a Thaoisigh, is deis í Uachtaránacht na hÉireann ar an gComhairle chun bheith ina guth ar son na síochána. Guth ar son cearta daonna agus an dlí idirnáisiúnta. Am chun ár mbunluachanna a chur chun cinn.

Unfortunately, though, the Irish Government's approach continues to be: 'We will be principled, but only when it costs us nothing'. 2-0099-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, a Thaoisigh, a Choimisinéir, comhghairdeas, a Thaoisigh, as ucht na hóráide breátha a thug tú dúinn. Mar a dúirt tú, tá tús maith déanta agat agus ar aghaidh leis an dea-obair.

The competitiveness, values and security theme of the Irish Presidency – I think most people can see that's good, and it captures the essentials for this mandate. I think Mario Draghi outlined in 2024 the need for competitiveness. This is the fifth presidency in this mandate, and I think we have outlined and identified key reports which need to be either finalised or progressed. 2-0101-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Taoiseach, I want to start by wishing you luck.

Má éiríonn leatsa, éireoidh linn ar fad mar Éireannaigh agus mar shaoránaigh Eorpacha.

This is a presidency which has to deliver on key issues facing Ireland and Europe. None among them are bigger than housing. During this presidency, the Commission will bring forward an Affordable Housing Act because we in the S&D Group demanded it.

You failed to mention housing at all in your address in Dublin Castle last week, and made only a passing reference today. The Irish Presidency must lead in making housing an urgent European priority.

Two weeks ago I brought my group president to Gardiner Street in Dublin, where 10 % of the entire homeless population of Ireland live. Service providers said schoolchildren are doing their homework on fire escapes. Taoiseach, our failure must stop here and the MFF must deliver on housing.

Likewise, on workers' rights and climate action, our record is nothing to be proud of. I want to be clear: we will not support any competitiveness agenda that comes on the backs of workers or our environment.

Taoiseach, we are a country of céad míle fáilte. We are not a country that chants 'send them back'. It angered me to see your government colleagues voting with that poison in this Chamber last month. Ireland, the country of coffin ships, undocumented in America and memories of 'no blacks, no dogs, no Irish' must strive for better.

On Gaza, I want to acknowledge that our government has shown some leadership and again today, in the face of abject failure for many in the EU, we have to use this presidency to end the EU-Israel Association Agreement once and for all.

We must stand with Ukraine unequivocally. Taoiseach, the government's position on Aughinish Alumina is indefensible. This week I will vote to progress sanctions so this facility cannot fuel Putin's war.

Taoiseach, as you have said, John Hume once said that the EU was the greatest peace process in history. In honour of his legacy, we should be persuaders for the UK to rejoin the EU and for greater unity on our island. John Hume also said that we cannot eat a flag.

Our Union has achieved so much. We can meet the challenges of today. We can house our children, stop our planet from burning, reject hate and racism, back our workers, unite the people of our island and uphold international law.

Mar a scríobh Ríordánach eile ó do chontae féin, a Thaoisigh, tráth dá raibh, 'Ba mhaith liom breith ar eireaball spideoige'. Is féidir linn breith ar eireaball na hEorpa, le chéile.

2-0107-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, ar son mé féin agus fhoireann Fhianna Fáil, cuirim fáilte roimh an Taoiseach. Mar is eol do chách, is cara pearsanta é an Taoiseach. Táimid inár gcairde le beagnach 40 bliain. Guím gach rath ort, a Thaoisigh, agus tú ag tosú ar d'uachtaránacht. Tá dúshláin mhóra romhat féin agus roimh ár nAontas, ach táim cinnte go bhfuil an taithí agus na scileanna agat iad a shárú. Agus go n-éirí an bóthar leat, a Thaoisigh.

Taoiseach, your presidency comes at a pivotal moment for the European Union. All of us must decide if we want to take our Union to the next level of development. To do so will require all of us – including our country, Ireland – to make some of our red lines a little less red. The EU isn't perfect compromise, but nothing today has come close to it being as successful in improving the lives of our citizens.

We must get real when it comes to the budget and that means being honest about the level of funding needed to sustain a dynamic, progressive and ambitious Union. We must get real about the threats facing us and invest in our defences. And finally, we must get real about our values and never again can we let a tinpot autocrat hold our Union to ransom.

Taoiseach, I know you care passionately about the European Union and I firmly believe that you will be the right person at the right time to meet these challenges head on. You have my full support and the support of the Renew Europe family in the European Parliament.

2-0111-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, fáilte romhat, a Mhichíl. Fáilte romhat, a Thomáis.

Madam President, when I got elected to the European Parliament, I got elected as a sceptic. I got elected because I was told by the Irish Government continuously when they weren't happy with the EU enforcing rules, that they were made to do it. I have discovered otherwise.

And since I got elected here, I have to say I believe the common agricultural policy is the most important policy of the European Union. In my county alone, a county of 80 000 people, EUR 1 billion in CAP payments has come to Roscommon since I was elected in 2014. Over the same period, in the future, if we stick with current budgetary proposals on the MFF, we would see a reduction in payments of EUR 200 million just to Roscommon, excluding inflation.

All the more reason then that we get this right when deciding who gets this money. In the Commission proposal, the text refers to those most in need. To me, the most in need are those that farm marginal lands on smallholdings and those on designated lands. We also need to respect those pluriactive farmers who, while not making a full-time living out of farming, are nonetheless contributing in a significant way to food sovereignty and the provision of public goods – the latter of which has never been properly remunerated for.

The proposals on fisheries are even worse: from 6 billion to 2 billion. As with agri funding, this means it has now been never more important that small-scale, low impact fishers are given this money. The money must be provided in a way that fishers can actually access it. As things stands, that is not the case.

Finally, in relation to defective concrete, when are you going to get your act together? Infringement proceedings remain open. They do so in spite of the fact that thousands of people's lives have been blighted by crumbling houses. The danger of this issue repeating itself remains very real. The European Parliament has backed this. You now need to do something about it. People deserve dignity. They don't have it.

2-0119-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, is éacht pearsanta duit an lá seo, a Thaoisigh. Guím gach ádh ort agus go n-éirí leat.

The success of the Irish Presidency will be built on long hours by countless Irish civil servants far from today's limelight and that of recent days, and I think we should remember their work and wish them success as well in their important tasks.

As we assume leadership of the EU budget, we must lead by example. Try to do more with less, not less with more. We need to invest in our beleaguered defence forces, but that does not mean abandoning the proud role of neutral, non-aligned states, and our place among them.

Instead, we're spending EUR 293 million on this presidency. It's far too much, Taoiseach. Pull back on it, it's not necessary. Included in that is EUR 135 000 for wool scarves to be of uniquely Irish artistic character, but not necessarily Irish wool. It's 30 degrees outside, Taoiseach. When it does cool down, everybody around here is well capable of buying their own scarves.

A Uachtaráin, a Thaoisigh, a Aire, tá fáilte romhaibh.

Colleagues, our former Taoiseach Garret Fitzgerald said that joining Europe completed Ireland's journey to independence and history has proven him to be so right. Every generation inherits moments that define the nation and for Ireland, one of those moments was in 1973, and Ireland chose Europe. And it was a choice about the kind of country that we wanted to become: open to the world, confident and engaged and at the table instead of on the sidelines.

As we begin our eighth presidency of the Council of the European Union, the challenges that we face today are very different, but we will not be found wanting. We will give more options to build long-term financial security for the people and their families. We must find solutions for businesses struggling to grow, our young people options to buy homes and really importantly, protect our children online. And vitally, we will stand by Ukraine and the defence of Europe, even if that means having to make difficult decisions when they're not the easiest at home.

Yes, we're a small island on the western edge of Europe but, by God, we have the power and determination to help build a stronger and brighter future for...

(The President cut off the speaker)

A Uachtaráin, a Thaoisigh, is maith an scáthán súil carad.

'A friend's eye is a good mirror'. My eyes see a country a little too fond of selling aluminium to Russia and tax benefits to American tech. But I also see a country committed to peace, the best live music in Europe and a beacon of democracy. 2-0149-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Ich beziehe mich auf Artikel 187. Gemäß dieser Regel sollte es den Abgeordneten möglich sein, Änderungsanträge zu diesem Beschluss einzubringen, doch dazu geben Sie uns heute keine Gelegenheit.

Deshalb bleibt mir nur eines zu sagen: Unser AfD‑Parteitag am Wochenende konnte nur unter einem massiven Polizeiaufgebot stattfinden. Gewalttätige Linksextremisten hatten öffentlich dazu aufgerufen, ihn zu verhindern. Den Mitgliedern der EVP und von Renew – also CDU, CSU und FDP – wurde offen mit Gewalt gedroht, falls sie mit uns zusammenarbeiten. Dass dies keine leeren Worte sind, haben sie erlebt. Nach den gemeinsamen Abstimmungen im Bundestag und im vergangenen Januar wurden ihre CDU‑Wahlkreisbüros angegriffen. Nach der Wahl von Thomas Kemmerich in Thüringen brauchten seine Frau und seine Kinder Polizeischutz.

Nichts dergleichen ging jemals von uns aus, was aus linksextremen Strukturen hervorgeht. Nicht wir müssen uns rechtfertigen, sondern diejenigen, denen die Argumente ausgegangen sind und die deshalb zu Gewalt …

(Die Präsidentin entzieht dem Redner das Wort.)
2-0149-0000.englishText:
Madam President! I refer to Article 187. According to this rule, Members should be able to table amendments to this decision, but you are not giving us the opportunity to do so today.

That's why I only have one thing to say: Our AfD party conference at the weekend could only take place with a massive police presence. Violent left-wing extremists had publicly called for it to be prevented. The members of the EPP and Renew – i.e. CDU, CSU and FDP – were openly threatened with violence if they worked with us. They have experienced that these are not empty words. After the joint votes in the Bundestag and last January, their CDU constituency offices were attacked. After Thomas Kemmerich was elected in Thuringia, his wife and children needed police protection.

Nothing like this has ever come from us that comes from left-wing extremist structures. It is not us who have to justify ourselves, but rather those who have run out of arguments and therefore resort to violence...

(The President cuts off the speaker.)

2-0190-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, la señora Nadia Calviño, exministra de Sánchez y ahora a la cabeza del Banco Europeo de Inversiones, anunció en redes sociales la asignación de 365 millones EUR para carreteras y ferrocarriles de Marruecos.

Por eso, nosotros creemos importante incluir la siguiente enmienda: Lamenta la asignación por parte del Banco Europeo de Inversiones de 365 millones EUR para reforzar la resiliencia y la seguridad de las redes viarias y ferroviarias de Marruecos, tal y como anunció la presidenta del Banco, Nadia Calviño, el 30 de junio de 2026.

Recuerda que estos recursos financieros deberían destinarse prioritariamente a mejorar las infraestructuras de transporte dentro de la Unión, especialmente a la luz de los graves accidentes ferroviarios ocurridos en los últimos años, que han puesto de manifiesto las deficiencias en el mantenimiento y la modernización de las infraestructuras de transporte en varios Estados miembros.

Considera que dicha financiación no se ajusta a la misión principal del Banco, establecida en el artículo 309 del Tratado de Funcionamiento, consistente en contribuir al desarrollo equilibrado y constante del mercado interior en interés de la Unión.
2-0190-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mrs. Nadia Calviño, Sánchez's former minister and now head of the European Investment Bank, announced on social media the allocation of €365 million for roads and railways in Morocco.

For this reason, we believe it is important to include the following amendment: Regrets the allocation by the European Investment Bank of EUR 365 million to strengthen the resilience and safety of Morocco's road and rail networks, as announced by the President of the Bank, Nadia Calviño, on June 30, 2026.

Recalls that these financial resources should be allocated as a priority to improving transport infrastructure within the Union, especially in light of the serious railway accidents that have occurred in recent years, which have highlighted deficiencies in the maintenance and modernization of transport infrastructure in several Member States.

Considers that such financing does not comply with the main mission of the Bank, established in Article 309 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the Bank, which consists of contributing to the balanced and constant development of the internal market in the interest of the Union.

2-0203-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, durante mucho tiempo vimos la expansión de internet y de las redes sociales con optimismo. Pensábamos que la información circularía libre y que la conversación pública sería más abierta. Sin embargo, el espacio digital que nos atraviesa por completo ha cambiado radicalmente y ese optimismo se ha nublado. La concentración de poder en pocas manos, la opacidad y un modelo de negocio basado en la adicción permanente ha transformado profundamente ese ecosistema. La desinformación circula con facilidad, los contenidos manipulados se multiplican y la inteligencia artificial ha acelerado y multiplicado este efecto.

Conocer cómo funciona este nuevo mundo debe ser hoy una prioridad democrática. Hace décadas, entendimos que no existía la ciudadanía plena sin saber leer y escribir. Hoy, nos ocurre algo parecido: en la era digital, nadie puede ejercer plenamente sus derechos si no distingue la realidad de la desinformación, si no reconoce una manipulación generada por inteligencia artificial o si no entiende cómo funcionan los algoritmos. Y si nuestra ciudadanía no tiene esas herramientas, nuestras democracias no están preparadas para esta nueva era digital.

Señorías, ningún Estado miembro puede afrontar este desafío por sí solo. Por eso, hoy votamos implementar una nueva estrategia de alfabetización mediática y de aprendizaje digital para toda Europa. Una estrategia que reconozca competencias como básicas y esenciales para toda la ciudadanía, a cualquier edad y a lo largo de toda la vida, especialmente para niños, niñas y adolescentes. Servirá para su protección frente al acoso, los contenidos inapropiados y el diseño adictivo, también para nuestros mayores y el conjunto de la ciudadanía, porque nadie puede ser libre en un entorno digital que no entiende.

La alfabetización mediática y digital es una necesidad democrática y hoy enviamos un mensaje claro. Gracias por su voto.
2-0203-0000.englishText:
Madam President, for a long time we viewed the expansion of the internet and social networks with optimism. We thought that information would circulate freely and that public conversation would be more open. However, the digital space that completely crosses us has changed radically and that optimism has been clouded. The concentration of power in a few hands, opacity and a business model based on permanent addiction has profoundly transformed that ecosystem. Misinformation circulates easily, manipulated content multiplies and artificial intelligence has accelerated and multiplied this effect.

Knowing how this new world works must be a democratic priority today. Decades ago, we understood that there was no such thing as full citizenship without knowing how to read and write. Today, something similar happens to us: in the digital age, no one can fully exercise their rights if they do not distinguish reality from misinformation, if they do not recognize manipulation generated by artificial intelligence or if they do not understand how algorithms work. And if our citizens do not have these tools, our democracies are not prepared for this new digital age.

Ladies and gentlemen, no Member State can meet this challenge alone. That is why today we voted to implement a new media literacy and digital learning strategy for all of Europe. A strategy that recognizes competencies as basic and essential for all citizens, at any age and throughout life, especially for boys, girls and adolescents. It will serve to protect them against harassment, inappropriate content and addictive design, also for our elders and the general public, because no one can be free in a digital environment that they do not understand.

Media and digital literacy is a democratic necessity and today we send a clear message. Thank you for your vote.

2-0218-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, no hay debate únicamente sobre un acuerdo comercial.

Hoy decidimos qué lugar quiere ocupar Europa en un mundo cada vez más dominado por la confrontación, el proteccionismo y las políticas de poder. Tras más de una década de negociaciones, la Unión Europea y México culminan una decisión geopolítica de primer orden: modernizar nuestro Acuerdo Global.

Este Acuerdo es mucho más que la eliminación de aranceles o la apertura de mercados. Es una respuesta política a quienes creen que el siglo XXI debe organizarse mediante amenazas, guerras comerciales, coerción económica o zonas de influencia.

Nosotros defendemos otra lógica con este Acuerdo Global: defendemos reglas frente a fuerza, cooperación frente a la confrontación, y Derecho internacional frente al unilateralismo. En un momento en el que algunos levantan muros, utilizan aranceles como armas y cuestionan décadas de construcción multilateral, Europa y México envían un mensaje distinto al mundo: más cooperación, más instituciones, más Derecho internacional y más comercio predecible con altos estándares medioambientales, sociales y laborales.

La alternativa al multilateralismo no es más soberanía, es la ley de la selva. En este contexto, Europa necesita socios fiables, socios democráticos, socios capaces de aportar estabilidad institucional, capacidad industrial, seguridad jurídica y compromiso con un orden internacional basado en normas.

Hay pocos en el mundo que combinan todos estos elementos como lo hace México. México es una potencia económica, industrial, tecnológica y diplomática de primerísimo orden. Es un miembro del G20 y uno de los socios estratégicos más importantes de la Unión Europea. Pero no solo eso: es una sociedad con una fuerte identidad propia, profunda y milenaria; una nación heredera de hondas raíces culturales ricas, diversas y vibrantes.

México es un país que ha sabido convertir su diversidad, mestizaje y pluralidad en una fuente de fortaleza nacional. Europa no mira a México únicamente como un mercado. Europa mira a México con respeto, nunca desde el reduccionismo, el paternalismo o la ignorancia, porque compartimos principios esenciales: la defensa de la Carta de las Naciones Unidas o el compromiso con la soberanía de los Estados. Compartimos la convicción de que ninguna potencia tiene derecho a imponer su voluntad sobre otros mediante la coerción económica o la fuerza. Compartimos la certeza de que los grandes desafíos a los que nos enfrentamos —la lucha contra las desigualdades, el cambio climático o la transición energética o digital— deben hacerse mediante cooperación, no haciendo de menos o mediante la confrontación.

Quiero destacar hoy aquí que la determinación de la presidenta Von der Leyen y del presidente Costa nos ha permitido llegar hasta aquí. También nos lo ha permitido la decisión estratégica de la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, por su liderazgo sereno, tranquilo y firme en la escena internacional.

Abrimos una nueva etapa de oportunidades compartidas para una prosperidad compartida.

Hoy que hablamos de las relaciones entre la Unión Europea y México, quiero recalcar que cuando Europa atravesó momentos oscuros durante el siglo XX, México abrió sus puertas a quienes huían de la guerra y de la persecución política; ofreció refugio, dignidad y esperanza. Y algunos —especialmente en España, por la acogida del exilio republicano español— tenemos un sentimiento de deber y gratitud con México que permanece.

Por eso, hoy hacemos algo más que aprobar un Acuerdo. Defendemos una idea del mundo. La idea de que la cooperación es más poderosa que el conflicto, de que las reglas son preferibles a la arbitrariedad, de que la apertura es más inteligente que el repliegue, y de que frente al nacionalismo económico, el proteccionismo y la política del poder, Europa debe responder construyendo alianzas con quienes creen en la democracia, el Derecho internacional y el multilateralismo.

Con este Acuerdo se trata de defender una idea del orden internacional, un orden basado en normas y no en amenazas, en cooperación y no en coerción, en relaciones entre socios y no vasallos. Ese es el verdadero significado de este Acuerdo. Y por eso hay que respaldarlo con convicción.
2-0218-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, there is no debate solely about a trade agreement.

Today we decide what place Europe wants to occupy in a world increasingly dominated by confrontation, protectionism and power politics. After more than a decade of negotiations, the European Union and Mexico have completed a major geopolitical decision: modernizing our Global Agreement.

This Agreement is much more than the elimination of tariffs or the opening of markets. It is a political response to those who believe that the 21st century should be organized through threats, trade wars, economic coercion or zones of influence.

We defend another logic with this Global Agreement: we defend rules against force, cooperation against confrontation, and international law against unilateralism. At a time when some are building walls, using tariffs as weapons and questioning decades of multilateral construction, Europe and Mexico send a different message to the world: more cooperation, more institutions, more international law and more predictable trade with high environmental, social and labor standards.

The alternative to multilateralism is not more sovereignty, it is the law of the jungle. In this context, Europe needs reliable partners, democratic partners, partners capable of providing institutional stability, industrial capacity, legal certainty and commitment to a rules-based international order.

There are few in the world that combine all these elements like Mexico does. Mexico is an economic, industrial, technological and diplomatic power of the highest order. It is a member of the G20 and one of the most important strategic partners of the European Union. But not only that: it is a society with a strong, deep and ancient identity; a nation heir to deep, rich, diverse and vibrant cultural roots.

Mexico is a country that has managed to convert its diversity, miscegenation and plurality into a source of national strength. Europe does not see Mexico only as a market. Europe looks at Mexico with respect, never from reductionism, paternalism or ignorance, because we share essential principles: the defense of the Charter of the United Nations or the commitment to the sovereignty of the States. We share the conviction that no power has the right to impose its will on others through economic coercion or force. We share the certainty that the great challenges we face – the fight against inequalities, climate change or the energy or digital transition – must be done through cooperation, not by ignoring or through confrontation.

I want to highlight here today that the determination of President Von der Leyen and President Costa has allowed us to get here. The strategic decision of President Claudia Sheinbaum has also allowed us to do so, due to her serene, calm and firm leadership on the international scene.

We open a new era of shared opportunities for shared prosperity.

Today, as we talk about relations between the European Union and Mexico, I want to emphasize that when Europe went through dark times during the 20th century, Mexico opened its doors to those fleeing war and political persecution; It offered refuge, dignity and hope. And some of us—especially in Spain, due to the reception of the Spanish republican exile—have a feeling of duty and gratitude towards Mexico that remains.

Therefore, today we do more than approve an Agreement. We defend an idea of ​​the world. The idea that cooperation is more powerful than conflict, that rules are preferable to arbitrariness, that openness is smarter than withdrawal, and that in the face of economic nationalism, protectionism and power politics, Europe must respond by building alliances with those who believe in democracy, international law and multilateralism.

This Agreement is about defending an idea of ​​international order, an order based on rules and not threats, on cooperation and not coercion, on relations between partners and not vassals. That is the true meaning of this Agreement. And that is why it must be supported with conviction.

2-0219-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, el Acuerdo Global con México va a ser una realidad. Es un punto de inflexión en una realidad que comenzó hace 25 años. Desde entonces, el comercio ha crecido un 148 %. Hoy supera los 82 000 millones de euros. No es una cifra abstracta: es industria, es empresa, es inversión, es competitividad, pero el mundo cambia rápido. Estamos en un contexto de fragmentación global, con tensiones comerciales, con amenazas recurrentes de nuevos aranceles. Europa no se puede quedar atrás. Necesitamos diversificar, más socios, más autonomía estratégica. Cuanto más comercio, más libre es la Unión. 25 años después de la modernización de nuestras relaciones comerciales, esta es más necesaria que nunca.

Los beneficios económicos son claros. La Unión y México suman más de 580 millones de consumidores. Es un mercado enorme. Las exportaciones europeas pueden crecer hasta un 75 %. Más de 45 000 empresas europeas se beneficiarán —la mayoría de ellas pymes— y el PIB de la Unión Europea puede aumentar en 1 800 millones de euros solo por la firma del Acuerdo. También es una buena noticia para nuestro sector agroalimentario. No debemos tener miedo: sectores como el porcino o el queso ganan, se eliminan aranceles y se protegen 568 indicaciones geográficas.

Además, es el primer acuerdo que incorpora una cláusula anticorrupción. Esto es clave si queremos inversiones transparentes y seguridad jurídica. Es también fundamental la incorporación de un sistema de tribunales de inversión permanente.

México y la Unión Europea comparten mucho: siglos de historia. Una historia compleja, profunda, que ha dado lugar a vínculos humanos, tradiciones, cultura, lengua. Todo ello forma parte de nuestra identidad.

Hoy decidimos sellar un destino común; hoy damos un paso más en nuestra relación. Este Acuerdo se basa en la confianza —confianza mutua— entre dos pueblos amigos que se aprecian y se respetan. Una relación así exige honestidad, la misma que entre buenos amigos. Y esa honestidad exige sinceridad, que nos hablemos claro, de lo que nos gusta y lo que no nos gusta tanto. Y hay cuestiones que nos preocupan, de forma sincera. La reforma del sistema judicial: la elección popular de todos los jueces genera serias dudas, debilita la separación de poderes. Sin estabilidad institucional no hay confianza, sin confianza no hay crecimiento. Nos preocupa la seguridad: 90 homicidios al día, impunidad del 94 %, el país con más periodistas asesinados, un crimen organizado que sabemos que ha permeado la sociedad y la economía. No podemos mirar hacia otro lado, fundamentalmente porque es un enorme drama humano, pero también económico. Y lamentamos profundamente, desde una perspectiva comercial, que el capítulo energético haya quedado fuera del Acuerdo. Esto va a dar lugar a vacíos regulatorios y desincentiva la inversión. Confiamos en que esta cuestión se pueda resolver pronto.

Somos amigos, somos socios y este Acuerdo sienta las bases para reafirmar nuestra relación. Una relación comercial ambiciosa, una relación política profunda, pero también una relación basada en el Estado de Derecho, en la independencia judicial, en la seguridad jurídica y en el respeto de los valores democráticos. Porque el comercio prospera cuando existen instituciones fuertes. La inversión llega cuando hay confianza.

Señorías, digamos sí a un Acuerdo fundamental para Europa: reforcemos nuestra posición global, mejoremos la competitividad, ampliemos alianzas. Cuanto más comercio, más libre será la Unión.
2-0219-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, the Global Agreement with Mexico is going to be a reality. It is a turning point in a reality that began 25 years ago. Since then, trade has grown by 148%. Today it exceeds 82 billion euros. It is not an abstract figure: it is an industry, it is a company, it is investment, it is competitiveness, but the world changes quickly. We are in a context of global fragmentation, with trade tensions, with recurring threats of new tariffs. Europe cannot be left behind. We need to diversify, more partners, more strategic autonomy. The more trade, the freer the Union. 25 years after the modernization of our commercial relations, this is more necessary than ever.

The economic benefits are clear. La Unión and Mexico have more than 580 million consumers. It is a huge market. European exports can grow by up to 75%. More than 45,000 European companies will benefit – most of them SMEs – and the GDP of the European Union can increase by €1.8 billion just from signing the Agreement. It is also good news for our agri-food sector. We should not be afraid: sectors such as pork or cheese win, tariffs are eliminated and 568 geographical indications are protected.

In addition, it is the first agreement that incorporates an anti-corruption clause. This is key if we want transparent investments and legal security. The incorporation of a system of permanent investment courts is also essential.

Mexico and the European Union share a lot: centuries of history. A complex, deep history that has given rise to human ties, traditions, culture, language. All of this is part of our identity.

Today we decided to seal a common destiny; Today we take another step in our relationship. This Agreement is based on trust – mutual trust – between two friendly peoples who appreciate and respect each other. A relationship like this requires honesty, the same as between good friends. And that honesty requires sincerity, that we speak clearly to each other, about what we like and what we don't like so much. And there are issues that concern us, honestly. The reform of the judicial system: the popular election of all judges raises serious doubts, weakens the separation of powers. Without institutional stability there is no trust, without trust there is no growth. We are concerned about security: 90 homicides a day, 94% impunity, the country with the most murdered journalists, an organized crime that we know has permeated society and the economy. We cannot look the other way, fundamentally because it is an enormous human drama, but also an economic one. And we deeply regret, from a commercial perspective, that the energy chapter has been left out of the Agreement. This will lead to regulatory gaps and discourage investment. We trust that this issue can be resolved soon.

We are friends, we are partners and this Agreement lays the foundations to reaffirm our relationship. An ambitious commercial relationship, a deep political relationship, but also a relationship based on the rule of law, judicial independence, legal certainty and respect for democratic values. Because commerce thrives when strong institutions exist. Investment comes when there is trust.

Ladies and gentlemen, let's say yes to a fundamental Agreement for Europe: let's strengthen our global position, improve competitiveness, expand alliances. The more trade, the freer the Union will be.

2-0221-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, o Acordo União Europeia-México é muito mais do que um acordo comercial. É uma escolha estratégica.

O México é o segundo maior parceiro comercial da União Europeia na América Latina. Mais de 45 000 empresas europeias exportam para o México, muitas delas pequenas e médias empresas que beneficiarão de regras mais claras, maior previsibilidade e novas oportunidades de investimento.

Num mundo cada vez mais fragmentado, esta parceria é essencial para uma relação transatlântica alargada, assente em interesses comuns e valores partilhados. Mas, precisamente porque este acordo é estratégico, este Parlamento não separa o seu avanço da realidade política e institucional no terreno.

O México enfrenta desafios profundos: violência do crime organizado, desaparecimentos, ataques e assassinatos de jornalistas, corrupção, pressões sobre a independência judicial e dificuldades no normal funcionamento das instituições democráticas. Estes desafios não são externos ao acordo, são parte das condições que determinam se o acordo será credível, eficaz e sustentável.

Não há verdadeira previsibilidade económica e confiança para as empresas sem instituições sólidas. Este Parlamento reconhece e apoia o acordo, mas exige compromissos claros e verificáveis em matéria de Estado de direito.

A União Europeia ganha ao reforçar a sua presença junto de um parceiro-chave na América Latina. Ganha peso, ganha influência. Mas perderia autoridade moral e coerência política se reforçasse esta parceria, fingindo não ver as fragilidades institucionais que persistem, porque quanto mais estratégica é uma parceria, maior deve ser a nossa exigência democrática.
2-0221-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the European Union-Mexico Agreement is much more than a trade agreement. It's a strategic choice.

Mexico is the European Union's second largest trading partner in Latin America. More than 45,000 European companies export to Mexico, many of them small and medium-sized companies that will benefit from clearer rules, greater predictability and new investment opportunities.

In an increasingly fragmented world, this partnership is essential for a broad transatlantic relationship, based on common interests and shared values. But, precisely because this agreement is strategic, this Parliament does not separate its progress from the political and institutional reality on the ground.

Mexico faces profound challenges: organized crime violence, disappearances, attacks and murders of journalists, corruption, pressure on judicial independence and difficulties in the normal functioning of democratic institutions. These challenges are not external to the agreement, they are part of the conditions that determine whether the agreement will be credible, effective and sustainable.

There is no true economic predictability and confidence for businesses without strong institutions. This Parliament recognizes and supports the agreement, but demands clear and verifiable commitments on the rule of law.

The European Union benefits from strengthening its presence with a key partner in Latin America. Gain weight, gain influence. But I would lose moral authority and political coherence if I strengthened this partnership, pretending not to see the institutional weaknesses that persist, because the more strategic a partnership is, the greater our democratic demands must be.

2-0222-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, este Parlamento está a punto de dar su consentimiento a un Acuerdo que ha tardado casi diez años en negociarse. Un Acuerdo que llega en un momento en el que el comercio global ya no puede entenderse únicamente en términos económicos.

Hoy, la Unión Europea es más consciente que nunca de que la política comercial es un pilar fundamental para nuestra seguridad económica y nuestra autonomía estratégica. Somos conscientes de la necesidad de diversificar nuestras relaciones comerciales y fortalecer alianzas con socios que comparten nuestro compromiso con el multilateralismo y con un comercio global basado en normas.

México es, sin duda, uno de los mejores ejemplos de esa clase de aliados estratégicos. Por eso, la firma del Acuerdo Global Modernizado entre la Unión Europea y México es una grandísima noticia que este Parlamento tiene que acompañar. Es un paso decisivo para adaptar nuestros lazos comerciales a las realidades del siglo XX. Y lo es porque elimina casi la totalidad de los aranceles que teníamos hasta ahora y porque actualiza los mecanismos de protección de inversiones al dar más certidumbre a operadores europeos y mexicanos.

Estos son elementos clave que facilitarán las operaciones de las más de 45 000 empresas europeas —muchas de ellas pymes— que exportan a México.

También se trata de un Acuerdo relevante para el acceso a minerales críticos como la fluorita o el cobre, un ámbito donde tenemos que asegurar que no se repitan las dinámicas extractivistas del pasado.

Pero lo importante de este Acuerdo no solo está en lo técnico. El nuevo marco incluye obligaciones vinculantes en materia ambiental, laboral y social. El Acuerdo garantiza el respeto al Acuerdo de París y, además, México ratifica nuevas convenciones de la Organización Internacional del Trabajo, un compromiso que tiene que incluirse como parte esencial del Acuerdo durante la próxima revisión.

En este camino, este Acuerdo tiene que ser un instrumento que contribuya a guiar la inversión hacia sectores de alto valor añadido en México, que diversifique la inversión europea en el país y que logre beneficiar a aquellos que tantas veces quedan atrás, que se convierta en un marco en el que la voz de la sociedad civil y las comunidades indígenas mexicanas sea escuchada y que asegure que sus prioridades no quedan de lado.

En definitiva, dando luz a este Acuerdo, el Parlamento Europeo deja claro que Europa apuesta por la cooperación con socios tan relevantes como México de la mano y sin paternalismos.

Es importante que desde este Parlamento se proyecte determinación en la cooperación con liderazgo, con una Europa que no debe quedarse atrás, que apuesta por su autonomía estratégica, y en un contexto en el que otros levantan barreras.
2-0222-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Mr Commissioner, this Parliament is about to give its consent to an Agreement that has taken almost ten years to negotiate. An Agreement that comes at a time when global trade can no longer be understood solely in economic terms.

Today, the European Union is more aware than ever that trade policy is a fundamental pillar for our economic security and our strategic autonomy. We are aware of the need to diversify our trade relationships and strengthen alliances with partners who share our commitment to multilateralism and rules-based global trade.

Mexico is, without a doubt, one of the best examples of this type of strategic allies. For this reason, the signing of the Modernized Global Agreement between the European Union and Mexico is great news that this Parliament must support. It is a decisive step to adapt our commercial ties to the realities of the 20th century. And it is because it eliminates almost all of the tariffs that we had until now and because it updates the investment protection mechanisms by giving more certainty to European and Mexican operators.

These are key elements that will facilitate the operations of the more than 45,000 European companies – many of them SMEs – that export to Mexico.

It is also a relevant Agreement for access to critical minerals such as fluorite or copper, an area where we have to ensure that the extractivist dynamics of the past are not repeated.

But the importance of this Agreement is not only technical. The new framework includes binding obligations on environmental, labor and social matters. The Agreement guarantees respect for the Paris Agreement and, in addition, Mexico ratifies new conventions of the International Labor Organization, a commitment that must be included as an essential part of the Agreement during the next review.

Along this path, this Agreement must be an instrument that helps guide investment towards sectors of high added value in Mexico, that diversifies European investment in the country and that manages to benefit those who are so often left behind, that becomes a framework in which the voice of civil society and Mexican indigenous communities is heard and that ensures that their priorities are not left aside.

In short, by giving light to this Agreement, the European Parliament makes it clear that Europe is committed to cooperation with partners as relevant as Mexico hand in hand and without paternalism.

It is important that this Parliament projects determination in cooperation with leadership, with a Europe that should not be left behind, that is committed to its strategic autonomy, and in a context in which others raise barriers.

2-0223-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'accordo che voteremo è vincente perché aiuterà Europa e Messico.

Si rafforza la cooperazione politica e commerciale con un paese amico, vicino ai nostri valori e alla nostra cultura.
