Diversi sono gli elementi positivi. In primo luogo, permetterà di rafforzare la cooperazione per la transizione verde e digitale. L'accordo, inoltre, offrirà un migliore accesso agli appalti pubblici messicani e nuove opportunità in settori strategici, come quello finanziario, digitale, dei trasporti e delle materie critiche.

Infine, i vantaggi per l'agricoltura europea. Il Messico è un importante importatore netto di prodotti alimentari: con il nuovo accordo, il Messico proteggerà 232 bevande spiritose e altre 336 indicazioni geografiche europee tra cui vino, birra e alimentari.

Questo aspetto è fondamentale anche per l'agricoltura italiana, perché difende realmente il made in Europe.
2-0223-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, the agreement we will vote on is a winner because it will help Europe and Mexico.

Political and commercial cooperation is strengthened with a friendly country, close to our values ​​and our culture.

There are several positive elements. Firstly, it will allow us to strengthen cooperation for the green and digital transition. The agreement will also offer better access to Mexican public procurement and new opportunities in strategic sectors, such as finance, digital, transport and critical materials.

Finally, the advantages for European agriculture. Mexico is a major net importer of food products: with the new agreement, Mexico will protect 232 spirit drinks and another 336 European geographical indications including wine, beer and food.

This aspect is also fundamental for Italian agriculture, because it truly defends what is made in Europe.

2-0224-0000.sourceText:
Austatud istungi juhataja! Head kolleegid! Saja kolmekümne kolme miljoni elanikuga Mehhiko on Euroopa Liidu strateegiline partner ja suuruselt teine kaubanduspartner Ladina-Ameerikas. Seega on Euroopa Liidu ja Mehhiko suhted juba seni olnud väga olulised. Samas on veelgi kasutamata potentsiaali. Seetõttu on ka parlamendi ees olevate Euroopa Liidu ja Mehhiko suhteid süvendavate lepete heakskiitmine tähtis nii meie kahepoolsetes suhetes kui ka globaalselt. Arvestades, et rahvusvaheline õigusruum on tugeva surve all, siis on rahvusvahelisel õigusel põhinev ja seda tugevdav uus kokkulepe väga vajalik ja selles on Euroopa Liidul oluline roll kanda. Riikidevahelisi suhteid ei tohi määrata mõne režiimi ühepoolne jõupoliitika, vaid rahvusvahelisel õigusel põhinevad kokkulepped. Teie ees olevad lepped loovad täiendavaid võimalusi Euroopa ettevõtetele ja majandusele tervikuna. Tollipiirangud ja tariifid vähenevad veelgi ning turud avanevad vastastikku rohkem. Euroopa Liidu ettevõtetel tekib märksa parem ligipääs Mehhiko turule.

Meie suhetes on oluline tähelepanu ka inimõiguste ja õigusriigi põhimõtete järgimisel. Nii on ette nähtud Euroopa Liidu ja Mehhiko dialoog ajakirjanike ja inimõiguste kaitsjate turvalisuse parandamiseks. Kavas on ühised tegevused korruptsiooni, rahapesu ja organiseeritud kuritegevusega võitlemiseks. On ka äärmiselt oluline, et Euroopa Liit on aktiivne ja jätkab sellelaadsete lepingute sõlmimist ka teiste meile potentsiaalselt lähedaste riikidega, et suurendada Euroopa Liidu positiivset mõju maailma arengutes.
2-0224-0000.englishText:
Dear chairman of the session! Dear colleagues! With a population of one hundred and thirty-three million, Mexico is a strategic partner of the European Union and the second largest trading partner in Latin America. Thus, the relations between the European Union and Mexico have been very important so far. However, there is still more untapped potential. Therefore, the approval of the agreements before the Parliament that deepen the relations between the European Union and Mexico is important both in our bilateral relations and globally. Considering that the international legal space is under strong pressure, a new agreement based on and strengthening international law is very necessary, and the European Union has an important role to play in this. Relations between countries must not be determined by the unilateral force policy of some regime, but by agreements based on international law. The agreements before you will create further opportunities for European companies and the economy as a whole. Customs restrictions and tariffs will be further reduced and markets will open more mutually. European Union companies will have much better access to the Mexican market.

In our relations, it is also important to pay attention to the observance of human rights and the principles of the rule of law. This is how the dialogue between the European Union and Mexico is intended to improve the safety of journalists and human rights defenders. Joint actions to fight corruption, money laundering and organized crime are planned. It is also extremely important that the European Union is active and continues to conclude such agreements with other potentially close countries in order to increase the positive influence of the European Union in world developments.

2-0225-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Morgen stimmen wir über die Modernisierung des Mexiko‑Handelsabkommens ab. Ich werde zustimmen, aber habe trotzdem Kritik am Abkommen.

Ja, in einer Welt, in der Donald Trump im Weißen Haus eine erratische Handelspolitik betreibt und China mit unfairen Regeln spielt, brauchen wir Partner. Und ja, Mexiko unter Präsidentin Sheinbaum ist eine solche verlässliche Partnerin – eine Regierung, die für Multilateralismus, Demokratie, soziale Gerechtigkeit und entschlossenen Klimaschutz eintritt, Werte, die momentan wichtiger sind denn je.

Ich begrüße ausdrücklich die engere Kooperation mit Mexiko. Ich befürworte auch die Verbesserungen, die die Modernisierung in den Bereichen Nachhaltigkeit, Korruptionsbekämpfung, Gender usw. mit sich bringt.

Aber zur Wahrheit gehört auch, dass dieses Abkommen weit weg von einem perfekten Abkommen ist. Es gibt kein einklagbares Nachhaltigkeitskapitel wie mit Neuseeland, was Klima-, Umwelt- und Arbeitsstandards am Ende leider zahnlos macht.

Und noch schlimmer: Dieses Abkommen erfüllt beim Investitionsschutz nicht die Forderungen dieses Parlaments. Die veralteten Klauseln verleihen Investoren unverhältnismäßig große Macht und die Möglichkeit, vor internationalen Schiedsgerichten gegen jegliche demokratische Entscheidung vorzugehen, sei es im Klimaschutz oder auch die Versorgung von Medikamenten, bei allen möglichen Themen. Es gibt so krasse Fälle, wo Investoren Staaten verklagen, und ich verstehe nicht, dass die Europäische Union diesen Mechanismus immer noch weiter perpetuiert.

Mitten in der Klimakrise, nachdem eine Hitzewelle in Europa gerade tausenden Menschen das Leben gekostet hat, schafft es die Kommission immer noch nicht, Handelspolitik und Klimaschutz zusammenzudenken. Das muss sich endlich ändern!

Ich erwarte, dass die Kommission bei dem Überprüfungsmechanismus, der bereits in einem Jahr ansteht, diese Zeit nutzt, um endlich Umwelt-, Arbeits- und Klimarechte zu stärken und den Investitionsschutz endlich an unsere demokratischen Werte anzupassen.
2-0225-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues! Tomorrow we will vote on modernizing the Mexico trade agreement. I will agree, but I still have criticisms of the agreement.

Yes, in a world where Donald Trump in the White House pursues erratic trade policies and China plays with unfair rules, we need partners. And yes, Mexico under President Sheinbaum is one such reliable partner – a government that stands up for multilateralism, democracy, social justice and decisive climate action, values ​​that are more important than ever right now.

I expressly welcome the closer cooperation with Mexico. I also support the improvements that modernization brings in the areas of sustainability, anti-corruption, gender, etc.

But the truth is that this agreement is far from a perfect agreement. There is no enforceable sustainability chapter like there is with New Zealand, which unfortunately ultimately makes climate, environmental and labor standards toothless.

And even worse: this agreement does not meet the demands of this Parliament when it comes to investment protection. The outdated clauses give investors disproportionate power and the opportunity to take action before international arbitration courts against any democratic decision, be it on climate protection or the supply of medicines, on all sorts of issues. There are such blatant cases where investors sue states, and I don't understand why the European Union is still perpetuating this mechanism.

In the middle of the climate crisis, after a heat wave in Europe has just cost the lives of thousands of people, the Commission is still unable to reconcile trade policy and climate protection. That finally has to change!

With the review mechanism, which is already a year away, I expect the Commission to use this time to finally strengthen environmental, labor and climate rights and finally align investment protection with our democratic values.

2-0227-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Sie reden hier viel über die Probleme in anderen Teilen der Welt, nur über die Probleme in Europa sprechen Sie nicht so gerne. Heute geht es um die Partnerschaft mit Mexiko: finden wir grundsätzlich wichtig – wichtiger Handelspartner.

Nur, leider beschränkt sich der Bericht nicht auf die Handelspolitik. EVP und Sozialisten zeigen sich besorgt über den Zustand der Demokratie in Mexiko. Sie ermahnen die Mexikaner, dass es wichtig sei, ein pluralistisches, demokratisches Umfeld zu erhalten, durch eine angemessene öffentliche Finanzierung politischer Parteien. Aber das, was Sie den Amerikanern vorschreiben wollen, lassen Sie für uns Europäer nicht gelten.

Erst vor wenigen Minuten haben Sie hier einen Verbotsantrag gegen unsere Partei beschlossen. Uns wollen Sie die Gelder streichen, den Mexikanern erklären Sie, dass die öffentliche Finanzierung von Parteien notwendig sei, sonst sei die Demokratie in Gefahr. Was für eine Doppelmoral!

Dann freuen Sie sich noch, dass in Mexiko die Armutsquote gesunken ist und die Renten gestiegen sind. Ist ja schön, nur in Deutschland ist es umgekehrt; da steigt die Armutsquote, und das Rentenniveau sinkt. Jeder fünfte Deutsche ist von Armut bedroht, 7 Millionen Rentner bekommen weniger als 1 000 EUR im Monat.

Statt die mexikanische Regierung für ihre Erfolge bei der Armutsbekämpfung zu loben, sollten wir die deutsche Regierung kritisieren, die immer mehr Menschen in Armut stürzt. Und genau das tun wir; deshalb sind wir erfolgreich. Unsere Partei, die Alternative für Deutschland, ist mit weitem Abstand stärkste Kraft in Deutschland. Sie können uns hier unsere Gelder streichen, aber wir werden trotzdem gewinnen, weil wir die Interessen unserer Bürger vertreten und nicht den Rest der Welt belehren wollen.
2-0227-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! You talk a lot here about the problems in other parts of the world, but you don't like to talk so much about the problems in Europe. Today it's about the partnership with Mexico: we think it's fundamentally important - an important trading partner.

Unfortunately, the report is not limited to trade policy. EPP and Socialists are concerned about the state of democracy in Mexico. They urge Mexicans that it is important to maintain a pluralistic, democratic environment through adequate public financing of political parties. But what you want to dictate to the Americans, you do not apply to us Europeans.

Just a few minutes ago you passed a motion to ban our party. You want to cut off our funds, you explain to the Mexicans that public financing of parties is necessary, otherwise democracy is in danger. What a double standard!

Then you'll be happy that the poverty rate in Mexico has fallen and pensions have increased. That's nice, but in Germany it's the other way around; The poverty rate is rising and the pension level is falling. One in five Germans is at risk of poverty, and 7 million pensioners receive less than EUR 1,000 a month.

Instead of praising the Mexican government for its successes in fighting poverty, we should criticize the German government for plunging more and more people into poverty. And that's exactly what we do; that's why we are successful. Our party, the Alternative for Germany, is by far the strongest force in Germany. You can defund us here, but we will still win because we represent the interests of our citizens and do not want to lecture the rest of the world.

2-0229-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, la Unión Europea necesita fortalecer sus alianzas con socios estratégicos. Y México, por supuesto, lo es. No solo por el peso de nuestra relación económica, sino porque compartimos una historia, unos intereses comunes y una responsabilidad de defender un orden internacional basado en normas.

Pero precisamente porque aspiramos a una alianza duradera, no podemos conformarnos con hablar únicamente de comercio. Las alianzas estratégicas no se sostienen solo sobre intercambios económicos, se sostienen sobre valores compartidos. Si queremos que este Acuerdo resista el paso del tiempo, debemos ser capaces de exigirnos mutuamente aquello que ambos hemos decidido defender: seguridad jurídica, Estado de Derecho, instituciones sólidas, independencia judicial, protección de las libertades y pleno respeto a los principios democráticos.

La confianza entre socios no nace del silencio, nace de la sinceridad y de la exigencia recíproca. Y eso es lo que hemos comprobado con México. Los Gobiernos negocian los acuerdos, pero son los Parlamentos quienes dan la legitimidad democrática y quienes garantizan su continuidad cuando cambian las mayorías. Por eso, como presidente de la Comisión Parlamentaria Mixta UE-México, quiero dar las gracias a los dos ponentes —Javi López y Borja Jiménez Larraz— por el magnífico trabajo en los informes, al embajador de México —Rogelio Granguillhome— y al embajador europeo —Francisco André—, porque han ayudado a que también el Parlamento Europeo esté representado por primera vez en una firma de un acuerdo. Muchísimas gracias por ello también a sus jefes en la Comisión y en el Consejo —importante—.
2-0229-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the European Union needs to strengthen its alliances with strategic partners. And Mexico, of course, is. Not only because of the weight of our economic relationship, but because we share a history, common interests and a responsibility to defend an international order based on rules.

But precisely because we aspire to a lasting alliance, we cannot be content to talk only about trade. Strategic alliances are not based only on economic exchanges, they are based on shared values. If we want this Agreement to stand the test of time, we must be able to demand from each other what we have both decided to defend: legal certainty, the rule of law, solid institutions, judicial independence, protection of freedoms and full respect for democratic principles.

Trust between partners is not born from silence, it is born from sincerity and reciprocal demand. And that is what we have verified with Mexico. Governments negotiate agreements, but it is Parliaments that provide democratic legitimacy and guarantee their continuity when majorities change. For this reason, as president of the EU-Mexico Joint Parliamentary Committee, I want to thank the two rapporteurs – Javi López and Borja Jiménez Larraz – for the magnificent work on the reports, the Mexican ambassador – Rogelio Granguillhome – and the European ambassador – Francisco André –, because they have helped ensure that the European Parliament is also represented for the first time at the signing of an agreement. Thank you very much for this also to your bosses in the Commission and in the Council – important.

2-0230-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Global leben wir in wirtschaftlich turbulenten Zeiten; das Wasser ist stürmisch. Und das erlebt Mexiko natürlich auch sehr, sehr stark. Herr Trump hat im letzten Jahr achtmal mit verschiedenen Zolldrohungen und Maßnahmen Mexikos Wirtschaft negativ beeinflusst. Es gab Streit über die Wasserverteilung. Wie kann man das heutzutage machen? Es gab andere Druckmittel, sodass die Wirtschaft in Mexiko stagniert.

Mit dem Abkommen erwarten wir eine deutliche Erholung der Wirtschaft in Mexiko, bis zu 35 %. Das ist, glaube ich, genau das, was wir im Moment brauchen – eine Solidarität in der wirtschaftlichen Beziehung und in der Investitionspolitik, sodass Menschen vor Ort die Perspektive auf ein gutes Leben haben.

Deswegen ist es gut, dass wir dieses Abkommen nach vorne bringen; das ist ein Zeichen der Solidarität von uns mit Mexiko. Let's build bridges over troubled water.
2-0230-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! Globally, we are living in economically turbulent times; the water is stormy. And of course Mexico is experiencing this very, very strongly. Mr. Trump has negatively impacted Mexico's economy eight times in the last year with various tariff threats and measures. There was a dispute over water distribution. How can you do that these days? There were other means of pressure, so the economy in Mexico stagnated.

With the agreement, we expect a significant economic recovery in Mexico, up to 35%. I think that's exactly what we need at the moment - solidarity in economic relations and investment policy, so that local people have the prospect of a good life.

That's why it's good that we are moving this agreement forward; This is a sign of our solidarity with Mexico. Let's build bridges over troubled water.

2-0232-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Az EU–Mexikó globális megállapodás kétségtelenül új lehetőségeket nyit mindkét fél számára: reméljük, új munkahelyeket és exportpiacokat – javítva a versenyképességünket. A tisztánlátás végett azonban két dolog. Az első: kérem a Bizottságot, sürgősen frissítse az összes szabadkereskedelmi megállapodás együttes hatását vizsgáló 24-es hatástanulmányát a mezőgazdaságra, hogy lássuk, pontosan mivel szembesülnek a gazdáink. Szenteljen különös figyelmet a mézpiacnak. Az ukrán import hatását pedig ezúttal legyen szíves, ne felejtse ki a számításból.

A másik: Ennek a megállapodásnak tagadhatatlanul van politikai vetülete, és az időközi jelentés hemzseg a baloldalnak tett elvtelen engedményektől. Pedig a szerző pontosan tudja: ami a mexikói jogállamisággal történik, az vállalhatatlan. A baloldal ideológiai harcostársainak bűne fölött Brüsszel mindig szemet huny. Scheinbaum Mexikóban, Magyar Péter Magyarországon veri szét a demokratikus rendszert, a Bizottság pedig mélyen hallgat. Önök ezzel a kettős mércével nemcsak ellehetetlenítik, de tönkre is teszik az Uniót, a kölcsönös bizalmat és az együttműködést.
2-0232-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President! The EU-Mexico Global Agreement will undoubtedly open up new opportunities for both parties: hopefully new jobs and export markets – improving our competitiveness. However, for the sake of clarity, two things. The first: I ask the Commission to urgently update its 24th impact study examining the combined impact of all free trade agreements on agriculture, so that we can see exactly what our farmers are facing. Pay special attention to the honey market. And this time, please do not forget the impact of Ukrainian imports from the calculation.

The other: This agreement undeniably has a political dimension, and the interim report is full of unprincipled concessions to the left. However, the author knows exactly: what is happening to the rule of law in Mexico is unacceptable. Brussels always turns a blind eye to the crimes of its ideological comrades-in-arms on the left. Scheinbaum is smashing the democratic system in Mexico, Péter Magyar in Hungary, and the Commission is deeply silent. With this double standard, you not only make it impossible, but also destroy the Union, mutual trust and cooperation.

2-0233-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Czy wy nie nauczyliście się jeszcze wyciągać wniosków z historii? To, co działo się we współpracy z Chinami, powinno pokazywać, w którym kierunku należy iść. Wiele lat temu dokładnie takie same nadzieje pokładano w handlu z Chinami jak dzisiaj z Mercosurem, z Indiami, teraz z Meksykiem. Do niczego dobrego to nie doprowadziło. Dzisiaj mamy czasy, w których powinniśmy budować odporność, niezależność, ponieważ geopolityka jest dzisiaj taka, że drobny konflikt na świecie powoduje dramatyczne konsekwencje.

A my idziemy cały czas w procesie uzależniania się od handlu zagranicznego z krajami bardzo odległymi od Unii Europejskiej. To jest zły kierunek. COVID i inne wojny na Bliskim Wschodzie pokazały, że to jest bardzo zły kierunek, ale nie wyciągamy z tego żadnych wniosków. Problem polega na tym, że kiedy Niemcy podejmowali głupie decyzje, szkodzili sami sobie i niszczyli własną gospodarkę właśnie poprzez handel gazem z Rosją, poprzez likwidowanie energii atomowej, poprzez handel z Chinami. To była ich sprawa. A dzisiaj problem polega na tym, że mają wpływ na całą Unię Europejską i te głupoty każą stosować i w nich uczestniczyć wszystkim członkom. I to jest największy problem dzisiejszej sytuacji.
2-0233-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Mr Commissioner! Haven't you learned to learn from history yet? What has happened in cooperation with China should show in which direction we should go. Many years ago, exactly the same hopes were placed on trade with China as today with Mercosur, with India, now with Mexico. It didn't lead to anything good. Today we have times when we should build resilience and independence, because geopolitics today is such that a minor conflict in the world causes dramatic consequences.

And we are constantly in the process of becoming dependent on foreign trade with countries very distant from the European Union. This is the wrong direction. COVID and other wars in the Middle East have shown that this is a very wrong direction, but we do not draw any conclusions from it. The problem is that when the Germans made stupid decisions, they harmed themselves and destroyed their own economy precisely by trading gas with Russia, by eliminating nuclear energy, by trading with China. It was their business. And today the problem is that they influence the entire European Union and force all members to use and participate in these stupidities. And this is the biggest problem of today's situation.

2-0234-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário Šefčovič, nesta altura em que parece mais fácil lançar tarifas, que são uma espécie de muros, dá particular gozo falar aqui de acordos comerciais, que são uma espécie de pontes. E esta modernização do acordo global com o México e o acordo comercial interino são uma bela ponte.

Não são só os 99 % de tarifas que desaparecem, que só no agroalimentar representam mais de 100 mil milhões de EUR de poupanças para os exportadores europeus, mas são também todos os outros impactos que este mercado vai ter, nomeadamente o facto de nos abrir 130 milhões de consumidores mexicanos, e fará com que as nossas trocas comerciais cresçam rapidamente, ultrapassarão os 100 mil milhões de EUR muito rapidamente.

Também clarifica as regras de acesso ao mercado digital e torna mais fácil o acesso dos europeus a matérias primas críticas.

Gostávamos que essa ponte tivesse mais um troço. Sim, gostávamos que tivesse o capítulo da energia e é nossa responsabilidade fazê-lo antes do fim do primeiro período de revisão deste acordo.

Mas também tem troços perfeitamente novos: o acesso a concursos públicos por parte de empresas europeias, nomeadamente em concursos públicos de nível estadual, e a inovadora cláusula de combate e prevenção da corrupção, porque não há comércio livre sem instituições livres e transparentes, fazendo fé daquilo que realmente é o primeiro passo para o combate à corrupção, que é o combate, também, à burocracia.

Portanto, pedimos, caros colegas, que aprovem este acordo quando vier à votação, porque acreditamos na força do comércio livre, acreditamos porque o comércio livre tirou centenas de milhões de pessoas da miséria nas últimas décadas e acreditamos que lutar por um comércio mais livre é lutar por uma Europa mais forte.
2-0234-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner Šefčovič, at a time when it seems easier to launch tariffs, which are a kind of walls, it is particularly enjoyable to talk here about trade agreements, which are a kind of bridges. And this modernization of the global agreement with Mexico and the interim trade agreement is a beautiful bridge.

It is not just the 99% of tariffs that disappear, which in agri-food alone represent more than 100 billion EUR in savings for European exporters, but it is also all the other impacts that this market will have, namely the fact that it will open up 130 million Mexican consumers to us, and will make our trade exchange grow rapidly, they will exceed 100 billion EUR very quickly.

It also clarifies the rules for accessing the digital market and makes it easier for Europeans to access critical raw materials.

We would like this bridge to have one more section. Yes, we would like to have an energy chapter and it is our responsibility to do so before the end of the first review period of this agreement.

But it also has completely new sections: access to public tenders by European companies, particularly in public tenders at state level, and the innovative clause to combat and prevent corruption, because there is no free trade without free and transparent institutions, demonstrating what really is the first step towards combating corruption, which is also combating bureaucracy.

Therefore, we ask, dear colleagues, that you approve this agreement when it comes to the vote, because we believe in the strength of free trade, we believe because free trade has lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty in recent decades, and we believe that fighting for freer trade is fighting for a stronger Europe.

2-0235-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, la Unión Europea debe buscar nuevas alianzas, de todo tipo: comerciales, políticas e incluso seguramente de defensa. El viejo mundo que conocíamos está agonizando y la Unión Europea debe hacerse un lugar en el nuevo mundo que está naciendo. Alianzas con países hermanos como México son claves. Son una oportunidad geopolítica de primer orden. Aquí, todos estamos de acuerdo; en lo que quizás ya no estamos todos de acuerdo es con qué herramientas construimos estas alianzas.

Para nosotros, un tipo de acuerdo que sí contempla medidas sancionadoras vinculantes en caso de no respetar el acuerdo comercial, pero que solo plantea meras recomendaciones cuando se vulneran los derechos humanos o medioambientales no ayuda a construir el mundo que queremos.

Pero es que además, en el ámbito comercial, son acuerdos que no responden a todos los intereses que necesitamos en Europa. Fíjense, por ejemplo, en la industria del automóvil. En los últimos meses, hemos visto cómo Audi cerraba definitivamente su planta en Bruselas y destruía 3 000 empleos directos. Mientras tanto, se consolida el traslado de la producción de modelos históricos como el Volkswagen Golf a la planta de Puebla, en México, lo que deja vacías las líneas de montaje en Alemania. ¿Esto es un buen acuerdo? Para la cuenta de resultados de las multinacionales, sí, pero para las familias trabajadoras evidentemente no. Y esto es solo la punta del iceberg.

La pregunta no es si queremos una alianza con México: la queremos. La pregunta es si estamos dispuestos a construirlo sobre estos cimientos. Nosotros lo tenemos claro: el progreso de Europa no se defiende destruyendo su industria ni su precarización, el empleo aquí o allá. Por eso, por coherencia y por justicia social, votaremos en contra.
2-0235-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the European Union must seek new alliances, of all kinds: commercial, political and probably even defense. The old world we knew is dying and the European Union must make a place for itself in the new world that is being born. Alliances with sister countries like Mexico are key. They are a geopolitical opportunity of the first order. Here, we all agree; What perhaps we no longer all agree on is what tools we build these alliances with.

For us, a type of agreement that does contemplate binding sanctioning measures in case the trade agreement is not respected, but that only proposes mere recommendations when human or environmental rights are violated does not help build the world we want.

But in addition, in the commercial field, they are agreements that do not respond to all the interests that we need in Europe. Look, for example, at the automobile industry. In recent months, we have seen Audi permanently close its plant in Brussels and destroy 3,000 direct jobs. Meanwhile, the transfer of production of historic models such as the Volkswagen Golf to the Puebla plant in Mexico is being consolidated, leaving the assembly lines in Germany empty. Is this a good agreement? For the bottom line of multinationals, yes, but for working families obviously not. And this is just the tip of the iceberg.

The question is not whether we want an alliance with Mexico: we do. The question is whether we are willing to build on this foundation. We are clear: Europe's progress is not defended by destroying its industry or its precariousness, employment here or there. Therefore, for consistency and social justice, we will vote against.

2-0236-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, donner tout le pouvoir aux multinationales, voilà ce que vous vous apprêtez à faire avec ce nouvel accord de libre-échange avec le Mexique. Et il faudrait qu’on soit là à applaudir des deux mains! Les entreprises ne s’y trompent d’ailleurs pas. Attirées par une main-d’œuvre bon marché et des droits de douane réduits à néant, elles en profitent déjà pour délocaliser massivement, comme le groupe Volkswagen qui, en même temps qu’il délocalise l’assemblage de ses voitures Audi et Golf au Mexique, supprime au moins 50 000 emplois en Europe.

Mais le scandale de cet accord ne s’arrête pas là. Demain, des entreprises pourront attaquer l’État mexicain ou les États européens devant une juridiction internationale privée et réclamer plusieurs centaines de millions d’euros si une politique publique ne leur convient pas, par exemple pour garder le contrôle public sur l’énergie ou préserver l’environnement. C’est exactement ce même mécanisme scandaleux qui était présent dans le TAFTA, dans le CETA, dans le traité sur la Charte de l’énergie, dont les Européens ont déjà dit haut et fort qu’ils n’en voulaient pas.

Alors, collègues de gauche, socialistes, écologistes qui vous apprêtez à voter cet accord, comment pouvez-vous accepter cet accord complètement injuste qui va accélérer la désindustrialisation, éroder un peu plus notre souveraineté alimentaire et promouvoir une extraction sans limite de matières premières? Au foot, on appelle ça un tir contre son camp. Monsieur le Commissaire, si vous me le permettez, votre politique du «tout libre-échange» mérite un carton rouge. C’est pourquoi notre groupe de la gauche continuera à se mobiliser contre ce «tout libre-échange» au niveau européen.
2-0236-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, giving all the power to multinationals is what you are preparing to do with this new free trade agreement with Mexico. And we should be there clapping with both hands! Companies are not mistaken. Attracted by cheap labor and reduced customs duties, they are already taking advantage of this to relocate massively, like the Volkswagen group which, at the same time as it relocates the assembly of its Audi and Golf cars to Mexico, is cutting at least 50,000 jobs in Europe.

But the scandal of this agreement does not end there. Tomorrow, companies will be able to attack the Mexican State or European States before a private international court and claim several hundred million euros if a public policy does not suit them, for example to maintain public control over energy or preserve the environment. It is exactly this same scandalous mechanism that was present in TAFTA, in CETA, in the Energy Charter Treaty, which the Europeans have already said loud and clear that they do not want.

So, colleagues on the left, socialists, ecologists who are about to vote for this agreement, how can you accept this completely unfair agreement which will accelerate deindustrialization, further erode our food sovereignty and promote unlimited extraction of raw materials? In football, we call it an own goal. Mr Commissioner, if you allow me, your “all free trade” policy deserves a red card. This is why our left group will continue to mobilize against this “all free trade” at European level.

2-0237-0000.sourceText:
Г-жо Председател, пред нас е споразумение, което ще отвори европейските пазари за безмитен внос на пчелен мед от Мексико в размер, сравним с производството на пчелен мед в три Българии. Първо, квотата се увеличава до 35 000 тона. След седмата година всички ограничения отпадат. Това се случва в момент, когато европейските институции сами предупреждават за риска от фалшифициран мед. Изследване от кошерите на съвместен изследователски център на Европейската комисия показва, че при 22 изследвания на проби мед с произход Мексико, при повече от една четвърт има съмнение за фалшифициране. Става въпрос за фалшив мед, пчелен мед, колеги.

Още по-необяснимо е, че Мексико дори не използва изцяло сегашната си безмитна квота. Защо тогава предлагаме още по-голяма либерализация? Не можем да жертваме европейските пчелари, в замяна на търговски отстъпки в други сектори, защото когато унищожим собственото си производство, губят не само пчеларите, губят и европейските потребители, които имат право на истински, качествен и безплатен мед.
2-0237-0000.englishText:
Madam President, before us is an agreement that will open European markets to duty-free imports of honey from Mexico in an amount comparable to the production of honey in three Bulgarias. First, the quota is increased to 35,000 tons. After the seventh year, all restrictions are removed. This is happening at a time when the European institutions themselves are warning about the risk of counterfeit honey. Research from the hives of the European Commission's Joint Research Center shows that in 22 tests of honey samples originating in Mexico, more than a quarter are suspected of adulteration. It's about fake honey, honey, colleagues.

Even more inexplicably, Mexico does not even fully use its current duty-free quota. Why then are we proposing even greater liberalization? We cannot sacrifice European beekeepers in exchange for trade concessions in other sectors, because when we destroy our own production, it is not only the beekeepers who lose, but also the European consumers who have the right to real, quality and free honey.

2-0239-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, mentre gli Stati Uniti mettono in discussione l'accordo che lega Stati Uniti, Canada e Messico, e che per trent'anni è stato il pilastro dell'integrazione economica nordamericana, l'Europa fa una scelta opposta e rafforza le proprie alleanze.

L'accordo con il Messico è una scelta geopolitica fondamentale: in un mondo frammentato, diversificare i mercati rafforza la nostra autonomia strategica.

Insieme al Canada, ai paesi del Mercosur, all'Australia e ad altri partner, stiamo lavorando per costruire uno spazio di medie potenze che credono nel commercio aperto e nelle regole, riducendo la dipendenza da attori terzi. E l'Unione europea, come spazio che può essere una grande potenza democratica, può ambire a guidare questo cambiamento.

Una strategia di importanza globale che ha anche benefici, per i nostri territori, molto immediati. Penso alle imprese dei nostri territori, dell'Italia, con indicazioni geografiche protette come quelle per i formaggi o quelle per i vini. Abbiamo prodotti che sono tutelati e che potranno raggiungere con maggiore facilità i consumatori messicani.

Anche questo è un pezzo importante della nostra strategia per il futuro dell'economia della nostra Unione.
2-0239-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, while the United States is questioning the agreement that binds the United States, Canada and Mexico, and which for thirty years has been the pillar of North American economic integration, Europe is making the opposite choice and strengthening its alliances.

The agreement with Mexico is a fundamental geopolitical choice: in a fragmented world, diversifying markets strengthens our strategic autonomy.

Together with Canada, Mercosur countries, Australia and other partners, we are working to build a space of middle powers that believe in open trade and rules, reducing dependence on third-party actors. And the European Union, as a space that can be a great democratic power, can aspire to lead this change.

A strategy of global importance which also has very immediate benefits for our territories. I am thinking of the companies in our territories, in Italy, with protected geographical indications such as those for cheeses or those for wines. We have products that are protected and that will be able to reach Mexican consumers more easily.

This is also an important piece of our strategy for the future of our Union's economy.

2-0240-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, sehr geehrte Damen und Herren! Dieses Haus wird heute vor vollendete Tatsachen gestellt. Die Kommission hat dieses Abkommen bewusst gesplittet. Das Interims-Handelsabkommen tritt in Kraft, sobald dieses Parlament und der mexikanische Senat zustimmen. Die nationalen Parlamente, der österreichische Nationalrat eingeschlossen, dürfen erst im Nachhinein ratifizieren, wenn längst vollendete Tatsachen geschaffen wurden. Das ist keine Handelspolitik, das ist Demokratieumgehung mit Ansage.

Und während man uns von Wachstum und Diversifizierung erzählt, werden unter dem Deckmantel des Freihandels munter Green Deal-Ideologie und Nachhaltigkeitsziele-Bürokratie in ein Handelsabkommen geschmuggelt, das eigentlich unseren Bauern und unserem Mittelstand dienen sollte, nicht Brüsseler Wunschprojekten. Diesem demokratiepolitisch fragwürdigen Vorgehen können wir unser Vertrauen nicht aussprechen.

Gleichzeitig wissen wir um die berechtigten Interessen jener heimischen Betriebe, die auf faire und verlässliche Marktchancen angewiesen sind. Diesen Widerspruch löst die Kommission mit ihrem Vorgehen nicht; sie hat ihn selbst geschaffen.
2-0240-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen! This House is today faced with a fait accompli. The Commission deliberately split this agreement. The interim trade agreement will come into force as soon as this Parliament and the Mexican Senate approve it. The national parliaments, including the Austrian National Council, are only allowed to ratify retrospectively, once a fait accompli has long since been established. This is not trade policy, this is an attempt to circumvent democracy.

And while we are being told about growth and diversification, under the guise of free trade, Green Deal ideology and sustainability goals bureaucracy are being smuggled into a trade agreement that should actually serve our farmers and our middle class, not Brussels' dream projects. We cannot express our trust in this approach, which is questionable in terms of democratic policy.

At the same time, we are aware of the legitimate interests of those local companies that rely on fair and reliable market opportunities. The Commission does not resolve this contradiction with its approach; she created it herself.

2-0241-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, commissaris, dit gemoderniseerde akkoord met Mexico komt op een cruciaal moment, en wel om verschillende redenen.

Op geopolitiek vlak versterken we onze positie in Latijns-Amerika en bouwen we een betrouwbaar partnerschap uit in een regio waarin ook andere spelers hun invloed trachten te vergroten.

Op economisch vlak opent dit akkoord bovendien nieuwe kansen voor onze bedrijven, onder meer via een betere toegang tot overheidsopdrachten en minder administratieve lasten.

Het bevestigt ons geloof in vrije, op regels gebaseerde handel in deze moeilijke tijden van deglobalisering en fragmentatie. Bovendien zet het duidelijke stappen vooruit in de verbetering van arbeidsomstandigheden en duurzaamheidsnormen.

Tot slot, mijnheer de commissaris, roep ik u op deze ambitieuze handelsagenda consequent voort te zetten. De EU moet blijven kiezen voor sterke handelsakkoorden die welvaart, veerkracht en een open strategische autonomie verder versterken.
2-0241-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, this modernized agreement with Mexico comes at a crucial time, for several reasons.

Geopolitically, we are strengthening our position in Latin America and building a reliable partnership in a region in which other players are also trying to increase their influence.

On an economic level, this agreement also opens up new opportunities for our companies, including better access to government contracts and reduced administrative burdens.

It reaffirms our belief in free, rules-based trade in these difficult times of deglobalization and fragmentation. Moreover, it is taking clear steps forward in improving working conditions and sustainability standards.

Finally, Commissioner, I call on you to consistently pursue this ambitious trade agenda. The EU must continue to opt for strong trade agreements that further strengthen prosperity, resilience and open strategic autonomy.

2-0242-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Jedes Mal, wenn wir hier über Freihandel reden, entblößen sich die Kollegen von links mit ihrem ökonomischen Unwissen. Deswegen sage ich das gerne noch mal ganz deutlich: Wirtschaftliche Abhängigkeit treibt uns in die politische Abhängigkeit. Das haben wir beim russischen Gas gesehen; das sehen wir bei kritischen Rohstoffen aus China. Die Lösung kann doch nicht Abschottung sein. Sie heißt mehr Handel mit mehr Partnern, auch wenn Linke das nicht wahrhaben wollen.

Das modernisierte Abkommen mit Mexiko ist ein wichtiger Erfolg für unseren Wohlstand und für Europas strategische Unabhängigkeit. Wohlstand entsteht nicht hinter Zollmauern; Wohlstand entsteht, wenn Menschen miteinander Handel treiben. Mit diesem Abkommen können unsere Exporte nach Mexiko um bis zu 75 % steigen. Europäische Unternehmen können bis zu 100 Millionen Euro an Zöllen sparen. Und wir sichern den Zugang zu kritischen Rohstoffen, schaffen neue Chancen von Mittelstand bis Landwirtschaft und Industrie. So geht strategische Unabhängigkeit, und so geht europäische Stärke, liebe Kollegen!
2-0242-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Every time we talk about free trade here, our colleagues on the left expose themselves with their economic ignorance. That's why I'd like to say this again very clearly: Economic dependence drives us into political dependence. We saw this with Russian gas; We see this with critical raw materials from China. The solution cannot be isolation. It means more trade with more partners, even if leftists don't want to believe that.

The modernized agreement with Mexico is an important success for our prosperity and for Europe's strategic independence. Prosperity is not created behind tariff walls; Prosperity arises when people trade with each other. With this agreement, our exports to Mexico can increase by up to 75%. European companies could save up to €100 million in tariffs. And we secure access to critical raw materials and create new opportunities from medium-sized businesses to agriculture and industry. This is how strategic independence works, and this is how European strength works, dear colleagues!

2-0243-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, collega's, dit beleid van de Europese Commissie is volstrekt onbegrijpelijk. Gisteren hebben we nog gedebatteerd over onze automobielindustrie, die uit Europa vertrokken is en elk jaar duizenden jobs verloren ziet gaan. En wat doet deze Commissie? Zij sluit opnieuw een neoliberaal handelsakkoord, een akkoord dat onze industriële capaciteit ondermijnt en werknemers wereldwijd tegen elkaar zal uitspelen.

Europese autoproducenten zullen hun assemblage nog goedkoper naar Mexico kunnen verplaatsen. Gevolg: opnieuw duizenden jobs weg. Ook geeft het akkoord grote bedrijven het recht om overheden aan te klagen als zij het nog maar durven om een sociaal beleid te voeren dat hun winstmarges zou kunnen hypothekeren.

Ik dacht dat de Europese Unie aan industriepolitiek ging doen, maar wat zien we in plaats daarvan? Opnieuw dezelfde neoliberale recepten die ons in deze crisis hebben gestort. Wat wij nodig hebben, is een eerlijke deal die welvaart creëert voor de EU en voor Mexico, en niet alleen voor multinationals. Stem dit akkoord dus weg.
2-0243-0000.englishText:
Mr President, colleagues, this policy of the European Commission is completely incomprehensible. Yesterday we debated our automotive industry, which has left Europe and is seeing thousands of jobs lost every year. And what does this Commission do? She is once again entering into a neoliberal trade deal, an agreement that will undermine our industrial capacity and pit workers worldwide against each other.

European car manufacturers will be able to move their assembly to Mexico even more cheaply. The result: thousands of jobs lost again. The agreement also gives large companies the right to sue governments if they dare to implement social policies that could jeopardize their profit margins.

I thought the European Union was going to do industrial policy, but what do we see instead? Once again the same neoliberal recipes that have plunged us into this crisis. What we need is a fair deal that creates prosperity for the EU and for Mexico, and not just for multinationals. So vote this agreement down.

2-0244-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, México es un socio estratégico de la Unión Europea y —por ende— en estos momentos de fragmentación del orden internacional es necesario reforzar nuestros lazos a través de la modernización del Acuerdo Global y de la aprobación del Acuerdo Comercial Interino.

De esta manera, incrementaremos el comercio reduciendo más los aranceles, abarcando más rubros y protegiendo mejor a los productores. Pero también es necesario profundizar el diálogo político, abrir temas como la independencia judicial y el Estado de Derecho. Y no podemos ignorar el grave problema de los desaparecidos. Cuando estuvimos con EuroLat en México, el número oficial era de 130 000 personas, pero ese número sigue incrementando.

Comparto la preocupación de Amnistía Internacional por los operativos de la Ciudad de México por la represión durante las manifestaciones de los familiares de desaparecidos. Por ello, no debemos callarnos. Hay que apoyar el Acuerdo Global Modernizado, pero también denunciar las derivas autoritarias porque nuestro compromiso y amistad no es con un Gobierno, sino con el hermano y querido pueblo mexicano.
2-0244-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mexico is a strategic partner of the European Union and - therefore - in these moments of fragmentation of the international order it is necessary to strengthen our ties through the modernization of the Global Agreement and the approval of the Interim Trade Agreement.

In this way, we will increase trade by further reducing tariffs, covering more items and better protecting producers. But it is also necessary to deepen the political dialogue, opening up issues such as judicial independence and the rule of law. And we cannot ignore the serious problem of the missing. When we were with EuroLat in Mexico, the official number was 130,000 people, but that number continues to increase.

I share Amnesty International's concern about the operations in Mexico City due to repression during demonstrations by relatives of the disappeared. Therefore, we must not remain silent. We must support the Modernized Global Agreement, but also denounce authoritarian drifts because our commitment and friendship is not with a Government, but with the brother and beloved Mexican people.

2-0245-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, con nuestro apoyo, Europa y México no solo sellarán un acuerdo estratégico, sino una forma compartida de entender el mundo. Es una alianza entre dos democracias que, frente a quienes usan su poder para imponer su voluntad y su beneficio propio, defienden el diálogo, la cooperación y las reglas claras y pactadas para construir la paz, la prosperidad y el desarrollo sostenible colectivo.

Lo apoyamos porque refuerza el diálogo político con un socio estratégico, porque se basa en la cooperación y beneficia a la salud, la educación y la investigación, también a la preparación contra los desastres, porque respeta a las personas y a los recursos naturales y porque está basado en el compromiso y los derechos humanos, el Acuerdo de París, los derechos laborales, el comercio, la igualdad y el medio ambiente. Porque, además, abre nuevas oportunidades a nuestras pymes y protege especialmente a sectores como el turrón o los cítricos.

Pero, sobre todo, lo apoyamos porque, en el actual tablero geopolítico, un acuerdo con un país como México es la mejor brújula. Desde el respeto mutuo, desde el reconocimiento a nuestra propia historia, a nuestra diversidad y desde la cooperación.
2-0245-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, with our support, Europe and Mexico will not only seal a strategic agreement, but a shared way of understanding the world. It is an alliance between two democracies that, in the face of those who use their power to impose their will and their own benefit, defend dialogue, cooperation and clear and agreed rules to build peace, prosperity and collective sustainable development.

We support it because it reinforces political dialogue with a strategic partner, because it is based on cooperation and benefits health, education and research, as well as disaster preparedness, because it respects people and natural resources and because it is based on commitment and human rights, the Paris Agreement, labor rights, trade, equality and the environment. Because, in addition, it opens new opportunities for our SMEs and especially protects sectors such as nougat or citrus.

But, above all, we support it because, in the current geopolitical situation, an agreement with a country like Mexico is the best compass. From mutual respect, from recognition of our own history, from our diversity and from cooperation.

2-0246-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, de Partij voor de Vrijheid kiest voor handel die Nederland sterker maakt en daarom steunen wij dit strategisch partnerschapsakkoord.

Mexico is met 130 miljoen inwoners een van de grootste economieën ter wereld en een belangrijke groeimarkt voor onze ondernemers. De Europese export van goederen en diensten kan met 75 % toenemen en Europese bedrijven besparen jaarlijks tot 100 miljoen EUR aan douanerechten. Dit akkoord verlaagt handelsbarrières, geeft onze bedrijven betere toegang tot Mexicaanse overheidsaanbestedingen en biedt enorme kansen voor de Nederlandse hightech machinebouw en logistiek. Ook onze boeren profiteren ervan, want hoge invoertarieven op onder meer kaas, kip en varkensvlees verdwijnen.

Maar hoewel wij voor het akkoord zijn, zijn we tegen de resolutie van het Parlement. Want opnieuw misbruikt links een handelsakkoord om zijn klimaathysterie, genderagenda en ngo-obsessie door te drukken. Strategische partnerschappen gaan over handel en wederzijds voordeel. "Woke" is geen exportproduct.
2-0246-0000.englishText:
President, the Party for Freedom opts for trade that makes the Netherlands stronger and that is why we support this strategic partnership agreement.

With 130 million inhabitants, Mexico is one of the largest economies in the world and an important growth market for our entrepreneurs. European exports of goods and services could increase by 75% and European companies will save up to EUR 100 million in customs duties every year. This agreement lowers trade barriers, gives our companies better access to Mexican government tenders and offers enormous opportunities for Dutch high-tech mechanical engineering and logistics. Our farmers also benefit from it, because high import tariffs on cheese, chicken and pork, among other things, will disappear.

But while we are in favor of the agreement, we are against Parliament's resolution. Because once again the left is abusing a trade agreement to push through its climate hysteria, gender agenda and NGO obsession. Strategic partnerships are about trade and mutual benefit. “Woke” is not an export product.

2-0248-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, vivimos en un contexto complejo y lleno de incertidumbres donde sabemos que —además— los aranceles se están utilizando como amenazas continuas.

En este contexto, los acuerdos comerciales con aliados que sean estables y de confianza y que nos den garantías de que se van a respetar valores compartidos y las reglas del juego que establezcamos parece que son más importantes que nunca.

Parece que este año 2026 es un año de nuevas oportunidades para nuevos mercados y para la reducción de dependencias. Se trata de Mercosur, la India, Australia y México, que es de lo que nos toca hablar hoy.

Qué vamos a decir: México es un aliado internacional estratégico para las empresas europeas y para las empresas vascas.

Resaltamos tres cosas que esperamos en el despliegue de este Acuerdo. Primero, que sirva para reducir los niveles de violencia que existen en el país y solucionar las denuncias que existen a ese respecto. Segundo, que se despliegue el comercio respetando derechos de comunidades locales e indígenas de forma íntegra. Y tercero, que seamos capaces, por supuesto, de acompañar a nuestras empresas e industrias a sacar el máximo provecho de este Acuerdo con relaciones que sean beneficiosas para ambas partes de una manera equilibrada.
2-0248-0000.englishText:
Madam President, we live in a complex context full of uncertainties where we know that—in addition—tariffs are being used as continuous threats.

In this context, trade agreements with allies that are stable and trustworthy and that give us guarantees that shared values ​​and the rules of the game that we establish will be respected seem to be more important than ever.

It seems that this year 2026 is a year of new opportunities for new markets and for the reduction of dependencies. These are Mercosur, India, Australia and Mexico, which is what we have to talk about today.

What are we going to say: Mexico is a strategic international ally for European companies and for Basque companies.

We highlight three things we hope for in the deployment of this Agreement. First, that it serves to reduce the levels of violence that exist in the country and resolve the complaints that exist in this regard. Second, that trade be deployed fully respecting the rights of local and indigenous communities. And third, that we are able, of course, to accompany our companies and industries to get the most out of this Agreement with relationships that are beneficial for both parties in a balanced way.

2-0250-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, viviamo un tempo di sfide verticali, la forza vale più delle regole, si proclama.

Attori globali puntano alla supremazia su vicini e lontani, agitano ricatti, impongono dazi, alzano muri, muovono guerra.

L'Unione europea sa e può percorrere la via opposta: incontro, negoziato, costruzione e custodia di regole condivise, partenariato vincente, l'unica reale vittoria.

Il rinnovato accordo globale con il Messico giunge in un momento cruciale, va nella giusta direzione, rafforza il dialogo politico con un partner strategico dell'America Latina, apre opportunità concrete per le imprese – specie PMI e agroalimentare – precisa impegni vincolanti sui diritti umani e dei lavoratori e sulle questioni climatiche.

Tutto ciò va realizzato e monitorato in un dialogo aperto con la società civile. Oggi più che mai l'Europa deve dimostrare che un altro modo di stare al mondo è possibile e dà frutti.
2-0250-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we live in a time of vertical challenges, force is worth more than rules, it is proclaimed.

Global actors aim for supremacy over near and far, they agitate blackmail, impose tariffs, raise walls, wage war.

The European Union knows and can take the opposite path: meeting, negotiation, construction and safeguarding of shared rules, winning partnership, the only real victory.

The renewed global agreement with Mexico comes at a crucial moment, it goes in the right direction, it strengthens political dialogue with a strategic partner in Latin America, it opens concrete opportunities for businesses - especially SMEs and agri-food - it specifies binding commitments on human and workers' rights and on climate issues.

All this must be achieved and monitored in an open dialogue with civil society. Today more than ever, Europe must demonstrate that another way of being in the world is possible and bears fruit.

2-0251-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, alors que toutes les grandes puissances protègent leurs économies de la concurrence étrangère, la Commission européenne est lancée dans une course sans fin aux traités de libre-échange. Avec quel pays nous n’avons pas encore signé de traité de libre-échange? La liste est courte.

Avec le Mexique, on nous dit qu’on a pris toutes nos garanties, et que ce sera très favorable. Mais je note quand même qu’on a abandonné totalement les contrôles sanitaires et phytosanitaires. Et deuxièmement, on va quand même importer de nombreux produits agricoles – bovins, miel, fruits – qui inquiètent nos agriculteurs. Alors à chaque fois, on nous dit: «Oui, mais ce sont de faibles volumes.»

Oui, mais: faibles volumes + faibles volumes = gros volumes. Parce que, dans le même temps, nous avons des traités de libre-échange avec l’Ukraine, la Malaisie, le Mercosur, l’Australie.

Nos agriculteurs vivent dans un contexte très tendu au niveau de leurs revenus. Ils ne supportent plus ces traités de libre-échange. Il est temps de cesser cette course en avant.
2-0251-0000.englishText:
Madam President, while all the great powers protect their economies from foreign competition, the European Commission is engaged in an endless race for free trade agreements. With which country have we not yet signed a free trade treaty? The list is short.

With Mexico, we are told that we have taken all our guarantees, and that it will be very favorable. But I still note that we have completely abandoned sanitary and phytosanitary controls. And secondly, we will still import many agricultural products – cattle, honey, fruit – which worry our farmers. So each time, we are told: “Yes, but these are low volumes.”

Yes, but: low volumes + low volumes = high volumes. Because, at the same time, we have free trade treaties with Ukraine, Malaysia, Mercosur, Australia.

Our farmers live in a very tense context in terms of their income. They no longer support these free trade agreements. It is time to stop this rush forward.

2-0252-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, la forza dell'Europa non si misura dal numero degli accordi che firma, ma dalla capacità di costruire partenariati che tutelino i suoi interessi e promuovano valori comuni, tra cui lo Stato di diritto e i diritti fondamentali.

Come vicepresidente della delegazione per le relazioni con il Messico, sono orgogliosa della firma dell'accordo globale modernizzato. È una scelta di politica estera, industriale e strategica, significa diversificare le nostre relazioni economiche, rafforzare le catene del valore, proteggere le nostre indicazioni geografiche e azzerare i dazi per le nostre imprese, in un contesto internazionale sempre più competitivo.

Ma nessun partenariato può essere solido senza un principio irrinunciabile: il rispetto reciproco, rispetto delle regole, degli impegni assunti e delle nostre imprese, e condizioni di concorrenza realmente eque.

Su queste basi la cooperazione diventa un fattore di crescita, sicurezza e prosperità condivisa, perché l'Europa davvero protagonista non è quella che firma più accordi, è quella che sa farli rispettare, che difende i propri interessi e che trasforma ogni partenariato in un vantaggio per i suoi cittadini e per le sue imprese.
2-0252-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, Europe's strength is not measured by the number of agreements it signs, but by its ability to build partnerships that protect its interests and promote common values, including the rule of law and fundamental rights.

As Vice-President of the Delegation for Relations with Mexico, I am proud of the signing of the Modernized Comprehensive Agreement. It is a foreign, industrial and strategic policy choice, it means diversifying our economic relations, strengthening value chains, protecting our geographical indications and eliminating duties for our companies, in an increasingly competitive international context.

But no partnership can be solid without an indispensable principle: mutual respect, respect for the rules, for the commitments undertaken and for our businesses, and truly fair competition conditions.

On this basis, cooperation becomes a factor of growth, security and shared prosperity, because the truly protagonist Europe is not the one that signs the most agreements, it is the one that knows how to enforce them, that defends its own interests and that transforms every partnership into an advantage for its citizens and for its businesses.

2-0253-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, europeos y mexicanos sabemos bien que nuestra prosperidad es mayor cuando es compartida y, en un mundo donde la confianza escasea y la lista de socios fiables cada vez es más corta, México se reafirma con este Acuerdo como un aliado comercial estratégico para España y para Europa.

Este Acuerdo abrirá nuevas oportunidades para nuestros exportadores y nuestras empresas y animará a muchas empresas europeas —ya presentes al otro lado del Atlántico— a seguir invirtiendo, creciendo y creando prosperidad junto con México.

Precisamente por eso, porque creemos que es una relación sólida y de futuro, lamentamos que no se haya incluido un capítulo ambicioso sobre energía. Pedimos por tanto a la Comisión que siga exigiendo al Gobierno de México la necesaria seguridad jurídica para las inversiones de nuestras empresas energéticas. Solo así garantizaremos que este acuerdo sea no solo una oportunidad comercial circunstancial, sino una verdadera alianza estratégica entre Europa y México.
2-0253-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr. Commissioner, Europeans and Mexicans know well that our prosperity is greater when it is shared and, in a world where trust is scarce and the list of reliable partners is increasingly shorter, Mexico reaffirms itself with this Agreement as a strategic commercial ally for Spain and for Europe.

This Agreement will open new opportunities for our exporters and our companies and will encourage many European companies – already present on the other side of the Atlantic – to continue investing, growing and creating prosperity together with Mexico.

Precisely for this reason, because we believe that it is a solid relationship with a future, we regret that an ambitious chapter on energy has not been included. We therefore ask the Commission to continue demanding from the Government of Mexico the necessary legal security for the investments of our energy companies. Only in this way will we guarantee that this agreement is not only a circumstantial commercial opportunity, but a true strategic alliance between Europe and Mexico.

2-0254-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, creo que esto es justo lo que necesitamos: relaciones honestas, proporcionales, con principios y valores democráticos y tolerantes.

Enhorabuena a los ponentes; más al ponente López que al ponente Larraz, porque he visto que ha «ayuseado» un poquito y no sé si era necesario.

Me parecen especialmente positivos los estándares acordados en materia de protección laboral, sanitaria y medioambiental. Por cierto, hablando de medio ambiente, en el informe se cita el Acuerdo de París, el Convenio sobre la Diversidad Biológica. Muy bien, señores del PP. Ya que han cogido esa racha con México, háganlo también aquí. No vaya a ser que defiendan el Pacto Verde Europeo en los acuerdos y después no lo hagan en la Unión Europea.

Por cierto, en cuanto al sector agroalimentario: creo que va a traer beneficios con relación a la eliminación de los aranceles mexicanos sobre nuestros productos. Para los que venimos de tierra de vino, es una muy buena noticia que se quiten estos aranceles. Por tanto, este es el camino: relaciones proporcionales, tolerantes, democráticas. Este es el camino.
2-0254-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I think this is just what we need: honest, proportional relations, with democratic and tolerant principles and values.

Congratulations to the speakers; more to speaker López than to speaker Larraz, because I have seen that he has "lightened" a little and I don't know if it was necessary.

The agreed standards regarding labor, health and environmental protection seem especially positive to me. By the way, speaking of the environment, the report cites the Paris Agreement, the Convention on Biological Diversity. Very good, gentlemen of the PP. Since you've caught that streak with Mexico, do it here too. It is not going to be that they defend the European Green Deal in the agreements and then do not do so in the European Union.

By the way, regarding the agri-food sector: I think it will bring benefits in relation to the elimination of Mexican tariffs on our products. For those of us who come from wine country, it is very good news that these tariffs are being removed. Therefore, this is the way: proportional, tolerant, democratic relations. This is the way.

2-0256-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, η συμφωνία στρατηγικής εταιρικής σχέσης μεταξύ της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης και του Μεξικού αποτελεί σίγουρα ένα σημαντικό βήμα για μια πιο ισχυρή, δημοκρατική και ανθεκτική συνεργασία σε μια περίοδο πολύ μεγάλων γεωπολιτικών ανακατατάξεων. Δεν αρκεί όμως να μιλάμε μόνο για περισσότερες εμπορικές συναλλαγές. Το εμπόριο πρέπει να συνοδεύεται από ισχυρές εγγυήσεις για τα ανθρώπινα δικαιώματα, την προστασία του περιβάλλοντος, τα δικαιώματα των εργαζομένων και την καταπολέμηση της διαφθοράς.

Για μας στην Ελλάδα αλλά και στην Ευρώπη, η συμφωνία μπορεί να δημιουργήσει νέες ευκαιρίες για τις εξαγωγές ποιοτικών αγροδιατροφικών προϊόντων και για τις μικρομεσαίες επιχειρήσεις μας. Είναι κρίσιμο όμως να διασφαλιστεί η ουσιαστική προστασία των ευρωπαϊκών γεωγραφικών ενδείξεων και να τηρούνται ισότιμοι κανόνες ανταγωνισμού, ώστε οι Ευρωπαίοι παραγωγοί να μη βρεθούν αντιμέτωποι με αθέμιτες πρακτικές.

Η Ευρώπη χρειάζεται αξιόπιστους εταίρους. Αυτή πρέπει να είναι η πυξίδα της ευρωπαϊκής εμπορικής πολιτικής μας.
2-0256-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the strategic partnership agreement between the European Union and Mexico is certainly an important step towards a stronger, democratic and resilient partnership in a period of very large geopolitical realignments. But it is not enough to just talk about more trade. Trade must be accompanied by strong guarantees on human rights, environmental protection, workers' rights and the fight against corruption.

For us in Greece but also in Europe, the agreement can create new opportunities for the export of quality agri-food products and for our small and medium enterprises. However, it is crucial to ensure the effective protection of European geographical indications and to observe equal competition rules, so that European producers are not faced with unfair practices.

Europe needs reliable partners. This must be the compass of our European trade policy.

2-0257-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, yo también celebro la modernización del Acuerdo con México, un país con el que nos unen profundos vínculos y uno de los dos socios estratégicos de la Unión Europea en América Latina.

Espero que esta modernización refuerce también nuestro diálogo político y nuestra coordinación ante desafíos comunes. Pienso, por ejemplo, en la lucha contra el crimen organizado y el narcotráfico, y en el deterioro del Estado de Derecho.

El Acuerdo es una buena noticia en general, pero lamento que, finalmente, no se haya incluido un capítulo específico sobre energía: habría sido conveniente para dar seguridad jurídica a la inversión europea en este sector de tanta importancia en México. Espero que la revisión a los tres años incluya una regulación de esta materia.

Me preocupa —señor comisario, usted lo sabe— la liberalización completa de las exportaciones mexicanas de conservas de atún a partir del séptimo año. Es un producto muy sensible para determinadas regiones de la Unión y México tiene un gran potencial exportador. La Comisión debe vigilar la evolución del volumen de estas importaciones. El sector conservero europeo está muy preocupado por el efecto acumulativo de estas concesiones a la conserva de atún en los acuerdos comerciales: ahora es México, mañana serán países del sudeste asiático, grandes productores. La Comisión tiene que ser cuidadosa en estas negociaciones.
2-0257-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I also celebrate the modernization of the Agreement with Mexico, a country with which we have deep ties and one of the two strategic partners of the European Union in Latin America.

I hope that this modernization will also strengthen our political dialogue and our coordination in the face of common challenges. I think, for example, of the fight against organized crime and drug trafficking, and the deterioration of the rule of law.

The Agreement is good news in general, but I regret that, finally, a specific chapter on energy has not been included: it would have been convenient to give legal certainty to European investment in this sector of such importance in Mexico. I hope that the three-year review includes regulation of this matter.

I am concerned—Mr. Commissioner, you know this—about the complete liberalization of Mexican exports of canned tuna starting in the seventh year. It is a very sensitive product for certain regions of the Union and Mexico has great export potential. The Commission must monitor the evolution of the volume of these imports. The European canning sector is very concerned about the cumulative effect of these concessions on canned tuna in trade agreements: now it is Mexico, tomorrow it will be Southeast Asian countries, large producers. The Commission has to be careful in these negotiations.

2-0258-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Wir sprechen heute über ein Abkommen, auf das wir lange und geduldig hingearbeitet haben: unsere neue Partnerschaft mit Mexiko. Fast zehn Jahre Verhandlungen, und seit dem 22. Mai liegt das Ergebnis unterschrieben vor uns. Das ist mehr als ein technisches Abkommen; es ist ein starkes Signal der Partnerschaft. Ich denke dabei an die vielen mittelständischen Unternehmen in Europa, die genau solche Abkommen als ein Signal brauchen – weniger Zölle und praktische Hürden im Unternehmensalltag, weniger Wartezeit an der Grenze und mehr Verlässlichkeit beim Exportieren.

Wir leben in einer Zeit, in der Lieferketten zerbrechen können und Handelspartner nicht mehr selbstverständlich verlässlich sind. Umso wichtiger, dass wir mit Mexiko einen Partner haben, mit dem uns schon seit über 25 Jahren eine gute Zusammenarbeit verbindet. Über 45 000 Unternehmen, die meisten davon klein und mittelständisch, werden von diesem Abkommen profitieren, durch einfachere Zollverfahren, klare Investitionsregeln, geschützte Herkunftsbezeichnungen. Und wir öffnen unsere Märkte, ohne unsere Standards preiszugeben – verbindliche Verpflichtungen bei Arbeitnehmerrechten und Umweltschutz, hohe Anforderungen an Lebensmittelsicherheit.

Aber, auch das ist zu bedenken: Das Vertrauen in Rechtsstaatlichkeit und Institutionen in Mexiko ist ausbaubar. Darauf müssen wir hinweisen. Trotzdem bin ich froh, dass wir über das Abkommen abstimmen, und bitte Sie deswegen um Ihre Zustimmung.
2-0258-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Today we are talking about an agreement that we have worked long and patiently towards: our new partnership with Mexico. Almost ten years of negotiations, and the result has been signed before us since May 22nd. This is more than a technical agreement; it is a strong signal of partnership. I'm thinking of the many medium-sized companies in Europe that need exactly such agreements as a signal - fewer tariffs and practical hurdles in everyday business life, less waiting times at the border and more reliability when exporting.

We live in a time in which supply chains can break down and trading partners are no longer naturally reliable. It is all the more important that we have a partner in Mexico with whom we have had a good working relationship for over 25 years. Over 45,000 companies, most of them small and medium-sized, will benefit from this agreement, through simpler customs procedures, clear investment rules, protected designations of origin. And we open our markets without sacrificing our standards – binding commitments on labor rights and environmental protection, high demands on food safety.

But this is also something to consider: trust in the rule of law and institutions in Mexico can be improved. We have to point this out. Nevertheless, I am glad that we are voting on the agreement and therefore ask for your approval.

2-0259-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Auf der Tagesordnung steht jetzt EU‑Mexiko – das klingt wie ein Fußballspiel in Tagen wie diesen, aber das ist es diesmal nicht. Die EU ist ja auch noch mit vielen Mannschaften im Rennen, unter anderem der Mannschaft von Belgien, dem Heimatland unserer europäischen Hauptstadt.

Diesmal geht es um Kooperation, und das ist es, wofür ich immer und immer wieder eintrete. In einer Welt voller Konfrontation, wo viele auch versuchen, ihre Ziele durch mehr und mehr Konfrontation zu erreichen, müssen wir die Kooperation suchen, auch weil das die Lehre aus der europäischen Geschichte ist und auch weil es unserem Wohlstand und dem Wohlstand kommender Generationen umso mehr dienen wird.

Mexiko teilt vieles mit uns: die Werte unserer Zivilisation; Mexiko ist ein verlässlicher Partner, und auf kontinentaler Ebene ist eindeutig Europa der verlässlichste Partner in der heutigen Welt. Daher ist es für beide Seiten gut, dass wir Wohlstand möglich machen, Wachstum möglich machen und das Abkommen mit Mexiko modernisieren.
2-0259-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! EU‑Mexico is now on the agenda – it sounds like a football match in days like these, but it isn't this time. The EU is still in the running with many teams, including the team from Belgium, the home country of our European capital.

This time it's about cooperation, and that's what I stand for over and over again. In a world full of confrontation, where many are trying to achieve their goals through more and more confrontation, we must seek cooperation, also because that is the lesson of European history and also because it will serve our prosperity and the prosperity of future generations all the more.

Mexico shares many things with us: the values ​​of our civilization; Mexico is a reliable partner, and on a continental level, Europe is clearly the most reliable partner in today's world. It is therefore good for both sides that we make prosperity possible, make growth possible and modernize the agreement with Mexico.

2-0262-0000.sourceText:
Paní předsedající, vážený pane komisaři, vážení kolegové, modernizace globální dohody mezi EU a Mexikem je další ze série liberalizací obchodu mezi EU a druhou stranou. A tak jako předchozí liberalizace je i tato namířena především na škodu našich pracujících. Opravdu nestačí, že si pracovní místa v automobilovém průmyslu likvidujeme zelenou transformací? Musíme se nyní snažit usnadnit přesouvání naší výroby do Mexika, kde mimochodem tak silná environmentální opatření neplatí? Jaký je k tomu důvod? Komu má toto pomoci, kromě několika nejbohatších? Lidem, co pracují v automobilkách tady v Evropě určitě ne, a životnímu prostředí, kvůli kterému si tady tento průmysl likvidujeme, to také jen uškodí.

Ale za skutečnou drzost považuji opět pokus obejít členské státy a jejich parlamenty s umístěním obchodní části dohody do prozatímní dohody, tedy tato část může fakticky platit i přes možný nesouhlas některého demokraticky zvoleného sboru. Pro mantru volného obchodu zde necháte likvidovat místní průmysl, životní prostředí i demokratické zásady a suverenitu členských států. Tato logika by skutečně měla skončit.
2-0262-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, the modernization of the EU-Mexico Global Agreement is another in a series of trade liberalizations between the EU and the other party. And just like the previous liberalization, this one is aimed primarily at the detriment of our workers. Is it really not enough that we are eliminating jobs in the automotive industry with the green transformation? Do we now have to try to make it easier to move our production to Mexico, where, by the way, such strong environmental measures do not apply? What is the reason for this? Who is this supposed to help, except the richest few? Certainly not for the people who work in car factories here in Europe, and it will only harm the environment, for the sake of which we are destroying this industry here.

But I consider the attempt to bypass the member states and their parliaments by placing the commercial part of the agreement in the interim agreement to be a real audacity, so this part can actually apply despite the possible disapproval of some democratically elected assembly. For the mantra of free trade, you will have the local industry, the environment and the democratic principles and sovereignty of the member states liquidated here. This logic really should end.

2-0265-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en primer lugar, como ponente, lo primero que querría hacer es reconocer la fantástica cooperación entre la Comisión de Asuntos Exteriores y la Comisión de Comercio Internacional, especialmente con Borja Jiménez Larraz, que ha sido su ponente, y con coponentes de Grupos diferentes, pero que han trabajado con visiones con un objetivo común —aun con matices—: el fortalecimiento de las relaciones entre la Unión Europea y México. No solo hemos trabajado con Borja Jiménez Larraz, sino también con todos los ponentes alternativos que han contribuido a una mejor resolución y a hacer un buen trabajo en el Parlamento.

Destacaría tres mensajes políticos. Uno: la diversificación de nuestra economía es una póliza de seguros geopolítica. Con esto estamos dando un paso hacia delante para nuestra diversificación económica. También lo hace México, que apuesta por su diversificación. Además, gracias al buen trabajo y la fantástica cooperación que siempre tienen el comisario Šefčovič y el Parlamento, hoy tenemos en marcha una batería de acuerdos de asociación —algunos de ellos importantes— con la región. Son acuerdos que van a apostar por esta diversificación. Es importante estratégicamente para la Unión Europea.

Dos: se ha hablado sobre los retos y algunos problemas que tiene México. No solo los tiene México, nosotros también tenemos algunos de ellos.
