Y, además, muchos de ellos no han aparecido ahora o en los últimos años, sino que han estado ahí durante largo tiempo. Lo importante para el Parlamento y para Europa es enviar el mensaje de que el Acuerdo Global Modernizado va a ayudarnos a afrontar conjuntamente los retos comunes y a cooperar para ser más eficaces. Entre los retos, obviamente, se encuentran el crimen organizado, fortalecer la seguridad, la transición ecológica, la transición digital, tener una verdadera prosperidad compartida... Lo que no hacemos es valorar las leyes que decide otro Parlamento, pues es otro Parlamento quien tiene que decidir los resultados de forma plural y diversa en función de las elecciones. Lo digo porque también el pueblo mexicano ha dejado bastante claro cuál es su opinión sobre las decisiones que toman sus autoridades.

En último lugar, todos coincidimos en que México es un socio fiable con el que compartimos valores y, por eso, mañana tendrá en esta Cámara un apoyo muy mayoritario en la votación, como tuvo unanimidad en el Consejo Europeo, con pluralidad de Gobiernos y colores políticos.
2-0265-0000.englishText:
Madam President, first of all, as rapporteur, the first thing I would like to do is recognize the fantastic cooperation between the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on International Trade, especially with Borja Jiménez Larraz, who has been your rapporteur, and with co-rapporteurs from different groups, but who have worked with visions with a common objective - even with nuances -: the strengthening of relations between the European Union and Mexico. We have not only worked with Borja Jiménez Larraz, but also with all the shadow rapporteurs who have contributed to a better resolution and to doing a good job in Parliament.

I would highlight three political messages. One: diversifying our economy is a geopolitical insurance policy. With this we are taking a step forward for our economic diversification. So does Mexico, which is committed to its diversification. Furthermore, thanks to the good work and fantastic cooperation that Commissioner Šefčovič and Parliament always have, today we have a battery of association agreements in place – some of them important – with the region. They are agreements that are going to bet on this diversification. It is strategically important for the European Union.

Two: we have talked about the challenges and some problems that Mexico has. Not only does Mexico have them, we also have some of them. And, furthermore, many of them have not appeared now or in recent years, but have been there for a long time. The important thing for Parliament and for Europe is to send the message that the Modernized Global Agreement will help us to jointly face common challenges and cooperate to be more effective. Among the challenges, obviously, are organized crime, strengthening security, the ecological transition, the digital transition, having true shared prosperity... What we do not do is evaluate the laws that another Parliament decides, since it is another Parliament that has to decide the results in a plural and diverse way based on the elections. I say this because the Mexican people have also made it quite clear what their opinion is about the decisions made by their authorities.

Lastly, we all agree that Mexico is a reliable partner with whom we share values ​​and, therefore, tomorrow it will have a very majority support in this House in the vote, as it had unanimity in the European Council, with a plurality of Governments and political colors.

2-0266-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en primer lugar, yo también querría dar las gracias al comisario por este afán y este objetivo que se ha marcado de diversificar las relaciones comerciales, que creo que es algo que es fundamental, y, por supuesto, por la colaboración con el ponente —con Javi López— durante estos últimos meses.

Este Acuerdo es, en esencia, una apuesta por la apertura, por la cooperación y por el comercio basado en reglas. México y la Unión comparten mucho más que intereses económicos. Compartimos fuertes lazos: historia, tradiciones, cultura, lengua. Este es un Acuerdo que refuerza además nuestra posición global, que mejora nuestra competitividad. Es también un mensaje claro: Europa sigue apostando por el comercio basado en reglas, frente al proteccionismo y al cierre de mercados.

Esta es, además, una oportunidad para consolidar una relación estratégica en Iberoamérica, pero también quiero insistir en que este nuevo nivel de relación exige honestidad y sinceridad —hablarnos claro—. Y ahí hay cuestiones que son mejorables, eso es lo que hemos venido expresando a lo largo de este debate: sin un fuerte Estado de Derecho no hay inversión, sin seguridad jurídica no hay confianza.

México y la Unión Europea comparten historia. Hoy tenemos la oportunidad de construir juntos un futuro, en un mundo en el que cada vez más actores se relacionan por medio de la imposición de la ley del más fuerte, en el que se desprecia la cooperación y el multilateralismo.

Este Acuerdo nace del convencimiento y de la determinación de quienes saben que estamos en el camino correcto. El camino de dos pueblos que se entienden, que dialogan y que saben que la cooperación es la mejor vía para generar prosperidad. Dos pueblos que creen que un orden internacional basado en reglas es la mejor inversión. Y este Acuerdo se sustenta, además, sobre una concepción básica: una Europa abierta es una Europa más libre.
2-0266-0000.englishText:
Madam President, first of all, I would also like to thank the Commissioner for this desire and this objective that he has set to diversify commercial relations, which I believe is something that is fundamental, and, of course, for the collaboration with the rapporteur – with Javi López – during these last months.

This Agreement is, in essence, a commitment to openness, cooperation and trade based on rules. Mexico and the Union share much more than economic interests. We share strong ties: history, traditions, culture, language. This is an Agreement that also reinforces our global position, which improves our competitiveness. It is also a clear message: Europe continues to support trade based on rules, in the face of protectionism and the closure of markets.

This is also an opportunity to consolidate a strategic relationship in Ibero-America, but I also want to insist that this new level of relationship requires honesty and sincerity—to speak clearly to each other. And there are issues that can be improved, that is what we have been expressing throughout this debate: without a strong rule of law there is no investment, without legal security there is no trust.

Mexico and the European Union share history. Today we have the opportunity to build a future together, in a world in which more and more actors relate through the imposition of the law of the strongest, in which cooperation and multilateralism are despised.

This Agreement is born from the conviction and determination of those who know that we are on the right path. The path of two peoples who understand each other, who dialogue and who know that cooperation is the best way to generate prosperity. Two peoples who believe that a rules-based international order is the best investment. And this Agreement is also based on a basic concept: an open Europe is a freer Europe.

2-0267-0000.sourceText:
Die gemeinsame Aussprache ist geschlossen.

Die Abstimmung findet morgen, Mittwoch, 8. Juli 2026, statt.

Schriftliche Erklärungen (Artikel 178)
2-0267-0000.englishText:
The joint debate is closed.

The vote will take place tomorrow, Wednesday, July 8, 2026.

Written declarations (Article 178)

2-0269-0000.sourceText:
Als nächster Punkt der Tagesordnung folgt die Aussprache über die Erklärungen des Parlaments zu den Folgen der türkischen Invasion von 1974 für zyprische Frauen und Mädchen, den von den türkischen Streitkräften verübten Verbrechen und den Konsequenzen für die Gleichstellung der Geschlechter (2026/2617(RSP)).

Ich weise die Mitglieder darauf hin, dass es bei dieser Aussprache nur eine Rednerrunde der Fraktionen geben wird. Deshalb werden weder spontane Wortmeldungen noch blaue Karten akzeptiert.
2-0269-0000.englishText:
The next item on the agenda is the debate on Parliament's statements on the consequences of the 1974 Turkish invasion on Cypriot women and girls, the crimes committed by the Turkish armed forces and the consequences for gender equality (2026/2617(RSP)).

I would point out to Members that there will only be one round of speakers from the political groups in this debate. Therefore, neither spontaneous requests to speak nor blue cards are accepted.

2-0270-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, αγαπητοί συνάδελφοι, δεν είναι μόνο το ψήφισμα για την Κύπρο που σας ζητώ να στηρίξετε. Είναι η ιστορία πίσω από το ψήφισμα. Είναι οι γυναίκες, τα κορίτσια, εκείνες που έφυγαν, εκείνες που είναι ακόμα εδώ, εκείνες που συναντήσαμε πριν από έναν χρόνο στην αποστολή μας, εκείνες που μας διηγήθηκαν τα πιο σκοτεινά γεγονότα βίας, απόγνωσης, εξευτελισμού και κακοποίησης· εκείνες που το 1974 ήταν ακόμα ανήλικα κορίτσια, έγκυες γυναίκες, νιόπαντρες κόρες, μητέρες, γιαγιάδες, και βασανίστηκαν, βιάστηκαν, κακοποιήθηκαν από τους Τούρκους εισβολείς.

Οι γυναίκες που συναντήσαμε πέρυσι έσπασαν τη σιωπή τους για πρώτη φορά 51 χρόνια μετά. Πολλές από αυτές μάς είδαν κρυφά από τους άντρες και τα παιδιά τους. Παραδέχτηκαν πως δεν έχουν μιλήσει ποτέ, είτε από φόβο είτε από ντροπή, γιατί ο βιασμός τους δεν τελείωσε τότε. Συνεχίστηκε από το στίγμα, την απομόνωση, την περιθωριοποίηση, την απόρριψη, τη μοναξιά. Οι γυναίκες που συναντήσαμε μίλησαν για όλες εκείνες που θα μείνουν για πάντα καταδικασμένες στη σιωπή. Εμείς, πάλι, δεν μπορούσαμε να πούμε πολλά. Οι λέξεις δεν έβγαιναν. Ήταν οι λυγμοί που κυριαρχούσαν και τα δάκρυα που μας ένωναν εκείνες τις ώρες.

Πριν αποχωρήσουμε από την Κύπρο, δώσαμε μια υπόσχεση: ότι θα κάνουμε τις κραυγές των γυναικών αυτών να ακουστούν παντού και δυνατά· ότι θα δώσουμε όλο μας το είναι για να αναγνωριστούν και εκείνες και όλες, και τότε και τώρα, ως θύματα εγκλημάτων πολέμου. Για να φροντίσει κάποιος επιτέλους, έστω και αργά, αυτές τις ανοιχτές πληγές. Για να αναγνωριστεί ο βιασμός ως όπλο σε περιοχές συγκρούσεων. Για να πληρώσει η Τουρκία αποζημιώσεις για τα θύματα και να στείλουμε δυνατά το μήνυμα πως όλα όσα έκανε δεν μπορούν να ξεχαστούν επειδή ανήκουν στο παρελθόν.

Δώσαμε μια υπόσχεση πως ο πόνος αυτών των γυναικών, το συλλογικό τραύμα των Κυπρίων, δεν θα παραμείνει ούτε βουβό ούτε αόρατο. Δεν είναι λοιπόν το ψήφισμα που σας καλώ να στηρίξετε, αγαπητοί συνάδελφοι. Είναι η ιστορία που έχει ήδη γραφτεί. Είναι η ψυχή, η ανάγκη για δικαίωση των θυμάτων, η υπόσχεση που δώσαμε, οι γυναίκες της Κύπρου που σας ζητώ να στηρίξετε.
2-0270-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, it is not only the resolution on Cyprus that I am asking you to support. It's the story behind the resolution. They are the women, the girls, those who left, those who are still here, those we met a year ago in our mission, those who told us the darkest events of violence, despair, humiliation and abuse; those who in 1974 were still minor girls, pregnant women, newly married daughters, mothers, grandmothers, and were tortured, raped, abused by the Turkish invaders.

The women we met last year broke their silence for the first time in 51 years. Many of them saw us secretly from their husbands and children. They admitted that they have never spoken, either out of fear or shame, because their rape did not end then. Continued by stigma, isolation, marginalization, rejection, loneliness. The women we met spoke of all those who will forever be condemned to silence. We, again, could not say much. The words wouldn't come out. It was the sobs that dominated and the tears that united us in those hours.

Before we left Cyprus, we made a promise: that we will make the cries of these women heard everywhere and loudly; that we will give our all so that they and all of them, then and now, are recognized as victims of war crimes. For someone to finally, if only slowly, tend to these open wounds. To recognize rape as a weapon in conflict zones. For Turkey to pay reparations for the victims and to send a strong message that everything he did cannot be forgotten because it belongs to the past.

We made a promise that the pain of these women, the collective trauma of Cypriots, will not remain silent or invisible. So it is not the resolution that I am asking you to support, dear colleagues. It is history that has already been written. It is the soul, the need for justice for the victims, the promise we made, the women of Cyprus that I ask you to support.

2-0271-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il 1974 fu un anno di violenza senza precedenti per la popolazione di Cipro.

L'invasione turca fece dell'isola un teatro di massacri e orrori contro la popolazione civile, con una ferocia inaudita. Lo stupro fu usato su larga scala come strumento di guerra e a farne le spese furono le donne e le bambine dell'isola.

Le forze turche condussero sistematicamente stupri di gruppo e violenze su donne greco‑cipriote dai 12 ai 70 anni. Le forze parlamentari fasciste di EOKA‑B violentarono e massacrarono la popolazione femminile di interi villaggi turco‑ciprioti.

Come in molti, troppi scenari di guerra, i responsabili sono rimasti impuniti e le vittime, nella maggior parte dei casi, non hanno avuto accesso a cure sanitarie e psicologiche adeguate.

Il 1974 a Cipro non è un evento isolato: si inserisce nel solco storico dell'uso dello stupro come arma di guerra, un abominio che ancora oggi qualcuno cerca di trattare come "casi isolati", "effetti collaterali". Ma non è così. La violenza di genere nei conflitti armati è un orrore sistematico e deliberato, che può e deve essere combattuto percorrendo due strade: assicurare alla giustizia i carnefici e offrire un supporto reale per le vittime.

Anche oggi, dall'Ucraina al Sudan, alla Palestina, le vittime di stupro ci chiedono giustizia e ci chiedono assistenza. Anche oggi, in Europa, abbiamo il dovere di garantire alle vittime di violenza di genere, incluse le donne e le bambine rifugiate, pieno accesso gratuito ai servizi di salute riproduttiva, incluso l'aborto e il trattamento delle malattie veneree. Abbiamo il dovere di portare in tribunale i criminali di guerra perseguibili sotto la giurisdizione universale e i ricercati dalla Corte penale internazionale dell'Aia.

Non è solo per rispetto del diritto: è l'unico modo per rispettare la dignità delle vittime in tutto il mondo, quelle passate e quelle future. Perché l'impunità dello stupro alimenta la cultura dello stupro e, invece, noi chiediamo giustizia per quello che è successo nel 1974 a Cipro, per quello che succede oggi, chiediamo giustizia perché non vogliamo più piangere le vittime di domani.
2-0271-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, 1974 was a year of unprecedented violence for the population of Cyprus.

The Turkish invasion made the island a theater of massacres and horrors against the civilian population, with unprecedented ferocity. Rape was used on a large scale as an instrument of war and the women and girls of the island paid the price.

Turkish forces systematically conducted gang rapes and violence against Greek Cypriot women aged 12 to 70 years. The fascist parliamentary forces of EOKA-B raped and massacred the female population of entire Turkish-Cypriot villages.

As in many, too many war scenarios, those responsible went unpunished and the victims, in most cases, did not have access to adequate health and psychological care.

1974 in Cyprus is not an isolated event: it fits into the historical wake of the use of rape as a weapon of war, an abomination that even today some people try to treat as "isolated cases", "collateral effects". But that's not the case. Gender-based violence in armed conflicts is a systematic and deliberate horror, which can and must be fought along two paths: bringing the perpetrators to justice and offering real support for the victims.

Even today, from Ukraine to Sudan, to Palestine, rape victims ask us for justice and ask us for assistance. Even today, in Europe, we have a duty to guarantee victims of gender violence, including refugee women and girls, full free access to reproductive health services, including abortion and the treatment of venereal diseases. We have a duty to bring to court war criminals prosecutable under universal jurisdiction and those wanted by the International Criminal Court in The Hague.

It's not just out of respect for the law: it's the only way to respect the dignity of victims around the world, both past and future. Because the impunity of rape fuels rape culture and, instead, we ask for justice for what happened in 1974 in Cyprus, for what happens today, we ask for justice because we no longer want to mourn the victims of tomorrow.

2-0272-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, «Οι νεκροί βρομούσαν από ένα μίλι μακριά. Ήταν ανελέητο το τελευταίο καλοκαίρι. Τρυπούσε τους ίσκιους των δέντρων, τις στέγες των σπιτιών. Φριχτό καλοκαίρι για τους ανθρώπους. Μπάσαν τους νεκρούς από την πίσω πόρτα στον Άη Γιάννη· δεν τους χωρούσαν, λέει, τα φέρετρα. Και ο πιτσιρικάς, πήχτρα το αίμα στα ρούχα του, άνοιγε λάκκους, τον χτυπούσε ο ήλιος ανελέητα στους κροτάφους, στη μνήμη βαθιά ως το μέλλον. Τον ήξερες αλλιώτικα τον κυπριώτικο ήλιο, θεία Μαρίνα, την αυγή με τα περιστέρια στους ώμους.» Λεύκιος Ζαφειρίου.

Κι όμως, στις 20 Ιουλίου 2026 συμπληρώνονται 52 ολόκληρα χρόνια που η ψυχή του Ελληνισμού με την αρπαγή της μισής Κύπρου μαύρισε για πάντα. Οικογένειες ξεριζώθηκαν, γυναίκες βιάστηκαν, άνδρες άνανδρα δολοφονήθηκαν από τον Τούρκο εισβολέα κατακτητή. Χιλιάδες οι αγνοούμενοι που πίσω τους έχουν μάνες, γυναίκες, αδελφές και κόρες που ακόμα περιμένουν να τους δοθούν οι σοροί τους. Γυναίκες, μητέρες και κορίτσια βιάστηκαν και βασανίστηκαν από Τούρκους στρατιώτες με κτηνώδη τρόπο.

Και εσείς εδώ αυτούς τους άνανδρους δολοφόνους, που συνεχίζουν έως και σήμερα να απειλούν την Ελλάδα, την Κύπρο μας και το Ισραήλ, θέλετε να τους βάλετε στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, και δεν ντρέπεστε. Για τον Ρώσο εισβολέα ξέρουμε να μιλάμε και να κάνουμε το σωστό· για τον Τούρκο εισβολέα όμως ξέρουμε μόνο να κάνουμε τα στραβά μάτια. Και η Κύπρος μας, η Αμμόχωστος, η Κερύνεια, η Καρπασία, η Μόρφου, ο Καραβάς, το Ριζοκάρπασο; Ακόμα εκεί τα αγιασμένα με αίμα εδάφη μας κάτω από τον Τούρκο εισβολέα. Κι εσείς μόνο σιωπή, μπουκωμένοι από τα βρόμικα χρήματα του κατακτητή. Ντροπή σας!
2-0272-0000.englishText:
Madam President, “The dead stank from a mile away. It was relentless last summer. It pierced the shadows of the trees, the roofs of the houses. Horrible summer for humans. They brought the dead through the back door to Ai Giannis; the coffins, he says, could not fit them. And the young man, blood soaked in his clothes, opened pits, the sun hit him mercilessly on the temples, in the memory deep into the future. You knew the Cypriot sun in another way, Aunt Marina, the dawn with the doves on your shoulders." Lefkios Zafiriou.

And yet, on July 20, 2026, it will be 52 whole years since the soul of Hellenism was blackened forever with the seizure of half of Cyprus. Families were uprooted, women raped, men brazenly murdered by the invading Turkish conqueror. Thousands of the missing have behind them mothers, wives, sisters and daughters who are still waiting for their bodies to be given to them. Women, mothers and girls were raped and tortured by Turkish soldiers in a brutal manner.

And you here, these cowardly murderers, who continue to this day to threaten Greece, our Cyprus and Israel, want to put them in the European Union, and you are not ashamed. To the Russian invader we know how to speak and do the right thing; to the Turkish invader we only know how to turn a blind eye. And our Cyprus, Famagusta, Kyrenia, Karpasia, Morphou, Karavas, Rizokarpaso? Still there our blood-sanctified lands under the Turkish invader. And you only silence, stuffed by the dirty money of the conqueror. Shame on you!

2-0273-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, σήμερα επαναφέρουμε στις μνήμες όλων μας ένα έγκλημα πολέμου που έμεινε ξεχασμένο: τους βιασμούς και τη σεξουαλική βία που υπέστησαν οι γυναίκες και τα κορίτσια της Κύπρου κατά την τουρκική εισβολή του '74. Υπενθυμίζουμε σε όλους ότι σε ένα κράτος μέλος της Ένωσης, 52 χρόνια μετά, ο πόνος παραμένει ανεξίτηλος, το δράμα αδικαίωτο, η μνήμη άσβεστη, η κατοχή συνεχιζόμενη.

Ενώ θα έπρεπε να μιλάμε για το αυτονόητο, είμαστε εδώ για να επαναφέρουμε την κοινή λογική. Αποτελεί ντροπή ότι ανώτατοι αξιωματούχοι της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, η κ. Kallas και η κ. Kos, επέλεξαν πριν λίγες μέρες να παρουσιάσουν την Τουρκία ως βασικό στρατηγικό εταίρο, μιλώντας για εμβάθυνση της συνεργασίας. Η στάση τους αυτή είναι προσβολή απέναντι στις γυναίκες που σήμερα δηλώνουμε ότι υπερασπιζόμαστε. Προσβολή απέναντι στις ίδιες τις αξίες της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης. Οι γυναίκες της Κύπρου είναι περήφανες και δεν εκλιπαρούν. Απαιτούν δικαιοσύνη και λογοδοσία. Όχι λήθη και υποκρισία.
2-0273-0000.englishText:
Madam President, today we bring back to the memories of all of us a war crime that was forgotten: the rape and sexual violence suffered by the women and girls of Cyprus during the Turkish invasion of '74. We remind everyone that in a member state of the Union, 52 years later, the pain remains indelible, the drama unjustified, the memory indelible, the occupation continuing.

While we should be talking about the obvious, we're here to restore common sense. It is a shame that high officials of the European Union, Mrs. Kallas and Mrs. Kos, chose a few days ago to present Turkey as a key strategic partner, talking about deepening cooperation. This attitude of theirs is an insult to the women who today we declare that we are defending. An insult to the very values ​​of the European Union. The women of Cyprus are proud and do not beg. They demand justice and accountability. No forgetfulness and hypocrisy.

2-0276-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, οι έμφυλες συνέπειες του πολέμου —από τις πιο ανατριχιαστικές πτυχές του— συχνά αποκρύβονται. Οι τουρκικές ένοπλες δυνάμεις το 1974 στην Κύπρο, συστηματικά και οργανωμένα, άσκησαν σεξουαλική βία σε βάρος Ελληνοκύπριων γυναικών αλλά και ανδρών κάθε ηλικίας. Ακόμα ένα στυγερό έγκλημα από την Τουρκία που παραμένει ατιμώρητο.

Πρέπει όμως να είμαστε ειλικρινείς. Βαρβαρότητες διαπράχθηκαν και από ελληνοκυπριακές παραστρατιωτικές ομάδες σε βάρος Τουρκοκυπρίων γυναικών. Ο βιασμός δεν έχει χρώμα, φυλή και θρησκεία. Τα τραύματα δύσκολα επουλώνονται. Τώρα που δειλά-δειλά ομολογούνται, ας είναι λυτρωτικά. Η Κύπρος και η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση έχουν υποχρέωση να διασφαλίσουν τα δικαιώματα, την αξιοπρέπεια και την ιστορική μνήμη όλων των γυναικών της Κύπρου. Ο κοινός πόνος να γίνει κινητήρια δύναμη για τη δικοινοτική συνεργασία και την ειρήνη στο νησί μας.
2-0276-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the gendered consequences of war—among its most chilling aspects—are often glossed over. In 1974, the Turkish armed forces in Cyprus systematically and organized sexual violence against Greek Cypriot women and men of all ages. Yet another heinous crime from Turkey that remains unpunished.

But we have to be honest. Barbarities were also committed by Greek Cypriot paramilitary groups against Turkish Cypriot women. Rape has no color, race or religion. Wounds are hard to heal. Now that they are timidly confessing, let them be redemptive. Cyprus and the European Union have an obligation to ensure the rights, dignity and historical memory of all Cypriot women. Let the common pain become a driving force for bi-communal cooperation and peace on our island.

2-0277-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Der Zypernkonflikt ist eines der Themen des heute stattfindenden NATO-Gipfels. Morgen treffen sich dazu der Präsident des Europäischen Rates, die Kommissionspräsidentin und der türkische Staatschef Erdoğan; mit einer Lösung des Zypernkonflikts ist dabei nicht zu rechnen. Während die Türkei die Zweistaatenlösung als Grundlage für weitere Verhandlungen fordert, bevorzugt die EU die Annäherung an ein Konföderationsmodell. Gerade wir Deutschen wissen, wie schwierig es ist, sich Jahrzehnte nach dem Ausbruch eines Konflikts zu versöhnen, wieder miteinander zu sprechen und sich vergeben zu können. Mit unseren polnischen Nachbarn ist uns das zu einem guten Stück gelungen: Mittlerweile kämpfen wir im Europäischen Parlament gemeinsam für ein Europa der souveränen Nationen.

Umso unverständlicher ist es, warum der FEMM-Ausschuss des Europäischen Parlaments ausgerechnet heute mit einer Entschließung zu den Übergriffen der türkischen Streitkräfte auf zypriotische Frauen und Mädchen aus dem Jahr 1974 um die Ecke kommt. Niemand möchte das Leid und die Verbrechen aus jener Zeit relativieren oder gar verharmlosen, doch hier wird erneut der Versuch unternommen, einen andauernden geopolitischen Konflikt mit EU-Richtlinien zu Gender Mainstreaming zu verknüpfen.

Eine Anhörung unter Beteiligung von gendergerechten NGOs, um damalige Zeugenaussagen im institutionellen Rahmen der EU formal anzuerkennen, eine nachträgliche Rechtfertigung von Abtreibungen, um den Schwangerschaftsabbruch in einen völkerrechtlichen Kontext zu heben, eine finanzielle und technische Unterstützung der EU für gendersensible Beratung sind nicht die vordringlichen Probleme zwischen der Türkei und Griechenland.

Erneut überschreitet der FEMM-Ausschuss seine Kompetenzen und möchte, dass dieser Konflikt gendergerecht gelesen wird. Was für eine Anmaßung! Lassen Sie uns stattdessen an einer besseren Zusammenarbeit zwischen diesen beiden NATO-Partnern arbeiten.
2-0277-0000.englishText:
Madam President! The Cyprus conflict is one of the topics at the NATO summit taking place today. Tomorrow the President of the European Council, the President of the Commission and the Turkish head of state Erdoğan will meet; A solution to the Cyprus conflict is not expected. While Turkey calls for the two-state solution as the basis for further negotiations, the EU prefers moving towards a confederation model. We Germans in particular know how difficult it is to reconcile, talk to each other again and forgive each other decades after a conflict has broken out. We have achieved this to a great extent with our Polish neighbors: we are now fighting together in the European Parliament for a Europe of sovereign nations.

It is all the more incomprehensible why the European Parliament's FEMM Committee came around the corner today of all days with a resolution on the attacks by the Turkish armed forces on Cypriot women and girls in 1974. Nobody wants to relativize or even trivialize the suffering and crimes of that time, but here again an attempt is being made to link an ongoing geopolitical conflict with EU guidelines on gender mainstreaming.

A hearing with the participation of gender-sensitive NGOs in order to formally recognize testimonies at the time within the EU's institutional framework, a subsequent justification of abortions in order to place abortion in an international legal context, and financial and technical support from the EU for gender-sensitive advice are not the most pressing problems between Turkey and Greece.

Once again, the FEMM committee is exceeding its authority and wants this conflict to be read in a gender-fair manner. What presumption! Instead, let us work on better cooperation between these two NATO partners.

2-0292-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, the more we digitize our lives, the more our society is vulnerable to cyber attacks. Where before hackers were only human beings, today we are facing bots and artificial intelligence models. These can further expose our vulnerabilities. We have seen what Anthropic's Mythos can do and in the future we will see much more powerful AI based hacking tools. This is not a matter to be taken lightly. Such situations can leave devastating repercussions: power outages, disruptions in the operation of airports or worse, in hospitals or other essential services when they are targeted.

Europe must anticipate, prepare and strengthen its defenses against AI-powered hacking. Let's use the most advanced models proactively, identifying the weaknesses of these attacks, while strengthening our digital defenses. But in this digital reality we can no longer rely solely on foreign technology to keep us safe. Let's direct the right resources and European technological talent in the right direction. Let's invest in European capabilities.

2-0293-0000.sourceText:
Pane předsedající, vážená paní komisařko, zajistit bezpečnost našich obyvatel je jednou z největších priorit, ale zároveň výzev, které v Evropské unii v současné době čelíme. A právě otázka kybernetické bezpečnosti se v dnešním světě stává stále palčivější. Nástup umělé inteligence dělá kybernetické útoky rychlejší, sofistikovanější a nebezpečnější než kdy dříve. Proto vítám akční plán Evropské komise pro kybernetickou bezpečnost a umělou inteligenci. Evropa musí být připravena chránit své občany a své podniky i svou kritickou infrastrukturu.

Současně si ale musíme přiznat jednu nepříjemnou skutečnost. Evropa v posledních letech přijímala jednu regulaci za druhou. Místo toho, abychom vytvářeli prostředí pro inovace, stali jsme se světovým lídrem v psaní pravidel. A výsledkem je prostředí, které přimělo mnoho startupů a inovativních firem přesunout svůj vývoj mimo Evropskou unii. A to opravdu není úspěch. To je spíše varování pro nás všechny. Pokud chceme být opravdu lídrem v oblasti kybernetické bezpečnosti a umělé inteligence, tak nemůžeme pouze regulovat technologie, které se vyvíjí jinde. Musíme vytvořit takové podmínky, aby tyto technologie vznikaly právě v Evropě, a proto bych měl na Komisi několik konkrétních otázek:

Jak tento akční plán zabrání dalšímu odlivu inovací z Evropské unie? Jak zajistí, že posilování kybernetické bezpečnosti nebude znamenat další administrativní zátěž pro evropské podniky, a zejména pro malé a střední firmy? A kde je stejně ambiciózní plán na podporu evropských vývojářů, startupů a technologických firem? Protože bez nich nebude Evropa nikdy technologicky soběstačná, ale bude jen regulovat technologie vyvinuté někde jinde. Jak Komise zajistí, aby citlivé bezpečnostní údaje zůstaly pod evropskou kontrolou a neopouštěly Evropskou unii? A závěrem. Podle jakých kritérií a ukazatelů bude Komise měřit úspěch tohoto akčního plánu?

Při projednávání nových pravidel kybernetické bezpečnosti máme příležitost poučit se z minulosti. Potřebujeme taková řešení, která zvýší bezpečnost, ale zároveň podpoří evropské inovace, investice a výzkum. Bezpečnost a konkurenceschopnost totiž nejsou protiklady a jedna bez druhé nemůže existovat. Bez evropských inovací totiž Evropa nebude bezpečná a suverénní.
2-0293-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, dear Commissioner, ensuring the safety of our residents is one of the biggest priorities, but also one of the challenges we are currently facing in the European Union. And it is precisely the issue of cyber security that is becoming more and more pressing in today's world. The advent of artificial intelligence is making cyber attacks faster, more sophisticated and more dangerous than ever before. That is why I welcome the European Commission's action plan for cyber security and artificial intelligence. Europe must be ready to protect its citizens and its businesses as well as its critical infrastructure.

At the same time, we have to admit one unpleasant fact. Europe has adopted one regulation after another in recent years. Instead of creating an environment for innovation, we have become a world leader in writing the rules. And the result is an environment that has forced many startups and innovative companies to move their development outside the European Union. And that's not really success. This is more of a warning to all of us. If we really want to be a leader in cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, we can't just regulate technologies that are being developed elsewhere. We need to create the conditions for these technologies to be developed in Europe, and therefore I would like to ask the Commission a few specific questions:

How will this action plan prevent a further drain of innovation from the European Union? How will they ensure that the strengthening of cyber security does not mean an additional administrative burden for European businesses, and especially for small and medium-sized enterprises? And where is the equally ambitious plan to support European developers, startups and technology firms? Because without them, Europe will never be technologically self-sufficient, but will only regulate technologies developed elsewhere. How will the Commission ensure that sensitive security data remains under European control and does not leave the European Union? And in conclusion. By what criteria and indicators will the Commission measure the success of this action plan?

When discussing new cybersecurity rules, we have an opportunity to learn from the past. We need solutions that increase security, but at the same time support European innovation, investment and research. Security and competitiveness are not opposites and one cannot exist without the other. Without European innovations, Europe will not be safe and sovereign.

2-0294-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Ta debata nie jest o cyberbezpieczeństwie i o sztucznej inteligencji. Ta debata jest dowodem klęski Unii Europejskiej w ciągu ostatnich 20-30 lat.

Europa niegdyś była kontynentem, gdzie dokonywano największych technicznych odkryć. Była kontynentem, gdzie odbywała się rewolucja przemysłowa. Była kontynentem, który dyktował rozwój praktycznie całego świata.

Dzisiaj jesteśmy wspólnotą, która ze swoich podatków dotuje biurokrację, która nie wnosi nic innowacyjnego ani nic nowoczesnego. Jedziemy wagonem drugiej klasy. Na naszych oczach odbywa się absolutna rewolucja, porównywalna z wprowadzeniem komputerów. Wpłynie ona na gospodarkę, na społeczeństwa, na każdy aspekt naszego życia. A my siedzimy w drugiej klasie, dlatego że biurokracja, regulacje i brak innowacyjności to motto dzisiejszej europejskiej biurokracji.
2-0294-0000.englishText:
Mr President! This debate is not about cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. This debate is proof of the failure of the European Union over the last 20-30 years.

Europe was once the continent where the greatest technical discoveries were made. It was the continent where the industrial revolution took place. It was a continent that dictated the development of virtually the entire world.

Today we are a community that subsidizes a bureaucracy with its taxes that brings nothing innovative or modern. We travel in a second-class carriage. An absolute revolution is taking place before our eyes, comparable to the introduction of computers. It will impact economies, societies, and every aspect of our lives. And we are in the second class because bureaucracy, regulations and lack of innovation are the motto of today's European bureaucracy.

2-0297-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária Virkkunen, a discussão sobre a cibersegurança e a inteligência artificial não é apenas uma discussão sobre a capacidade de resistir a ataques cibernéticos ou de prevenir usos prejudiciais da tecnologia.

É também, e sobretudo, uma discussão sobre o direito dos povos ao seu desenvolvimento, sobre a cooperação internacional e a partilha de conhecimento científico, sobre a capacidade de garantir a coesão, esbatendo as assimetrias nacionais, e uma discussão também sobre a garantia dos direitos fundamentais dos cidadãos em geral, incluindo nos seus dados pessoais.

É absolutamente imprescindível que seja definida de forma clara a responsabilidade dos Estados em matéria de controlo e fiscalização do funcionamento de equipamentos e redes de comunicação. Deixar essas questões nas mãos das grandes multinacionais que operam nestas áreas não é solução.

É absolutamente essencial definir estratégias nacionais de desenvolvimento científico e tecnológico, robustecer estruturas públicas de investigação e desenvolvimento, qualificar recursos humanos. Também o desenvolvimento da infraestrutura tecnológica e de comunicações tem de ser orientado para estes objetivos.
2-0297-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner Virkkunen, the discussion about cybersecurity and artificial intelligence is not just a discussion about the ability to resist cyber attacks or prevent harmful uses of technology.

It is also, and above all, a discussion about the right of people to their development, about international cooperation and the sharing of scientific knowledge, about the ability to guarantee cohesion, blurring national asymmetries, and a discussion also about guaranteeing the fundamental rights of citizens in general, including their personal data.

It is absolutely essential that the responsibility of States in terms of control and supervision of the functioning of communication equipment and networks is clearly defined. Leaving these issues in the hands of large multinationals that operate in these areas is not a solution.

It is absolutely essential to define national strategies for scientific and technological development, strengthen public research and development structures, and qualify human resources. The development of technological and communications infrastructure must also be oriented towards these objectives.

2-0301-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Viele Kolleginnen und Kollegen haben von hier aus schon darauf hingewiesen, wie hoch die Sicherheitsrisiken mittlerweile im Cyber-Raum geworden sind. Und es ist ja eine alltägliche Erfahrung mittlerweile, dass entweder kriminelle Quellen oder Drittstaaten, die es mit der Sicherheit der Europäischen Union nicht so richtig gut meinen, uns immer wieder an der Stelle angreifen. Es ist keine abstrakte Gefahr – sie ist komplex und konkret, und sie ist alltäglich.

Machen wir es mal an einem Beispiel deutlich: deutsche Offshore-Windkraftanlagen – in denen sind Sensoren verbaut aus einem Land außerhalb der EU, und sie werden von dort überwacht. Das heißt also, wenn etwas mit dieser Windkraftanlage nicht in Ordnung ist, dann melden das diese Sensoren und sie führen dazu – so wenigstens der Plan –, dass sie repariert wird. Aber in diesen Drittstaaten gibt es einen death switch, d. h. man kann diese Anlagen ausschalten, wann immer man will. Und ich finde, einer der wichtigen Sicherheitsaspekte müsste sein, dass es in Zukunft keinen death switch mehr gibt und Daten auf Servern sind, die der EU-Gesetzgebung unterliegen.
2-0301-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! Many colleagues have already pointed out how high the security risks have now become in cyberspace. And it is now an everyday experience that either criminal sources or third countries that don't really mean well with the security of the European Union repeatedly attack us on the spot. It's not an abstract danger - it's complex and concrete, and it's everyday.

Let's make it clear with an example: German offshore wind turbines - they have sensors installed in them from a country outside the EU and they are monitored from there. So that means that if there's something wrong with this wind turbine, these sensors will report it and they'll - at least that's the plan - lead to it being repaired. But in these third countries there is a death switch, i.e. h. you can turn these systems off whenever you want. And I think one of the important security aspects should be that there will no longer be a death switch in the future and that data will be on servers that are subject to EU legislation.

2-0302-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Vice-Présidente, chers collègues, alors aujourd’hui vous nous présentez le nouveau plan d’action de la Commission européenne sur la cybersécurité et l’intelligence artificielle. Les États-Unis ont Mythos, la Chine à DeepSeek, et l’Union européenne a un plan d’action. Plutôt, je dirais, un plan en réaction – encore une fois. En réaction à l’interdiction imposée par l’administration américaine d’accéder à Mythos, d’Anthropic, aux non-Américains – interdiction depuis levée.

Ce plan repose sur des formules qui sonnent comme des incantations: créer une capacité européenne des modèles d’IA, donner un cadre européen pour l’accès structuré aux capacités d’IA en cybersécurité, une énième plateforme européenne sécurisée pour tester les modèles d’IA avancés, un grand défi européen pour faire émerger des solutions de cybersécurité fondées sur l’IA.

Mais voici le paradoxe: d’un côté, la Commission met des solutions européennes – OK, très bien, on est tous d’accord –, mais, de l’autre, elle signe le traité Pax Silica, rédigé par ce sous-secrétaire d’État américain qui assume son opposition à la souveraineté numérique. Résultat: vous venez d’obliger les Européens à acheter des puces américaines et 750 milliards de dollars de GNL. Or, sans maîtrise de l’architecture des microprocesseurs ou de notre indépendance énergétique, les Américains pourront toujours nous déconnecter quand bon leur semblera.

Pourtant, une solution existe: un vrai consortium européen avec ASML, cette entreprise néerlandaise de semi-conducteurs, ou les terres rares de Guyane, mais vous avez encore choisi la dépendance. Alors, à quoi bon nous parler d’indépendance, de souveraineté, quand, de l’autre main, vous signez encore notre soumission? Les plans, c’est bien, l’action c’est mieux!
2-0302-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Vice-President, dear colleagues, today you are presenting to us the European Commission's new action plan on cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The United States has Mythos, China has DeepSeek, and the European Union has an action plan. Rather, I would say, a reaction plan – again. In response to the US administration's ban on access to Anthropic's Mythos by non-Americans – ban since lifted.

This plan is based on formulas that sound like incantations: creating a European capacity for AI models, providing a European framework for structured access to AI capabilities in cybersecurity, yet another secure European platform for testing advanced AI models, a major European challenge to bring about the emergence of cybersecurity solutions based on AI.

But here is the paradox: on the one hand, the Commission puts forward European solutions – OK, very good, we all agree – but, on the other hand, it signs the Pax Silica treaty, written by this American Under-Secretary of State who assumes his opposition to digital sovereignty. Result: you just forced the Europeans to buy American chips and $750 billion in LNG. However, without mastery of the architecture of microprocessors or our energy independence, the Americans will always be able to disconnect us whenever they want.

However, a solution exists: a real European consortium with ASML, this Dutch semiconductor company, or rare earths from Guyana, but you have still chosen dependence. So, what is the point of talking to us about independence, about sovereignty, when, with the other hand, you still sign our submission? Plans are good, action is better!

2-0303-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, la inteligencia artificial ya está teniendo impacto en todos nosotros, en nuestras relaciones personales, en nuestro negocio y en nuestra vida diaria. En todo.

Antes encontrábamos datos, comparábamos información, formábamos nuestra propia opinión. Hoy preguntamos a la IA y lo damos todo por válido, y eso puede convertirse en un gran problema, en un problema muy serio.

Si esa inteligencia artificial es atacada, manipulada o alterada de forma maliciosa, no solo estarán en riesgo nuestros datos, también estarán en riesgo nuestras opiniones, nuestras decisiones y nuestras libertades. En definitiva, estará en riesgo nuestra percepción.

Y en ciberseguridad ocurre algo parecido. Antes hablábamos de hackers intentando acceder a nuestros sistemas durante ciertas horas. Ahora tenemos bots que están intentando atacar nuestros sistemas veinticuatro horas al día, siete días a la semana, intentando aprender, adaptándose y buscando acceder a los datos más sensibles.

Por eso, Europa debe actuar, pero no puede hacerlo solo desde la regulación. Debemos facilitar la creación y —más importante— la permanencia de empresas en Europa. Debemos trabajar con la industria tecnológica, con los desarrolladores de software, con los grandes proveedores de nube, con las empresas de ciberseguridad y con quienes lideran la inteligencia artificial. Solo así estaremos por delante de quienes quieren buscar debilitar nuestras empresas, manipular a nuestros ciudadanos y socavar nuestras libertades. Protejamos Europa, pero hagámoslo...

(el presidente retira la palabra al orador)
2-0303-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, artificial intelligence is already having an impact on all of us, in our personal relationships, in our business and in our daily lives. Throughout.

Before we found data, we compared information, we formed our own opinion. Today we ask AI and we accept everything as valid, and that can become a big problem, a very serious problem.

If this artificial intelligence is attacked, manipulated or altered maliciously, not only will our data be at risk, our opinions, our decisions and our freedoms will also be at risk. Ultimately, our perception will be at risk.

And something similar happens in cybersecurity. Before we talked about hackers trying to access our systems during certain hours. We now have bots that are trying to attack our systems 24/7, trying to learn, adapt, and seeking to access the most sensitive data.

Therefore, Europe must act, but it cannot do so through regulation alone. We must facilitate the creation and – more importantly – the permanence of companies in Europe. We must work with the technology industry, with software developers, with large cloud providers, with cybersecurity companies and with those who lead artificial intelligence. Only then will we stay ahead of those who want to seek to weaken our companies, manipulate our citizens and undermine our freedoms. Let's protect Europe, but let's do it...

(the president removes the speaker from speaking)

2-0304-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, ayons confiance! Ayons confiance en nos entreprises européennes d’intelligence artificielle et investissons dès maintenant les milliards d’euros nécessaires au développement de nos propres modèles d’intelligence artificielle avancée!

La décision du président Trump de restreindre l’accès aux modèles américains d’IA les plus performants ne fait que confirmer ce que nous, libéraux et démocrates, dénoncions depuis son arrivée au pouvoir: un pays qui se sert de notre dépendance contre nous n’est pas un allié fiable. L’indépendance numérique doit être notre priorité, car c’est elle qui déterminera l’avenir de l’Europe.

Je salue les annonces que vous avez faites, Madame la Commissaire, pour notre cybersécurité face aux dangers nouveaux que représente l’IA, et nous vous soutiendrons pour toute mesure nouvelle que vous prendrez pour renforcer notre indépendance européenne dans l’intelligence artificielle et la cybersécurité.
2-0304-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, let us have confidence! Let's have confidence in our European artificial intelligence companies and invest now the billions of euros necessary to develop our own advanced artificial intelligence models!

President Trump's decision to restrict access to the most efficient American AI models only confirms what we, liberals and Democrats, have been denouncing since he came to power: a country that uses our dependence against us is not a reliable ally. Digital independence must be our priority, because it will determine the future of Europe.

I welcome the announcements you have made, Madam Commissioner, for our cybersecurity in the face of the new dangers posed by AI, and we will support you for any new measures you take to strengthen our European independence in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.

2-0306-0000.sourceText:
Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left). – Señor presidente, señorías, durante el minuto que dura mi intervención, el patrimonio de Elon Musk habrá aumentado 280 000 dólares, el de Zuckerberg 74 000 dólares, el de Bezos habrá aumentado 40 000 dólares. Insisto, solamente en un minuto.

Y mientras los oligarcas amigos de Trump se enriquecen, ¿para qué nos sirve la IA? ¿Para vivir mejor, para que los avances científicos se pongan al servicio del interés general? Pues no.

Mire, señora comisaria, hoy en la cumbre de la OTAN todos ustedes le prometerán a Donald Trump más aumento del gasto militar, más guerra y, sobre todo, también comprar precisamente servicios y sistemas de inteligencia artificial para sus amigos, los amigos de Donald Trump. Justo, por cierto, la misma semana que Donald Trump ha reconocido que sus hijos —que se dedican a fabricar drones militares— han tenido acceso a información privilegiada sobre las decisiones de Donald Trump. Supongo que también habrá tenido acceso a la información sobre cómo Trump impone a esta Europa sumisa las decisiones, a esta Europa sumisa respecto al imperialismo estadounidense.

Eso es todo lo que ustedes les ofrecen a los europeos, por parte de la Comisión Europea: guerra, más aumento del gasto militar, sumisión y mucho poder para los...

(el presidente retira la palabra a la oradora)

(La oradora se niega a que Diego Solier le formule una pregunta con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
2-0306-0000.englishText:
Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left). – Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, during the minute that my speech lasts, Elon Musk's assets will have increased by $280,000, Zuckerberg's by $74,000, and Bezos's will have increased by $40,000. I insist, only in a minute.

And while Trump's oligarch friends get rich, what good is AI for us? To live better, so that scientific advances are put at the service of the general interest? Well no.

Look, Commissioner, today at the NATO summit you will all promise Donald Trump more increases in military spending, more war and, above all, also precisely to buy artificial intelligence services and systems for your friends, Donald Trump's friends. Exactly, by the way, the same week that Donald Trump has acknowledged that his sons—who are dedicated to manufacturing military drones—have had access to privileged information about Donald Trump's decisions. I suppose you have also had access to information about how Trump imposes decisions on this submissive Europe, on this submissive Europe regarding American imperialism.

That is all that you offer to the Europeans, from the European Commission: war, more increase in military spending, submission and a lot of power for the...

(the president removes the speaker from speaking)

(The speaker refused to allow Diego Solier to ask her a question under the “blue card” procedure)

2-0307-0000.sourceText:
Marcin Sypniewski (ESN). – Panie Przewodniczący! Ta debata jest o rzeczy oczywistej. Sztuczna inteligencja może współtworzyć obronność europejską, ale może też atakować nasze systemy i wtedy jest bardzo groźna, czyli może przynosić korzyści, ale wiąże się też z ryzykiem. No i pytanie: czy naszą odpowiedzią będzie realna odporność Europy, czy kolejny segregator procedur, których już mamy wystarczająco dużo?

My dzisiaj przegrywamy wyścig technologiczny przez to, że boimy się ryzyka, mamy nadmiar regulacji, i odnoszę wrażenie, że nadal wierzymy, że innowacje da się zadekretować w Brukseli. A tak nie jest, bo rozwój nie dzieje się dzięki regulacjom. Rozwój dzieje się dzięki temu, że ludzie mają swobodę działania, i jeżeli ten nowy plan będzie oznaczał tylko nowe obowiązki, audyty i certyfikaty, na które będzie stać tylko i wyłącznie gigantów, na które będzie stać tylko wielkie korporacje, to małe europejskie firmy AI nie będą w stanie zbudować nam i zabezpieczyć nam cyberbezpieczeństwa. One po prostu wyjadą albo zostaną klientami Amerykanów i Chińczyków. A wierzę, że może być inaczej.

(Mówca nie zgodził się na pytanie zasygnalizowane przez podniesienie niebieskiej kartki przez Nicolae Ștefănuță)
2-0307-0000.englishText:
Marcin Sypniewski (ESN). – Mr. President! This debate is about the obvious. Artificial intelligence can contribute to European defense, but it can also attack our systems and then it is very dangerous, which means it can bring benefits, but it is also associated with risks. And the question is: will our answer be the real resilience of Europe, or another binder of procedures, of which we already have enough?

We are losing the technological race today because we are afraid of risk, we have too many regulations, and I have the impression that we still believe that innovations can be decreed in Brussels. But this is not the case, because development does not happen thanks to regulations. Development happens thanks to people having freedom of action, and if this new plan only means new obligations, audits and certificates that only giants will be able to afford, and only large corporations will be able to afford, then small European AI companies will not be able to build and secure our cybersecurity. They will simply leave or become customers of the Americans and Chinese. And I believe it can be different.

(The speaker disagreed with the question signaled by Nicolae Ștefănuță raising a blue card)

2-0308-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, Madame la Vice-Présidente, deux ans après le rapport Draghi, moins d’un tiers de ses recommandations ont été suivies.

Si nos infrastructures sont essentielles, l’Europe ne peut ignorer deux autres leviers stratégiques: les talents et le financement.

Nous formons d’excellents ingénieurs en cyber et en IA, mais les laissons partir peupler la Silicon Valley, affaiblissant ainsi notre capacité d’innovation. Il est temps de construire le récit d’une Europe fière de ses talents, capable de les valoriser pour les retenir. Cela passe aussi par une meilleure rémunération.

Nous devons également alléger la réglementation trop complexe qui mobilise une part excessive des budgets de mise en conformité. Quatre start-ups sur dix envisagent de quitter l’Union européenne pour cette raison.

Enfin, l’Europe doit changer d’échelle en matière de financement. Lorsque Arthur Mensch, fondateur de Mistral, lève 3 milliards, son plus petit concurrent américain, lui, lève 30 milliards.

Il est temps, chers collègues, de bâtir un véritable Nasdaq européen. Le sursaut ne peut plus attendre.
2-0308-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, Madam Vice-President, two years after the Draghi report, less than a third of its recommendations have been followed.

If our infrastructure is essential, Europe cannot ignore two other strategic levers: talent and financing.

We train excellent cyber and AI engineers, but let them populate Silicon Valley, weakening our capacity for innovation. It is time to build the story of a Europe proud of its talents, capable of promoting them in order to retain them. This also involves better remuneration.

We must also reduce overly complex regulations that take up an excessive share of compliance budgets. Four out of ten start-ups are considering leaving the European Union for this reason.

Finally, Europe must change scale in terms of financing. When Arthur Mensch, founder of Mistral, raised 3 billion, his smallest American competitor raised 30 billion.

It is time, dear colleagues, to build a true European Nasdaq. The surge can no longer wait.

2-0309-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, Colegas, imagine-se um hospital onde um médico se prepara para assistir um doente. De repente, os sistemas informáticos deixam de responder. Não, não se trata de uma falha técnica. Foi, sim, um ciberataque.

Hoje, com recurso à inteligência artificial, esse ataque pode ser preparado, adaptado e lançado em poucos minutos, mas a mesma tecnologia pode também detetar a ameaça, conter a sua propagação, impedir que os serviços essenciais sejam interrompidos.

É esta a nova realidade da cibersegurança. A inteligência artificial já não é apenas uma ferramenta de inovação, é também uma ferramenta de defesa e, infelizmente, uma ferramenta ao serviço de quem procura explorar as nossas vulnerabilidades.

A Europa tem todas as condições para liderar esta transformação, mas só o conseguirá se souber equilibrar inovação, segurança e competitividade. É precisamente por isso que o plano de ação hoje apresentado é tão importante. Precisamos de investir num verdadeiro ecossistema europeu de cibersegurança, capaz de reunir conhecimento, talento, inovação e cooperação entre os Estados-Membros.

Precisamos de apoiar as pequenas e médias empresas, reforçar a partilha de informação sobre ameaças e garantir que a segurança acompanhe o desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial, desde a conceção das tecnologias.

Quando falamos de cibersegurança, não estamos apenas a proteger computadores ou redes. Estamos a proteger hospitais, escolas, empresas, serviços públicos essenciais e, acima de tudo, as nossas pessoas.

(O orador aceita responder a uma pergunta «cartão azul»)
2-0309-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, Colleagues, imagine a hospital where a doctor is preparing to treat a patient. Suddenly, computer systems stop responding. No, this is not a technical failure. Yes, it was a cyber attack.

Today, using artificial intelligence, this attack can be prepared, adapted and launched in a few minutes, but the same technology can also detect the threat, contain its spread, and prevent essential services from being interrupted.

This is the new reality of cybersecurity. Artificial intelligence is no longer just an innovation tool, it is also a defense tool and, unfortunately, a tool at the service of those who seek to exploit our vulnerabilities.

Europe has all the conditions to lead this transformation, but it will only achieve this if it knows how to balance innovation, security and competitiveness. This is precisely why the action plan presented today is so important. We need to invest in a true European cybersecurity ecosystem, capable of bringing together knowledge, talent, innovation and cooperation between Member States.

We need to support small and medium-sized companies, strengthen the sharing of information about threats and ensure that security follows the development of artificial intelligence, right from the design of technologies.

When we talk about cybersecurity, we are not just protecting computers or networks. We are protecting hospitals, schools, businesses, essential public services and, above all, our people.

(The speaker agrees to answer a “blue card” question)

2-0310-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhor Deputado Paulo Cunha, imagine milhares de alunos à espera dos resultados dos exames nacionais por uma falha informática dos serviços do Ministério da Educação em Portugal. Não precisa de imaginar, está a acontecer.

A minha pergunta é: não vale a pena falarmos sobre grandes discursos sobre a inovação, é preciso ter responsabilidade e que a administração pública respeite os cidadãos, responda com clareza e, por isso, pergunto-lhe de quem é a responsabilidade do que está a acontecer em Portugal, que está a deixar milhares de alunos com o futuro comprometido pelos erros informáticos da administração pública na correção dos seus exames?
2-0310-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Mr Paulo Cunha, imagine thousands of students waiting for the results of national exams due to a computer failure in the services of the Ministry of Education in Portugal. You don't need to imagine, it's happening.

My question is: isn't it worth talking about big speeches about innovation, we need to have responsibility and for the public administration to respect citizens, respond clearly and, therefore, I ask you who is responsible for what is happening in Portugal, which is leaving thousands of students with their future compromised by the computer errors of the public administration in correcting their exams?

2-0311-0000.sourceText:
(início da intervenção com o microfone desligado)... informada porque não está a acontecer nada do que disse, muito menos pelas causas que invocou.

As circunstâncias são diferentes, senhora deputada. O que está em causa é uma mudança, uma evolução.

A senhora deputada prefere o imobilismo, o passadismo, a manutenção, a perseverança no erro e a recusa da inovação e da mudança.

Está em causa uma mudança e as consequências para os alunos e para as comunidades não são tão graves como aquelas que aponta.
2-0311-0000.englishText:
(beginning of the intervention with the microphone turned off)... informed because nothing like what you said is happening, much less because of the causes you invoked.

The circumstances are different, Madam Deputy. What is at stake is a change, an evolution.

The deputy prefers immobility, stalemate, maintenance, perseverance in mistakes and the refusal of innovation and change.

Change is at stake and the consequences for students and communities are not as serious as those he points out.

2-0312-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, nós tivemos oportunidade, recentemente, de falar na Comissão. Queria saudar o plano de ação, apesar de ter chegado apenas no início deste debate. Quero saudar a apresentação, porque é mais um instrumento que ajuda a que todos percebamos como os Estados-Membros devem responder com a inteligência artificial e com mais cibersegurança.

E não, eu não trouxe aqui, a este plenário, um caso utópico. Ele está a acontecer em Portugal e nós estamos a falar de sistemas críticos. E quando uma falha informática, pela implementação da transição digital, põe em causa o futuro de milhares de jovens, estamos a falar de uma transição digital que não está a cuidar da igualdade de oportunidades para todos.

E o meu apelo, Senhora Comissária, é que com este plano de ação, onde exorta os Estados-Membros a que tenham mais coordenação, eu exorto a que haja mais coordenação, maior responsabilidade e melhor capacidade de colocar a inteligência artificial ao serviço das nossas democracias, ao serviço da igualdade de oportunidades, ao serviço dos nossos cidadãos.
2-0312-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, we recently had the opportunity to speak at the Commission. I would like to welcome the action plan, despite it only coming at the beginning of this debate. I want to welcome the presentation, because it is another instrument that helps us all understand how Member States should respond with artificial intelligence and more cybersecurity.

And no, I did not bring here, to this plenary, a utopian case. It is happening in Portugal and we are talking about critical systems. And when a computer failure, due to the implementation of the digital transition, puts the future of thousands of young people at risk, we are talking about a digital transition that is not taking care of equal opportunities for everyone.

And my appeal, Commissioner, is that with this action plan, where you call on Member States to have more coordination, I call for there to be more coordination, greater responsibility and better capacity to put artificial intelligence at the service of our democracies, at the service of equal opportunities, at the service of our citizens.

2-0316-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, nel dibattito che in questi mesi si sta svolgendo sul ruolo che l'Europa dovrebbe andare a ricoprire nel campo dello sviluppo dell'intelligenza artificiale, tra chi vorrebbe un'Europa all'inseguimento di Stati Uniti e Cina e chi invece sogna un'Europa capace di valorizzare le proprie eccellenze grazie all'intelligenza artificiale, Commissaria, non sottovalutiamo il tema della sicurezza e della cibersicurezza.

Perché, se vogliamo proteggere i nostri dati, se vogliamo proteggere le nostre infrastrutture, se vogliamo proteggere le nostre aziende, l'intelligenza artificiale è e può essere un alleato fondamentale.

Nel campo della cibersicurezza – Lei lo sa molto meglio di me – l'Europa oggi non deve inseguire, non è arretrata: l'Europa oggi è leader in questo settore. Allora, grazie all'intelligenza artificiale, possiamo porci un obiettivo: diventare lo spazio digitale più sicuro al mondo.
2-0316-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, in the debate that has been taking place in recent months on the role that Europe should play in the field of the development of artificial intelligence, between those who would like a Europe in pursuit of the United States and China and those who instead dream of a Europe capable of enhancing its own excellence thanks to artificial intelligence, Commissioner, let us not underestimate the issue of security and cybersecurity.

Because, if we want to protect our data, if we want to protect our infrastructures, if we want to protect our companies, artificial intelligence is and can be a fundamental ally.

In the field of cybersecurity – you know this much better than me – Europe today must not follow, it is not backward: Europe today is a leader in this sector. Then, thanks to artificial intelligence, we can set ourselves a goal: to become the safest digital space in the world.

2-0317-0000.sourceText:
Hr. formand! Kunstig intelligens har ændret cybersikkerhed fundamentalt. Det giver os et stærkere forsvar, men det giver også vores angribere stærkere våben. Derfor har Europa brug for handling, og vi har brug for handling nu!

Den vigtigste opgave er ikke nødvendigvis – som nogen af kollegerne peger på – flere regler. Den vigtigste opgave er at sikre, at europæiske virksomheder og myndigheder faktisk har adgang til de bedste værktøjer, og med kommissærens handlingsplan har vi faktisk taget et skridt i den rigtige retning. Så tak for det!

Det er en vigtig pointe, at vi ikke skal ty til de sædvanlige europæiske løsninger her, nemlig flere regler. Cybersikkerhed er ikke kun et spørgsmål om sikkerhed, det er også blevet et spørgsmål om konkurrenceevne. Vi skal derfor have styrket den europæiske konkurrenceevne. Vi skal ikke regulere mere, vi skal investere mere i europæisk sikkerhed, europæisk AI, og det skal ske nu!
2-0317-0000.englishText:
Mr. chairman! Artificial intelligence has fundamentally changed cyber security. It gives us a stronger defense, but it also gives our attackers stronger weapons. That is why Europe needs action, and we need action now!

The most important task is not necessarily – as some of the colleagues point out – more rules. The most important task is to ensure that European companies and authorities actually have access to the best tools, and with the Commissioner's action plan we have indeed taken a step in the right direction. So thanks for that!

It is an important point that we should not resort to the usual European solutions here, namely more rules. Cyber ​​security is not only a matter of security, it has also become a matter of competitiveness. We must therefore have strengthened European competitiveness. We must not regulate more, we must invest more in European security, European AI, and it must happen now!

2-0327-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora Virkkunen, con todos los respetos, pero, de verdad: cómo nos presenta hoy aquí un plan de ciberseguridad cuando han sido jaqueados dos veces en tres meses.

En marzo les robaron 350 GB de datos de sus propios funcionarios. Y, cuando hemos preguntado, nos hemos dado cuenta de dónde guardaban toda la soberanía tecnológica europea —a ver si lo adivina la Cámara—: en Amazon, en un servidor de Seattle. Esa es la soberanía tecnológica europea.

En fin, qué ridículo es esto. El 70 % de toda la nube europea pertenece a tres empresas americanas. Eso sí, nos felicitamos por lo modernos que somos porque aquí habéis prohibido que se utilice el wifi de los diputados para usar TikTok. Es alucinante.

¿No se da usted de que son como esa típica alumna que no estudia pero va con complejo de profesora y corrige absolutamente a todos los demás sobre qué tenemos que hacer bien o mal? 100 leyes digitales, 270 reguladores, Informe Draghi. Y mientras China está fabricando chips y Estados Unidos gigantes tecnológicos, ¿qué estamos haciendo nosotros? Formularios, certificados y más... (el presidente retira la palabra al orador).
2-0327-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Mrs. Virkkunen, with all due respect, but, really: how do you present a cybersecurity plan to us here today when you have been hacked twice in three months.

In March, 350 GB of data from their own officials was stolen. And, when we asked, we realized where they kept all the European technological sovereignty - let's see if the Chamber can guess -: on Amazon, on a server in Seattle. That is European technological sovereignty.

Well, how ridiculous is this? 70% of all European cloud is owned by three American companies. Of course, we congratulate ourselves on how modern we are because here you have prohibited the use of the deputies' Wi-Fi to use TikTok. It's amazing.

Don't you realize that they are like that typical student who doesn't study but goes with a teacher complex and corrects absolutely everyone else about what we have to do right or wrong? 100 digital laws, 270 regulators, Draghi Report. And while China is making chips and the United States is making technological giants, what are we doing? Forms, certificates and more... (the president cuts off the speaker).

2-0328-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Künstliche Intelligenz wird zum entscheidenden Faktor für unsere Cybersecurity und damit auch für Europas Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, für Europas Souveränität und Resilienz. Wichtig, dass die Kommission nun einen Aktionsplan vorgelegt hat, denn eines ist klar: Europa darf bei den sogenannten Frontier‑KI‑Modellen nicht dauerhaft von Entscheidungen in anderen Drittstaaten abhängig sein.

Wenn der Zugang zu kritischen KI‑Modellen von heute auf morgen eingeschränkt werden kann, dann ist das nicht nur ein technologisches Problem, es ist vor allem ein Sicherheitsproblem für Europa. Daher habe ich auch einige Fragen an Sie: Ist eine europäische Evaluierungsstelle ab 2027 nicht zu spät? Technologische Entwicklung wartet nicht auf unsere EU‑Zeitpläne. Und wie stellen wir sicher, dass Europa bereits jetzt über die notwendigen Fähigkeiten verfügt, Risiken zu bewerten und gleichzeitig Innovationen zu ermöglichen?

Zweitens: Der Entwurf reagiert auf die Abhängigkeit von außereuropäischen KI-Modellen. Reicht ein europäischer Blueprint aus, oder braucht Europa nicht vor allem eigene leistungsfähige KI‑Modelle und Rechenkapazitäten? Und gerade die KMU liegen mir sehr am Herzen, sie verfügen aber nicht über große Rechenzentren oder über große Budgets. Wie werden wir sicherstellen, dass auch KMU einfachen Zugang zu vertrauenswürdigen europäischen KI‑Sicherheitslösungen erhalten?

Für mich ist klar: Digitale Souveränität entsteht nicht nur durch Ankündigung, sondern vor allem durch Geschwindigkeit und Wettbewerbsfähigkeit.
2-0328-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner! Artificial intelligence is becoming a decisive factor for our cybersecurity and thus also for Europe's competitiveness, for Europe's sovereignty and resilience. It is important that the Commission has now presented an action plan, because one thing is clear: Europe must not be permanently dependent on decisions in other third countries when it comes to the so-called frontier AI models.

If access to critical AI models can be restricted overnight, then this is not just a technological problem, it is above all a security problem for Europe. I therefore also have a few questions for you: Isn't a European evaluation body from 2027 too late? Technological development does not wait for our EU timetables. And how do we ensure that Europe already has the necessary skills to assess risks while enabling innovation?

Second: The draft responds to the dependence on non-European AI models. Is a European blueprint sufficient, or does Europe not primarily need its own powerful AI models and computing capacities? And SMEs in particular are very important to me, but they don't have large data centers or large budgets. How will we ensure that SMEs also have easy access to trusted European AI security solutions?

For me it is clear: Digital sovereignty comes not only through announcement, but above all through speed and competitiveness.

2-0329-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, Europa ya ha demostrado que sabe regular la tecnología. Ahora tiene que demostrar que también sabe construirla.

Si en el siglo XX la soberanía se defendía con tanques y cañones, en el siglo XXI también se defiende con algoritmos, semiconductores o datos. Hace apenas unos días, la empresa estadounidense Palantir, proveedora de tecnologías de inteligencia y defensa, afirmaba que politizar la tecnología es un error, pero decidir quién desarrolla la inteligencia artificial que protege nuestras infraestructuras críticas —hospitales, parlamentos, bancos— no es una cuestión técnica, es profundamente política y existencial. Pero, mientras todavía debatimos la soberanía tecnológica de Europa, muchos de nuestros Gobiernos financian con dinero público muchas tecnologías críticas desarrolladas fuera de la Unión Europea.

Nadie construiría una casa para darle las llaves a otro. Europa tampoco puede hacerlo con su seguridad digital. Por eso, damos la bienvenida al plan de acción sobre ciberseguridad e IA presentado por la Comisión, pero necesitamos muchos más recursos: gastar más, pero sobre todo gastar «europeo», apoyar empresas europeas y gigafactorías para construir nuestra soberanía digital.
2-0329-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Europe has already shown that it knows how to regulate technology. Now he has to show that he also knows how to build it.

If in the 20th century sovereignty was defended with tanks and cannons, in the 21st century it is also defended with algorithms, semiconductors or data. Just a few days ago, the American company Palantir, a provider of intelligence and defense technologies, stated that politicizing technology is a mistake, but deciding who develops the artificial intelligence that protects our critical infrastructures—hospitals, parliaments, banks—is not a technical issue, it is deeply political and existential. But, while we are still debating Europe's technological sovereignty, many of our governments are funding many critical technologies developed outside the European Union with public money.

No one would build a house to give the keys to someone else. Europe cannot do it either with its digital security. Therefore, we welcome the action plan on cybersecurity and AI presented by the Commission, but we need many more resources: spend more, but above all "European" spending, support European companies and gigafactories to build our digital sovereignty.

2-0330-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, geschätzte Kollegen! Wir haben ja erst letztes Mal in Straßburg hier über die Elektrifizierungsinitiative von der Kommission gesprochen, die ja auch ähnliche Ausmaße annimmt wie das, was wir jetzt sehen. Und wir sagen ganz klar Ja zum Schutz, aber Nein zu einer Brüsseler Bürokratie-Krake.

Die KI macht Cyberangriffe smarter und gefährlicher – das wissen wir. Doch dieser Aktionsplan der Kommission droht wieder einmal ein Monster an Formularen, Berichtspflichten und Gebühren zu werden. Das schützt keinen Server und hilft vor allem den kleinen Betrieben nicht; statt echter Hilfe gibt es einmal mehr Verwaltung und Zentralisierung.

Wir müssen wachsam sein: Cybersicherheit darf keine Hintertür für Massenüberwachung und Meinungskontrolle werden. Unser klarer Kurs in dieser Sache heißt Ja zu realer Sicherheit, Nein zu Papierkram und Machtkonzentration in Brüssel und zu Freiheitsabbau für die Bürger.
2-0330-0000.englishText:
Mr President, esteemed colleagues! We only spoke here last time in Strasbourg about the Commission's electrification initiative, which is of similar proportions to what we are seeing now. And we say clearly yes to protection, but no to a Brussels bureaucratic octopus.

AI is making cyberattacks smarter and more dangerous – we know that. But this Commission action plan threatens to once again become a monster of forms, reporting requirements and fees. This doesn't protect any server and especially doesn't help small businesses; Instead of real help, there is once again administration and centralization.

We must be vigilant: cybersecurity must not become a backdoor for mass surveillance and opinion control. Our clear course in this matter is yes to real security, no to paperwork and concentration of power in Brussels and to a reduction in freedom for citizens.

2-0331-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, o dronă maritimă ucraineană a fost aproape să distrugă recent portul Constanța din România, iar noi nu am avut capacitatea tehnică de a o opri. Un model de inteligență artificială controlat de forțe rău-intenționate poate paraliza o întreagă economie. Acestea sunt vulnerabilități reale ale Uniunii Europene, nu lipsa de reglementare.

Securitatea cibernetică se construiește prin investiții, prin competențe și prin tehnologii proprii. Nu putem vorbi despre suveranitate digitală câtă vreme tehnologiile critice rămân controlate din afara Uniunii. Europa trebuie să-și dezvolte propriile capacități, iar România, cu unul dintre cele mai performante ecosisteme IT din Europa, poate și trebuie să contribuie. Singura condiție este ca fondurile europene să ajungă și în estul Uniunii.

Statele membre trebuie să rămână actorii principali în securitatea națională și, nu în ultimul rând, combaterea criminalității cibernetice nu poate deveni pretext pentru supravegherea generalizată a cetățenilor.
2-0331-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, dear colleagues, a Ukrainian maritime drone recently came close to destroying the port of Constanța in Romania, and we did not have the technical ability to stop it. An AI model controlled by malicious forces can cripple an entire economy. These are real vulnerabilities of the European Union, not lack of regulation.

Cyber ​​security is built through investments, skills and proprietary technologies. We cannot talk about digital sovereignty as long as critical technologies remain controlled from outside the Union. Europe must develop its own capabilities, and Romania, with one of the best performing IT ecosystems in Europe, can and must contribute. The only condition is that the European funds also reach the eastern part of the Union.

Member States must remain the main actors in national security and, last but not least, the fight against cybercrime cannot become a pretext for general surveillance of citizens.

2-0332-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, liebe Kollegen! Von Großbanken über Mittelstand bis zur kritischen Infrastruktur – Europas Sicherheit hängt davon ab, ob KI‑Technologie hier entsteht und skalieren kann. Deshalb muss der Cybersecurity und AI Action Plan vor allem eins: Bürokratie abbauen, Investitionen ermöglichen und neue Technologien schneller in die Anwendung bringen.

Wenn in den USA und China in rasantem Tempo neue KI‑Modelle entstehen, schreibt Europa nach wie vor vor allen Dingen Regeln. Aber Cyberangriffe und technologische Abhängigkeit bekämpft man eben nicht mit Berichtspflichten, sondern mit technologischem Vorsprung. Europa wird sicherer, wenn die besten Technologien von hier kommen. Dafür brauchen wir weniger Bürokratie, mehr Kapital, günstigere Energie und einen echten europäischen Binnenmarkt, damit unsere klügsten Köpfe einfach mal machen können.
