Denn digitale Souveränität wächst nicht aus Abschottung, und Cybersecurity entsteht nicht in Gesetzestexten, sondern durch Innovation.

Hören wir auf, die Welt regulieren zu wollen! Zeigen wir der Welt endlich wieder, dass Europa sie verändern kann!
2-0332-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues! From large banks to medium-sized businesses to critical infrastructure, Europe's security depends on whether AI technology can emerge and scale here. That's why the Cybersecurity and AI Action Plan must do one thing above all: reduce bureaucracy, enable investments and bring new technologies into use more quickly.

While new AI models are emerging at a rapid pace in the USA and China, Europe is still primarily writing rules. But cyber attacks and technological dependency are not combated with reporting requirements, but with technological advances. Europe will be safer if the best technologies come from here. For this we need less bureaucracy, more capital, cheaper energy and a real European internal market so that our brightest minds can just do it. Because digital sovereignty does not grow from isolation, and cybersecurity does not arise in legal texts, but through innovation.

Let's stop trying to regulate the world! Let's finally show the world again that Europe can change it!

2-0333-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Eine Quizfrage: Wie viele Ressourcen benötigt eine Minute KI-generiertes Video? 200 Kilowattstunden. Das ist der Stromverbrauch einer Durchschnittsfamilie an zwei Tagen. Sieben Liter Wasser, sauberes Trinkwasser, das unseren Bürgerinnen und Bürgern und auch unserer Landwirtschaft nicht mehr zur Verfügung steht. Die Techkonzerne haben nicht nur extremen Hunger nach Daten, sondern auch extremen Durst nach Wasser.

Deshalb: Ja, die EU muss im Digitalsektor unabhängiger werden, aber es kann nicht sein, dass knappe Ressourcen für die Profite Weniger geopfert werden, wenn diese auch noch obendrein keine Arbeitsplätze schaffen, sondern eher welche vernichten. Kluge Menschen lernen aus ihren Fehlern; weise lernen aus den Fehlern anderer. Der wachsende Widerstand gegen Datenzentren in den USA wegen steigender Strompreise, wegen der Wasserfrage, wegen Luftverschmutzung – daraus müssen wir lernen.

Deshalb: Wir brauchen Datenzentren – ja, mit klaren Regeln –, effiziente Technologie, erneuerbare Energien, Abwärmenutzung, Transparenz, Beteiligung der Bevölkerung: Dann wird daraus was.
2-0333-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! A quiz question: How many resources does one minute of AI-generated video require? 200 kilowatt hours. This is the electricity consumption of an average family over two days. Seven liters of water, clean drinking water, which is no longer available to our citizens and also to our agriculture. The tech companies are not only extremely hungry for data, but also extremely thirsty for water.

Therefore: Yes, the EU must become more independent in the digital sector, but it cannot be the case that scarce resources are sacrificed for the profits of a few if, on top of that, these do not create jobs but rather destroy them. Smart people learn from their mistakes; wise learn from the mistakes of others. The growing resistance to data centers in the US because of rising electricity prices, because of the water issue, because of air pollution - we have to learn from that.

That's why: We need data centers - yes, with clear rules -, efficient technology, renewable energies, use of waste heat, transparency, participation of the population: then something will come of it.

2-0334-0000.sourceText:
Hr. formand! Jeg synes det er ærgerligt, at Kommissionen ikke fremlægger sine forslag i så god tid, at vi har mulighed for at læse dem, inden vi skal diskutere dem. Det synes jeg er særlig ærgerligt, fordi der også i det her forslag faktisk er positive ting omkring udviklingen af open source og en strategi for det.

Men hvis vi for alvor tager EU's cybersikkerhed alvorligt, hvorfor skulle vi så ikke starte med at lukke helt åbenlyse huller? Hvorfor skifter vi ikke hurtigt EU væk fra programmer som Outlook, Webex og Teams og fylder dem ud med europæisk forankrede open source-programmer, der sikrer vores data og digitale suverænitet? Og jeg må også sige, at vi hører også advarsler om, at retsakten om udvikling af cloudtjenester og kunstig intelligens risikerer at ende som en "continuous American dependancy act". Og vi er vel enige om, at fortsat afhængighed af USA på det her område er et alvorligt problem for vores cybersikkerhed.
2-0334-0000.englishText:
Mr. chairman! I think it is a pity that the Commission does not present its proposals in sufficient time for us to have the opportunity to read them before we have to discuss them. I think this is particularly unfortunate, because in this proposal there are actually positive things about the development of open source and a strategy for it.

But if we really take the EU's cyber security seriously, why shouldn't we start by closing obvious gaps? Why don't we quickly switch the EU away from programs like Outlook, Webex and Teams and fill them with European-rooted open source programs that secure our data and digital sovereignty? And I must also say that we are also hearing warnings that the legislation on the development of cloud services and artificial intelligence risks ending up as a "continuous American dependency act". And we probably agree that continued dependence on the US in this area is a serious problem for our cyber security.

2-0337-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, chaque apport à l’innovation technologique, chaque progrès humain s’est toujours accompagné de son lot de risques et de nouvelles vulnérabilités. L’intelligence artificielle n’y fera pas exception.

Motivés par des siècles d’expérience en matière de risques technologiques, nous serons avisés de nous assurer que l’IA ne devienne pas une nouvelle source de dépendance de nos nations. L’Europe, berceau de la révolution industrielle, fut à la pointe des grandes découvertes qui ont façonné le monde moderne. Aujourd’hui, néanmoins, nous avons raté le virage numérique, dépassés par les nouveaux géants que sont les États-Unis et la Chine, et nous ne rattraperons pas notre retard sans retrouver cet esprit européen qui fut jadis notre moteur. Or, nous connaissons tous ici la formidable capacité de la Commission européenne à innover dans un seul domaine: celui de générer toujours plus de normes, qui étouffent cet esprit créatif européen.

Alors oui, la prudence est de mise, mais pas à n’importe quel prix. Rien ne servira d’imposer des normes contraignantes à des entreprises que nous n’aurons jamais réussi à développer. Rien ne servira de parler de résilience si nous dépendons toujours de pays tiers dans les domaines des nouvelles technologies. Nous resterons donc vigilants à ce que la Commission ne se serve pas de la cybersécurité pour justifier son inaction, d’autant plus que, en risquant d’étouffer nos entrepreneurs, la Commission pourrait aussi écraser les innovations européennes en matière de cybersécurité.
2-0337-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, dear colleagues, each contribution to technological innovation, each human progress has always been accompanied by its share of risks and new vulnerabilities. Artificial intelligence will be no exception.

Motivated by centuries of experience with technological risks, we will be wise to ensure that AI does not become a new source of dependence for our nations. Europe, cradle of the industrial revolution, was at the forefront of the great discoveries that shaped the modern world. Today, however, we have missed the digital shift, overtaken by the new giants that are the United States and China, and we will not catch up without rediscovering this European spirit which was once our driving force. However, we all know here the formidable capacity of the European Commission to innovate in a single area: that of generating ever more standards, which stifle this creative European spirit.

So yes, caution is required, but not at any cost. There will be no point in imposing restrictive standards on companies that we will never succeed in developing. There will be no point in talking about resilience if we continue to depend on third countries in the areas of new technologies. We will therefore remain vigilant to ensure that the Commission does not use cybersecurity to justify its inaction, especially since, by risking stifling our entrepreneurs, the Commission could also crush European innovations in cybersecurity.

2-0341-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora vicepresidenta, gracias por la presentación de este plan de acción en un momento en el que los acontecimientos en torno al modelo Mythos ponen de manifiesto otra vez el grado de dependencia de la Unión Europea respecto al acceso externo a sistemas de IA críticos.

Dado que vemos que no es solo Anthropic quien decide conceder o denegar el acceso a modelos avanzados porque la Comisión directamente ya no pregunta a la Casa Blanca qué estrategia política seguir —parece una locura, ¿no?—, me gustaría saber cuál ha sido la conclusión de las discusiones del G7 sobre inteligencia artificial y qué ha aportado exactamente la Unión Europea en términos de cooperación para definir normas comunes sobre la inteligencia artificial y los nuevos modelos de frontera.

Teniendo en cuenta que hoy no existen normas internacionales, ¿cómo afecta esto a la aplicación del Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial —cuya aplicación ya se ha retrasado— en casos de alto riesgo? La gobernanza de IA debe desarrollarse con colaboración internacional, pero sin sustituir y priorizando nuestra capacidad para garantizar acceso, evaluación independiente y seguridad jurídica... (El presidente retira la palabra a la oradora).
2-0341-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Vice President, thank you for presenting this action plan at a time when developments around the Mythos model once again highlight the degree of dependence of the European Union on external access to critical AI systems.

Given that we see that it is not just Anthropic that decides to grant or deny access to advanced models because the Commission no longer directly asks the White House what political strategy to follow - it seems crazy, doesn't it? - I would like to know what the conclusion of the G7 discussions on artificial intelligence has been and what exactly the European Union has contributed in terms of cooperation to define common standards on artificial intelligence and new frontier models.

Taking into account that there are no international standards today, how does this affect the application of the Artificial Intelligence Regulation – the application of which has already been delayed – in high-risk cases? AI governance must be developed with international collaboration, but without replacing and prioritizing our ability to guarantee access, independent evaluation and legal certainty... (The President cuts off the speaker.)

2-0342-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président – cher Roberts Zīle –, Madame la Vice-Présidente – chère Henna Virkkunen –, les récents blocages d’accès aux modèles d’intelligence artificielle les plus avancés ont été un signal d’alarme pour l’Europe. En quelques heures, nous avons découvert à quel point notre sécurité, nos administrations, nos entreprises dépendaient de technologies que nous ne contrôlons pas.

Le plan d’action européen sur la cybersécurité, qu’on est ravis de découvrir – mais je n’ai pas d’intelligence artificielle pour le lire, je n’ai pas encore tout pu lire –, doit donc intégrer une véritable stratégie de souveraineté. Cela signifie: investir dans des capacités européennes, soutenir des modèles de confiance, garantir un accès sécurisé aux technologies les plus avancées et renforcer nos infrastructures de calcul. Cela signifie qu’il est besoin de répondre à une question essentielle: comment l’Union peut-elle faire face au risque qu’un pays tiers puisse, du jour au lendemain, restreindre l’accès de l’Europe à des technologies d’IA essentielles?

Notre objectif n’est pas de nous isoler, mais de faire en sorte que la protection de nos citoyens, de leurs données, de leurs droits fondamentaux ne dépende jamais de décisions prises en dehors de l’Union.
2-0342-0000.englishText:
Mr President – ​​dear Roberts Zīle –, Madam Vice-President – ​​dear Henna Virkkunen – the recent blockages of access to the most advanced models of artificial intelligence have been a wake-up call for Europe. In a few hours, we discovered to what extent our security, our administrations, our businesses depended on technologies that we do not control.

The European action plan on cybersecurity, which we are delighted to discover – but I do not have artificial intelligence to read it, I have not yet been able to read everything – must therefore integrate a real sovereignty strategy. This means: investing in European capabilities, supporting trust models, ensuring secure access to the most advanced technologies and strengthening our computing infrastructures. This means that a key question needs to be answered: how can the Union address the risk that a third country could, overnight, restrict Europe's access to essential AI technologies?

Our objective is not to isolate ourselves, but to ensure that the protection of our citizens, their data, their fundamental rights never depends on decisions taken outside the Union.

2-0343-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, meine sehr geehrten Damen und Herren! Wir reden heute über künstliche Intelligenz, aber in Wahrheit reden wir über Europas Zukunft, und diese Zukunft entsteht gerade woanders. Europa verfügt über lediglich rund 5 % der weltweiten KI‑Rechenkapazität; die Vereinigten Staaten von Amerika liegen bei fast 75 %. Amerikanische Digitalkonzerne investieren hunderte Milliarden in Rechenzentren, Chips, Netze und Energie. Was macht Europa? Wir prüfen, regulieren, wir verzögern.

KI braucht nicht nur gute Absichten; KI braucht Strom, Flächen, Glasfaser, Genehmigungen und Tempo, aber genau dort scheitern wir. Und wir haben auch in der Debatte schon gehört, dass das teilweise gewollt ist von den politischen Mitbewerbern. Die KI‑Verordnung, denke ich, steht für diese europäische Krankheit: Erst kommen die Auflagen, dann vielleicht irgendwann die Wertschöpfung.

So wird Europa nicht souverän werden. Wir brauchen disruptive Entscheidungen, den konsequenten Abbau jener Partikularinteressen, die wir über Jahre in Gesetze gegossen haben und die heute fast jede Zukunftsinvestition blockieren.
2-0343-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! We're talking about artificial intelligence today, but what we're really talking about is Europe's future, and that future is happening somewhere else. Europe only has around 5% of the world’s AI computing capacity; the United States is at nearly 75%. American digital companies are investing hundreds of billions in data centers, chips, networks and energy. What is Europe doing? We check, we regulate, we delay.

AI doesn't just need good intentions; AI needs power, space, fiber optics, permits and speed, but that's exactly where we fail. And we have already heard in the debate that this is partly what the political competitors want. I think the AI ​​regulation represents this European disease: first come the requirements, then perhaps at some point the added value.

This is not how Europe will become sovereign. We need disruptive decisions, the consistent dismantling of those special interests that we have cast into laws over the years and that are now blocking almost every investment in the future.

2-0344-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il "kill switch" non è più un'ipotesi: è stato premuto. A giugno, con una firma, Donald Trump ha chiuso l'accesso al modello di intelligenza artificiale più potente al mondo, anche all'Agenzia per la cibersicurezza europea, che l'aveva appena ottenuto.

Le nostre regole decidono come possiamo usare l'intelligenza artificiale in sicurezza, oggi, altri decidono se possiamo usarla: questa è la dipendenza.

Quindi, bene il piano sulla cybersecurity, ma senza fondi e scadenze vincolanti rischia di restare un elenco di intenzioni. Servono risorse per l'Ufficio europeo per l'intelligenza artificiale, che avrà sempre più responsabilità, una legge su cloud e AI davvero ambiziosa, e capacità pubblica europea e non sussidi ai giganti da cui già dipendiamo.

E nessuno si azzardi a pensare di comprare l'accesso ai modelli americani, allentando in segreto l'applicazione delle nostre leggi. La sicurezza digitale europea non va più affittata a nessuno, va costruita, con apertura, ma con determinazione, per difendere i nostri interessi.
2-0344-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, the "kill switch" is no longer a hypothesis: it has been pressed. In June, with a signature, Donald Trump closed access to the most powerful artificial intelligence model in the world, even to the European Cybersecurity Agency, which had just obtained it.

Our rules decide how we can use artificial intelligence safely today, others decide whether we can use it: this is addiction.

So, the cybersecurity plan is good, but without funds and binding deadlines it risks remaining a list of intentions. We need resources for the European Office for Artificial Intelligence, which will have ever more responsibilities, a truly ambitious law on cloud and AI, and European public capacity and not subsidies to the giants on which we already depend.

And let no one dare think of buying access to American models by secretly relaxing the application of our laws. European digital security must no longer be rented to anyone, it must be built, with openness, but with determination, to defend our interests.

2-0345-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Sehr geehrte Frau Kommissarin, ich danke Ihnen ausdrücklich für Ihren Bericht zur Sicherheit im Cyberraum und zu künstlicher Intelligenz, weil die Sicherheit im Cyberraum sich massiv verändert durch den Einsatz von künstlicher Intelligenz. Und selbstverständlich haben die Sicherheitsbehörden dort ihre Aufgabe, so wie auch im öffentlichen Raum, und natürlich muss die Politik den Rahmen gestalten, damit Sicherheitsbehörden arbeiten können.

Zu dem, was Sie aber nicht gesagt haben, Frau Kommissarin: Sie haben nichts zu Quantencomputern gesagt. Was ist die Strategie der Europäischen Union bei Quantencomputern? Wie schützen wir unsere Infrastruktur in Quantencomputer-Technologie, die auf uns zukommt?

Sie haben auch nichts dazu gesagt, dass ja neben den vielen Kriminellen, die unternehmerisch tätig sind, um andere Unternehmer zu betrügen, auch Drittstaaten ganz konkret Hacker dafür einsetzen, um die Europäische Union und ihre Mitgliedstaaten anzugreifen, ganz konkret die Bundesregierung Deutschland: Die Regierungsbehörden werden täglich mit 800 Hackerangriffen angegriffen. Da dürfen wir nicht nur reparieren, sondern müssen auch agieren; wir müssen Hackerangriffe von Drittstaaten zurück angreifen. Und da ist meine Frage: Was tun Sie dort? Haben Sie Gespräche mit Herrn Kubilius geführt?
2-0345-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! Dear Commissioner, I would like to thank you expressly for your report on security in cyberspace and artificial intelligence, because security in cyberspace is changing massively through the use of artificial intelligence. And of course the security authorities have their job there, just as they do in public spaces, and of course politics must create the framework so that security authorities can work.

As for what you didn't say, Commissioner: you didn't say anything about quantum computers. What is the European Union's strategy for quantum computers? How do we protect our infrastructure in quantum computing technology that is coming our way?

You also didn't say anything about the fact that, in addition to the many criminals who are active in business to defraud other entrepreneurs, third countries also specifically use hackers to attack the European Union and its member states, specifically the Federal Government of Germany: the government authorities are attacked with 800 hacker attacks every day. We are not only allowed to repair things, we also have to act; We have to fight back against hacker attacks from third countries. And there's my question: What are you doing there? Have you had discussions with Mr. Kubilius?

2-0346-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, l'action plan che la Commissione ha appena presentato rappresenta un passaggio non risolutivo, ma certo importante nel percorso verso la sovranità tecnologica europea.

Autonomia non è autarchia, certo, ma è protagonismo, perché l'Unione non può continuare a dipendere da processi opachi e decisioni unilaterali di paesi terzi.

E i recenti episodi legati proprio alle restrizioni sull'accesso a modelli di frontiera dimostrano quanto questa vulnerabilità sia oggi una questione di sicurezza, ancora prima che di competitività.

L'Europa, quindi, deve costruire una propria capacità tecnologica autonoma nell'intelligenza artificiale di frontiera e questo richiede una scelta politica chiara.

Oltre ai provvedimenti, però, che si stanno finalmente adottando, servono investimenti adeguati, pubblici e privati, capaci di colmare il divario con Stati Uniti e Cina.

Per questo, la scelta dei governi su un bilancio previsionale per l'Europa, che hanno fatto è un errore: è timido, è sbagliato e in parte in contraddizione con le scelte giuste che stiamo facendo.

Senza risorse concrete, non si va da nessuna parte.
2-0346-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the action plan that the Commission has just presented represents a step that is not decisive, but certainly important on the path towards European technological sovereignty.

Autonomy is not autarky, of course, but it is protagonism, because the Union cannot continue to depend on opaque processes and unilateral decisions of third countries.

And the recent episodes linked precisely to restrictions on access to frontier models demonstrate how this vulnerability is today a question of security, even before that of competitiveness.

Europe, therefore, must build its own autonomous technological capacity in frontier artificial intelligence and this requires a clear political choice.

In addition to the measures, however, which are finally being adopted, adequate public and private investments are needed, capable of bridging the gap with the United States and China.

For this reason, the governments' choice of a budget forecast for Europe, which they have made, is a mistake: it is timid, it is wrong and partly in contradiction with the right choices we are making.

Without concrete resources, you won't go anywhere.

2-0347-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, geschätzte Frau Exekutiv-Vizepräsidentin der Kommission, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! KI und Quantencomputing entscheiden darüber, ob wir wirtschaftlich erfolgreich sind. Cybersicherheit entscheidet darüber, ob wir in Zukunft überhaupt noch handlungsfähig sind. Deshalb müssen wir dringend die Weichen für die Zukunft stellen.

Es ist positiv, dass die Kommission nun diesen Aktionsplan vorgestellt hat, allerdings geht es jetzt um die Umsetzung. Und eines ist klar: Unsere KMU brauchen mehr digitale Sicherheit, schnelle Hilfe im Ernstfall und vor allem keine neuen Bürokratielasten. Europa muss digital, souverän und wettbewerbsfähig werden – mit europäischen Cloudlösungen, einer eigenen digitalen Infrastruktur und Exzellenz beim Quantencomputing. Denn wer die Schlüsseltechnologien entwickelt, sichert Wohlstand, Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Arbeitsplätze und setzt auch die Spielregeln für unsere Zukunft.

Und Cyberkompetenzen müssen auch in unsere Klassenzimmer. Sie müssen dort so selbstverständlich unterrichtet werden wie Lesen, Rechnen und Schreiben, denn die wichtigste Firewall sitzt vor den Bildschirmen.

Die Botschaft ist klar: Digitale Souveränität und Sicherheit sind keine technische Frage; sie sind die Grundlage unserer Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, unserer Sicherheit und unserer Freiheit.
2-0347-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Executive Vice-President of the Commission, dear colleagues! AI and quantum computing determine whether we are economically successful. Cybersecurity determines whether we will still be able to act in the future. We therefore urgently need to set the course for the future.

It is positive that the Commission has now presented this action plan, but it is now a matter of implementation. And one thing is clear: our SMEs need more digital security, quick help in an emergency and, above all, no new bureaucratic burdens. Europe must become digital, sovereign and competitive – with European cloud solutions, its own digital infrastructure and excellence in quantum computing. Because whoever develops the key technologies secures prosperity, competitiveness, jobs and also sets the rules for our future.

And cyber skills need to be in our classrooms too. They have to be taught there as naturally as reading, arithmetic and writing, because the most important firewall is in front of the screens.

The message is clear: digital sovereignty and security are not a technical issue; they are the basis of our competitiveness, our security and our freedom.

2-0350-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora Virkkunen, comparto este plan y, fundamentalmente, sus tres objetivos, que hablan de promover, fomentar y animar, pero, mientras en ese plan se utilizan estos verbos, la realidad es que la amenaza se está ya ejecutando en tiempo real.

Por lo tanto, me gustaría decirle que creo que es muy importante implementar la Directiva SRI 2 en el conjunto del sistema europeo. Hay que exigir, financiar y también sancionar, por qué no decirlo.

ENISA, que es el gran pilar en el que usted se basa, tiene un gran déficit y es que plantea 341 millones en siete años y, lamentablemente, en la práctica en un año o año y medio la computación cuántica va a estar aquí y eso va a ser una gran amenaza.

Fíjense, yo creo que aparte de hablar de infraestructuras críticas, también tenemos que hablar de personas. Por ejemplo, el ejemplo que dio ayer el Gobierno de España —con mi querido amigo Óscar López— al implementar una gran coalición con Francia y Kenia, junto con las Naciones Unidas, va en esa dirección, para precisamente proteger también de la IA a nuestros menores, que es un reto muy importante para el futuro.
2-0350-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Mrs. Virkkunen, I share this plan and, fundamentally, its three objectives, which speak of promoting, encouraging and encouraging, but, while these verbs are used in this plan, the reality is that the threat is already being carried out in real time.

Therefore, I would like to tell you that I think it is very important to implement the NIS Directive 2 throughout the European system. We must demand, finance and also sanction, why not say it.

ENISA, which is the great pillar on which you are based, has a great deficit and it raises 341 million in seven years and, unfortunately, in practice in a year or a year and a half, quantum computing is going to be here and that is going to be a great threat.

Look, I believe that apart from talking about critical infrastructure, we also have to talk about people. For example, the example that the Government of Spain gave yesterday - with my dear friend Óscar López - by implementing a great coalition with France and Kenya, together with the United Nations, goes in that direction, to precisely also protect our minors from AI, which is a very important challenge for the future.

2-0351-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, il piano d'azione europeo sulla cibersicurezza e l'intelligenza artificiale rappresenta una scelta strategica per rafforzare la sicurezza, la competitività e la resilienza dell'Unione.

Perché proteggere reti, infrastrutture critiche e i nostri dati significa tutelare le nostre imprese e garantire la continuità dei servizi essenziali ai cittadini.

L'intelligenza artificiale è una leva decisiva per l'innovazione, per l'autonomia strategica e per la nostra sicurezza. Allo stesso tempo, se utilizzata da attori ostili, può trasformarsi in uno strumento capace di colpire i nostri sistemi, le nostre economie e persino le nostre democrazie.

Per questo, l'Europa deve governare questo processo e non aspettarne l'evoluzione. Come autorevolmente richiamato dalla lettera enciclica "Magnifica Humanitas" di Papa Leone XIV, il progresso tecnologico acquista il suo pieno valore solo quando è al servizio della persona umana e ne custodisce la dignità.

Per questo, l'intelligenza artificiale deve restare uno strumento nelle mani dell'uomo e mai un sostituto del suo giudizio e della sua responsabilità. Solo così l'Europa saprà vincere le sfide della cibersicurezza, costruendo un futuro più forte, protetto e profondamente libero.
2-0351-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the European action plan on cybersecurity and artificial intelligence represents a strategic choice to strengthen the security, competitiveness and resilience of the Union.

Because protecting networks, critical infrastructures and our data means protecting our businesses and guaranteeing the continuity of essential services to citizens.

Artificial intelligence is a decisive lever for innovation, for strategic autonomy and for our security. At the same time, if used by hostile actors, it can transform into a tool capable of affecting our systems, our economies and even our democracies.

For this reason, Europe must govern this process and not wait for its evolution. As authoritatively recalled by the encyclical letter "Magnifica Humanitas" by Pope Leo XIV, technological progress acquires its full value only when it is at the service of the human person and safeguards his dignity.

For this reason, artificial intelligence must remain a tool in the hands of man and never a substitute for his judgment and responsibility. Only in this way will Europe be able to overcome the challenges of cybersecurity, building a stronger, more protected and profoundly free future.

2-0354-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, digitalna suverenost nije pitanje protekcionizma, nego otpornosti. Cilj nije zamijeniti jednu ovisnost drugom, već smanjenje strateške ovisnosti i povećanje europske konkurentnosti.

Stoga pozdravljam akcijski plan Komisije jer umjetna inteligencija više nije samo pokretač inovacija, već i novi čimbenik europske sigurnosti. Danas već više od 80 posto phishing kampanja koristi elemente generativne umjetne inteligencije, a kibernetičke prijetnje razvijaju se, nažalost, brže od naših obrambenih sustava.

Pred nama su ključna pitanja, hoćemo li dovoljno ulagati, imamo li stručnjake za koordinaciju i za zaštitu kritične infrastrukture i jesmo li spremni na prijelaz za post-kvantnu kriptografiju prije nego što kvantna računala ugroze današnje sustave enkripcije i činimo li na kraju dovoljno da bismo zaštitili djecu i naše osobne podatke.
2-0354-0000.englishText:
Dear Speaker, Commissioner, digital sovereignty is not a matter of protectionism, but of resilience. The goal is not to replace one dependency with another, but to reduce strategic dependency and increase European competitiveness.

Therefore, I welcome the Commission's action plan because artificial intelligence is no longer just a driver of innovation, but also a new factor in European security. Today, more than 80 percent of phishing campaigns use elements of generative artificial intelligence, and cyber threats are developing, unfortunately, faster than our defense systems.

The key questions before us are whether we will invest enough, whether we have experts to coordinate and protect critical infrastructure, and whether we are ready to transition to post-quantum cryptography before quantum computers threaten today's encryption systems, and whether we are ultimately doing enough to protect children and our personal data.

2-0355-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, OpenAI, Mythos, Anthropos, inteligencia artificial de frontera... ¿Por qué se revuelven contra el poder regulatorio de la Unión Europea? Porque lo temen.

Por tanto, una estrategia de ciberseguridad en inteligencia artificial que sea netamente europea tiene que abundar en lo que la distingue y exactamente en lo que los mastodontes temen: su transparencia, su dotación de cuentas, su sujeción a derechos fundamentales. Y se debe explicar, además, que no lo hacemos por pánico a una revolución tecnológica imparable, sino porque nos importa la supervisión humana, que es la que las hace consistentes con nuestro estándar de derechos fundamentales.

Estamos dispuestos —claro que sí— a reconvertir nuestro mercado de trabajo sabiendo que la inteligencia artificial tendrá un impacto tremendo sobre muchos empleos que ahora existen y no existirán pasado mañana. Pero a lo que no estamos dispuestos es a que un algoritmo imponga un veredicto de culpabilidad en la justicia. Eso es lo que diferencia al modelo europeo y lo que tiene que preservar la ciberseguridad en inteligencia artificial distintivamente europea.
2-0355-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, OpenAI, Mythos, Anthropos, frontier artificial intelligence... Why are you rebelling against the regulatory power of the European Union? Because they fear it.

Therefore, a cybersecurity strategy in artificial intelligence that is purely European has to elaborate on what distinguishes it and exactly what the mastodons fear: its transparency, its provision of accounts, its subjection to fundamental rights. And it must also be explained that we do not do it out of panic about an unstoppable technological revolution, but because we care about human supervision, which is what makes them consistent with our standard of fundamental rights.

We are willing—of course we are—to reconvert our labor market knowing that artificial intelligence will have a tremendous impact on many jobs that exist now and will not exist the day after tomorrow. But what we are not willing to do is for an algorithm to impose a guilty verdict in court. That is what differentiates the European model and what has to preserve distinctively European cybersecurity in artificial intelligence.

2-0356-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, tuon esille muutamia tilastoja tekoälystä. Suomessa tekoälyä käyttävien yritysten osuus on noussut melkein 38 prosenttiin. Se on EU:n keskiarvoon verrattuna lähes kaksi kertaa enemmän.

Mutta mikä Euroopan tekoälykehitystä oikein kurjistaa? Luvut tarjoavat vastauksen. EU:n tasolla isoista yrityksistä tekoälyn käyttöprosentti yltää jopa 55 prosenttiin. Sitten tulee mutta: EU:n tasolla vain 30 prosenttia keskisuurista ja vain 17 prosenttia pienistä yrityksistä käyttää tekoälyä.

EU:n tekoälysääntelyn noudattamiseen tarvitaan suuria resursseja, joita pienemmillä yrityksillä ei yksinkertaisesti ole. Euroopan rooli tulevaisuuden kansainvälisellä näyttämöllä on kiinni siitä, kuinka hyödynnämme uusinta teknologiaa. Tämä rooli lähtee rakentumaan, kun lakkaamme olemasta sääntelyn suurvalta.
2-0356-0000.englishText:
Dear Speaker, I will bring up some statistics about artificial intelligence. In Finland, the share of companies using artificial intelligence has risen to almost 38 percent. It is almost twice as much as the EU average.

But what is really making Europe's artificial intelligence development miserable? The numbers provide the answer. At the EU level, the usage percentage of artificial intelligence reaches up to 55% among large companies. Then comes the but: at the EU level, only 30 percent of medium-sized and only 17 percent of small companies use artificial intelligence.

Complying with EU AI regulation requires large resources, which smaller companies simply do not have. Europe's role on the international stage of the future depends on how we utilize the latest technology. This role starts to take shape when we cease to be a regulatory superpower.

2-0358-0000.sourceText:
Gerbiamas Pirmininke, gerbiamieji, vis tik turite pripažinti, kad Europą reguliuoja Jungtinės Amerikos Valstijos ir Kinija investuoja. Mes nesugebame investuoti, negaminame kompiuterių, negaminame telefonų, negaminame programinių įrangų, bet reguliuoti – reguliuojame geriausiai. Šiandien du reguliavimai. Putinas primena man Rusijos situaciją. Putino diktatūra uždraudžia „TikTok“, ir mes reguliuojame „TikTok“, „WhatsApp“, „Telegram“. Jam tai kelia pavojų. Jums kelia pavojų „Tik tok“, dirbtinis intelektas. Tai kuo jūs skiriatės nuo Rusijos? Ogi niekuo. Tik pas jus reguliavimas demokratinis, pas Putiną – diktatūrinis. Šiandien jūs uždraudėte, pradėję procedūrą, vieną iš partijų, kuri netinka jums. O Putinas seniai uždaręs partijas, kurios nepritaria jo politikai. Na, kuo jūs skiriatės? Jūs niekuo kitokie. Dar šiandien priėmėte vieną sprendimą... 

(posėdžio pirmininkas iš kalbėtojo atima žodį)
2-0358-0000.englishText:
Dear President, ladies and gentlemen, you still have to admit that Europe is being regulated by the United States of America and China is investing. We are not able to invest, we don't make computers, we don't make phones, we don't make software, but we regulate - we regulate best. Two adjustments today. Putin reminds me of the Russian situation. Putin's dictatorship bans TikTok, and we regulate TikTok, WhatsApp, Telegram. It puts him in danger. You are at risk from Tik Tok, artificial intelligence. So how are you different from Russia? Well, nothing. Only with you is the regulation democratic, with Putin it is dictatorial. Today you have banned one of the parties that is not suitable for you by starting the procedure. And Putin has long closed parties that do not support his policies. Well, what makes you different? You are no different. You made one decision today... 

(the chairman of the meeting takes away the floor from the speaker)

2-0360-0000.sourceText:
Szanowny Panie Przewodniczący! AI, sztuczna inteligencja, jest z jednej strony narzędziem wzmacniającym cyberbezpieczeństwo, ale to również źródło nowych wyzwań. To, co jest ważne, to przede wszystkim współpraca, wymiana informacji, wspólne mechanizmy reagowania i koordynacja działań. Panie Przewodniczący Zīle, możemy dzisiaj wspólnie powiedzieć: nasze zadanie zostało wykonane. Mamy stanowisko Parlamentu Europejskiego w sprawie ważnego rozporządzenia, jakim jest mobilność wojskowa, i w przyszłym tygodniu rozpoczniemy wspólnie negocjacje międzyinstytucjonalne.

Ale to, z czego się szczególnie cieszę i czym chciałbym się przed Wysoką Izbą pochwalić, to przede wszystkim to, że uwzględniliśmy problematykę bezpieczeństwa systemów z problematyką bezpieczeństwa łączności w naszej regulacji. To jest bardzo ważna podstawa do wspólnych, dalszych działań.
2-0360-0000.englishText:
Dear Mr. Chairman! AI, artificial intelligence, is on the one hand a tool that strengthens cybersecurity, but it is also a source of new challenges. What is important is, above all, cooperation, exchange of information, common response mechanisms and coordination of activities. Mr. Zīle, today we can say together: our task has been accomplished. We have the European Parliament's position on the important regulation of military mobility, and we will start interinstitutional negotiations together next week.

But what I am particularly happy about and what I would like to boast about before the House is, above all, the fact that we have taken into account the issues of system security and communications security in our regulation. This is a very important basis for joint, further actions.

2-0365-0000.sourceText:
Good afternoon, colleagues. It is my honour to chair the next point.

Următorul punct de pe ordinea de zi este raportul dlui Michael Gahler, în numele Comisiei pentru afaceri externe, referitor la Raportul Comisiei din 2025 privind Ucraina (2025/2259(INI)) (A10-0172/2026). Aș dori să amintesc vorbitorilor că, având în vedere măsurile de testare, va fi necesară respectarea strictă a timpului aferent luărilor de cuvânt.
2-0365-0000.englishText:
Good afternoon, colleagues. It is my honor to chair the next point.

The next item on the agenda is the report by Mr Michael Gahler, on behalf of the Committee on Foreign Affairs, on the 2025 Commission Report on Ukraine (2025/2259(INI)) (A10-0172/2026). I would like to remind the speakers that, given the testing measures, strict adherence to the speaking time will be required.

2-0367-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Die Ukraine und die Ukrainer sind auf dem Weg in die Europäische Union. Dieser Weg ist unwiderruflich, weil die Ukrainer das wollen und weil auch wir das wollen. Es ist im beiderseitigen Interesse, dass diese europäische Nation ihren Platz in der Gemeinschaft der freien Völker Europas findet. Das imperialistische Russland, das von einem Mann geführt wird, der nach Hitler und Stalin die drittgrößten Verbrechen der europäischen Neuzeit begeht, an Ukrainern und am eigenen Volk, wird das nicht verhindern. Russland wird historisch scheitern, wenn die Ukraine auf dem Weg in die EU ist.

Das erste Cluster von Verhandlungskapiteln ist eröffnet. Ich finde, es wäre ein gutes Signal, auch die anderen idealerweise beim nächsten Europäischen Rat mit zu eröffnen. Das kürzt nichts ab; das ersetzt nicht die Notwendigkeit, die Voraussetzungen für den Beitritt inhaltlich zu erfüllen. Es wäre aber ein weiteres deutliches Signal an Ukrainer, EU‑Bürger und den Aggressor Russland, dass es keinen Weg zurück in den sowjetischen Gulag, sondern vorwärts in eine gemeinsame europäische Zukunft gibt.

In diesem Bericht, der im Wesentlichen von fünf Fraktionen und darüber hinaus einer Anzahl weiterer Abgeordneter getragen wird, machen wir deutlich, wo die Ukraine auf dem Weg in die EU steht. Wir haben hierzu eine Vielzahl von Quellen genutzt, vor allem aber auch den Dialog praktiziert mit den politisch Verantwortlichen in Kyjiw, in den Regionen bis hin zur kommunalen Ebene, und natürlich mit unseren eigenen Vertretern vor Ort und in Brüssel und mit der starken und beeindruckend kompetenten ukrainischen Zivilgesellschaft.

Daraus ergibt sich ein klares Bild, was zu tun ist. Alle Institutionen, die für den Rechtsstaat relevant sind, müssen gestärkt bzw. reformiert werden. Das heißt, die Antikorruptionsbehörden müssen ihre Arbeit unabhängig verrichten können. Die obersten Gerichte müssen nach einem transparenten Auswahlprozess besetzt werden. Absolventen der Universitäten, die die Befähigung zum Richteramt erworben haben, müssen von unten die Richterschaft erneuern. Die Generalstaatsanwaltschaft hat nicht die Aufgabe, Weisungen an die Antikorruptionsbehörden zu erteilen. Der Geheimdienst muss Staatsfeinde bekämpfen. Die Antikorruptionsbehörden sind keine Staatsfeinde, sondern bekämpfen diejenigen, die ein falsches Staatsverständnis haben; es kann daher nicht Aufgabe des Geheimdienstes sein, Antikorruptionsbehörden auszuforschen. Ein State Bureau of Investigation sollte nicht ein Bezirksgericht anrufen, um zu verhindern, dass das Ergebnis einer journalistischen Investigativrecherche veröffentlicht wird, die den Bruder des Direktors betrifft. Gewählte Politiker sind keine öffentlichen Angestellten; für sie gilt kein Beamtenrecht; sie können daher auch nicht mit Maßnahmen des Beamtenrechts sanktioniert werden; die freie Mandatsausübung ist auch in Kriegszeiten ein hohes Gut.

Da für alle Parteien in der Werchowna Rada neben dem EU‑Beitrittsprozess die Bekämpfung des Aggressors Russland an erster Stelle steht, rate ich an, innenpolitische Auseinandersetzungen oder taktische Spielchen auf die Zeit nach dem Ende der Kampfhandlungen und die Vorbereitung auf Wahlen zu konzentrieren und stattdessen gemeinsam gegen den Aggressor zu stehen.

Und hier kommt noch mal der Beitrittsprozess ins Spiel: Wir müssen uns klarmachen, dass neben dem traditionellen merit-based approach, also einem Fortschritt entsprechend der Erfüllung des acquis, eine geopolitische Dimension hinzutritt, und die ist zunehmend auch in unserem Interesse. Es ist die Ukraine, die uns die Zeit verschafft, gegenüber der Bedrohung durch den Aggressor Russland verteidigungsfähig zu werden. Die Ukrainer sind derzeit die einzigen, die Russland aufhalten können.

Daraus ergibt sich eine Gesamtschau, die die Ukrainer und uns zusammenführt in dem Interesse, gemeinsam nach dem Ende des Kriegszustands beide Prozesse zu gestalten – den EU‑Beitritt und eine gegenseitige Sicherheitsgarantie, dass wir auch vor einer EU‑ oder NATO‑Mitgliedschaft füreinander einstehen. Keine direkte, aber eine entsprechende Anwendung des Artikels 42 Absatz 7, die nicht nur für uns gegenüber der Ukraine, sondern auch für die Ukraine uns gegenüber gilt. Nur gemeinsam sind wir stark genug. Slawa Europa! Slawa Ukrajini!
2-0367-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! Ukraine and Ukrainians are on their way to the European Union. This path is irreversible because the Ukrainians want it and because we want it too. It is in the interest of both sides that this European nation finds its place in the community of free peoples of Europe. Imperialist Russia, led by a man who, after Hitler and Stalin, commits the third greatest crimes of modern Europe, against Ukrainians and against its own people, will not prevent this. Russia will fail historically if Ukraine is on its way to the EU.

The first cluster of negotiating chapters has opened. I think it would be a good signal to also open the others, ideally at the next European Council. This doesn't shorten anything; This does not replace the need to fulfill the requirements for accession. But it would be another clear signal to Ukrainians, EU citizens and the aggressor Russia that there is no way back to the Soviet gulag, but rather forward to a common European future.

In this report, which is essentially supported by five political groups and a number of other MPs, we make it clear where Ukraine stands on the path to the EU. To this end, we used a variety of sources, but above all we also practiced dialogue with those politically responsible in Kyiv, in the regions up to the municipal level, and of course with our own representatives on site and in Brussels and with the strong and impressively competent Ukrainian civil society.

This gives a clear picture of what needs to be done. All institutions that are relevant to the rule of law must be strengthened or reformed. This means that the anti-corruption authorities must be able to carry out their work independently. The highest courts must be filled following a transparent selection process. University graduates who have acquired the qualifications to serve as judges must renew the judgeship from below. The Attorney General's Office is not responsible for issuing instructions to the anti-corruption authorities. The secret service must fight enemies of the state. The anti-corruption authorities are not enemies of the state, but fight those who have a false understanding of the state; It cannot therefore be the task of the secret service to investigate anti-corruption authorities. A State Bureau of Investigation should not go to district court to prevent the publication of the results of a journalistic investigative investigation involving the director's brother. Elected politicians are not public employees; No civil service law applies to them; They therefore cannot be sanctioned with measures under civil service law; The free exercise of mandates is a valuable asset even in times of war.

Since fighting the aggressor Russia is the top priority for all parties in the Verkhovna Rada, in addition to the EU accession process, I recommend concentrating domestic political disputes or tactical games on the period after the end of the hostilities and the preparation for elections and instead standing together against the aggressor.

And this is where the accession process comes into play again: We have to realize that in addition to the traditional merit-based approach, i.e. progress in line with the fulfillment of the acquis, there is also a geopolitical dimension, and this is increasingly in our interest. It is Ukraine that is giving us the time to become capable of defending ourselves against the threat posed by the aggressor Russia. The Ukrainians are currently the only ones who can stop Russia.

This results in an overall view that brings the Ukrainians and us together in the interest of shaping both processes together after the end of the state of war - EU accession and a mutual security guarantee that we will stand up for each other even before EU or NATO membership. Not a direct, but a corresponding application of Article 42 paragraph 7, which applies not only to us in relation to Ukraine, but also to Ukraine in relation to us. Only together are we strong enough. Slava Europe! Slava Ukraini!

2-0369-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Wszyscy chcemy, żeby Ukraina wygrała z Putinem. Zbrodnicza rosyjska armia napadła na Ukrainę dlatego, że Ukraińcy chcą europejskiej przyszłości dla swojego kraju. I my chcemy Ukrainy europejskiej. Chcemy i wierzymy, że to może się zdarzyć. Do tego potrzebne są oczywiście konsekwentne działania. Dlatego tak ważne są reformy, tak ważne jest oparcie państwa na praworządności, na prawdziwej, realnej, konsekwentnej walce z korupcją, bo żadne euro nie może być przekazane i zdefraudowane.

Ale także niezbędne jest poszanowanie wspólnych europejskich wartości, bo nie można we Wspólnocie gloryfikować tych, którzy opierali swoją przeszłość, swoją aktywność na walce z mniejszościami, na działaniach o charakterze ludobójczym. Jeżeli przypominamy ten fakt jako Parlament Europejski, przypominamy to po to, by jeszcze raz powiedzieć jedno przesłanie: to wy wybieracie swoją przyszłość. Ale jeżeli chcecie być we Wspólnocie, musicie szanować te wartości, które opisane są w art. 2, i rzeczywiście promować to, co jest naszą wspólną europejską zasadą.

Nie ma miejsca na gloryfikowanie zbrodniarzy. Żadne euro nie może być wydane na te oddziały, które mają imię zbrodniarzy odpowiedzialnych za ludobójstwo. Europejska przyszłość leży w waszych rękach.
2-0369-0000.englishText:
Mr President! We all want Ukraine to win against Putin. The criminal Russian army attacked Ukraine because Ukrainians want a European future for their country. And we want a European Ukraine. We want and believe it can happen. This, of course, requires consistent actions. That is why reforms are so important, it is so important to base the state on the rule of law, on a real, real, consistent fight against corruption, because no euro can be transferred and embezzled.

But it is also necessary to respect common European values, because in the Community we cannot glorify those who based their past and their activity on the fight against minorities and on genocidal activities. If we recall this fact as the European Parliament, we recall it to repeat one message: you choose your future. But if you want to be in the Community, you must respect the values ​​described in Art. 2, and actually promote what is our common European principle.

There is no place for glorifying criminals. No euro can be spent on those units that bear the name of criminals responsible for genocide. The European future is in your hands.

2-0371-0000.sourceText:
Mr. President, Commissioner, I'm speaking Portuguese.

Estamos, sem hesitações, ao lado do povo ucraniano, ao lado das mães que perderam filhos, de um povo que viu a sua terra invadida, as suas cidades destruídas e o seu futuro suspenso. A agressão russa deve ser condenada com toda a clareza, como a condenaríamos se se tratasse do nosso próprio país.

A soberania e a independência da Ucrânia não podem ser moeda de troca, e nenhuma paz pode ser negociada sem a Ucrânia. Mas estar com a Ucrânia é também dizer a verdade. O melhor para a Ucrânia não é uma guerra sem fim. O melhor é uma paz justa, segura e duradoura, uma paz que chegue quanto antes.

E também temos de dizer a verdade aos portugueses: esta guerra entrou nas casas portuguesas pela fatura da energia, pelo preço dos combustíveis, pela inflação, pela perda do poder de compra e pela erosão silenciosa da sua qualidade de vida.

O dinheiro europeu para a Ucrânia tem de ser escrutinado, não pode ser um cheque em branco. Já se descobriram desvios de fundos europeus na Ucrânia de mais de 90 milhões de EUR. Temos o dever de proteger os nossos contribuintes e garantir que cada euro chega ao seu destino.

Mas o problema não é apenas o mérito na entrada da Ucrânia para a União Europeia, é também o impacto. Qual será o impacto na vida da coesão, nos pequenos países como Portugal, na agricultura, nos transportes, na energia, na indústria, no mercado interno e nos sectores críticos das nossas economias?

Não pode haver exceção. Os critérios de Copenhaga têm de ser absolutamente cumpridos.

A Europa deve apoiar a Ucrânia, sim, mas deve fazê-lo com seriedade, não com irresponsabilidade. Ninguém tem o direito de decidir isto com leviandade. Ninguém tem o direito de sacrificar a coesão europeia nem de fragilizar os pequenos Estados para alimentar gestos simbólicos ou calendários políticos.
2-0371-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Commissioner, I'm speaking Portuguese.

We are, without hesitation, on the side of the Ukrainian people, on the side of mothers who lost children, of a people who saw their land invaded, their cities destroyed and their future suspended. Russian aggression must be condemned as clearly as we would if it were our own country.

Ukraine's sovereignty and independence cannot be a bargaining chip, and no peace can be negotiated without Ukraine. But being with Ukraine is also telling the truth. The best thing for Ukraine is not an endless war. The best thing is a just, safe and lasting peace, a peace that comes as soon as possible.

And we also have to tell the truth to the Portuguese: this war entered Portuguese homes due to energy bills, fuel prices, inflation, the loss of purchasing power and the silent erosion of their quality of life.

European money for Ukraine must be scrutinized, it cannot be a blank check. Embezzlement of European funds amounting to more than EUR 90 million has already been discovered in Ukraine. We have a duty to protect our taxpayers and ensure that every euro reaches its destination.

But the problem is not just the merit of Ukraine's entry into the European Union, it is also the impact. What will be the impact on the life of cohesion, in small countries like Portugal, on agriculture, transport, energy, industry, the internal market and critical sectors of our economies?

There can be no exception. The Copenhagen criteria must be absolutely met.

Europe must support Ukraine, yes, but it must do so seriously, not irresponsibly. No one has the right to decide this lightly. No one has the right to sacrifice European cohesion or weaken small states to fuel symbolic gestures or political calendars.

2-0372-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Od pierwszego dnia rosyjskiej agresji wspieramy Ukrainę politycznie, militarnie i humanitarnie, ponieważ jej niestrudzona walka z rosyjskim reżimem stanowi dzisiaj ważny filar bezpieczeństwa całej Europy. Polacy pozostają w tym procesie narodem, który okazał największe zaangażowanie i wsparcie.

Z drugiej strony, europejskie aspiracje Ukrainy oraz rozpoczęte negocjacje akcesyjne są niewątpliwie źródłem nadziei milionów Ukraińców na europejską przyszłość Ukrainy. Należy docenić reformy i zmiany w prawie implementowane na Ukrainie, których celem jest realizacja europejskich standardów.

Jednak europejska integracja oznacza nie tylko dostosowanie prawa krajowego, lecz także wierność podstawowym wartościom, na których zbudowana jest Unia Europejska, w tym prawdzie historycznej, szacunku dla ofiar oraz odwadze w mierzeniu się z własną, nawet najcięższą przeszłością. Dlatego absolutnie jako nieakceptowalną przyjęliśmy decyzję o nadaniu elitarnej jednostce Sił Zbrojnych Ukrainy imienia „bohaterów UPA”, formacji odpowiedzialnej za wymordowanie około 100 tysięcy cywilów, głównie polskich kobiet i dzieci, choć wśród ofiar znaleźli się również Żydzi, Czesi oraz Ukraińcy ratujący swoich sąsiadów.

Nie może być zgody na gloryfikację i nawiązywanie do organizacji oraz środowisk odpowiedzialnych za zbrodnie wojenne, takich jak 14. Dywizja Grenadierów SS Galizien, batalion „Nachtigall” czy batalion „Roland”. Decyzja prezydenta Zełenskiego zbezcześciła pamięć wszystkich ofiar ludobójstwa dokonanego na terenie południowo-wschodnich województw II Rzeczypospolitej przez ukraińskich nacjonalistów.

Pojednanie wymaga prawdy. Ukraina powinna jednoznacznie potępić ideologię UPA, która doprowadziła do masowych zbrodni, oraz umożliwić pełne ekshumacje i godny pochówek wszystkich ofiar. Prawda historyczna nie jest przeszkodą dla pojednania, nie jest przeszkodą w drodze do Europy. Wręcz odwrotnie, jest jej fundamentem. Tylko na fundamencie prawdy i wzajemnego szacunku możemy budować wspólną europejską przyszłość.
2-0372-0000.englishText:
Mr President! From the first day of Russian aggression, we have supported Ukraine politically, militarily and humanitarianly, because its tireless fight against the Russian regime is today an important pillar of security for all of Europe. In this process, Poles remain the nation that has shown the greatest commitment and support.

On the other hand, Ukraine's European aspirations and the commenced accession negotiations are undoubtedly a source of hope for millions of Ukrainians for Ukraine's European future. The reforms and changes in law implemented in Ukraine, which aim to implement European standards, should be appreciated.

However, European integration means not only the adjustment of national law, but also fidelity to the basic values ​​on which the European Union is built, including historical truth, respect for victims and courage in facing one's own past, even the most difficult one. Therefore, we found it absolutely unacceptable the decision to name an elite unit of the Ukrainian Armed Forces after the "UPA heroes", a formation responsible for the murder of approximately 100,000 civilians, mainly Polish women and children, although the victims also included Jews, Czechs and Ukrainians saving their neighbors.

There cannot be consent to glorification and references to organizations and groups responsible for war crimes, such as the 14th SS Galizien Grenadier Division, the "Nachtigall" battalion or the "Roland" battalion. President Zelensky's decision desecrated the memory of all victims of the genocide committed in the south-eastern voivodeships of the Second Polish Republic by Ukrainian nationalists.

Reconciliation requires truth. Ukraine should unequivocally condemn the UPA ideology, which led to mass crimes, and allow full exhumations and dignified burials of all victims. Historical truth is not an obstacle to reconciliation, it is not an obstacle to Europe. On the contrary, it is its foundation. Only on the foundation of truth and mutual respect can we build a common European future.

2-0374-0000.sourceText:
Hr. formand! Jeg og kollegerne fra Parlamentet er netop kommet hjem fra et besøg i Ukraine, hvor vi så og hørte om konsekvenserne af de massive terrorbombninger af civilbefolkningen.

Men samtidig er Ukraine også et land, hvor vi ser glimt af håb, jeg ikke har oplevet i løbet af krigens forløb. Vi ser det ved fronten, hvor ukrainerne vinder initiativet mod syd, mens russerne stadig væk presser på mod øst. Vi ser det, når det ukrainske militær slår tilbage mod energi og militære strategiske mål langt inde i Rusland og dermed svækker både den russiske økonomi, men også deres militær. Vi ser det også, når Putins regime mister fodfæste. Putins løgne om krigens årsag og krigens gang er begyndt at sætte spor i den russiske befolkning.

Vi er ved et afgørende øjeblik. Derfor skal EU og medlemslandene ikke alene fastholde, men styrke hjælpen til Ukraine, så Putin tvinges til at respektere de internationalt anerkendte grænser. Tyrannen og vanviddet må og skal stoppes!
2-0374-0000.englishText:
Mr. chairman! I and my colleagues from Parliament have just returned home from a visit to Ukraine, where we saw and heard about the consequences of the massive terrorist bombings of the civilian population.

But at the same time, Ukraine is also a country where we see glimpses of hope that I have not experienced during the course of the war. We see it at the front, where the Ukrainians are gaining the initiative to the south, while the Russians are still away pushing to the east. We see it when the Ukrainian military strikes back against energy and military strategic targets deep inside Russia, weakening both the Russian economy and their military as well. We also see it when Putin's regime loses its footing. Putin's lies about the cause of the war and the course of the war have begun to leave their mark on the Russian population.

We are at a defining moment. Therefore, the EU and its member states must not only maintain, but strengthen aid to Ukraine, so that Putin is forced to respect the internationally recognized borders. The tyrant and the madness must and must be stopped!

2-0375-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Es ist wieder soweit – der Jahresbericht zur Ukraine. Alle Jahre wieder sprechen Sie hier vor allem über Waffen, Aufrüstung und geopolitische Interessen, aber viel zu selten sprechen Sie über die Menschen, über eine Friedensperspektive. Seit über vier Jahren leben Millionen Menschen in der Ukraine im Krieg; Arbeiterinnen und Arbeiter verlieren ihre Existenz; soziale Rechte und Gewerkschaften stehen unter Druck. Die Regierung Selenskyj steht wegen Korruption und Angriffen auf soziale Rechte in der Kritik, gleichzeitig wird der Ausverkauf des Landes vorangetrieben.

Doch über diese Realitäten reden Sie nicht gerne. Stattdessen feiern Sie neue Waffen und Drohnentechnologien, als wäre Krieg ein Spiel. Aber die Folge dieser Eskalation tragen nicht Sie hier – die tragen die Menschen vor Ort. Ihre Antwort bleibt immer dieselbe: mehr Waffen, mehr Aufrüstung, mehr Militarisierung. Und dieser Bericht spricht erneut über Taurus-Lieferungen.

Während immer mehr Menschen in der Ukraine und in Russland versuchen, diesem Krieg zu entkommen, soll nun sogar der Schutz ukrainischer Geflüchteter der Kriegsfähigkeit der Ukraine untergeordnet werden. Männer im wehrfähigen Alter sollen zurückgewiesen werden; Männer sollen damit zur militärischen Ressource gemacht werden. Das ist zynisch. Menschen sind keine Waffen; Kriegsdienstverweigerung ist ein Menschenrecht.

Auch der Beitrittsprozess wird mitten im Krieg geopolitischen Interessen untergeordnet. Solidarität bedeutet nicht, einen Krieg endlos zu verlängern. Solidarität bedeutet Schutz für Menschen, soziale Rechte und einen Wiederaufbau im Interesse der Menschen. Europa braucht keine Eskalation, sondern den Weg zum Frieden.
2-0375-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! It’s that time again – the annual report on Ukraine. Every year you talk here primarily about weapons, rearmament and geopolitical interests, but far too rarely do you talk about people and a perspective for peace. Millions of people in Ukraine have been living at war for over four years; Workers lose their livelihoods; social rights and trade unions are under pressure. Zelensky's government has been criticized for corruption and attacks on social rights, while at the same time the country is being sold out.

But you don't like to talk about these realities. Instead, celebrate new weapons and drone technologies as if war were a game. But the consequences of this escalation are not borne by you here - they are borne by the people on site. Their answer always remains the same: more weapons, more rearmament, more militarization. And this report again talks about Taurus deliveries.

While more and more people in Ukraine and Russia are trying to escape this war, even the protection of Ukrainian refugees is now being subordinated to Ukraine's ability to wage war. Men of military age should be turned away; The aim is to turn men into military resources. That's cynical. People are not weapons; Conscientious objection is a human right.

The accession process is also subordinated to geopolitical interests in the middle of the war. Solidarity does not mean prolonging a war indefinitely. Solidarity means protection for people, social rights and reconstruction in the interests of people. Europe does not need escalation, but rather the path to peace.

2-0376-0000.sourceText:
, от името на групата ESN. – Господин Председател, pъководителите в Киев носят главната отговорност за това Украйна да не е изпълнила нито един от основните критерии за влизане в Европейския съюз. Най-близките приятели и сътрудници на Владимир Зеленски са обвинени, че са създали корупционни схеми за присвояването на огромни суми пари.

Представяте ли си какво ще направят тези хора или други подобни с европейските средства, ако страната им все пак влезе в Европейския съюз? Ако това присъединяване наистина се случи, ще имаме държава - член на Евросъюза, в която няма независими медии, няма свобода на словото, няма и политически плурализъм. Властите в Киев в момента провеждат активна политика по възвеличаването на хора, които активно са участвали в нацистките престъпления през Втората световна война. Личности и организации, отговорни за престъпления срещу човечеството, днес там се честват като герои, а Евросъюзът винаги категорично е осъждал подобни чудовищни деяния. Ето защо държавни ръководители, които се прекланят пред нацистки престъпници, няма как да преговарят за членство в Европейския съюз. А напоследък властите в Киев правят всичко възможно, за да забранят официално и украинската православна църква, просто защото тя не желае да се подчинява на диктата им.

Изобщо днешната власт в Киев е олицетворение на всичко това, срещу което Европейският съюз твърди, че се бори, Тя е корумпирана, унищожава свободата, величае нацизма и принуждава милиони украинци да търсят спасение в чужбина. Ако Брюксел допусне такива управляващи в Европейския съюз, той без съмнение ще спечели Световното първенство по лицемерие.
2-0376-0000.englishText:
, on behalf of the ESN Group. - Mr. President, the leaders in Kyiv bear the main responsibility for the fact that Ukraine has not fulfilled any of the main criteria for entering the European Union. The closest friends and associates of Volodymyr Zelensky are accused of creating corruption schemes for the embezzlement of huge sums of money.

Can you imagine what these people or others like them will do with European funds if their country does enter the European Union? If this accession really happens, we will have a member state of the European Union in which there is no independent media, no freedom of speech, and no political pluralism. The authorities in Kiev are currently pursuing an active policy of glorifying people who actively participated in Nazi crimes during World War II. Individuals and organizations responsible for crimes against humanity are today celebrated there as heroes, and the European Union has always categorically condemned such monstrous acts. That is why heads of state who bow down to Nazi criminals cannot negotiate membership of the European Union. And lately, the authorities in Kiev have been doing everything they can to officially ban the Ukrainian Orthodox Church as well, simply because it does not want to obey their dictates.

In general, today's government in Kiev is the embodiment of everything that the European Union claims to fight against. It is corrupt, destroys freedom, glorifies Nazism and forces millions of Ukrainians to seek salvation abroad. If Brussels allows such rulers into the European Union, it will no doubt win the World Cup of Hypocrisy.

2-0379-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, na madrugada da passada quinta-feira, as forças russas lançaram drones e mísseis sobre Kiev, num ataque que o presidente da câmara descreveu como «o mais massivo contra a capital». Alguns de nós tinham acabado de regressar da Ucrânia, de mais uma reunião da Comissão Parlamentar de Associação.

Também por isso, hoje, quero deixar aqui uma nota pessoal. O relatório que discutimos não é só sobre um país que, há mais de uma década, escolheu um futuro europeu. É sobre um processo de adesão de um país que tem territórios ilegalmente ocupados e se defende de uma guerra de agressão, enquanto progride no processo de reformas. Um país que não compreende porque é que os seus aliados não reforçam o apoio de meios de defesa aérea ou porque é que o Conselho não lhe permite a abertura de todos os capítulos temáticos de uma reforma. Um país perante o qual eu, hoje, coraria de vergonha com as palavras de alguns deputados nesta casa, que invocam os pequenos interesses dos seus países e os seus medos.

Apesar da lei marcial, mais de 80 % dos ucranianos defendem que o país deve continuar a reforma judicial e mais de 65 % desejam maior exigência externa nesse sentido, mostra um estudo. Este é um sinal claro de que a via de integração é uma escolha de toda a sociedade. Saibamos estar à altura.
2-0379-0000.englishText:
Mr President, in the early hours of last Thursday, Russian forces launched drones and missiles over Kiev, in an attack that the mayor described as “the most massive against the capital”. Some of us had just returned from Ukraine, from another meeting of the Parliamentary Association Committee.

That's also why, today, I want to leave a personal note here. The report we discuss is not just about a country that, more than a decade ago, chose a European future. It is about the accession process of a country that has illegally occupied territories and is defending itself from a war of aggression, while progressing in the reform process. A country that does not understand why its allies do not reinforce support for air defense assets or why the Council does not allow it to open all the thematic chapters of a reform. A country before which, today, I would blush with shame at the words of some Members in this House, who invoke the small interests of their countries and their fears.

Despite martial law, more than 80 % of Ukrainians argue that the country should continue judicial reform and more than 65 % want greater external demands in this regard, a study shows. This is a clear sign that the integration path is a choice for the entire society. Let us know how to rise to the occasion.

2-0380-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, commissaris, de Nederlandse bevolking wil niet dat Oekraïne toetreedt tot de EU. Dat werd tien jaar geleden al duidelijk. Meer dan 60 % van de Nederlanders sprak zich toen in een referendum uit tegen het EU-associatieverdrag met Oekraïne. De Nederlandse regering negeerde de uitkomst van het referendum en tekende uiteindelijk toch, nadat de EU in een juridisch bindende verklaring had bevestigd dat dit verdrag geen opstap zou zijn naar EU-lidmaatschap. Vandaag handelt de EU in strijd met die bindende verklaring door de toetreding van Oekraïne juist te versnellen.

De EU spreekt zich graag uit over democratie en rechtsstaat, maar trekt zich niets aan van de Nederlandse kiezer of van haar eigen afspraken.

Oekraïne is een door en door corrupt land. De Commissie erkent dan ook zelf dat ingrijpende hervormingen nodig zijn. Toch worden de onderhandelingen voortgezet. Bovendien is Oekraïne een land in oorlog. De wederopbouw van het land zal naar verwachting meer dan 507 miljard EUR kosten. Iedereen weet wie dit uiteindelijk zal moeten betalen: de Europese belastingbetaler. Onze kiezers hebben daar nooit mee ingestemd. We hebben de afgelopen jaren al genoeg miljarden naar Oekraïne gestuurd.

Nederland kan niet blijven opdraaien voor de rekening van anderen. Genoeg is genoeg. Bescherm Europa. Stop de uitbreiding van de EU.
2-0380-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, the Dutch people do not want Ukraine to join the EU. That became clear ten years ago. More than 60% of Dutch people spoke out in a referendum against the EU association treaty with Ukraine. The Dutch government ignored the outcome of the referendum and eventually signed it anyway, after the EU confirmed in a legally binding declaration that this treaty would not be a stepping stone to EU membership. Today the EU is acting in violation of that binding declaration by accelerating Ukraine's accession.

The EU likes to speak out about democracy and the rule of law, but does not care about the Dutch voter or its own agreements.

Ukraine is a thoroughly corrupt country. The Commission itself therefore recognizes that far-reaching reforms are needed. Nevertheless, negotiations continue. Moreover, Ukraine is a country at war. The country's reconstruction is expected to cost more than EUR 507 billion. Everyone knows who will ultimately have to pay for this: the European taxpayer. Our voters never agreed to that. We have already sent enough billions to Ukraine in recent years.

The Netherlands cannot continue to foot the bill for others. Enough is enough. Protect Europe. Stop EU expansion.

2-0381-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, è nei momenti più difficili che si misura la credibilità dell'Europa, e oggi essere credibili significa sostenere l'Ucraina, ma anche lavorare con determinazione per una pace giusta, duratura e fondata sul rispetto del diritto internazionale.

Sostenere Kiev significa ribadire la sicurezza dell'Europa e dell'Alleanza atlantica, che è una responsabilità comune, da assumere secondo le capacità di ciascuno Stato membro, nel pieno coordinamento con la NATO.

Significa anche rafforzare la pressione sulla Russia, rendendo più efficaci le sanzioni e contrastando ogni forma di elusione, a partire dalle cosiddette flotte ombra, che continuano ad alimentare lo sforzo bellico di Mosca.

Allo stesso tempo, il percorso di adesione dell'Ucraina all'Unione europea rappresenta una prospettiva che sosteniamo, ovviamente, con convinzione. Ma, proprio perché crediamo nel progetto europeo, questo percorso dovrà rispettare integralmente i criteri di adesione, le riforme richieste e i tempi necessari. Accelerazioni dettate dalla contingenza politica, dal cuore piuttosto che dalla mente, non rafforzano l'Unione e rischiano, al contrario, di indebolirne la credibilità.

La libertà non è mai un bene acquisito per sempre: va difesa ogni giorno con responsabilità, coerenza e coraggio ed è questo il compito che oggi spetta all'Unione europea.
2-0381-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, it is in the most difficult moments that Europe's credibility is measured, and today being credible means supporting Ukraine, but also working with determination for a just, lasting peace based on respect for international law.

Supporting Kiev means reaffirming the security of Europe and the Atlantic Alliance, which is a common responsibility, to be assumed according to the capabilities of each member state, in full coordination with NATO.

It also means strengthening pressure on Russia, making sanctions more effective and countering any form of evasion, starting from the so-called shadow fleets, which continue to fuel Moscow's war effort.

At the same time, Ukraine's path to joining the European Union represents a prospect that we obviously support with conviction. But, precisely because we believe in the European project, this path will have to fully respect the accession criteria, the required reforms and the necessary times. Accelerations dictated by political contingency, by the heart rather than by the mind, do not strengthen the Union and, on the contrary, risk weakening its credibility.

Freedom is never a good acquired forever: it must be defended every day with responsibility, coherence and courage and this is the task that falls to the European Union today.

2-0382-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, sehr geehrte Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! „Wir wollen nicht Sklaven Putins sein“ – das ist der Satz, den ich in der Ukraine am häufigsten gehört habe. Ja, die Menschen in der Ukraine reden von Freiheit; sie wollen in Freiheit leben wie wir, und natürlich gehören sie deswegen auch in die Europäische Union. Da muss noch viel gemacht werden.

Und wenn hier ausgerechnet von rechts, wo es schon wieder Korruptionsskandale gibt, von Korruption gesprochen wird: Ja, das weiß man auch in der Ukraine, aber es gibt eine starke Zivilgesellschaft; das gefällt ihnen auch nicht. Die Leute sind auf die Straße gegangen, als ihnen ein Gesetz nicht gefallen hat. Wir haben mit den Chefs der Antikorruptionsbehörden gesprochen; sie haben uns das alles erklärt. Das hat gezeigt, was das für ein lebhafter Staat ist und ein demokratischer Staat, der natürlich zu uns passt.

Vor Kurzem war Garri Kasparow in Wien, und ich habe ihn gefragt, warum diese Rechtsextremen immer wie Putin reden. Er hat gesagt, er kann sich gar nicht vorstellen, dass die nicht von dort finanziert werden. Bitte, das sagt Kasparow, ist aber interessant, weil die Desinformation natürlich genauso läuft.

Wir stehen auf der Seite des ukrainischen Volkes, weil das ukrainische Volk auch auf unserer Seite steht. Slawa Ukrajini!

Und eines möchte ich noch; ich weiß, ich darf keine Fotos zeigen, aber jeder kann sich das im Internet anschauen. Wenn Sie diese Bilder gesehen haben, dann hören Sie denen auch nicht mehr zu.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
2-0382-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues! “We don’t want to be Putin’s slaves” – that’s the phrase I heard most often in Ukraine. Yes, people in Ukraine talk about freedom; They want to live in freedom like we do, and of course that's why they belong in the European Union. A lot still needs to be done.

And when people talk about corruption here from the right, where there are already corruption scandals: Yes, we know that in Ukraine too, but there is a strong civil society; They don't like that either. People took to the streets when they didn't like a law. We spoke to the heads of the anti-corruption authorities; they explained everything to us. That showed what a lively state it is and a democratic state that naturally suits us.

Garry Kasparov was recently in Vienna and I asked him why these right-wing extremists always talk like Putin. He said he couldn't imagine that they wouldn't be financed from there. Please, Kasparov says, but it's interesting because disinformation naturally works in the same way.

We are on the side of the Ukrainian people because the Ukrainian people are also on our side. Slava Ukraini!

And I want one more thing; I know I'm not allowed to show photos, but anyone can look at them on the Internet. Once you've seen these pictures, stop listening to them.

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question about the “blue card” procedure.)

2-0383-0000.sourceText: (ESN), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Ja, lieber Kollege Brandstätter, vielen Dank für Ihren Einsatz für die Demokratie und Freiheit in der Ukraine. Mich würde interessieren: Haben Sie dafür auch gekämpft ein Jahr vor dem Krieg, als Selenskyj die Demokratische, damals die stärkste Partei in den Umfragen, verbieten ließ, als er vier Fernsehsender verboten hat und zehn Radiosender? Was haben Sie damals gemacht?
2-0383-0000.englishText: (ESN), question about the “blue card” procedure. – Yes, dear colleague Brandstätter, thank you very much for your commitment to democracy and freedom in Ukraine.
