If the Germans called the unit SS heroes and built monuments to Hitler, Himmler, Goebbels or Eichmann, would you invite them to join the EU? NO! You would call them neo-Nazis. And rightly so. There is no moral difference between worshiping the SS and worshiping the UPA. The same cult of power, the same ethnic hatred.

The report on Ukraine is silent on this subject. This is the silence that murders the memory of the victims of genocide in Volhynia and the Eastern Borderlands for the second time. Ukraine's march to Europe with genocides on its banners is a disgrace. As Poles, we should never agree to Ukraine's entry into Europe. Down with Bandera's Nazism!

2-0441-0000.sourceText:
(początek wystąpienia poza mikrofonem) rosyjskich zbrodni wojennych na Ukrainie. Pytam jednak, co ze zbrodniami ukraińskich nacjonalistów z okresu II wojny światowej? Co z dziećmi, kobietami, starcami wymordowanymi tylko dlatego, że byli Polakami? Wrzuconymi do bezimiennych dołów bez krzyża, nazwiska, szacunku. Ludobójstwo dokonane przez OUN i UPA w imię nacjonalistycznej ideologii wzorowanej na niemieckim nazizmie.

Ponad 100 tysięcy Polaków, ale także Żydów, Czechów, Białorusinów i Ukraińców ratujących swoich sąsiadów. Byli tacy. Symbolami tych zbrodni są Bandera i Szuchewycz, bohaterowie Zełenskiego, a faktycznie bestie odpowiedzialne za te zbrodnie.

Dziś Ukraina głosi, że to formacje walczące z Sowietami. Fakty są jednak bardziej złożone. W latach 1944–53 z rąk ukraińskiego podziemia życie straciło ok. 3000 żołnierzy i funkcjonariuszy sowieckich. 8000 Sowietów, a z drugiej strony ponad 100 000 Polaków. Tak więc tak – dla pomocy Ukrainie, ale zdecydowanie nie – dla członkostwa Ukrainy w Unii Europejskiej bez uznania prawdy historycznej i z Banderą na sztandarach.
2-0441-0000.englishText:
(beginning of speech off the microphone) Russian war crimes in Ukraine. But I ask, what about the crimes of Ukrainian nationalists during World War II? What about children, women, elderly people murdered just because they were Poles? Thrown into nameless pits without a cross, name or respect. Genocide committed by the OUN and UPA in the name of nationalist ideology modeled on German Nazism.

Over 100,000 Poles, but also Jews, Czechs, Belarusians and Ukrainians saving their neighbors. They were like that. The symbols of these crimes are Bandera and Shukhevych, Zelensky's heroes, and in fact the beasts responsible for these crimes.

Today, Ukraine claims that these are formations fighting the Soviets. However, the facts are more complex. In the years 1944–53, approximately 3,000 Soviet soldiers and officers lost their lives at the hands of the Ukrainian underground. 8,000 Soviets, and on the other hand over 100,000 Poles. So yes - for helping Ukraine, but definitely not - for Ukraine's membership in the European Union without recognizing the historical truth and with Bandera on the banner.

2-0442-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Menschen Europas! Ich war letzte Woche in einem ausgebombten Haus in Kyjiw. Da musste ich an einen Song denken, und der geht so:

Meine Freunde sind Iraner.

Meine Freunde sind aus Gaza.

Meine Freunde sind Ukrainer, Russen.

Und Amerikaner.

Meine Freunde sagen Politik macht diese Welt kaputt.

Meine Freunde empfinden die Gier nach Macht nur als Schmutz.

Ihre Feinde sind die Trumps, Netanjahus und Khameneis.

Ihre Feinde sind die Hamas, Putins.

Alle mit Raketen.

Ihre Feinde haben mit normalen Menschen Nichts zu tun.

Säen auf die Erde Hass und vergießen darauf Blut.

Meine Freunde schreien.

Free Palestine.

Free Iran.

Meine Freunde hassen Krieg.

Doch sie sind nicht radikal.

Ihre Feinde sind nicht Juden und Muslime oder Christen.

Ihre Feinde sind Diktatoren und Faschisten.

Die uns aufeinander hetzen, guck wir drehen uns im Kreis.

Wie oft in der Geschichte zahlten wir denselben Preis.

Ich hab′ es Leid!

Denn ein Mensch hat Emotionen.

Doch wozu sie fähig sind.

Macht sie eher zu Dämonen!

Slawa Ukrajini!
2-0442-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear people of Europe! I was in a bombed out house in Kyiv last week. I thought of a song and it goes like this:

My friends are Iranian.

My friends are from Gaza.

My friends are Ukrainians, Russians.

And Americans.

My friends say politics is destroying this world.

My friends see the greed for power as just dirt.

Their enemies are the Trumps, Netanyahu and Khamenei.

Their enemies are Hamas, Putin's.

All with rockets.

Your enemies have nothing to do with normal people.

Sowing hatred on the earth and shedding blood on it.

My friends are screaming.

Free Palestine.

Free Iran.

My friends hate war.

But they are not radical.

Their enemies are not Jews and Muslims or Christians.

Your enemies are dictators and fascists.

Those who turn us on each other look like we're going around in circles.

How many times in history did we pay the same price.

I'm tired of it!

Because a person has emotions.

But what they are capable of.

Rather make them demons!

Slava Ukraini!

2-0444-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Rysslands brutala krig mot Ukraina kräver vårt fortsatta och solidariska stöd. Samtidigt måste vi göra mer för att försvaga Putins krigsmaskin. EU:s länder måste sluta köpa den ryska gasen.

EU måste också sätta stopp för den ryska skuggflottan som kringgår sanktionerna. Den är ett hot både mot säkerheten och miljön i våra hav.

Vi får aldrig, aldrig glömma krigets mest oskyldiga offer: barnen. Tiotusentals ukrainska barn har tvångsdeporterats från sina hem, och vi kräver att Ryssland omedelbart och säkert återför alla kidnappade barn till sina hem.

Slutligen: Ukraina visar en imponerande framtidstro. Trots kriget pågår ett målmedvetet arbete för en grön återuppbyggnad och en uppbyggnad av förnybar energi. Där ska EU vara. Där ska vi stödja dem och välkomna dem i den europeiska gemenskapen. Slava Ukraini.
2-0444-0000.englishText:
Madam Speaker! Russia's brutal war against Ukraine requires our continued and solidarity support. At the same time, we must do more to weaken Putin's war machine. EU countries must stop buying Russian gas.

The EU must also put an end to the Russian shadow fleet that circumvents the sanctions. It is a threat to both safety and the environment in our seas.

We must never, ever forget the most innocent victims of war: the children. Tens of thousands of Ukrainian children have been forcibly deported from their homes, and we demand that Russia immediately and safely return all kidnapped children to their homes.

Finally: Ukraine shows an impressive faith in the future. Despite the war, purposeful work is underway for a green reconstruction and a build-up of renewable energy. That's where the EU should be. There we shall support them and welcome them in the European community. Slave Ukraine.

2-0445-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! 100 tysięcy pomordowanych Polek i Polaków to nie jest kwestia polsko-ukraińska, w dodatku „historyczna″. Uhonorowanie morderców Polaków nie jest konfliktem polsko-ukraińskim. To prowokacja.

Prowokacja nie tylko wycelowana w Polskę, która przecież zawsze była orędownikiem i wsparciem dla Ukrainy. Ale prowokacja wobec wartości europejskiej, bo to wartości europejskie zapisane w traktatach. Nikt na takich wartościach nie może budować relacji z Unią Europejską. To tak jakbyśmy Niemcom pozwolili na to, by gloryfikowali z powrotem Hitlera i jego zbrodniarzy.

Chcemy zakończenia wojny, bo przecież to warunek podstawowy, żeby wejść do Unii Europejskiej. Chcemy uregulowania granic, bo to kolejny warunek, żeby przystąpić do Unii Europejskiej. Wreszcie chcemy realnych negocjacji. A co proponujemy? Powiedzcie to Europie: punkt 102 – otwarcie granic i wolny handel. Mówicie o tym, że CBAM, czyli podatek graniczny, przestał być ważny. Wyrzućcie go do kosza, bo produkty z całego świata przez Ukrainę dotrą do Europy bez żadnych obostrzeń...

(Przewodnicząca odebrała mówczyni głos)
2-0445-0000.englishText:
Madam President! 100,000 murdered Polish men and women are not a Polish-Ukrainian issue, nor a "historical" one at that. Honoring the murderers of Poles is not a Polish-Ukrainian conflict. It is a provocation.

The provocation is not only aimed at Poland, which has always been an advocate and supporter of Ukraine. But it is a provocation towards European values, because these are European values written in the treaties. No one can build relations with the European Union on such values. It's as if we allowed the Germans to glorify Hitler and his criminals again.

We want the war to end because it is a basic condition for joining the European Union. We want borders to be regulated because it is another condition for joining the European Union. Finally, we want real negotiations. What do we propose? Tell it to Europe: point 102 - opening borders and free trade. You say that CBAM, i.e. border tax, is no longer valid. Throw it in the trash, because products from all over the world will reach Europe through Ukraine without any restrictions...

(The President cut off the speaker's floor)

2-0446-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, het is gemakkelijk om Oekraïne een toekomst in Europa te beloven. De vraag is: hoe gaan we samen met Oekraïne die belofte ook waarmaken?

Oekraïne is een land in oorlog. Juist daarom vraagt het toetredingsproces om urgentie. Wij hebben Oekraïne nodig voor onze veiligheid. Tegelijkertijd moet het toetredingsproces zorgvuldig verlopen om de stabiliteit van Europa te waarborgen.

Oekraïne is geen doorsnee kandidaat-lidstaat. Het land beschikt over een landbouwgebied dat groter is dan dat van Frankrijk. Dit biedt veel kansen voor de toekomstige bio-economie van Europa. Tegelijkertijd ligt het bruto binnenlands product per inwoner ver onder het Europees gemiddelde.

De toetreding van Oekraïne betekent een modernisering van Europa. Anders blijven onze beloften louter beloften, zonder inhoud.
2-0446-0000.englishText:
Mr President, it is easy to promise Ukraine a future in Europe. The question is: how are we going to fulfill that promise together with Ukraine?

Ukraine is a country at war. That is precisely why the accession process requires urgency. We need Ukraine for our security. At the same time, the accession process must be conducted carefully to guarantee the stability of Europe.

Ukraine is not an average candidate country. The country has an agricultural area larger than that of France. This offers many opportunities for Europe's future bioeconomy. At the same time, the gross domestic product per inhabitant is far below the European average.

Ukraine's accession means a modernization of Europe. Otherwise our promises will remain mere promises, without substance.

2-0447-0000.sourceText: Gerbiama Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Tebevykstant precedento neturinčiam karo spaudimui, Ukraina sėkmingai stiprina demokratines institucijas, vykdo teismų reformas, siekia kovoti su korupcija ir įrodo, kad geba atsakingai įsisavinti kiekvieną paramos eurą. Tuo tarpu Europos Sąjunga privalo, jau privalėjo atverti likusius derybų klasterius, toliau teikti finansinę paramą ir dar griežtinti sankcijas Rusijai, įskaitant kovą su sankcijų apeidinėjimu. Šiandien ukrainiečiai vėl atakavo kelis sankcionuotus šešėlinius rusų tanklaivius, bet iki sisteminio užkardymo vis dar toli. Rusijos šešėlinis laivynas vis dar perveža du trečdalius Rusijos naftos eksporto. Privalome didinti spaudimą, užtikrindami nuolatinį sistemingą Rusijos ekonomikos, jų bankinės sistemos ardymą, įšaldyto turto konfiskavimą, kad rusai pagaliau nutrauktų agresiją.
2-0447-0000.englishText: Dear President, Commissioner, colleagues. Under the unprecedented pressure of war, Ukraine is successfully strengthening democratic institutions, carrying out judicial reforms, seeking to fight corruption and proving that it can responsibly absorb every euro of aid. Meanwhile, the European Union must, and already had to, open the remaining negotiation clusters, continue to provide financial support and further tighten sanctions against Russia, including the fight against sanctions evasion. Today, the Ukrainians again attacked several sanctioned shadow Russian tankers, but they are still a long way from a systematic deterrence. Russia's shadow fleet still carries two-thirds of Russia's oil exports. We must increase the pressure by ensuring the continuous systematic destruction of the Russian economy, their banking system, the confiscation of frozen assets, so that the Russians finally stop their aggression.

2-0448-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, is ábhar fíorthábhachtach é seo dúinn uile.

Therefore, our support for Ukraine must continue to be unconditional and unwavering. This support must remain unconditional even where this brings economic or political challenges for all of us. Ukraine is defending all of Europe, and we must take every single measure possible to choke the Russian economy and ensure nothing we do in the EU enhances its ability to maintain this war.

I support the strongest possible sanctions against Russia and we must build on this in the 21st package, and also on our energy independence. Yesterday, we saw more deadly missile and drone attacks in Kyiv – another stark reminder of the horrors that the Ukrainian people must live with.

On Ukraine's accession: reforms are needed. Enlargement is and must remain merit-based. But we should applaud Ukraine for the work it is doing to make reform after reform, whilst under constant bombardment from Russia.

As regards peace, I will quote Warren Buffett: 'you can't do good business with a bad person'.

Bí cúramach, buaigh an cogadh agus gheobhaimid cogadh agus síocháin bhuan.
2-0448-0000.englishText:
Mr President, this is a very important matter for all of us.

Therefore, our support for Ukraine must continue to be unconditional and unwavering. This support must remain unconditional even where this brings economic or political challenges for all of us. Ukraine is defending all of Europe, and we must take every single measure possible to choke the Russian economy and ensure nothing we do in the EU enhances its ability to maintain this war.

I support the strongest possible sanctions against Russia and we must build on this in the 21st package, and also on our energy independence. Yesterday, we saw more deadly missile and drone attacks in Kyiv – another stark reminder of the horrors that the Ukrainian people must live with.

On Ukraine's accession: reforms are needed. Enlargement is and must remain merit-based. But we should applaud Ukraine for the work it is doing to make reform after reform, whilst under constant bombardment from Russia.

As regards peace, I will quote Warren Buffett: 'you can't do good business with a bad person'.

Be careful, win the war and we will have lasting war and peace.

2-0452-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Ukraina har bevisat att det går att slå mot Rysslands hjärta. Genom precisionsattacker mot raffinaderier, militärbaser och annan strategisk infrastruktur höjs kostnaden för Putins krig.

Europa har en skyldighet att ge Ukraina fler av de långdistansrobotar och vapensystem som gör skillnad. Vår plikt är inte bara att hjälpa Ukraina att överleva, utan att göra Ryssland för svagt för att kunna fortsätta sitt anfallskrig.

Gripen-samarbetet mellan Sverige och Ukraina visar att enskilda länder kan gå före. Nu måste politiska begränsningar av attacker mot legitima militära mål i Ryssland avskaffas. Samtidigt måste vi övergå från att skicka materiel till att bygga en gemensam försvarsindustri med Ukraina, och att göra ukrainska företag till en självklar del av Europas försvarsmarknad.

Ledarskap handlar inte om att inte visa vägen när andra tvekar. Det handlar om att agera kraftfullare för att säkra freden i Europa. Slava Ukraini.
2-0452-0000.englishText:
Madam Speaker! Ukraine has proven that it is possible to strike at the heart of Russia. Through precision attacks against refineries, military bases and other strategic infrastructure, the cost of Putin's war is increased.

Europe has an obligation to provide Ukraine with more of the long-range robots and weapon systems that make a difference. Our duty is not only to help Ukraine survive, but to make Russia too weak to continue its war of aggression.

The Gripen cooperation between Sweden and Ukraine shows that individual countries can lead the way. Now, political restrictions on attacks against legitimate military targets in Russia must be removed. At the same time, we must move from sending materiel to building a joint defense industry with Ukraine, and making Ukrainian companies a natural part of Europe's defense market.

Leadership is not about not showing the way when others hesitate. It is about acting more forcefully to secure peace in Europe. Slave Ukraine.

2-0453-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Przyjmujemy bardzo ważne sprawozdanie dotyczące relacji Unia Europejska–Ukraina. Oceniamy kandydata. Rozpoczął się formalnie proces negocjacji akcesyjnych z Ukrainą. Został po długim okresie odblokowany. Ta decyzja była jednością i tu również ma pełne nasze wsparcie.

Ale Unia to nie tylko wspólny rynek, nie tylko Schengen, nie tylko budżet, to przede wszystkim wartości. I musi to wybrzmieć wprost. W rozmowie o wspólnej przyszłości jedna sprawa pozostała niezałatwiona. Unię Europejską tworzą państwa i społeczeństwa, które potrafiły przezwyciężyć demony przeszłości i stanąć w prawdzie wobec zła. I zawsze fundamentem do pojednania i współpracy była prawda.

Ukraina i jej elity muszą tę sprawę rozwiązać. To nie jest sprawa między Polską a Ukrainą. Tu chodzi o europejskie wartości. Nie ma zgody na odwoływanie się do osób i formacji odpowiedzialnych za zbrodnie ludobójstwa. Ta sprawa musi wybrzmieć również w tym sprawozdaniu.
2-0453-0000.englishText:
Madam President! We are adopting a very important report on European Union-Ukraine relations. We evaluate the candidate. The process of accession negotiations with Ukraine has formally begun. It was unlocked after a long time. This decision was one of unity and here too it has our full support.

But the EU is not only the common market, not only Schengen, not only the budget, it is, above all, values. And it has to be clear. In the conversation about our common future, one issue remained unresolved. The European Union is made up of states and societies that were able to overcome the demons of the past and stand truthfully in the face of evil. And the foundation for reconciliation and cooperation has always been truth.

Ukraine and its elites must solve this matter. This is not a matter between Poland and Ukraine. This is about European values. There is no consent to refer to persons and formations responsible for the crimes of genocide. This issue must also be mentioned in this report.

2-0455-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, este debate intenso y prolongado sobre Ucrania pone de manifiesto dos evidencias que necesitan ser expresadas.

La primera es que la conexión entre el apoyo a la defensa de Ucrania frente a la agresión de Rusia y las negociaciones de la futura adhesión es tan estrecha que no podrá resolverse si la Unión Europea no madura lo bastante y crece lo bastante para ser sentada en la mesa de la negociación que decida el futuro de Ucrania y establezca una paz digna y honorable para este país vecino que aspira a la adhesión.

La segunda es que esa adhesión no basta sencillamente con resolverla con una cuestión de examen de sus méritos individuales en Estado de Derecho y lucha contra la corrupción, sino que hará falta —más pronto que tarde— traer también al debate las reformas institucionales que permitan crear el espacio para acomodar a todos los candidatos a la adhesión y, particularmente, a un país tan enorme, con una agricultura tan significativa y con problemas de Estado de Derecho y lucha contra la corrupción tan importantes como los que representa Ucrania.
2-0455-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, this intense and prolonged debate on Ukraine highlights two pieces of evidence that need to be expressed.

The first is that the connection between support for the defense of Ukraine against Russian aggression and future accession negotiations is so close that it cannot be resolved if the European Union does not mature enough and grow enough to be seated at the negotiating table that decides the future of Ukraine and establishes a dignified and honorable peace for this neighboring country that aspires to accession.

The second is that this accession is not enough to simply resolve it with a question of examining their individual merits in the rule of law and the fight against corruption, but it will be necessary - sooner rather than later - to also bring to the debate the institutional reforms that will create the space to accommodate all the candidates for accession and, particularly, such a huge country, with such significant agriculture and with problems of the rule of law and the fight against corruption as important as those represented by Ukraine.

2-0456-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Oczywistym jest, że Rosja jest ogromnym zagrożeniem dla Europy, również dla Ukrainy, co widzimy w działaniach wojennych, które prowadzi ten kraj przeciwko Ukrainie. Natomiast musimy też zdawać sobie sprawę, gdy dyskutujemy dzisiaj tutaj o sprawozdaniu w sprawie Ukrainy, z tego, że wszelkie ruchy ze strony Ukrainy w kierunku europejskim muszą być poprzedzone prawdą. I jestem niestety zszokowany decyzją, którą podjął prezydent Zełenski, decydując się na taki krok, który poczynił, to znaczy nazwanie jednej z jednostek ukraińskich imieniem UPA, czyli zbrodniarzy wojennych, którzy wymordowali ponad 100 tysięcy Polaków w czasie II wojny światowej.

Bez jasnej deklaracji Parlamentu Europejskiego, że było to ludobójstwo, bez jasnej deklaracji Parlamentu Europejskiego, że nie ma zgody na czczenie takich osób jak Bandera, nie możemy mówić w przyszłości o integracji europejskiej, głębszej z Ukrainą. Musi to dzisiaj wybrzmieć. I dlatego apeluję do moich kolegów ze wszystkich frakcji politycznych, również do kolegów z Polski, aby poparli poprawki, które zgłosiła grupa ECR.
2-0456-0000.englishText:
Madam President! It is obvious that Russia is a huge threat to Europe, including to Ukraine, as we can see in the hostilities that this country is conducting against Ukraine. However, we must also realize, when we discuss the report on Ukraine here today, that any moves by Ukraine towards Europe must be preceded by the truth. And I am unfortunately shocked by the decision that President Zelensky made, taking the step he took, namely naming one of the Ukrainian units after the UPA, i.e. war criminals who murdered over 100,000 Poles during World War II.

Without a clear declaration of the European Parliament that it was genocide, without a clear declaration of the European Parliament that there is no consent to honoring people like Bandera, we cannot talk about European integration, deeper with Ukraine, in the future. It must be heard today. And that is why I appeal to my colleagues from all political factions, including my colleagues from Poland, to support the amendments submitted by the ECR Group.

2-0459-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, dragi colegi, eu știam că atunci când o țară aderă la Uniunea Europeană, trebuie să îndeplinească niște criterii și să ne gândim logic, fără niciun fel de probleme colaterale: Îndeplinește Ucraina aceste criterii? De pildă, Ucraina respectă drepturile minorităților? Am auzit aici de la toți colegii că nu. Vă pot spune și eu despre minoritatea românească, și este a doua minoritate din Ucraina, după minoritatea rusă, că a pățit tot felul de nenorociri și că preoții noștri au fost acolo bătuți, arestați și acuzați de toate prostiile din lume.

Nu este niciunul astăzi condamnat pentru nimic, pentru că nu era nimic adevărat. Respectă Ucraina libertatea de exprimare? Era un coleg aici care spunea că nu este adevărat că ar fi închis Zelenski niște televiziuni în 2021. Vă spun eu că le-a închis și se numesc Zic, New Swan și un 112. Erau televiziunile opoziției de la acea vreme, Care opoziție mai avea puțin și ajungea pe primul loc. Sigur că da, putem să spunem orice dorim, dar Ucraina (...)

(Președinta a retras cuvântul vorbitorului)
2-0459-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, I knew that when a country joins the European Union, it must meet certain criteria and let's think logically, without any collateral problems: Does Ukraine meet these criteria? For example, does Ukraine respect the rights of minorities? I heard from all the colleagues here that no. I can also tell you about the Romanian minority, and it is the second minority in Ukraine, after the Russian minority, that it suffered all kinds of misfortunes and that our priests were beaten, arrested and accused of all the nonsense in the world.

No one is convicted of anything today, because nothing was true. Does Ukraine respect freedom of expression? There was a colleague here who said that it is not true that Zelenski closed some televisions in 2021. I tell you that he closed them and they are called Zic, New Swan and a 112. They were the opposition televisions at that time, Which opposition had a little left and reached the first place. Of course yes, we can say whatever we want, but Ukraine (...)

(The President withdrew the speaker)

2-0463-0000.sourceText:
La discussione è chiusa.

La votazione si svolgerà domani, mercoledì 8 luglio 2026.

Dichiarazioni scritte (articolo 178)
2-0463-0000.englishText:
The discussion is closed.

Written declarations (Article 178)

2-0465-0000.sourceText: Conformemente all'articolo 251, paragrafo 4, del regolamento, informo l'Aula che non è pervenuta richiesta di mettere ai voti le rettifiche annunciate in plenaria lunedì 6 luglio, per cui le rettifiche si considerano approvate e saranno pubblicate sulla pagina web della plenaria.
2-0465-0000.englishText: In accordance with Rule 251(4) of the Rules of Procedure, I inform the House that no request has been received to put to the vote the corrections announced in the plenary on Monday 6 July, so the corrections are deemed to have been approved and will be published on the plenary webpage.

2-0467-0000.sourceText: L'ordine del giorno reca la relazione di Sven Mikser, a nome della commissione per gli affari esteri, sulla relazione 2025 della Commissione sulla Moldova (2025/2258(INI)) (A10-0164/2026).
2-0467-0000.englishText: The next item is the report by Sven Mikser, on behalf of the Committee on Foreign Affairs, on the Commission's 2025 report on Moldova (2025/2258(INI)) (A10-0164/2026).

2-0471-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, en las elecciones de septiembre, el pueblo moldavo dio una lección y dijo claramente que quiere avanzar junto a la Unión Europea y hacia la Unión Europea. Además, lo hizo en un contexto difícil marcado por injerencias externas, por presiones, por desinformación y por mucha intoxicación.

Por eso, el mensaje que lanzaron los ciudadanos y ciudadanas de Moldavia tiene todavía más valor político. Y nosotros, la Unión Europea, tenemos la obligación de responder con responsabilidad y exigencia. La responsabilidad y la exigencia implican reformas, independencia de la justicia, Estado de Derecho y lucha contra la corrupción. Pero también tenemos que responder con una actitud constructiva para que cada avance que dé Moldavia se tenga en cuenta.

Además, nos encontramos en un momento en el que algunos están incluso trabajando desde dentro, desde la Unión Europea, para debilitar la Unión y sus valores. En ese momento, Moldavia nos está recordando firmemente a todos por qué nuestro proyecto —el proyecto de Unión Europea— sigue teniendo sentido, porque todavía hay pueblos que ven en Europa una promesa de libertad, de democracia, de seguridad y de prosperidad como nosotros la vivimos.

Ahora es el momento de ser ambiciosos y abrir todos los clústeres de negociación de una vez, porque Moldavia necesita a la Unión Europea, y Europa también necesita pueblos que sigan creyendo en la Unión Europea.
2-0471-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, in the September elections, the Moldovan people taught a lesson and clearly said that they want to move forward together with the European Union and towards the European Union. Furthermore, he did so in a difficult context marked by external interference, pressure, misinformation and a lot of intoxication.

Therefore, the message sent by the citizens of Moldova has even more political value. And we, the European Union, have the obligation to respond with responsibility and demand. Responsibility and demand imply reforms, independence of justice, the rule of law and the fight against corruption. But we also have to respond with a constructive attitude so that every progress that Moldova makes is taken into account.

Furthermore, we find ourselves at a time when some are even working from within, from within the European Union, to weaken the Union and its values. At that moment, Moldova is firmly reminding us all why our project – the European Union project – still makes sense, because there are still people who see in Europe a promise of freedom, democracy, security and prosperity as we live it.

Now is the time to be ambitious and open all the negotiation clusters at once, because Moldova needs the European Union, and Europe also needs people who continue to believe in the European Union.

2-0472-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, dragi colegi, doamnă comisar, o Europă mai puternică înseamnă o Republică Moldova parte a Uniunii Europene. Integrarea este un proces tehnic și politic. De aceea este important să privim în perspectivă istorică: în 20 de ani, unde vedem Moldova și Uniunea Europeană? Atunci când lăsăm un gol de securitate la granițele noastre, acel gol este umplut de instabilitate, iar Republica Moldova se află astăzi în prima linie a acestei realități.

Sprijinirea Moldovei nu este doar un act de solidaritate, ci și o investiție strategică în securitatea și stabilitatea întregii Uniuni Europene. În ciuda presiunilor externe, a atacurilor hibride și a încercărilor constante de destabilizare, Republica Moldova a ales democrația, statul de drept și valorile occidentale. Această alegere necesită din partea noastră însă un sprijin ferm și consecvent.

O Moldovă în Uniunea Europeană înseamnă frontiera estică mai sigură, o reziliență mai mare împotriva ingerințelor externe și un mesaj clar că Europa își protejează partenerii care aleg libertatea și pacea. Extinderea europeană a fost întotdeauna unul dintre cele mai puternice instrumente ale UE pentru a consolida pacea, prosperitatea și stabilitatea în Europa. Cu fiecare extindere, toate țările UE au devenit mai puternice, mai prospere, iar Europa mai stabilă.

Sprijinind Republica Moldova, consolidăm atât viitorul unui stat vecin, cât și întărim securitatea, unitatea și credibilitatea întregului proiect european. Tocmai de aceea, viitorul Republicii Moldova trebuie să fie în Uniunea Europeană.
2-0472-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, a stronger Europe means a Republic of Moldova part of the European Union. Integration is a technical and political process. That is why it is important to look in historical perspective: in 20 years, where do we see Moldova and the European Union? When we leave a security gap at our borders, that gap is filled with instability, and the Republic of Moldova is today on the front line of this reality.

Supporting Moldova is not only an act of solidarity, but also a strategic investment in the security and stability of the entire European Union. Despite external pressures, hybrid attacks and constant destabilization attempts, the Republic of Moldova chose democracy, the rule of law and Western values. This choice, however, requires firm and consistent support from us.

A Moldova in the European Union means a more secure eastern border, greater resilience against external interference and a clear message that Europe protects its partners who choose freedom and peace. European enlargement has always been one of the EU's most powerful tools to strengthen peace, prosperity and stability in Europe. With each enlargement, all EU countries have become stronger, more prosperous and Europe more stable.

By supporting the Republic of Moldova, we strengthen both the future of a neighboring state and strengthen the security, unity and credibility of the entire European project. That is precisely why the future of the Republic of Moldova must be in the European Union.

2-0473-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisar, domnule raportor, raportul pe care îl dezbatem astăzi confirmă o realitate incontestabilă: Republica Moldova avansează accelerat și hotărât spre obiectivul său de a deveni un stat membru al Uniunii Europene.

Vreau să salut reziliența extraordinară a cetățenilor moldoveni, în ciuda amenințărilor hibride, a dezinformării și a interferențelor fără precedent orchestrate de Kremlin. Aceștia și-au apărat democrația și au reconfirmat ireversibilitatea parcursului european al Moldovei.

Progresele tehnice și reformele de la Chișinău sunt remarcabile. Faptul că am deschis recent negocierile pe primul cluster, cel al valorilor fundamentale, este o dovadă a seriozității acestui angajament. Moldova este deja parte a spațiului european de roaming și se integrează în zona unică de plăți. De asemenea, prin planul de creștere de 1,9 miliarde aprobat, susținem tangibil și direct modernizarea școlilor, a spitalelor și a întreprinderilor locale.

Republica Moldova nu mai este doar un beneficiar, ci contribuie deja activ la securitatea continentului nostru. Responsabilitate este să renunțăm la scuze și pretexte formale și să rămânem alături de Chișinău la fiecare pas, deoarece locul firesc al Moldovei este aici, în familia europeană.
2-0473-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, Mr. Rapporteur, the report we are debating today confirms an indisputable reality: the Republic of Moldova is advancing rapidly and decisively towards its goal of becoming a member state of the European Union.

I want to salute the extraordinary resilience of Moldovan citizens despite hybrid threats, disinformation and unprecedented interference orchestrated by the Kremlin. They defended their democracy and reconfirmed the irreversibility of Moldova's European path.

The technical progress and reforms in Chisinau are remarkable. The fact that we recently opened negotiations on the first cluster, that of fundamental values, is proof of the seriousness of this commitment. Moldova is already part of the European roaming space and integrates into the single payment area. Also, through the approved 1.9 billion growth plan, we are tangibly and directly supporting the modernization of schools, hospitals and local businesses.

The Republic of Moldova is no longer just a beneficiary, but already actively contributes to the security of our continent. It is our responsibility to give up formal excuses and pretexts and to stand by Chisinau every step of the way, because Moldova's natural place is here, in the European family.

2-0474-0000.sourceText: Fru formand! Den 28. september 2025 var jeg sammen med andre kolleger herfra valgobservatør ved parlamentsvalget i Moldova. Der var stor nervøsitet op til valget på grund af en massiv russisk påvirkning med misinformation, med bestikkelse med videre. Men heldigvis vandt de proeuropæiske demokratiske partier. Derfor kan Moldova fortsætte sin vej mod et EU-medlemskab, og vi støtter reformer, men der er stadig udfordringer med korruption og med organiseret kriminalitet. Den største udfordring er selvsagt udbryderregionen Transnistrien, men også generelt de fortsatte russiske forsøg på hybridkrig, på misinformation, på destabilisering. Det er mit håb, at Moldova som Europas fattigste land vil fortsætte reformprocessen og gøre sig klar til et EU-medlemskab, så Moldova definitivt bliver en del af Europa. Vi vil gerne hjælpe dem, så meget, vi kan.
2-0474-0000.englishText: Madam President! On 28 September 2025, together with other colleagues from here, I was an election observer at the parliamentary elections in Moldova. There was great nervousness leading up to the election due to a massive Russian influence with misinformation, with bribery and so on. But luckily the pro-European democratic parties won. Therefore, Moldova can continue its path towards EU membership and we support reforms, but there are still challenges with corruption and with organized crime. The biggest challenge is of course the breakaway region of Transnistria, but also in general the continued Russian attempts at hybrid war, at misinformation, at destabilization. It is my hope that Moldova, as Europe's poorest country, will continue the reform process and get ready for EU membership, so that Moldova will definitely become part of Europe. We want to help them as much as we can.

2-0475-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Jag skulle också vilja tacka föredraganden Sven Mikser för ett bra betänkande. Flera av de punkter som var viktiga för oss i vänstern finns med, som att bekämpa fattigdomen i Moldavien, att fortsätta arbetet mot korruptionen, att stödja investeringar i förnybar energi och för ett verkligt energioberoende och att värna miljön. Som helhet är det ett bra betänkande.

Just nu skakas Moldavien av lite turbulens i inrikespolitiken. Viktiga personer har avgått. Det finns anklagelser om korruption. Det är naturligtvis illa, men det hade varit ännu mer illa om det inte hade kommit fram, om man inte hade dragit fram oegentligheter i ljuset.

På ett sätt är det ett gott tecken att även i det statsbärande partiet avslöjas korruption. Det visar att arbetet mot korruptionen tas på allvar.
2-0475-0000.englishText:
Madam Speaker! I would also like to thank the rapporteur Sven Mikser for a good report. Several of the points that were important to us on the left are included, such as fighting poverty in Moldova, continuing the work against corruption, supporting investments in renewable energy and for real energy independence and protecting the environment. As a whole, it is a good report.

Right now, Moldova is being shaken by some turbulence in domestic politics. Important people have resigned. There are allegations of corruption. It is of course bad, but it would have been even worse if it had not come to light, if irregularities had not been brought to light.

In a way, it is a good sign that even in the state-bearing party corruption is exposed. It shows that the work against corruption is taken seriously.

2-0476-0000.sourceText:
, от името на групата ESN. – Г-жо Председател, пред Молдова продължават да стоят сериозни предизвикателства в борбата с корупцията, реформата на съдебната система и укрепването на държавните институции. Именно затова призивите за незабавното отваряне на всички групи преговорни глави и ускоряването на присъединителния процес не са в интерес нито на гражданите на Европейския съюз, нито на гражданите на Молдова.

Европейската интеграция е силен инструмент, който трябва да създава реални икономически ползи за бизнеса, да укрепва конкурентоспособността и да защитава традиционните национални общности като българската. Прибързаното придвижване към членство, преди изпълнението на необходимите реформи, би поставило под риск именно тези дългосрочни ползи. Европейският съюз трябва да прилага собствените си критерии по еднакъв начин към всички държави кандидатки. Само така ще запазим доверието в политиката на разширяване и ще гарантираме, че членството се основава на реални заслуги, а не на политическа целесъобразност.
2-0476-0000.englishText:
, on behalf of the ESN Group. - Madam President, Moldova continues to face serious challenges in the fight against corruption, the reform of the judicial system and the strengthening of state institutions. That is why calls for the immediate opening of all groups of negotiating chapters and the acceleration of the accession process are not in the interest of either the citizens of the European Union or the citizens of Moldova.

European integration is a powerful tool that should create real economic benefits for business, strengthen competitiveness and protect traditional national communities like the Bulgarian one. A hasty move towards membership, before the necessary reforms are implemented, would put precisely these long-term benefits at risk. The European Union must apply its own criteria equally to all candidate countries. Only then will we maintain confidence in enlargement policy and ensure that membership is based on real merit, not political expediency.

2-0477-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, stimați colegi, doamnă comisar, în ultimul an, Republica Moldova este statul candidat pentru aderarea la Uniunea Europeană, care a înregistrat cele mai semnificative progrese pe calea integrării europene. Cetățenii Republicii Moldova încep să simtă beneficiile concrete ale integrării în Uniunea Europeană. Deja împreună, prin efortul autorităților din Republica Moldova și prin efortul instituțiilor europene, reușim să integrăm Republica Moldova în tot mai multe programe europene, astfel încât cetățenii să simtă deja, înainte de data aderării, avantajele integrării europene.

În urmă cu puține săptămâni am reușit să deschidem, și la nivel politic, la cel mai înalt nivel politic, negocierile pe primul cluster al negocierilor de aderare, ca urmare a progreselor bune înregistrate la nivel tehnic.

Prin raportul Parlamentului European, pe care îl vom adopta mâine. Solicităm trei lucruri.

În primul rând, deschiderea negocierilor pe toate clasele de negociere la nivel politic, cât mai curând posibil, nu mai târziu de finalul acestui an. Unu la mână. Doi la mână: continuarea reformelor pe calea integrării europene și, trei la mână, creșterea sprijinului financiar și tehnic din partea Uniunii Europene pentru Republica Moldova, fiindcă Federația Rusă a încercat în ultimii ani să țină Republica Moldova pe loc și a eșuat. Dar Federația Rusă va continua să încerce să răspândească știri false, propagandă, dezinformare în Republica Moldova, încercând să țină Republica Moldova pe loc.

Noi trebuie să fim mai puternici, să fim solidari cu oamenii din Republica Moldova, astfel încât Republica Moldova să continue să avanseze rapid pe calea integrării europene. O Republică Moldovă puternică, stabilă, reformată este bună pentru cetățenii Republicii Moldova, dar este o veste bună și pentru Uniunea Europeană în ansamblu.
2-0477-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, in the last year, the Republic of Moldova is the candidate state for joining the European Union, which recorded the most significant progress on the path of European integration. The citizens of the Republic of Moldova are beginning to feel the concrete benefits of integration into the European Union. Already together, through the efforts of the authorities of the Republic of Moldova and the efforts of the European institutions, we manage to integrate the Republic of Moldova into more and more European programs, so that the citizens already feel, before the date of accession, the advantages of European integration.

A few weeks ago we managed to open, also at the political level, at the highest political level, the negotiations on the first cluster of the accession negotiations, as a result of the good progress made at the technical level.

Through the European Parliament's report, which we will adopt tomorrow. We ask for three things.

First, the opening of negotiations on all levels of negotiation at the political level, as soon as possible, no later than the end of this year. One in hand. Two in hand: the continuation of reforms on the path of European integration and, three in hand, the increase of financial and technical support from the European Union for the Republic of Moldova, because the Russian Federation tried in recent years to keep the Republic of Moldova in place and failed. But the Russian Federation will continue to try to spread fake news, propaganda, disinformation in the Republic of Moldova, trying to keep the Republic of Moldova in place.

We must be stronger, be in solidarity with the people of the Republic of Moldova, so that the Republic of Moldova continues to advance rapidly on the path of European integration. A strong, stable, reformed Republic of Moldova is good for the citizens of the Republic of Moldova, but it is also good news for the European Union as a whole.

2-0478-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, doresc în primul rând să îl felicit pe colegul meu social-democrat, Sven Mikser, pentru raportul său. Noi, social-democrații, am sprijinit mereu parcursul european al Republicii Moldova. Pentru că da, locul Republicii Moldova este în familia europeană. În ciuda presiunilor externe, a atacurilor hibride și a tentativelor repetate de destabilizare, cetățenii săi au ales calea europeană.

Autoritățile au datoria să facă toate reformele necesare aderării în vederea respectării termenului ambițios fixat pentru finalizarea negocierilor, finalul anului 2028 și suntem aici pentru a sprijini Republica Moldova, iar pentru atingerea acestui obiectiv consolidarea statului de drept, independența justiției, combaterea corupției și modernizarea administrației trebuie să rămână priorități.

Încurajez actorii politici de la Chișinău să gestioneze eficient actualul context politic și să îl transforme într-un impuls pentru accelerarea reformelor europene prin participarea întregii populații. Tocmai de aceea, Parlamentul European transmite astăzi un mesaj clar: Republica Moldova a făcut progrese remarcabile și merită să continue acest parcurs prin deschiderea tuturor capitolelor de negociere la Uniunea Europeană și dorim această deschidere să se întâmple de îndată, pentru că nu putem avea întârzieri.

De asemenea, Uniunea Europeană trebuie să recompenseze meritul, determinarea și rezultatele concrete obținute de Republica Moldova și, în sensul acesta trebuie să oferim un parcurs accelerat de aderare, un parcurs propriu și, de ce nu, chiar fonduri europene suplimentare. În sensul acesta, Republica Moldova, vă așteptăm aici, în Uniunea Europeană.
2-0478-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, I would first of all like to congratulate my Social Democrat colleague, Sven Mikser, on his report. We, the social democrats, have always supported the European path of the Republic of Moldova. Because yes, the place of the Republic of Moldova is in the European family. Despite external pressures, hybrid attacks and repeated attempts at destabilization, its citizens have chosen the European path.

The authorities have the duty to make all the reforms necessary for the accession in order to meet the ambitious deadline set for the completion of the negotiations, the end of 2028, and we are here to support the Republic of Moldova, and to achieve this goal, the strengthening of the rule of law, the independence of the judiciary, the fight against corruption and the modernization of the administration must remain priorities.

I encourage political actors from Chisinau to effectively manage the current political context and turn it into an impetus for accelerating European reforms through the participation of the entire population. That is precisely why the European Parliament is sending a clear message today: the Republic of Moldova has made remarkable progress and deserves to continue this path by opening all the negotiation chapters with the European Union, and we want this opening to happen immediately, because we cannot have delays.

Also, the European Union must reward the merit, determination and concrete results obtained by the Republic of Moldova and, in this sense, we must offer an accelerated accession path, an own path and, why not, even additional European funds. In this sense, Republic of Moldova, we are waiting for you here in the European Union.

2-0479-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Otwarcie faktycznych negocjacji akcesyjnych Mołdawii z Unią Europejską to dobry i zasłużony krok na europejskiej drodze tego państwa. Mołdawia ma prawo i wolę wyrwania się z postsowieckiej strefy wpływów, a my chcemy jej w tym pomóc.

Naszym zadaniem jest wsparcie mołdawskich partnerów w budowie silnego, nowoczesnego i demokratycznego państwa. Oznacza to m.in. konsekwentną walkę z korupcją i oligarchią, które są zmorą każdego społeczeństwa postkomunistycznego.

Unia musi również wspierać działania na rzecz integralności terytorialnej Mołdawii. Odzyskanie przez Kiszyniów kontroli nad Naddniestrzem jest sprawą kluczową. Unia ma narzędzie nacisku, gdyż 70% eksportu towarów z Naddniestrza trafia na rynek europejski. Należy stosować twardą politykę sankcyjną i celną – albo lojalność wobec Mołdawii, albo koniec interesów z Europą.

Pani Komisarz, dużym problemem dotyczącym tempa integracji Mołdawii z Unią jest połączenie jej kandydatury z kandydaturą Ukrainy. Ukraina nie radzi sobie dziś ani z korupcją, ani z oligarchizacją, ani z odradzającym się nacjonalizmem. Dlatego trzeba przyjąć zasadę, że każde państwo jest oceniane na podstawie indywidualnych osiągnięć.
2-0479-0000.englishText:
Madam President! The opening of actual accession negotiations between Moldova and the European Union is a good and well-deserved step on this country's European path. Moldova has the right and will to break out of the post-Soviet sphere of influence, and we want to help it do so.

Our task is to support Moldovan partners in building a strong, modern and democratic state. This means, among others: consistent fight against corruption and oligarchy, which are the nightmare of every post-communist society.

The Union must also support efforts to promote the territorial integrity of Moldova. Chisinau regaining control over Transnistria is crucial. The EU has a pressure tool because 70% of goods exports from Transnistria go to the European market. A tough sanctions and customs policy should be applied - either loyalty to Moldova or the end of business with Europe.

Commissioner, a big problem regarding the pace of Moldova's integration with the EU is combining its candidacy with Ukraine's. Today, Ukraine cannot cope with corruption, oligarchization, or resurgent nationalism. Therefore, it is necessary to adopt the principle that each country is assessed on the basis of individual achievements.

2-0480-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, raportul pe care îl discutăm astăzi nu trebuie privit ca o simplă evaluare a progreselor Republicii Moldova în procesul de integrare. Discuția despre extindere s-a concentrat adesea pe costul aderării. Poate că este momentul să nu mai privim totul doar în termeni ce țin de valoarea investiției, ci sa ne întrebăm care ar fi costul dacă nu am aduce mai rapid Republica Moldova în Uniunea Europeană.

Securitatea Uniunii Europene depinde și de securitatea Republicii Moldova, care luptă de peste 35 de ani să scape de influența malefică a Moscovei, ce menține ilegal trupe militare pe teritoriul său. Cetățenii Republicii Moldova și-au câștigat dreptul de a primi o perspectivă clară de aderare la Uniunea Europeană, iar aceasta trebuie doar accelerată.

Republica Moldova, în pofida presiunii agresive și constante a Rusiei, a reușit să înceapă reformele necesare pentru a fi pregătită de aderare, iar acest drum trebuie încurajat și susținut. De aceea, cred că este important să fim cu toții alături de Chișinău în fiecare clipă.
2-0480-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the report we are discussing today should not be seen as a simple assessment of the progress of the Republic of Moldova in the integration process. The debate about enlargement has often focused on the cost of joining. Perhaps it is time to stop looking at everything only in terms of the value of the investment, but to ask ourselves what the cost would be if we did not bring the Republic of Moldova into the European Union more quickly.

The security of the European Union also depends on the security of the Republic of Moldova, which has been fighting for over 35 years to escape the evil influence of Moscow, which illegally maintains military troops on its territory. The citizens of the Republic of Moldova have earned the right to receive a clear perspective of joining the European Union, and this must only be accelerated.

The Republic of Moldova, despite the aggressive and constant pressure from Russia, managed to start the necessary reforms to be ready for accession, and this path must be encouraged and supported. That's why I think it's important that we all stand by Chisinau every moment.

2-0482-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, Moldova este singurul candidat care a atins 28 din 30 de obiective de aderare. Și asta sub atacuri hibride, șantaj energetic, otrăvire a Prutului și multe alte scumpiri generate de război. Și eu cred că e rândul nostru să fim la înălțimea lor și nu rândul moldovenilor să fie la înălțimea noastră. Ei o fac deja de mult timp.

Eu sunt român, știu ce înseamnă să lupți pentru Europa, când alții te conving că nu meriți, că România s-a chinuit să demonstreze că trebuie să fie în Europa și iată că împlinim 20 de ani. Dar pentru oamenii ăștia care se chinuie de la o alegere la alta prin greutăți, să intre în Uniunea Europeană și o fac convingător, cu un guvern dedicat, trebuie să arătăm solidaritate.

Așa că nu vreau să ne oprim deloc, pentru că Moldova vrea, Europa vrea, Moldova poate, Europa poate. Și cred că este un moment unic, o fereastră de oportunitate care nu se deschide mereu. Așa că chiar îmi doresc, doamna Kos, să facem hora aia în care ați dansat și dumneavoastră la Chișinău, cu Uniunea Europeană (...)
2-0482-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Moldova is the only candidate that achieved 28 out of 30 accession objectives. And this under hybrid attacks, energy blackmail, poisoning of the Prut and many other price increases generated by the war. And I think it's our turn to live up to them and not the Moldovans' turn to live up to us. They have been doing it for a long time.

I'm Romanian, I know what it means to fight for Europe, when others convince you that you don't deserve it, that Romania struggled to prove that it should be in Europe and here we are turning 20 years old. But for these people who struggle from one election to another through difficulties, to enter the European Union and do it convincingly, with a dedicated government, we must show solidarity.

So I don't want us to stop at all, because Moldova wants, Europe wants, Moldova can, Europe can. And I think it's a unique moment, a window of opportunity that doesn't always open. So I really want, Mrs. Kos, to do that hora in which you also danced in Chisinau, with the European Union (...)

2-0483-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Die Republik Moldau befindet sich auf ihrem europäischen Weg – und das ist auch gut so, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen. Doch dieser Weg bedeutet nicht nur Reform auf dem Papier; er bedeutet auch, europäische Grundwerte in der Praxis umzusetzen.

Noch immer gibt es schwerwiegende Menschenrechtsprobleme. Der Europäische Gerichtshof für Menschenrechte hat wiederholt Verstöße festgestellt, unter anderem wegen unmenschlichen Haftbedingungen, Gewalt und erniedrigender Behandlung. Menschenrechte gelten universell: Eine Strafe darf die Freiheit nehmen, aber niemals die Menschlichkeit.

Diese Verantwortung zeigt sich auch im Umgang mit Tieren. Die Situation von streunenden Hunden in Moldau ist weiterhin besorgniserregend: Berichte über schlechte Haltungsbedingungen, grausame Behandlung und Tötungspraktiken müssen ernst genommen werden.

Der Umgang mit den Schwächsten ist ein Maßstab für die Werte einer Gesellschaft. Deswegen braucht es auch im Tierschutz europäische Standards: Kastrations- und Impfprogramme, bessere Bedingungen in Tierheimen und Unterstützung für lokale Akteure.

Der Schutz der Menschenrechte und der Tierschutz folgen beide derselben Grundidee. Eine Gesellschaft zeigt ihre Stärke daran, wie sie mit den Schwächsten umgeht.
2-0483-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! The Republic of Moldova is on its European path - and that's a good thing, dear colleagues. But this path doesn't just mean reform on paper; it also means putting basic European values ​​into practice.

There are still serious human rights problems. The European Court of Human Rights has repeatedly found violations, including inhumane prison conditions, violence and degrading treatment. Human rights are universal: punishment can take away freedom, but never humanity.

This responsibility is also reflected in how we deal with animals. The situation of stray dogs in Moldova remains worrying: reports of poor housing conditions, cruel treatment and killing practices must be taken seriously.

How we treat the most vulnerable is a measure of a society's values. That's why European standards are also needed in animal protection: castration and vaccination programs, better conditions in animal shelters and support for local actors.

The protection of human rights and animal protection both follow the same basic idea. A society shows its strength by how it treats the weakest.

2-0484-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, dragi colegi, eu nu am să mă înscriu în corul lăudătorilor acestei chestiuni cu aderarea Moldovei și Ucrainei la Uniunea Europeană, pentru că eu știam că întotdeauna aceste țări care sunt candidate trebuie să respecte niște criterii. Și criteriul corupției, care este printre primele, nu este deloc respectat. Așa cum știți, probabil Moldova nu mai are premier. Tocmai și-a dat demisia.

De ce și-a dat demisia? În ce context și-a dat demisia? În contextul în care verișoara Maiei Sandu, pseudo președinta acestei pseudo republici... pentru că, de fapt, nu e a noastră Moldova? E parte din România. Mă frapează faptul că nimeni nu spune treaba asta aici, ca și cum ar fi fost normal un pact Ribbentrop-Molotov, de pildă.

Deci ne-am trezit cu verișoara președintei că are salariu de 6000, peste 6000 de euro. Păi noi ajutăm Moldova, noi ducem acolo miliarde pentru reforme și ei își dau salarii de 6000. Dar nu vi se pare (...)

(Președintele a retras cuvântul vorbitorului)
2-0484-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, dear colleagues, I will not join the chorus of praisers of this issue with the accession of Moldova and Ukraine to the European Union, because I knew that these candidate countries always have to respect certain criteria. And the criterion of corruption, which is among the first, is not respected at all. As you know, probably Moldova no longer has a prime minister. He just resigned.

Why did he resign? In what context did he resign? In the context in which Maia Sandu's cousin, the pseudo-president of this pseudo-republic... because, in fact, Moldova is not ours? It is part of Romania. It strikes me that no one says this here, as if a Ribbentrop-Molotov Pact, for example, was normal.

So we found out with the president's cousin that she has a salary of 6,000, over 6,000 euros. Well, we help Moldova, we take billions there for reforms and they give themselves salaries of 6000. But you don't think so (...)

(The President cut off the speaker)

2-0485-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, Moldova je, kao prvo, neovisna država, htio to netko priznati ili ne. I to neovisna država koja se unatoč snažnom ruskom uplitanju i pritisku odlučila za europsku budućnost.

Kada se neke zemlje zapadnog Balkana žale na navodna dvostruka pravila Europske unije, na zastoj u otvaranju nekih poglavlja ili klastera, onda bih im preporučio da pogledaju sve što je Moldova učinila počevši, naravno, od sankcija protiv ruske agresije.

Ja ću ovdje podsjetiti da je Općinski sud u Kišinjevu ustanovio postojanje kampova, na žalost, u Srbiji u entitetu Republika Srpska u Bosni i Hercegovini u kojima se uvježbavalo ljude koji su kasnije trebali u Moldovi potkopavati proeuropsku orijentaciju te zemlje.

Dakako, Moldova ima još puno posla za obaviti, prvenstveno vezano za borbu protiv korupcije, ali njen je napredak očit i stoga Europski parlament mora joj i dalje davati snažnu potporu.
2-0485-0000.englishText:
Honorable Chairman, Moldova is, first of all, an independent country, whether someone wants to admit it or not. And an independent country that, despite strong Russian interference and pressure, decided for a European future.

When some countries of the Western Balkans complain about the alleged double rules of the European Union, about the delay in opening some chapters or clusters, then I would recommend them to look at everything that Moldova has done, starting, of course, with sanctions against Russian aggression.

I will remind here that the Municipal Court in Chisinau established the existence of camps, unfortunately, in Serbia in the Republika Srpska entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where people were trained who were later to undermine the pro-European orientation of that country in Moldova.

Of course, Moldova still has a lot of work to do, primarily related to the fight against corruption, but its progress is obvious and therefore the European Parliament must continue to give it strong support.

2-0486-0000.sourceText:
Г-н Председател, Молдова заслужава категорична и последователна подкрепа от страна на Европейския парламент. Въпреки войната до нейните граници, въпреки хибридните атаки и постоянния външен натиск, страната показва устойчивост и ангажимент към европейския си път.

Европейската перспектива на Молдова трябва да остане надпартиен национален приоритет, основан на демокрация, социална справедливост, върховенство на закона и реални ползи за гражданите. Когато една страна кандидат изпълнява своите ангажименти, Европейският съюз също трябва да изпълни своите. Затова приветствам напредъка на Молдова и призовавам Съвета да даде зелена светлина за следващата стъпка в подготовката и преговорите за членство.

Но подкрепата за Молдова не означава да си затваряме очите за предизвикателствата. Напротив, европейската интеграция изисква реални резултати в съдебната реформа, в борбата с корупцията, в независимостта на институциите и във възстановяването на общественото доверие, особено след оставката на премиера Монтяну. Следващото правителство трябва бързо да върне стабилността, да запази европейския курс и да покаже на гражданите, че реформите не са само изискване на Брюксел, а път към повече сигурност, по-добър живот и по-силна социална защита.

Искам да подчертая и нещо особено важно. Зачитането на правата на малцинствата е основен критерий за всяка страна кандидат. Това включва и българската общност в Тараклия. Всяка административна реформа трябва да гарантира културното и езиково многообразие на общностите в Молдова и тяхното политическо представителство.
2-0486-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Moldova deserves strong and consistent support from the European Parliament. Despite the war at its borders, despite hybrid attacks and constant external pressure, the country shows resilience and commitment to its European path.

Moldova's European perspective must remain a cross-party national priority based on democracy, social justice, the rule of law and real benefits for citizens. When a candidate country fulfills its commitments, the European Union must also fulfill its commitments. I therefore welcome Moldova's progress and call on the Council to give the green light to the next step in membership preparations and negotiations.

But supporting Moldova does not mean closing our eyes to the challenges. On the contrary, European integration requires real results in judicial reform, in the fight against corruption, in the independence of institutions and in the restoration of public trust, especially after the resignation of Prime Minister Montagnou. The next government must quickly restore stability, maintain the European course and show citizens that reforms are not just a demand from Brussels, but a path to more security, a better life and stronger social protection.

I want to emphasize something particularly important. Respect for the rights of minorities is a fundamental criterion for any candidate country. This includes the Bulgarian community in Taraklia. Any administrative reform must guarantee the cultural and linguistic diversity of Moldova's communities and their political representation.

2-0487-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, suntem cu toții de acord că locul Moldovei este în Uniunea Europeană. Sunt frații noștri, ai românilor, vorbesc limba română, sunt creștini ortodocși majoritatea și împărtășesc același trecut și aceleași valori cu România, stat membru UE. Când și cum se va face această aderare? Aici este adevărata cheia a acestei dezbateri.

Prima, cea mai rapidă și firească totodată, ar fi soluția germană, despre care eu și colegii mei din partid am tot vorbit. A doua variantă, aderarea propriu-zisă, trebuie făcută pe un calendar propriu, independent de Ucraina. Moldova are propriul ei drum și propria ei viteză de îndeplinire a condițiilor pentru aderare la UE. Deci nu există niciun motiv să o tratăm la pachet cu Ucraina.

În plus, Ucraina este, din păcate, o țară aflată încă în război cu teritoriul disputat, deci nu putem vorbi de aderare efectivă în acest stadiu. Și ar fi nedrept să susținem și Moldova blocată la pachet cu ea. Orice țară care dorește să adere la UE trebuie să îndeplinească fix aceleași condiții ca și antemergători ei, iar din acest punct de vedere trebuie să spunem clar: Moldova se află cu mulți pași înaintea Ucrainei, deci cu mulți pași mai aproape de Uniunea Europeană.
2-0487-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, we all agree that Moldova's place is in the European Union. They are our brothers, the Romanians, they speak the Romanian language, most of them are Orthodox Christians and share the same past and the same values ​​with Romania, an EU member state. When and how will this accession be made? Herein lies the real crux of this debate.

The first, the fastest and natural at the same time, would be the German solution, which I and my party colleagues have been talking about. The second option, the actual accession, must be done on its own calendar, independent of Ukraine. Moldova has its own way and its own speed of fulfilling the conditions for EU accession. So there is no reason to treat it as a package with Ukraine.

In addition, Ukraine is, unfortunately, a country still at war with the disputed territory, so we cannot talk about actual accession at this stage. And it would be unfair to support Moldova stuck together with it. Any country that wants to join the EU must meet exactly the same conditions as its predecessors, and from this point of view we must say clearly: Moldova is many steps ahead of Ukraine, so many steps closer to the European Union.

2-0488-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, ainsi donc, les négociations d’adhésion s’ouvrent enfin avec la Moldavie: il était temps! Le peuple moldave l’a dit, redit et le répète encore: il se sent européen, il veut entrer dans l’Union européenne. Il a voté en ce sens à plusieurs reprises, en dépit des pressions insensées que la Russie a fait peser sur lui. Manipulation de l’information, achats de voix, oligarques à la botte de Moscou, gangs criminels, pressions économiques: la petite Moldavie a eu droit à tout et a résisté à tout.

On la regarde parfois avec condescendance: on ferait mieux d’en prendre de la graine. Parce que des manipulations de l’information, des groupes de médias étrangers bienveillants vis-à-vis de Vladimir Poutine et des tentatives d’intimidation, eh bien ça ne se passe pas qu’en Moldavie.

Le peuple moldave veut rejoindre l’Union européenne, et ses autorités savent ce qu’elles ont à faire, les réformes qu’elles ont à mener pour y parvenir. Mais nous, est-ce que nous savons ce que nous voulons? Sommes-nous prêts à accueillir de nouveaux membres dans notre Union? J’ai bien peur que nous n’ayons pas encore pris la mesure du monde qui nous entoure.

L’élargissement de l’Union européenne peut être une chance: celle d’échapper à notre encerclement. Mais sa réussite va dépendre aussi de nous.
2-0488-0000.englishText:
Mr President, so the accession negotiations are finally opening with Moldova: it’s about time! The Moldovan people have said it, said it again and again: they feel European, they want to join the European Union. He voted in this direction several times, despite the insane pressure that Russia put on him. Manipulation of information, vote buying, oligarchs under the thumb of Moscow, criminal gangs, economic pressures: little Moldova was entitled to everything and resisted everything.

We sometimes look at it with condescension: we would do better to learn from it. Because manipulation of information, foreign media groups benevolent towards Vladimir Putin and attempts at intimidation, well, it’s not just happening in Moldova.

The Moldovan people want to join the European Union, and their authorities know what they have to do, the reforms they have to carry out to achieve this. But do we know what we want? Are we ready to welcome new members to our Union? I'm afraid we haven't yet grasped the extent of the world around us.

The enlargement of the European Union can be an opportunity: that of escaping our encirclement. But its success will also depend on us.

2-0490-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă comisar, domnule președinte, stimați colegi, programul ambițios al Republicii Moldova pentru a încheia aderarea la sfârșitul anului 2028 trebuie susținut. Este de salutat, dar nu va putea fi pus în aplicare dacă nu îl susținem toți. Și vreau de la bun început să mulțumesc și doamnei comisar, și colegilor care au susținut acest proiect.

Sunt româncă, sunt moldoveancă, cunosc foarte bine Republica Moldova, cunosc cetățenii de acolo, cetățenii își doresc acest lucru și trebuie să-i încurajăm pentru a avea încredere în proiectul Uniunii Europene, pentru că are nevoie administrația de la Chișinău de susținerea populară.

Sigur că nu văd alt drum și trebuie să fim și realiști: Republica Moldova e la graniță, cât de greu este să reziste la atacurile directe, indirecte, fake news-urile și tot ce se întâmplă acolo cu Rusia. Uniunea Europeană este un proiect la care eu, ca româncă, mi-am dorit să fim cu țara mea acolo. De aceea, doamna comisar, Consiliul, Parlamentul trebuie să înțeleagă că Republica Moldova are locul ei în Uniunea Europeană și trebuie să o susținem.

Și mai vreau să adaug un lucru: cred foarte tare că ceea ce acum se întâmplă în Ucraina ține în loc și Republica Moldova. Trebuie să separăm. România și Bulgaria a pățit același lucru cu Schengen. Haideți să fim corecți, obiectivi - în Ucraina nu se pot respecta termenele și jaloanele - și să dăm drumul Moldovei și, la terminarea anului 2028, Republica Moldova să fie în marea familie.
2-0490-0000.englishText:
Madam Commissioner, Mr. President, dear colleagues, the ambitious program of the Republic of Moldova to conclude the accession at the end of 2028 must be supported. It is to be welcomed, but it cannot be implemented unless we all support it. And I want from the very beginning to thank the Commissioner and the colleagues who supported this project.

I am Romanian, I am Moldovan, I know the Republic of Moldova very well, I know the citizens there, the citizens want this and we must encourage them to trust the European Union project, because the administration in Chisinau needs popular support.

Of course, I don't see any other way and we have to be realistic: the Republic of Moldova is on the border, how hard it is to resist direct and indirect attacks, fake news and everything that happens there with Russia. The European Union is a project in which I, as a Romanian, wanted to be there with my country. That is why, Madam Commissioner, the Council, the Parliament must understand that the Republic of Moldova has its place in the European Union and we must support it.

And I want to add one more thing: I strongly believe that what is happening in Ukraine now also holds the Republic of Moldova in place. We have to separate. Romania and Bulgaria suffered the same thing with Schengen. Let's be fair, objective - deadlines and milestones cannot be respected in Ukraine - and let Moldova go and, at the end of 2028, the Republic of Moldova will be in the big family.

2-0491-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, mă bucur că Republica Moldova a deschis primul capitol de negociere pentru aderarea la Uniunea Europeană. De acum, datoria noastră este să nu transformăm acest drum european într-o sală de așteptare fără sfârșit. Republica Moldova trebuie evaluată corect. Este firesc ca România să susțină Republica Moldova în parcursul său de aderare la Uniunea Europeană.

Sprijinirea românilor de peste Prut este o datorie istorică și o necesitate strategică. Cu atât mai mult cu cât aproape jumătate din ei sunt și cetățeni ai României. Integrarea sa în Uniunea Europeană reprezintă mai multă stabilitate și mai multă siguranță la frontiera estică a Uniunii. Însă Republica Moldova trebuie să continue să se desprindă de moștenirea sa sovietică, precum și de reflexele trecutului, iar Bruxelles-ul trebuie să-și dovedească deschiderea pentru un rezultat final concret și neîntârziat.

Dacă românii de peste ambele maluri ale Prutului nu s-au putut reunifica precum berlinezii, atunci Republica Moldova și România trebuie să se reunifice măcar prin apartenența lor la Uniunea Europeană.
2-0491-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, dear colleagues, I am glad that the Republic of Moldova has opened the first chapter of negotiations for the accession to the European Union. From now on, our duty is not to turn this European road into an endless waiting room. The Republic of Moldova must be evaluated correctly. It is natural for Romania to support the Republic of Moldova during its accession to the European Union.

Supporting the Romanians across the Prut is a historical duty and a strategic necessity. All the more so since almost half of them are also citizens of Romania. Its integration into the European Union means more stability and security at the Union's eastern border. But the Republic of Moldova must continue to detach itself from its Soviet heritage, as well as from the reflexes of the past, and Brussels must prove its openness to a concrete and immediate end result.

If the Romanians from across both banks of the Prut could not reunify like the Berliners, then the Republic of Moldova and Romania must at least reunify through their membership in the European Union.

2-0492-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Mołdawia daje nadzieję tak potrzebną dziś Unii Europejskiej, bo członkostwo Mołdawii w Unii Europejskiej pokazuje, że te starania europejskie to coś więcej niż zabieganie o fundusze, o instytucje. To walka o wartości. I ta droga europejska Mołdawii pokazuje, że można pokonać ruski mir, że można wygrać z ruskimi służbami. Z tym Goliatem Dawid może wygrać prawdą, konsekwencją i determinacją.

Mołdawia jest dla nas wzorcem, w jaki sposób walczyć z oligarchami, którzy próbują destabilizować nasze społeczeństwa, jak walczyć z kłamstwem, ale też jak walczyć z takimi zjawiskami jak kryptowaluty, które nadal w niektórych państwach Unii Europejskiej używane są do niszczenia demokracji, niszczenia Unii Europejskiej. Bierzmy przykład z Mołdawii – małego, ale wielkiego duchem państwa.
2-0492-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Moldova gives hope so needed to the European Union today, because Moldova's membership in the European Union shows that these European efforts are more than just seeking funds and institutions. It's a fight for values. And this European path of Moldova shows that it is possible to defeat the Russian rule, that it is possible to win against the Russian services. David can win against this Goliath with truth, consistency and determination.

Moldova is a model for us on how to fight oligarchs who try to destabilize our societies, how to fight lies, but also how to fight phenomena such as cryptocurrencies, which are still used in some European Union countries to destroy democracy and destroy the European Union. Let's take the example of Moldova - a small but great-spirited country.

2-0494-0000.sourceText: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Moldova šiandien demonstruoja įspūdingą europinį pagreitį: užbaigta dvišalė patikra, visi šeši narystės derybų klasteriai jau potencialiai atverti, o dvidešimt keturi iš dvidešimt šešių reformos žingsnių jau įgyvendinti. Matoma akivaizdi pažanga pamatinių vertybių, vidaus rinkos ir išorės santykių srityse. Moldova toliau bando nuosekliai judėti išteklių, žemės ūkio bei sanglaudos kryptimis. Mums, Europos Sąjungai, tai argumentas veikti drąsiai ir atverti derybas dėl narystės, parodant, kad reformos duoda realų politinį rezultatą. Žinoma, Rusijos karinis buvimas Padniestrėje yra tarptautinės teisės pažeidimas ir tiesioginė grėsmė. Rusai privalo besąlygiškai pasitraukti, o mes privalome padėti Moldovai stiprinti atsparumą energetinę nepriklausomybę ir pasitikėjimą europiniu keliu.
2-0494-0000.englishText: Dear President, Commissioner, colleagues. Today, Moldova is showing impressive European momentum: the bilateral verification has been completed, all six accession negotiation clusters are already potentially open, and twenty-four out of twenty-six reform steps have already been implemented. Visible progress can be seen in the areas of core values, the internal market and external relations. Moldova continues to try to move consistently in the directions of resources, agriculture and cohesion. For us, the European Union, this is an argument to act boldly and open negotiations on membership, showing that the reforms produce a real political result. Of course, Russia's military presence in Transnistria is a violation of international law and a direct threat. The Russians must leave unconditionally, and we must help Moldova strengthen its resilience, energy independence and confidence in the European path.

2-0495-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, doamnelor și domnilor, astăzi nu decidem doar asupra parcursului european al Republicii Moldova. Decidem și cât de credibilă este Uniunea Europeană atunci când un popor își asumă valorile noastre și are curajul să le apere.

Republica Moldova nu cere favoruri. Vine cu reforme, cu sacrificii și cu alegere democratică reafirmate de cetățenii săi. Vine cu demnitate și cu rezistența remarcabilă în fața presiunii și amenințării ruse. De aceea, Republica Moldova nu este doar un stat candidat. Este dovada că proiectul european inspiră, mobilizează și oferă speranțe. Pentru România acest sprijin este o responsabilitate istorică. Pentru Uniunea Europeană, este o chestiune de credibilitate.

Nu putem cere curaj celor care aleg Europa și apoi să-i părăsim. Reformele trebuie să continue în Moldova, iar noi trebuie să răspundem cu un sprijin ferm și consecvent. Astăzi, votul nostru trebuie să fie direct pentru Moldova, cât și pentru Uniunea Europeană unită.
2-0495-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Madam Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, today we are not only deciding on the European course of the Republic of Moldova. We also decide how credible the European Union is when a people assumes our values ​​and has the courage to defend them.

The Republic of Moldova does not ask for favors. It comes with reforms, sacrifices and democratic choice reaffirmed by its citizens. It comes with dignity and remarkable resilience in the face of Russian pressure and threat. That is why the Republic of Moldova is not just a candidate state. It is proof that the European project inspires, mobilizes and offers hope. For Romania, this support is a historical responsibility. For the European Union, it is a matter of credibility.
