We cannot ask for courage from those who choose Europe and then leave them. Reforms must continue in Moldova, and we must respond with firm and consistent support. Today, our vote must be directly for Moldova, as well as for the united European Union.

2-0496-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Moldau steht erneut an einem Wendepunkt. Die jüngsten politischen Entwicklungen in Chișinău zeigen, wie sensibel die innenpolitische Lage bleibt und wie entscheidend Stabilität, Reformfähigkeit und ein klarer europäischer Kurs jetzt sind.

Gerade vor diesem Hintergrund halte ich diesen Bericht für besonders wichtig. Er zeigt deutlich: Moldau hat trotz enormen äußeren Drucks bemerkenswerte Fortschritte gemacht im EU‑Beitrittsprozess – bei Reformen im Justiz- und Verwaltungsbereich und bei der wirtschaftlichen Annäherung an die Europäische Union.

Aber wir dürfen nicht naiv sein. Moldau steht unter einem anhaltenden hybriden Angriff – Desinformation, Cyberangriffe, Energie-Erpressung und russische Einflussnahme zielen darauf, den europäischen Kurs des Landes zu brechen.

Unsere Antwort muss klar sein: Wir unterstützen Moldau politisch, finanziell und sicherheitspolitisch. Die Beitrittsverhandlungen müssen auf Leistung beruhen, nicht auf Blockaden. Wer Reformen liefert, muss Fortschritt sehen. Moldaus europäische Zukunft ist nicht nur eine moldauische Frage, sie ist eine Frage der Glaubwürdigkeit und Sicherheit Europas.
2-0496-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! Moldova is once again at a turning point. The latest political developments in Chișinău show how sensitive the domestic political situation remains and how crucial stability, the ability to reform and a clear European course are now.

It is precisely against this background that I consider this report to be particularly important. It shows clearly that, despite enormous external pressure, Moldova has made remarkable progress in the EU accession process - in judicial and administrative reforms and in economic rapprochement with the European Union.

But we must not be naive. Moldova is under a sustained hybrid attack – disinformation, cyberattacks, energy blackmail and Russian influence aimed at disrupting the country's European trajectory.

Our answer must be clear: we support Moldova politically, financially and in terms of security. The accession negotiations must be based on performance, not on blockages. Anyone who delivers reforms must see progress. Moldova's European future is not just a Moldovan question, it is a question of Europe's credibility and security.

2-0497-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Mołdawia jest wyjątkowym krajem kandydatem. I chciałbym bardzo serdecznie podziękować również Pani, Pani Komisarz, że od samego początku stawia Pani na Mołdawię – na kraj, który również według tego przedstawionego sprawozdania ma największe postępy, jeśli chodzi o przygotowania do członkostwa. I chcemy to bardzo wyraźnie powiedzieć.

Ale to jest też kraj, który inspiruje i który motywuje również odpowiedzialnością za odporność społeczną i demokratyczną, za rozumienie, czym jest bezpieczeństwo, czym są zagrożenia hybrydowe obecne wokół naszego sąsiedztwa.

Jako sprawozdawca ds. mobilności wojskowej zaproponowałem, żeby Mołdawia była jednym z bliskich partnerów, którzy zostaną uwzględnieni w tej regulacji, ponieważ budując mobilność wojskową, budując korytarze mobilności, chcemy uwzględnić również kraje kandydujące. Mołdawia ma tam swoje miejsce.
2-0497-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Madam Commissioner! Moldova is an exceptional candidate country. And I would also like to thank you, Commissioner, very much, for choosing Moldova from the very beginning - the country which, according to this report, is making the greatest progress in preparation for membership. And we want to say this very clearly.

But it is also a country that inspires and that also motivates us with responsibility for social and democratic resilience, for understanding what security is, what the hybrid threats present around our neighborhood are.

As rapporteur for military mobility, I proposed that Moldova be one of the close partners to be included in this regulation, because when building military mobility, building mobility corridors, we also want to include candidate countries. Moldova has its place there.

2-0500-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, no entiendo en absoluto qué hacéis algunos diputados —casi todos españoles— aplaudiendo la ampliación de la Unión Europea antes en el debate anterior de Ucrania y ahora en el de Moldavia.

Que lo hagan los alemanes lo puedo entender, pero nosotros, los españoles, ¿no hemos leído aquí el estudio interno filtrado del propio Consejo de la Unión Europea en 2023, en el que se señala que España va a ser el único país que va a pasar de cobrar a pagar? ¿Saben ustedes lo que significan 3 000 millones de euros de la PAC menos para un agricultor en España, en Rumanía, en Portugal o en Italia?

¿Saben lo que significa meter al país más pobre de Europa, que es Moldavia, con 2,4 millones de habitantes —lo sé porque he estado en Moldavia como voluntario, con refugiados de Moldavia— y con una corrupción sistémica del 12 % del PIB? Hablamos de meter ahora mismo a un territorio que tiene 1 500 soldados rusos dentro, en Transnistria, con un referéndum europeo, por cierto, que sacó un 50,4 %, y gracias al voto de la diáspora, porque uno de cada tres moldavos viven fuera de su país.

En fin, entiendo que algunos sí, pero que los diputados españoles apoyen esto me parece surrealista.
2-0500-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, I do not understand at all what some deputies—almost all Spanish—are doing applauding the enlargement of the European Union before in the previous debate on Ukraine and now in the one on Moldova.

I can understand that the Germans do it, but we, the Spanish, haven't we read here the leaked internal study of the Council of the European Union itself in 2023, which indicates that Spain is going to be the only country that is going to go from collecting to paying? Do you know what 3 billion euros less CAP means for a farmer in Spain, Romania, Portugal or Italy?

Do you know what it means to put the poorest country in Europe, which is Moldova, with 2.4 million inhabitants – I know this because I have been in Moldova as a volunteer, with Moldovan refugees – and with systemic corruption of 12% of the GDP? We are talking about putting in right now a territory that has 1,500 Russian soldiers inside, in Transnistria, with a European referendum, by the way, that won 50.4%, and thanks to the vote of the diaspora, because one in three Moldovans live outside their country.

Anyway, I understand that some do, but that the Spanish deputies support this seems surreal to me.

2-0504-0000.sourceText:
Ďakujem spravodajcovi a všetkým zúčastneným v debate, ako aj pani komisárke.

Rozprava k tomuto bodu sa týmto skončila a hlasovanie sa uskutoční zajtra.
2-0504-0000.englishText:
I thank the rapporteur and all those who took part in the debate, as well as the Commissioner.

The debate on this item is now closed and the vote will take place tomorrow.

2-0506-0000.sourceText: Dalším bodom programu je správa, ktorú predkladá poslanec Picula: správa Komisie o Srbsku za rok 2025 (2025/2255(INI) (A10-0163/2026). Chcel by som informovať poslancov a poslankyne, že pri tejto rozprave bude len jedno kolo rečníkov za politické skupiny. Preto sa nebude uplatňovať postup prihlásenia sa o slovo zdvihnutím ruky, ani nebudú akceptované žiadne modré karty. A na úvod poprosím spravodajcu, pána kolegu Piculu, nech sa páči.
2-0506-0000.englishText: The next item on the agenda is the report presented by Mr Picula: the Commission's report on Serbia 2025 (2025/2255(INI) (A10-0163/2026). I would like to inform Members that there will be only one round of speakers per political group in this debate. Therefore, there will be no show of hands and no blue cards will be accepted. to the rapporteur, colleague Picula, please.

2-0507-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, ovogodišnje izvješće odražava stvarnost u Srbiji u jednom od ključnih razdoblja njezine novije povijesti. Gotovo da nema poglavlja u kojem napredak prema članstvu u Europskoj uniji nije ocijenjen kao ograničen ili nepostojeći.

I naša se misija u Beogradu početkom godine odvijala u neobično teškim okolnostima. Zastupnici su bili izloženi verbalnim napadima predstavnika vlasti i provladinih medija, a visoki dužnosnici Srbije više su puta iznosili neutemeljene tvrdnje da Europska unija i neke njezine države članice potiču ili podržavaju tzv. obojenu revoluciju u Srbiji.

Uglavnom, napredak Srbije u ostvarivanju reformi važnima za napredak prema članstvu u Europskoj uniji značajno se usporio. U nekoliko ključnih područja, a posebno u vladavini prava, došlo je i do nazadovanja.

To se reflektira i preko ograničenog napretka u dijalogu Beograda i Prištine, kontinuiranog manjka usklađivanja sa zajedničkom vanjskom i sigurnosnom politikom, nedostatka istinske političke predanosti reformama, agresivne retorike prema Europskoj uniji, pogoršanja uvjeta za rad slobodnih medija i organizacija civilnog društva. Bilježi se kontinuirani neuspjeh u sveobuhvatnoj provedbi preporuka u izbornoj reformi jer i dalje postoji problem s regulatornim tijelom i s biračkim spiskom.

Dok vlasti u Srbiji i dalje predstavljaju članstvo u Europskoj uniji kao svoj strateški cilj, postupci njenog političkog vodstva često to ne potvrđuju. Zadnje izvješće Europske komisije također ukazuje na kontinuirano demokratsko nazadovanje, nedovoljan napredak u reformama vladavine prava i sve veći jaz između izrečenih europskih težnji Srbije i njezine političke prakse. Nažalost, ne vidimo ni napredak u istrazi o urušavanju nadstrešnice željezničkog kolodvora u Novom Sadu, što je potaknulo masovno nezadovoljstvo građana.

Zbog neispunjenih obveza ili ozbiljnog nedostatka rezultata, osobito u području vladavine prava, izvješće poziva Komisiju da zaustavi buduće isplate u okviru Instrumenta za reforme i rast za zapadni Balkan. Također se zalažem za reprogramiranje postojećih i budućih sredstava Europske unije kako bi se ojačala podrška reformi pravosuđa, naporima u borbi protiv korupcije, neovisnim medijima, organizacijama civilnog društva i neovisnom kulturnom sektoru.

Podsjetio bih kako je politika stabilokracije i gledanja kroz prste autokratima u posljednjih desetak godina stimulirala postojeće loše prilike na dobrom dijelu zapadnog Balkana.

Zato se ne moramo pitati kako bi danas prošao referendum o ulasku Srbije u Europsku uniju, upravo zbog niske podrške članstvu. Ima puno razloga zašto je ta podrška najniža u regiji, budući da se protueuropska retorika koristi godinama. Međutim, svakako je važan element za gubitak povjerenja u Europsku uniju i njezine institucije i toleriranje lažnog proeuropskog narativa vlasti u Beogradu svih proteklih godina.

Zbog toga sam uvjeren da je promašeno inzistiranje na otvaranju pregovaračkog klastera 3, čime bi se obnovili pregovori o pristupanju Srbije Europskoj uniji nakon četiri godine zastoja. Ta je stagnacija imala svoje jasne i opravdane razloge, baš kao što ih pokretanje nema ni danas.

Izvješće reflektira kontinuirano urušavanje demokratskih standarda u Srbiji. Zar treba nagraditi neusklađenost s europskom vanjskom politikom koja je tek na 63 posto, unatoč tome što druge države kandidatkinje nemaju problem potpunog usklađivanja? Uz jačanje veza s Kinom i Rusijom, imamo i slučaj da ministar u vladi ide u posjet Iranu, a nemojmo zaboraviti kako je predsjednica srpskog parlamenta svojedobno otišla i na inauguraciju Nicolasa Madura.

Osim toga, nemoguće je ne reagirati na pokušaje iz Beograda da se ugrozi održavanje samita Europske unije zapadnog Balkana nedavno u Crnoj Gori. Sve to pokazuje da odnosi Europske unije i Srbije ne mogu biti tek tako resetirani.

Izuzetno veliki problem je i stanje medija. Upravo se odvija proces preuzimanja i ono malo preostalih slobodnih medija koji lako mogu biti dovedeni u ovisnost od vlasti koja je dokazala da ne tolerira nikakvu kritiku.

(Predsjedavajući je govorniku oduzeo riječ)
2-0507-0000.englishText:
Dear chairman, commissioners, colleagues, this year's report reflects the reality in Serbia in one of the key periods of its recent history. There is almost no chapter in which progress towards membership in the European Union is not assessed as limited or non-existent.

And our mission in Belgrade at the beginning of the year took place in unusually difficult circumstances. Deputies were exposed to verbal attacks from government representatives and pro-government media, and high-ranking Serbian officials repeatedly made unfounded claims that the European Union and some of its member states encourage or support the so-called color revolution in Serbia.

Basically, Serbia's progress in achieving reforms important for progress towards membership in the European Union has slowed down significantly. In several key areas, especially in the rule of law, there has been a setback.

This is also reflected in the limited progress in the dialogue between Belgrade and Pristina, the continuous lack of coordination with the common foreign and security policy, the lack of true political commitment to reforms, aggressive rhetoric towards the European Union, worsening conditions for the work of free media and civil society organizations. There is a continuous failure in the comprehensive implementation of the recommendations in the electoral reform because there is still a problem with the regulatory body and with the voter list.

While the authorities in Serbia continue to present membership in the European Union as their strategic goal, the actions of its political leadership often do not confirm this. The European Commission's latest report also points to continued democratic backsliding, insufficient progress in rule of law reforms, and a growing gap between Serbia's stated European aspirations and its political practice. Unfortunately, we do not see any progress in the investigation into the collapse of the railway station canopy in Novi Sad, which has fueled mass dissatisfaction among citizens.

Due to outstanding commitments or a serious lack of results, particularly in the area of ​​the rule of law, the report calls on the Commission to freeze future disbursements under the Reform and Growth Instrument for the Western Balkans. I am also in favor of reprogramming existing and future EU funds to strengthen support for judicial reform, anti-corruption efforts, independent media, civil society organizations and the independent cultural sector.

I would like to remind you that the policy of stabilocracy and looking through the fingers of the autocrats in the last ten years stimulated the existing bad conditions in a good part of the Western Balkans.

That's why we don't have to wonder how the referendum on Serbia's entry into the European Union would pass today, precisely because of the low support for membership. There are many reasons why this support is the lowest in the region, since anti-European rhetoric has been used for years. However, it is certainly an important element for the loss of trust in the European Union and its institutions and toleration of the false pro-European narrative of the authorities in Belgrade for all the past years.

For this reason, I am convinced that the insistence on the opening of negotiating cluster 3, which would renew the negotiations on Serbia's accession to the European Union after four years of stagnation, was a failure. That stagnation had its own clear and justified reasons, just as the start-up does not have them even today.

The report reflects the continuous collapse of democratic standards in Serbia. Should non-compliance with the European foreign policy, which is only 63 percent, be rewarded, despite the fact that other candidate states do not have a problem with full compliance? In addition to the strengthening of ties with China and Russia, we also have the case of a minister in the government visiting Iran, and let's not forget that the president of the Serbian parliament once went to the inauguration of Nicolas Maduro.

In addition, it is impossible not to react to the attempts from Belgrade to jeopardize the holding of the summit of the European Union of the Western Balkans recently in Montenegro. All this shows that the relations between the European Union and Serbia cannot be reset just like that.

The state of the media is also an extremely big problem. The process of taking over the few remaining free media, which can easily be brought into dependence on the government, which has proven that it does not tolerate any criticism, is taking place.

(The chairman interrupted the speaker)

2-0512-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Mindnyájan egyetérthetünk abban, hogy Szerbia előtt ma komoly kihívások állnak. Folytatni kell a reformokat, erősíteni kell a társadalmi párbeszédet, és előre kell vinni az európai integrációs folyamatot. Ugyanakkor fontos, hogy a mai vitát a jelenlegi európai politikai környezetben értelmezzük. Az elmúlt hetekben világos üzenetet kaptunk: az Európai Unió stratégiai prioritásként tekint a bővítésre. Montenegró újabb tárgyalási fejezeteket zár le. Ukrajna és Moldova megnyitotta első tárgyalási klaszterét. Tegnap az Európai Bizottság egyértelművé tette, hogy támogatja a harmadik tárgyalási klaszter júliusi megnyitását Szerbia számára, mert megítélése szerint ennek feltételei teljesültek. Ez egy kedvező politikai pillanat, amelyet sem Szerbiának, sem az Európai Uniónak nem szabad elszalasztania.

A hiányosságokat meg kell nevezni, de ugyanolyan fontos elismerni azokat az eredményeket is, amelyek megszülettek. Az elmúlt hónapokban Szerbia 23 kulcsfontosságú törvényt fogadott el, köztük uniós jogharmonizációs, igazságügyi és választási reformokat. A szerb parlament ezen a héten további, az ODIR ajánlásait, valamint a 23/24-es tárgyalási fejezetet érintő jogszabályokat tárgyal. Májusban a kormány elfogadta a kisebbségi cselekvési tervet is. Sajnálatos módon a jelentés hangvétele nem tükrözi ezt a kiegyensúlyozott megközelítést. Szinte kizárólag a hiányosságokra összpontosít, miközben a reformok és az elért eredmények csak elvétve jelennek meg benne.

Ha meg is jelenik benne dicséret, újabb bírálatok relativizálják az elismerést. A hiteles és érdemalapú bővítési politika nem csak a hiányosságok feltárását, hanem a reformok eredményeinek elismerését is megköveteli. Csak így őrizhetjük meg a bővítési politika hitelességét, ami Szerbia, a Nyugat-Balkán és az Európai Unió közös érdekét szolgálja.
2-0512-0000.englishText:
Dear Mr. President! We can all agree that Serbia faces serious challenges today. Reforms must be continued, social dialogue must be strengthened and the European integration process must be advanced. At the same time, it is important to interpret today's debate in the current European political environment. In recent weeks, we have received a clear message: the European Union regards enlargement as a strategic priority. Montenegro closes new negotiation chapters. Ukraine and Moldova opened their first negotiation cluster. Yesterday, the European Commission made it clear that it supports the opening of the third negotiation cluster for Serbia in July, because in its opinion the conditions for this have been met. This is a favorable political moment that neither Serbia nor the European Union should miss.

Shortcomings must be named, but it is equally important to acknowledge the results that have been achieved. In recent months, Serbia has adopted 23 key laws, including EU law harmonisation, judicial and electoral reforms. This week, the Serbian parliament is debating additional legislation related to the ODIR recommendations as well as the 23/24 negotiation chapter. In May, the government also adopted the minority action plan. Unfortunately, the tone of the report does not reflect this balanced approach. It focuses almost exclusively on shortcomings, while reforms and achievements are only sporadically mentioned.

Even if praise appears in it, new criticisms relativize the recognition. A credible and merit-based enlargement policy requires not only the identification of shortcomings, but also the recognition of the results of the reforms. Only in this way can we preserve the credibility of the enlargement policy, which serves the common interest of Serbia, the Western Balkans and the European Union.

2-0513-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, aderarea Serbiei la Uniunea Europeană trebuie să însemne reforme reale, stat de drept și respect deplin pentru minoritățile naționale. Este necesar ca Serbia să trateze drepturile românilor de pe teritoriul său cu seriozitate, fără atribuirea de identități artificiale precum vlahi. Românii sunt români, oriunde ar fi.

Totodată, trebuie să vedem relații de bună vecinătate prin fapte și aici mă refer la proiectul Porților de Fier III de pe Dunăre, pentru că vorbim despre un fluviu internațional, nu despre proprietatea exclusivă a unui stat. De aceea, orice proiect major care poate afecta regimul apelor, securitatea energetică, echilibrul ecologic sau agricultura trebuie discutat transparent cu vecinii, înainte de a deveni o problemă politică.

Integrarea europeană înseamnă încredere, iar încrederea se construiește prin transparență, cooperare și respect reciproc.
2-0513-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, Serbia's accession to the European Union must mean real reforms, the rule of law and full respect for national minorities. It is necessary for Serbia to treat the rights of Romanians on its territory seriously, without assigning artificial identities such as Vlachs. Romanians are Romanians, wherever they are.

At the same time, we must see good neighborly relations through deeds, and here I am referring to the Iron Gates III project on the Danube, because we are talking about an international river, not the exclusive property of a state. Therefore, any major project that may affect the water regime, energy security, ecological balance or agriculture must be transparently discussed with the neighbors, before it becomes a political issue.

European integration means trust, and trust is built through transparency, cooperation and mutual respect.

2-0515-0000.sourceText:
Gospod predsednik, spoštovani! Evropski parlament ni sovražnik srbskega naroda. Prav tako Evropski parlament ni ovira Srbije na poti k Evropski uniji. Je pa Evropski parlament neomajni podpornik demokracije ter vseh tistih, ki se zanjo borijo.

Svoboda medijev, svoboda izražanja, vladavina prava, spoštovanje drugače mislečih in boj proti korupciji žal nimajo domovinske pravice v Srbiji.

Ker je najprej oblast odgovorna za zaščito demokracije, Evropski parlament pošilja jasno sporočilo: „Ne, nismo zadovoljni s stanjem demokracije in bomo vztrajno zahtevali izpolnjevanje vseh temeljnih vrednot demokracije v Srbiji“.

Srbija si zasluži poštene in svobodne volitve čim prej. Da bo to mogoče, je treba izpeljati reforme, zato poziv Evropski komisiji: „Prišel je čas dejanj nosilcev oblasti in ne odpuščanja“.
2-0515-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, respected! The European Parliament is not an enemy of the Serbian nation. Nor is the European Parliament an obstacle for Serbia on its way to the European Union. However, the European Parliament is an unwavering supporter of democracy and all those who fight for it.

Freedom of the media, freedom of expression, the rule of law, respect for those with different opinions and the fight against corruption unfortunately do not have a homeland right in Serbia.

Since the authorities are primarily responsible for the protection of democracy, the European Parliament sends a clear message: "No, we are not satisfied with the state of democracy and will persistently demand the fulfillment of all the fundamental values ​​of democracy in Serbia".

Serbia deserves fair and free elections as soon as possible. In order for this to be possible, reforms must be carried out, hence the call to the European Commission: "The time has come for actions by the authorities, not dismissals".

2-0516-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Serbien står inför ett verkligt vägskäl. På ena sidan Vučićs auktoritära högerregering som aktivt förtrycker oppositionen – ett styre i grunden präglat av korruption och maktmissbruk. Vi ser hur rättsstaten undergrävs. Vi ser hur medias frihet inskränks.

På den andra sidan finns en av Europas mest dynamiska, intressanta och välorganiserade demokratirörelser. De serbiska studenterna har skapat någonting unikt, en gräsrotsrörelse, demokratisk från grunden, som utmanar makten genom ständiga nytänkande, demokratiska protester. De bär fröet till en bättre framtid för Serbien.

Vår uppgift är väldigt tydlig: Det är att göra allt vi kan för ett rättvist val. När det gäller vallagen, när det gäller registreringen av väljare och inte minst när det gäller genomförandet. Det är vårt ansvar.
2-0516-0000.englishText:
Mr Speaker! Serbia faces a real crossroads. On the one hand, Vučić's authoritarian right-wing government that actively represses the opposition – a government fundamentally characterized by corruption and abuse of power. We see how the rule of law is undermined. We see how the freedom of the media is curtailed.

On the other side is one of Europe's most dynamic, interesting and well-organized democracy movements. The Serbian students have created something unique, a grassroots movement, democratic from the ground up, that challenges power through constant innovative, democratic protests. They carry the seeds of a better future for Serbia.

Our task is very clear: It is to do everything we can for a fair election. Regarding the electoral law, regarding the registration of voters and not least regarding the implementation. It is our responsibility.

2-0517-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Gestern hat Lars Klingbeil in Berlin den Bundeshaushalt für 2027 vorgestellt: 200 Milliarden Euro neue Schulden; der deutsche Staat ist nur noch auf Pump finanzierbar. Während Deutschland pleite geht, wollen Sie hier immer mehr Mitglieder in die Europäische Union aufnehmen. Die Konrad‑Adenauer‑Stiftung der CDU schätzt, dass der Beitritt Serbiens 3 Milliarden Euro kosten wird, der gesamte Westbalkan 7 Milliarden Euro im Jahr. Deutsche Steuerzahler werden ein Viertel der Kosten schultern müssen, also etwa 2 Milliarden Euro – das ist ungefähr der Betrag, den die Bundesregierung bei pflegenden Angehörigen einsparen möchte. Mit anderen Worten: Deutsche, die ihre Eltern pflegen, bekommen die Rente gekürzt, damit CDU und SPD ihre Steuergelder auf dem Balkan verjubeln können. Ich wundere mich, dass es überhaupt noch Wähler gibt, die diesen Parteien ihre Stimmen geben.

Seit zwei Jahren gehen die Serben jetzt auf die Straße wegen der Korruption in ihrem Land. Der serbische Präsident hat deshalb seinen Rücktritt erklärt, weil er im Unterschied zu deutschen Politikern bereit ist, Verantwortung für die Fehler seiner Regierung zu übernehmen. Ich finde das vorbildlich; Ursula von der Leyen oder Friedrich Merz sollten sich daran ein Beispiel nehmen und es ihm gleichtun.

Wir wollen eine privilegierte Partnerschaft mit Belgrad. Bevor wir aber mit deutschen Steuergeldern den Balkan sanieren, müssen wir erst einmal Deutschland wieder aufbauen.
2-0517-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! Yesterday in Berlin, Lars Klingbeil presented the federal budget for 2027: 200 billion euros in new debt; the German state can only be financed on credit. While Germany is going bankrupt, you want to admit more and more members into the European Union. The CDU's Konrad Adenauer Foundation estimates that Serbia's accession will cost 3 billion euros and the entire Western Balkans 7 billion euros a year. German taxpayers will have to shoulder a quarter of the costs, or around 2 billion euros - which is roughly the amount the federal government wants to save on carers. In other words: Germans who care for their parents have their pensions reduced so that the CDU and SPD can spend their tax money on the Balkans. I'm surprised there are still voters who vote for these parties.

For two years now, Serbs have been taking to the streets because of corruption in their country. The Serbian president announced his resignation because, unlike German politicians, he is prepared to take responsibility for his government's mistakes. I think that's exemplary; Ursula von der Leyen or Friedrich Merz should follow this example and do the same.

We want a privileged partnership with Belgrade. But before we renovate the Balkans with German tax money, we first have to rebuild Germany.

2-0519-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, naravno, zahvaljujem svima na doprinosu u večerašnjoj raspravi, a pogotovo kolegama izvjestiteljima iz sjene na odličnoj suradnji.

Vjerujem da su današnju raspravu pratili ne samo građani Europske unije, već, prije svega, i građani Srbije. Vjerujem i da građani Srbije žele slobodne i poštene izbore i priliku da grade bolju europsku budućnost, ali nakon godina demokratskog nazadovanja Europska unija ne smije nagraditi srpsku vlast napretkom na pristupnom putu na temelju kvazi reformi.

Srbija je najveća zemlja na zapadnom Balkanu s najvećim kapacitetom za napredak na putu prema članstvu u Europsku uniju. Međutim, umjesto otvaranja i zatvaranja pregovaračkih poglavlja, srpska vlada samo otvara nove dileme i nove napetosti prema susjedima.

Ne možemo govoriti o napretku u dijalogu s Kosovom ako se ne privedu odgovorni za teroristički napad u Banjskoj. Ne možemo govoriti o iskoraku u vladavini prava ako se pokušava ispravljati nešto što je prvobitno urađeno potpuno pogrešno jer ti Mrdićevi zakoni, zapravo Vučićevi zakoni, nisu ni trebali biti usvojeni.

Mi kao Europski parlament moramo biti čvrsti u svojoj predanosti poštivanju vrijednosti i pravila. Ne možemo odšutjeti nazadovanje u vladavini prava, eroziji demokratskih standarda i destruktivnom utjecaju na stabilnost regije.

Ako vlasti u Srbiji žele napredovati na svom putu prema Europskoj uniji, moraju donijeti jasan strateški izbor, napraviti ključne reforme te se u potpunosti uskladiti s vanjskom sigurnosnom politikom Europske unije i sankcijama Europske unije prema Rusiji.
2-0519-0000.englishText:
Honorable Chairman, of course, I thank everyone for their contribution to tonight's debate, and especially my fellow shadow rapporteurs for their excellent cooperation.

I believe that today's debate was followed not only by the citizens of the European Union, but also, above all, by the citizens of Serbia. I also believe that the citizens of Serbia want free and fair elections and the opportunity to build a better European future, but after years of democratic decline, the European Union must not reward the Serbian government with progress on the accession path based on quasi-reforms.

Serbia is the largest country in the Western Balkans with the greatest capacity for progress on the path to membership in the European Union. However, instead of opening and closing negotiation chapters, the Serbian government only opens new dilemmas and new tensions towards its neighbors.

We cannot talk about progress in the dialogue with Kosovo if those responsible for the terrorist attack in Banjska are not brought to justice. We cannot talk about a step forward in the rule of law if there is an attempt to correct something that was originally done completely wrong, because Mrdić's laws, actually Vučić's laws, should not have been adopted.

We as the European Parliament must be firm in our commitment to respecting values ​​and rules. We cannot ignore the decline in the rule of law, the erosion of democratic standards and the destructive impact on the stability of the region.

If the authorities in Serbia want to progress on their way to the European Union, they must make a clear strategic choice, make key reforms and fully align with the European Union's external security policy and the European Union's sanctions against Russia.

2-0525-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ο κανονισμός που ψηφίστηκε επικαλείται τα δικαιώματα των επιβατών στις αεροπορικές μεταφορές, ενώ ικανοποιεί όλες τις απαιτήσεις των μεγάλων ομίλων του κλάδου που σημειώνουν κέρδη ρεκόρ και έχουν ήδη μπουκώσει από κρατικές και ευρωενωσιακές επιδοτήσεις. Μειώνει περαιτέρω τις υποχρεώσεις των αεροπορικών εταιρειών, ψαλιδίζει τις αποζημιώσεις για τους επιβάτες και ανοίγει τον δρόμο για οριστικό περιορισμό τους, διατηρώντας την έννοια-λάστιχο των έκτακτων περιστάσεων, που δίνει την ικανότητα στους ομίλους να αποφεύγουν αποζημιώσεις κατά το δοκούν και να θησαυρίζουν ακόμα και από τις χειραποσκευές στην καμπίνα, όπως και από τις διαστάσεις της βαλίτσας.

Την ίδια στιγμή, οι εταιρείες, στη βάση της απελευθερωμένης αγοράς, έχουν εκτοξεύσει τις τιμές και εκμηδενίσει τις όποιες υπηρεσίες στους επιβάτες. Κριτήριο δράσης τους είναι το κέρδος, όπως βεβαίως και των κυβερνήσεων και της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, που καταδικάζουν τις υπηρεσίες πολιτικής αεροπορίας να λειτουργούν με απαρχαιωμένες υποδομές και λιγοστό προσωπικό σε καθεστώς εντατικοποίησης, βάζοντας σε κίνδυνο την ασφάλεια των πτήσεων. Δεν υπάρχει άλλος δρόμος: Για να κερδίσει δικαιώματα και ασφάλεια ο λαός, πρέπει να χάσει το κεφάλαιο.
2-0525-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the regulation that has been passed invokes the rights of air passengers while satisfying all the demands of the large industry groups who are making record profits and are already stuffed with state and EU subsidies. It further reduces airlines' obligations, slashes compensation for passengers and paves the way for a permanent cap, maintaining the concept of emergency rubber, which gives groups the ability to avoid compensation at will and hoard even from hand luggage in the cabin, as well as from the dimensions of the suitcase.

At the same time, the companies, on the basis of the liberalized market, have skyrocketed the prices and annihilated any services to the passengers. Their criterion of action is profit, just like of course the governments and the European Union, which condemn the civil aviation services to operate with obsolete infrastructures and few personnel in a state of intensification, endangering the safety of flights. There is no other way: For the people to gain rights and security, they must lose capital.

2-0526-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, en este pleno de julio del Parlamento Europeo ha tenido lugar la votación definitiva del Reglamento sobre los derechos de los pasajeros aéreos y es una votación que tiene dos rasgos extraordinarios que merecen subrayarse.

El primero es la amplísima mayoría: ha votado favorablemente el arco parlamentario casi entero. Ha recibido votos favorables de todos los grupos parlamentarios. La razón es sencilla: después de trece años de bloqueo, por fin se ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Consejo.

El segundo rasgo extraordinario es que, por fin, se produce un avance en los derechos de la ciudadanía y, particularmente, de los pasajeros y muchas veces los derechos laborales —incluso los derechos fundamentales en la Unión Europea— han venido de la mano de los derechos de los consumidores.

Por fin hay un derecho de compensación frente a los abusos de las compañías aéreas, los retrasos, los sobreprecios y las sobreventas, por fin el derecho reconocido a embarcar la maleta en cabina y por fin facilidades expresas para las personas con dificultades de movilidad, para que puedan ejercer sus derechos en igualdad de condiciones con respecto de todos los demás.
2-0526-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, in this July plenary session of the European Parliament the final vote on the Regulation on the rights of air passengers took place and it is a vote that has two extraordinary features that deserve to be underlined.

The first is the very large majority: almost the entire parliamentary arc has voted favorably. It has received favorable votes from all parliamentary groups. The reason is simple: after thirteen years of deadlock, an agreement has finally been reached with the Council.

The second extraordinary feature is that, finally, there is progress in the rights of citizens and, particularly, of passengers, and many times labor rights—even fundamental rights in the European Union—have come hand in hand with consumer rights.

Finally there is a right to compensation against abuses by airline companies, delays, overpricing and overselling, finally the recognized right to load the suitcase in the cabin and finally express facilities for people with mobility difficulties, so that they can exercise their rights on equal terms with everyone else.

2-0528-0000.sourceText: A teraz nasleduje ústne vysvetlenie hlasovania k správe Gabriele Bischoff: Koordinácia systému sociálneho zabezpečenia.
2-0528-0000.englishText: And now comes the oral explanation of vote on the Gabriele Bischoff report: Coordination of the social security system.

2-0529-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ο κανονισμός υπηρετεί τις ανάγκες του κεφαλαίου για φθηνότερη και πιο ευέλικτη εργατική δύναμη. Στην πράξη, προσαρμόζει το ισχύον πλαίσιο εξατομικευμένης και εμπορευματοποιημένης ασφάλισης πείνας, με γενίκευση των επαγγελματικών ταμείων στις ανάγκες της αγοράς, όπως προανήγγειλε πρόσφατα η κυβέρνηση της Νέας Δημοκρατίας μέσω της Τράπεζας της Ελλάδας. Επιδίωξή του η διασυνοριακή κινητικότητα, δηλαδή η μαζική μετανάστευση από χώρα σε χώρα, κυνηγώντας ένα μεροκάματο.

Στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση της πολεμικής οικονομίας και εμπλοκής, όπου ο ένας στους τρεις εργαζόμενους είναι και επίσημα φτωχός και η ανεργία θερίζει, ο κανονισμός προτείνει πιο αυστηρούς όρους πρόσβασης στο επίδομα ανεργίας και διατήρησής του. Στόχος του κανονισμού είναι το ξήλωμα των εργατικών δικαιωμάτων, τα βάρη κράτους/ εργοδοσίας να μετατραπούν σε απώλειες για τους εργαζόμενους.

Για να κερδίσουν οι εργαζόμενοι, πρέπει να χάσει το κεφάλαιο, τα κόμματα που το υπηρετούν και οι διεθνείς του συμμαχίες. Να οργανώσουν τώρα την πάλη τους για συλλογικές συμβάσεις εργασίας με αξιοπρεπείς μισθούς, με πλήρη ασφαλιστικά δικαιώματα και μείωση του εργάσιμου χρόνου.
2-0529-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, the regulation serves the needs of capital for a cheaper and more flexible labor force. In practice, it adapts the current framework of personalized and commercialized hunger insurance, by generalizing professional funds to the needs of the market, as recently announced by the government of New Democracy through the Bank of Greece. Its pursuit is cross-border mobility, i.e. mass migration from country to country, chasing a daily wage.

In the European Union of the war economy and engagement, where one in three workers is officially poor and unemployment is rife, the regulation proposes stricter conditions for accessing and maintaining unemployment benefits. The goal of the regulation is the removal of labor rights, the burdens of the state/employer to turn into losses for the workers.

For workers to win, capital must lose, the parties that serve it and its international alliances. To organize now their fight for collective labor contracts with decent wages, with full insurance rights and a reduction in working time.

2-0530-0000.sourceText: Týmto sme ukončili vysvetlenia hlasovania a aj dnešné debaty.
2-0530-0000.englishText: This concludes the explanations of the vote and today's debates.

2-0534-0000.sourceText: Nasledujúce rokovanie sa uskutoční zajtra v stredu 8. júla 2026 so začiatkom o 9. hodine ráno. Program schôdze je uverejnený, bol uverejnený a je k dispozícii na webovom sídle Európskeho parlamentu.
2-0534-0000.englishText: The next meeting will take place tomorrow, Wednesday 8 July 2026, starting at 9 am. The agenda of the meeting is published, has been published and is available on the website of the European Parliament.

2-0536-0000.sourceText: Zápisnica z tohto rokovania bude predložená Parlamentu na schválenie zajtra po hlasovaní.
2-0536-0000.englishText: The minutes of this meeting will be submitted to the Parliament for approval tomorrow after the vote.
